# Roadmap: algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry

**Summary.** This roadmap builds the representability and moduli machinery that arithmetic moduli
problems need on top of the scheme and stack foundations: projective parameter spaces for arbitrary
quasi-coherent and coherent modules (projective bundles with all integer twists and their
cohomology, coherent Grassmannians, Plücker embeddings, partial and complete flags, relative very
ampleness, Hilbert polynomials, Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and Chow-type boundedness); Hilbert
functors, Hom, Isom and automorphism schemes and coherent dévissage; effective descent of
quasi-coherent modules, of algebraic spaces and of polarized objects, with relative Hom and Weil
restriction of algebraic spaces along finite locally free morphisms; gerbes with abelian bandings,
their neutralizations, their classification by derived `H²`, profinite limits of finite-stage
gerbes and the intrinsic band; rigidification of stacks along flat subgroups of inertia, rigid
level structures, finite correspondences and normalizations of Deligne–Mumford stacks; Artin
approximation over henselian G-rings; Artin's representability criteria, Picard sheaves and their rigidifications, arithmetic coefficient
comparisons and nonarchimedean analytification of algebraic spaces; framed deformation groupoids
and completed local comparisons; and applications of supplied characteristic-zero resolution and
strict normal crossings compactification to the vanishing theorems and the uniform
numerical boundedness used to construct moduli. We want it because these are the representability
inputs of moduli of curves, abelian varieties and Shimura data over arithmetic bases. Mathlib has
schemes, sites, sheaf cohomology and stacks as pseudofunctors, but no relative projective bundles of
modules, gerbes, rigidification, Artin criteria, Picard spaces or resolution; SchemeAndStackFoundations
stops at algebraic spaces and stacks, scheme formal existence and Schlessinger's theorem, and the
arithmetic moduli roadmaps (ModularCurvesPartII, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, PELModuli,
ShimuraVarieties) need one common set of these carriers rather than private versions.

The roadmap starts from Mathlib's schemes, module sheaves, Grassmannian functor, `Proj`, descent
data, stacks (`Pseudofunctor.IsStack`) and site cohomology (`Sheaf.H`), from Tau Ceti's invertible
sheaves, line-bundle classes, rigidified line bundles, scheme-module tensor products and coherent
cohomology, and from the algebraic spaces, stacks, site cohomology and deformation theory of
SchemeAndStackFoundations. It is built in nine layers. Its end theorems are the universal property
and cohomology of `P(E)` for every quasi-coherent `E`, representability of coherent Grassmannians
and flags, Mumford's uniform regularity bound and the boundedness of Hilbert polynomials (Layer 1);
representability of Hom schemes with quasi-projective targets, automorphism schemes and coherent
dévissage (Layer 2); effective fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules on algebraic spaces, from the
scheme case of SchemeAndStackFoundations, and algebraicity of relative Hom and Weil restriction
along finite locally free morphisms (Layer 3); the classification of
`A`-gerbes up to band-preserving equivalence by derived `H²(A)`, with neutrality equivalent to the
vanishing of the class (Layer 4); the rigidification theorem and level removal (Layer 5); Artin
approximation (Layer 6); Artin's criteria, Picard sheafification and infinitesimal lifting, general group-space
components and nonarchimedean GAGA for proper algebraic spaces (Layer 7); effectivity, versality and
algebraization of formal objects (Layer 8); and comparisons with supplied embedded resolution,
principalization and SNC compactification, Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing and the Kollár–Matsusaka
boundedness theorem (Layer 9).

|---|---|---|

| [2](#layer-2-hom-isom-and-coherent-dévissage) | Hom, Isom and coherent dévissage | Hilbert functors as Quot, `Hom/Isom/Aut` schemes, Quot into Grassmannians, dévissage |
| [3](#layer-3-effective-descent-and-finite-source-restriction) | Effective descent and finite-source restriction | affine module descent in overlap and coalgebra form on the imported quasi-coherent descent pseudofunctor, fpqc descent on spaces, relative Hom, Weil restriction, polarized descent |
| [4](#layer-4-gerbes-bands-and-profinite-stages) | Gerbes, bands and profinite stages | gerbes, abelian bandings, neutralizations, derived `H²` classification, finite-stage and profinite gerbes, intrinsic band, Isom torsors and Hom sheaves of banded morphisms |

## Scope and ownership

**This roadmap owns** the projective bundle `P(E) = Proj Sym E` of an arbitrary quasi-coherent
module with its twists, cup products and direct images; coherent Grassmannians of finite-type
modules, the Plücker embedding, partial and complete flag bundles, and smoothness and tangent spaces
of the Grassmannians of locally free modules; relative very ampleness over an arbitrary base;
Hilbert–Serre, Hilbert polynomials, Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity, Chow parameters,
characteristic-free bounded-support parameters, bigness and numerical boundedness; determinantal and
Frobenius-stable loci; Hilbert functors, the extension of Hom schemes to quasi-projective targets,
automorphism schemes and coherent dévissage; the affine overlap and coalgebra presentations of
quasi-coherent descent, descent of finite presentation and finite local freeness, and effective
fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules on algebraic spaces, relative Hom and Weil restriction of
algebraic spaces along finite locally free morphisms, polarized descent over a general base;
gerbes, bandings, neutralizations and their `H²` classification, change of band and of site,
faithful flatness of arbitrary commutative Hopf inclusions and quotients of arbitrary affine groups
by closed normal subgroups, finite-stage and profinite gerbes, the intrinsic band and the Hom
sheaves of banded morphisms; finite-stage twisted-inertia pair stacks, their internal mapping-stack
comparisons and their stackified filtered two-colimit; rigidification, level structures, finite correspondences, schematic
closures and normalizations of Deligne–Mumford stacks; the Artin approximation property; formal
points, Artin's criteria, module obstruction theories, openness of versality from strong formal
effectiveness, perfect-complex rank loci on algebraic spaces, universal flattening of
modules with proper support, Picard stacks as groupoid-valued carriers, Picard sheafification,
section rigidification and infinitesimal lifting, general group-space components, analytification
and proper coherent GAGA for algebraic spaces over complete nonarchimedean fields, boundary duality and `K/O` coefficients; framed deformation groupoids,
formal objects of algebraic stacks and their algebraization; and the applications of supplied
characteristic-zero resolution and SNC compactification to algebraic vanishing theorems and uniform
numerical boundedness.

## Conventions

Projective bundles use the quotient convention `P(E) = Proj Sym(E)`: a `T`-point over `S` is an
invertible quotient `f^*E → L`, modulo isomorphism of its line target, and the universal quotient is
`π^*E → O(1)`. For locally free `E` this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.4's `projectiveBundle` of
`E^∨`, which uses the lines convention. Grassmannians parametrize finite locally free quotients
(Mathlib's `Module.Grassmannian`), and flags retain the nested kernels, not only their ranks.
Integer twists use the inverse line bundle at negative exponents. “Projective locally on the base”
means a closed immersion into a finite projective space after a Zariski cover; a global immersion is
asserted only when the stated hypotheses supply one.

Declaration names are relative to `TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry`; the
displayed prefixes fix their namespaces. Scheme statements are made over schemes; each
algebraic-space extension is a separate target. Names in target descriptions and intended signatures
specify the library to be built; `Suggested.lean` contains headline theorem statements and the
definitions needed to state them.

A site has fixed object and arrow universes. A gerbe is a predicate on Mathlib's `Cat`-valued
pseudofunctors: a stack (`Pseudofunctor.IsStack`) with groupoid fibres, local objects and local
isomorphisms. A banding is specified data, and equivalences in the fixed-band classification
preserve it. For a site without a terminal object, global cohomology and neutrality are taken over
the terminal sheaf of its topos. The lifting gerbe of a quotient torsor uses positive translation by
its kernel; the quotient torsor attached to a chosen object `z` of the changed-band gerbe uses arrows
`z → j(x)`.

Quasi-coherent and invertible modules on an algebraic space live on its ringed small étale site.
The relative Picard object is the fppf sheafification of line-bundle classes modulo base classes; a
section of the sheaf need not have a global line-bundle representative. Formal objects retain the
complete compatible tower and all morphisms. Smooth presentations are versal; a hull additionally has
a bijective tangent map. The supplied characteristic-zero resolution retains ordered exceptional
history; local-isomorphism comparisons omit precisely the steps with empty centre.

## How to read the build

Layer 1 constructs the projective parameter spaces used in Layer 2. Layer 3 assembles descent and
finite-source restriction on top of them. Layer 4 builds gerbes, bands and coherent finite-stage
limits, and Layer 5 applies them to rigidification and finite correspondences. Layer 6 supplies
approximation, Layer 7 Artin's criteria, Picard sheaves and rigidifications, nonarchimedean analytification and the
arithmetic coefficient comparisons, and Layer 8 the formal deformation comparisons. Layer 9 consumes
resolution, preservation of the resolved locus and algebraic SNC compactification from
ResolutionOfSingularitiesCharacteristicZero, then constructs algebraic vanishing and numerical boundedness. Checks are listed under each definition.

Where the section order differs from the order of construction, the target-level order is the
following. In Layer 1, construct `coherentGrassmannian` before `rankOneGrassmannComparison`.
In Layer 3, build the overlap, coalgebra and chosen-pullback comparisons of §§3.2–3.3 before
§3.1’s `moduleDescentCoaction` and `affineModuleDescentEquivalence`. In Layer 2,
`automorphismGroupScheme` uses only the Isom scheme of §2.1 with its composition and inverse; the polarized Isom of §7.6.3 builds on it, not the reverse. In Layer 4, the
auxiliary carriers of §§4.9–4.21 (Isom torsors, banded transformations, pullback and Hom sheaves,
object descent, fibre Hom sheaves and their transport, `CoherentInverse`) are built before the
theorems of §§4.2–4.3 that cite them. In Layer 7, §7.7 (ringed small étale sites,
`SpaceInvertibleModule`, `spaceDQCoh`, `spacePerfect`) comes first, followed by the Artin criteria
of §7.1 and the rank loci of §7.2, using EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.9 for perfect pushforwards.
DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.E.1 supplies `perfectInverseSystemEffectivity`.
The independent inputs `cohStackFiniteTypeModel`,
`universalFlatteningProperSupport`, `coherentModuleHom`, `coherentModuleIsom` and Picard stack
carriers are in §7.3; proper-space formal existence is in §7.8. Picard sheafification and
rigidification use §§7.6.1/7.7. Nonarchimedean local models and quotients (§7.10.2) supply the
analytification comparisons of §7.4. In Layer 9, the algebraic SNC construction of §9.5 and
CrystallineCohomology §§CR.5:log-algebra.4/CR.5.1 supply the logarithmic carrier of §9.10.

## Layer 1: projective parameter spaces

### 1.1 Projective quotients and all integer twists

Define `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`. For a quasi-coherent module E on S, form `P_S(E)=Proj_S Sym(E)`, using the quotient convention: a T-point over S is an invertible quotient `f*E→L`, modulo isomorphism of its line target. The tautological quotient `π*E→O(1)` is surjective and commutes with arbitrary base change. For E finite type the projection is projective locally on S, and for E finitely presented it is finitely presented. Construct it as SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.3's `relativeProj` of the symmetric algebra `Sym E`, a graded quasi-coherent algebra generated in degree one (AlgebraicVectorBundles L0C). When `Sym E` is finitely generated this is StableReduction Layer 2's relative Proj, by §0.3's `relativeProj_eq_stableReduction`; for finite locally free `E` it is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.4's `projectiveBundle` of `E^∨`, by `projectiveBundle_dual_convention`.

Here S arbitrary; E quasi-coherent. Projectivity and finite presentation have the finiteness hypotheses in the statement.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/constructions.pdf), §21, Definition 21.1 and following unnumbered quotient universal property, p.45).

The API gives `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projection`: The structure map `π:P(E)→S`; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.universalQuotient`: The actual surjection `π*E→O(1)`; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.quotient_characterisation`: A map g over S is the classifying map of q exactly when pulling back the tautological quotient gives q up to an isomorphism of its line target; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.baseChange`: `P_T(f*E)≅P_S(E)×_S T`, preserving the quotient; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.rankOne`: `P_S(L)≅S` for invertible L, with `O(1)` identified with L; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.fromQuotient`: Construct the classifying map of an invertible quotient of `f*E`; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.fromQuotient_over`: The classifying map composed with the projection is f; `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.universalQuotient_epi`: The universal quotient is an epimorphism of module sheaves.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.3, StableReduction Layer 2, AlgebraicVectorBundles L0C, Mathlib `SymmetricAlgebra`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.4.

**Checks.**

- `ProjectiveBundleTests.rankOne`: the identity quotient of an invertible `L` gives `P(L) = S`.
- `ProjectiveBundles.noLineQuotientZero`: no invertible quotient of the zero module exists on a nonempty test

- `ProjectiveBundleTests.rankTwo`: Over `Spec R`, points over the identity of `P(O²)` correspond to rank-one quotient Grassmannian data for `R²`.
- `ProjectiveBundleTests.baseChange`: A nonflat base change also gives `P(f*E)≅P(E)×_S T`.

These are invertible since `Sym(E)` is generated in degree one. The canonical tensor, base-change and rank-one comparisons are part of the construction; do not claim invertibility for arbitrary graded algebras.

Here E quasi-coherent; the degree-one generated `Sym(E)` case; no finite-type or flatness hypothesis is needed for invertibility and tensor coherence.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/constructions.pdf), §16, Lemmas 16.10–16.11, p.40; §21, Definition 21.1, p.45 (absolute twist comparison: §10, Lemma 10.3, p.18)).

- `TwistingSheafTests.rankOne`: on `P(L)`, the universal quotient line is `L`, fixing the quotient

On finite locally free E this compares with ModularCurves §0G; on general finite-type E it uses the coherent extension below.

Here S arbitrary; E quasi-coherent finite type.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/constructions.pdf), §21, Definition 21.1 and following unnumbered quotient universal property, p.45).

For the proof, both constructions represent invertible quotients of `f*E`, modulo target isomorphism. Apply the universal properties in both directions and prove identity by uniqueness.

### 1.1a Signatures of the projective-bundle carriers

The intended carrier `ProjectiveBundles.LineQuotient f E` records an invertible module `line` on
`T`, a morphism `quotient : f^*E → line` and the proof `surjective` that it is an epimorphism. It retains
the quotient map, not only the isomorphism class of the line, and is the data of a `T`-point of
`P(E)` over `f`. The projective bundle itself, its structure map, universal quotient, classifying
maps, base change and rank-one comparison (§1.1), the integer twists with their unit, tensor and
pullback comparisons, the cup products (§1.2), relative very ampleness and its evaluation map
(§1.4), regularity (§1.5) and the comparison of `P^n` with the Laurent basis (§1.2) are targets with
the following intended signatures. `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveSpace S n` is the projective bundle
of the free module of rank `n + 1`. (Stacks, §27.21, Definition 27.21.1 and the following
quotient-functor construction, tag 01OA.)

```lean
namespace ProjectiveBundles

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits AlgebraicGeometry Scheme.Modules

open TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

open scoped TensorProduct ZeroObject

noncomputable section

def projectiveBundle (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent] : Scheme.{u}

namespace projectiveBundle

variable (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]

def projection : projectiveBundle S E ⟶ S

def twistingSheaf (m : ℤ) : InvertibleSheaf (projectiveBundle S E)

def universalQuotient :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (projection S E)).obj E ⟶ (twistingSheaf S E 1).obj

def fromQuotient {T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) (q : LineQuotient f E) :
    T ⟶ projectiveBundle S E

def baseChange (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S)
    [((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E).IsQuasicoherent] :
    projectiveBundle T ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) ≅
      Limits.pullback (projection S E) f

def rankOne (L : InvertibleSheaf S) [L.obj.IsQuasicoherent] :
    projectiveBundle S L.obj ≅ S

end projectiveBundle

abbrev projectiveSpace (S : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ) :=
  projectiveBundle S (SheafOfModules.free (R := S.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))))

namespace projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf

variable (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]

def zero : (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E 0).obj ≅
    SheafOfModules.unit (projectiveBundle S E).ringCatSheaf

def add (a b : ℤ) :
    MonoidalCategory.tensorObj (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E a).obj
      (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E b).obj ≅
      (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E (a + b)).obj

def pullback {T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) [((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E).IsQuasicoherent]
    (m : ℤ) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (projectiveBundle.baseChange S E T f).hom).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.fst
        (projectiveBundle.projection S E) f)).obj (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E m).obj) ≅
      (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf T ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) m).obj

end projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf

def twistMultiplication (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    (a b : ℤ) (i j : ℕ) :
    Cohomology (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E a).obj i →+
    Cohomology (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E b).obj j →+
    Cohomology (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E (a + b)).obj (i + j)

namespace twistMultiplication

variable (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]

def sectionProduct (a b : ℤ) :
    Γ((projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E a).obj, ⊤) →+
      Γ((projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E b).obj, ⊤) →+
      Γ((projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E (a + b)).obj, ⊤)

def unit : Cohomology (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E 0).obj 0

end twistMultiplication

def IsRelativelyVeryAmple {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L : InvertibleSheaf X) : Prop :=
  ∃ (E : S.Modules) (_ : E.IsQuasicoherent) (i : X ⟶ projectiveBundle S E),
    IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ projectiveBundle.projection S E = f ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf S E 1).obj ≅ L.obj)

namespace IsRelativelyVeryAmple

variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L : InvertibleSheaf X)

def evaluationQuotient
    [Epi ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app L.obj)] :
    LineQuotient f ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj L.obj)

def completeMap [((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj L.obj).IsQuasicoherent]
    [Epi ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app L.obj)] :
    X ⟶ projectiveBundle S ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj L.obj)

end IsRelativelyVeryAmple

def projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (n : ℕ) (m : ℤ) (q : ℕ) :
    Cohomology (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf (Spec (.of A))
      (SheafOfModules.free (R := (Spec (.of A)).ringCatSheaf)
        (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)))) m).obj q ≃+
      (projectiveTwistBasis n q m →₀ A)

def IsCMRegular (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (F : (projectiveSpace (Spec (.of k)) n).Modules) (m : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → Subsingleton (Cohomology
    (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj F
      (projectiveBundle.twistingSheaf (Spec (.of k))
        (SheafOfModules.free (R := (Spec (.of k)).ringCatSheaf)
          (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)))) (m - (i : ℤ))).obj) i)

end

end ProjectiveBundles
```

**Checks.**

- `ProjectiveBundles.noLineQuotientZero`: no invertible quotient of the zero module exists on a nonempty test
  scheme, so `P(0)` is empty.
- `ProjectiveBundleTests.rankOne`: the identity quotient of an invertible `L` gives `P(L) = S`.
- `TwistingSheafTests.rankOne`: on `P(L)`, the universal quotient line is `L`, fixing the quotient
  convention against its dual.

### 1.2 Cohomology and multiplication

Define `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication`. Construct the natural cup maps `Hⁱ(O(a))×H^j(O(b))→H^{i+j}(O(a+b))`. In degree zero they agree with homogeneous polynomial multiplication. For `Hⁿ`, multiplication by a homogeneous polynomial is multiplication of Laurent representatives followed by discarding terms whose exponent vector is not all negative; equivalently it is dual to multiplication under the determinant-twisted top pairing.

Here Projective bundles for the cup maps; on projective space use the preceding explicit basis.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §8, Lemma 8.2, pp.19–20 and proof of Lemma 8.4, pp.20–22).

The API gives `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication.zero_left`: The cup map is zero when its first input is zero; `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication.add_left`: The cup map is additive in each argument; `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication.section_product`: Via the `H⁰`/global-section equivalence, degree-zero cup product is the tensor product of sections; `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication.sectionProduct`: Canonical tensor product of global sections through `O(a)⊗O(b)≅O(a+b)`; `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication.unit`: The `H⁰(O(0))` class obtained from the actual section 1 through `O(0)≅O` and the `H⁰≅Γ` equivalence.

*Needs:* `integerTwists`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyZeroEquiv`, Tau Ceti `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.instMonoidalCategory`.

**Checks.**

- `TwistMultiplicationTests.zero`: Zero section times any class is zero.
- `TwistMultiplicationTests.unit`: The section 1 of `O(0)` acts as identity on `H⁰(O(1))`.
- `TwistMultiplicationTests.topBoundary`: On `P¹`, `H¹(O(-2))` times `H⁰(O(1))` lands in zero `H¹(O(-1))`.

Prove `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`. For a commutative ring `A`,
integers `n ≥ 0`, `m` and `q ≥ 0`, the cohomology `H^q(P^n_A, O(m))` of the projective space
`P^n_A = P(O^{n+1})` of §1.1 is additively isomorphic to the free `A`-module on
`ProjectiveBundles.projectiveTwistBasis n q m`: the exponent vectors `e ∈ ℤ^{n+1}` with
`Σ e_i = m` which are nonnegative when `q = 0`, all negative when `q = n ≥ 1`, and arbitrary when
`n = q = 0`; there are none in other degrees. The isomorphism is natural in `A`, and it identifies
this roadmap's `P^n_A` with the projective space of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6, whose `projectiveSpace_cohomology`
computes the same groups as `Sym^m` in degree `0` and the dual module in degree `n`. In dimension
zero both terms sit in degree `0`, so `H⁰(P⁰_A, O(m)) = A` for every `m`.

Here `A` an arbitrary commutative ring; the exponent set is the Laurent Čech basis.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §8, Lemmas 8.1–8.3, pp.16–20; tags 01XS, 01XT).

For the proof, compute the Čech complex of the standard affine cover by Laurent monomials; the
complex splits by multidegree, and the multidegree-`e` summand is the cochain complex of the
simplex on the coordinates with `e_i < 0`, which is acyclic unless that set is empty or everything.
Compare the cover of `P(O^{n+1})` with the standard cover of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6's projective space through
the quotient description of §1.1.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, `integerTwists`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`.

**Checks.**

- `ProjectiveTwistCohomologyTests.pointNegative`: `H⁰(P⁰_A, O(−7)) = A`: the basis

- `ProjectiveTwistCohomologyTests.topLine`: `H¹(P¹_A, O(−2)) = A`: the only basis vector is `(−1, −1)`.
- `ProjectiveTwistCohomologyTests.lineBoundary`: `H¹(P¹_A, O(−1)) = 0`: no vector of sum `−1` has

- `ProjectiveTwistCohomologyTests.globalSections`: `H⁰(P¹_A, O(2))` has the three basis vectors
  `(2,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(0,2)`.

Prove `relativeBundleCohomology`. If E is locally free of rank `n+1` with `n≥1` and `π:P(E)→S`, then `R⁰π*O(m)=Sym^m E` for `m≥0` and zero for `m<0`; `Rⁿπ*O(m)=Hom(Sym^(-m-n-1)E⊗det E,O_S)` for `m≤-n-1` and zero otherwise; all other `R^q` vanish. These isomorphisms commute with arbitrary base change and multiplication. For rank-one `E=L`, π is an isomorphism and `R⁰π*O(m)=L^m` for every integer m. For rank-zero E, `P(E)` is empty and every direct image is zero. In particular, at `m=−(n+1)`, the top direct image is `det(E)` dual.

Here S arbitrary; E finite locally free of the indicated fixed rank. The symmetric-power formula is not asserted for arbitrary coherent E.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §8, Lemma 8.4, pp.20–22; tag 01XX).

For the proof, trivialize E and apply the Čech basis computation. Track changes of frame in top cohomology: the volume pairing transforms by `det E`, hence its dual contains the inverse determinant; then glue the explicit isomorphisms and their multiplication maps. The local free models show arbitrary base change, beyond merely flat base change.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication`, StableReduction Layer 2, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback`.

The threshold depends on F and L; no uniform bound over all coherent F is asserted.

Here A Noetherian; X proper of finite type; L ample; F coherent. The threshold depends on F and L.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §14, Lemma 14.1, pp.34–36; §16, Lemma 16.1, pp.42–43; tags 01YS,0B5T).

For the proof, for projective space, clear denominators of affine coherent generators to obtain finitely many homogeneous global generators in high degrees; then choose a very ample power of L and a projective embedding. Apply the projective presentation to each residue class of twists modulo that power, then use Serre vanishing (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6) to obtain the graded multiplication comparison in high degrees.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, StableReduction Layer 2, JacobianChallenge Layer B, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`.

Prove `relativeSerre`. For a proper morphism `f:X→S` with S locally Noetherian, coherent F and f-ample L, locally on S sufficiently high `F⊗L^m` has surjective evaluation `f*f*(F⊗L^m)→F⊗L^m` and `R^qf*(F⊗L^m)=0` for all `q>0`. Here Proper f of finite type; locally Noetherian S; f-ample L; coherent F.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §16, Lemma 16.2, p.43; tag 02O1).

For the proof, restrict to affine opens of S and apply absolute Serre `A/B`. ### 1.3 Coherent quotients, Plücker and partial flags

Define `coherentGrassmannian`. For a quasi-coherent finite-type E on arbitrary S and `d≥0`, represent T↦locally free rank-d quotients `f*E` modulo quotient isomorphism by `Gr_d(E)`. Locally choose `O^N→E` and impose vanishing of its relation sheaf in the universal quotient of the Grassmannian of `O^N` (ModularCurves §0G). This is a closed Zariski-locally-projective S-scheme, finitely presented if E is finitely presented. It has universal quotient Q and commutes with arbitrary base change. Smoothness is not claimed for general E.

Here S arbitrary; E finite type and quasi-coherent; quotient Q finite locally free of fixed rank d.

([Jarod Alper](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/moduli-versions/moduli-8-19-24.pdf), §1.4.3, proof of Theorem 1.4.5, pp.61–62 (relation-vanishing argument)).

The API gives `coherentGrassmann.universalQuotientSheaf`: The universal finite locally free quotient Q of rank d; `coherentGrassmann.fromQuotient`: Every rank-d locally free quotient over T has a unique classifying `T→Gr_d(E)` over S; `coherentGrassmann.baseChange`: `Gr_d(f*E)≅Gr_d(E)×_S T`, with its actual quotient; `coherentGrassmann.rankOne`: `Gr_1(E)≅P(E)`, preserving `O(1)`; `coherentGrassmann.affinePoints`: For `S=Spec R` and E=tilde M, S-points are equivalent to `Module.Grassmannian R M d`.

Once the Tau Ceti pin includes the post-pin affine Grassmannian, for `S=Spec R` and `E` the sheaf of a finite `R`-module `M` the coherent Grassmannian is identified with `Module.Grassmannian.scheme R M d` over `Spec R`, compatibly with `coherentGrassmann.affinePoints` and `Module.Grassmannian.schemeHomEquiv`; local finite presentation and properness in this case then come from that carrier.

*Needs:* ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`, Mathlib `Module.Grassmannian`, Mathlib `Module.Grassmannian.functor`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.tilde`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree`.

**Checks.**

- `CoherentGrassmannTests.rankZero`: `Gr_0(E)≅S`.
- `CoherentGrassmannTests.zeroPositive`: `Gr_1(0)≅∅`.
- `CoherentGrassmannTests.rankOne`: `Gr_1(E)≅P(E)` with quotient line convention.
- `CoherentGrassmannTests.affinePoints`: Affine S-points give the finite projective quotient Grassmannian, not arbitrary submodules of kernel rank d.

Prove `grassmannSmoothness`. Let `E` be finite locally free of constant rank `n` on `S` and
`0 ≤ d ≤ n`. The Grassmannian `Gr_d(E)` of locally free rank-`d` quotients (ModularCurves §0G) is
smooth over `S` of relative dimension `d(n−d)`, its relative tangent sheaf is
`Hom(K, Q)` for the universal quotient `π^*E → Q` with kernel `K`, and its formation commutes with
arbitrary base change. The extreme ranks give `Gr_0(E) = S` and `Gr_n(E) = S`, and `Gr_d(E)` is empty
for `d > n` over a nonempty base. On the graph chart of a splitting `O^n = O^d ⊕ O^{n−d}` the
coordinates are the entries of a `d × (n−d)` matrix.

Here `E` finite locally free of constant rank; the coherent Grassmannian of a non-locally-free `E`
is not asserted to be smooth.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Lemma 5.8 and Theorem 5.9, pp.58–59, affine chart cover and smoothness over ℤ in the subspace convention; [Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §1, construction of the Grassmannian by gluing affine patches, pp.8–9, in the quotient convention. The tangent-sheaf identification and base change are proved here by the route below.)

For the proof, the graph charts are affine spaces of dimension `d(n−d)` and cover `Gr_d(E)` after
trivializing `E`; the tangent space at a quotient `q` is computed by first-order deformations of
`q` over the dual numbers, which are the maps `K → Q`.

*Needs:* ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `Module.Grassmannian`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`.

**Checks.**

- `GrassmannTests.dimension`: `Gr_2(O^4)` has relative dimension `4`.
- `GrassmannTests.projectiveLine`: `Gr_1(O^2) = P^1` with tangent sheaf `Hom(K, Q) = O(2)`.
- `GrassmannTests.empty`: `Gr_3(O^2)` is empty over a nonempty base; over the empty base every
  Grassmannian is empty.

Define `plucker`. The universal rank-d quotient of E induces an invertible quotient `∧^dE→det Q` and hence a closed immersion `Gr_d(E)→P(∧^d E)`. Its pullback of `O(1)` is `det Q` and it commutes with arbitrary base change. For finite locally free E, chart coordinates are signed maximal minors and the image is defined scheme-theoretically by Plücker relations. For finite-type E use its relation-cut presentation to restrict the finite-free embedding.

Here E quasi-coherent finite type; exterior and determinant sheaves are imported from AlgebraicVectorBundles L0C.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Theorem 5.10, p.59, closed immersion over ℤ in the subspace convention, proof sketched; [Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §1, projective embedding by the sections of `det U`, p.9, in the quotient convention. The scheme-theoretic description by the Plücker relations is proved here by the chart argument below.)

The API gives `pluckerEmbedding.isClosedImmersion`: The exterior-quotient classifying map is a closed immersion; `pluckerEmbedding.pullback_twist`: Pullback `O(1)≅det Q`, naturally in the quotient; `pluckerEmbedding.over`: The embedding is over S; the exterior and determinant maps commute with pullback; `pluckerEmbedding.chartCoordinates`: For a two-row quotient matrix of `O⁴`, compute the six Plücker coordinates as its ordered `2×2` minors. Over any commutative ring R, on the unit p12 quotient graph chart with matrix `((1,0,a,b),(0,1,c,d))`, they are (1,c,d,-a,-b,ad-bc), ordered as p12,p13,p14,p23,p24,p34. The coordinate formula uses zero-based increasing column indices; the scheme map is identified with these coordinates.

For the coordinate formula, trivialize a rank-d quotient `Rⁿ→Rᵈ` and apply its exterior power to each wedge of standard basis vectors with increasing column indices. Multilinearity and alternation give the determinant of the selected `d×d` submatrix. A change of quotient basis multiplies every coordinate by the same unit determinant, so the resulting line quotient is independent of that basis. Normalize a unit minor to the identity block to identify the exterior-quotient map with the graph chart; expand the six `2×2` determinants for the displayed matrix. These polynomial identities commute with arbitrary ring maps and hold in every characteristic. Once the pin includes them, these identities are the post-pin Tau Ceti lemmas `TauCeti.plucker_eq_repr_ιMulti` (minors as exterior-power coordinates), `TauCeti.plucker_sum_smul` (basis change) and `TauCeti.plucker_map` (ring change), and are not reproved. For the scheme-theoretic image, let `Z ⊂ P(∧^d E)` be cut out by the quadratic Plücker relations, which the image satisfies. On the open set where the coordinate `p_I` is a unit, the relations express each `p_J/p_I` as the `J`-minor of the graph matrix whose entries are the coordinates `p_{(I∖{i})∪{j}}/p_I`, by induction on `|J∖I|` using the relation that exchanges one index; so `Z` meets that open set in the graph chart `A^{d(n−d)}`, and `Z` equals the image.

*Needs:* `coherentGrassmannian`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `Matrix.det`, Mathlib `Matrix.submatrix` and `Matrix.det_fin_two`.

**Checks.**

- `PluckerTests.rankOne`: For `d=1` the Plücker map is `Gr_1(E)≅P(E)`.
- `PluckerTests.twoPlanesFourSpace`: The six minor coordinates on `Gr_2(O⁴)` satisfy `p12 p34-p13 p24+p14 p23=0`; its unit-minor charts recover `2×2` quotient graph matrices.
- `PluckerTests.rankZero`: For `d=0`, `Gr_0(E)=S` and ∧⁰E=O, so the map is an isomorphism.

Define `flagBundle`. For finite locally free E of rank n and a strictly increasing list `0≤a₁`<…<`a_s≤n`, represent flags of subbundles `F_i⊂E_T` of ranks `a_i`, with every quotient `E_T/F_i` locally free. It is the closed incidence subscheme of the product over S of `Gr_(n-a_i)(E)`, defined by `F_i→E_T/F_j=0` for `i<j`. It is smooth and Zariski-locally projective, of relative dimension `Σ_i(a_i-a_(i-1))(n-a_i)`, where `a₀=0`; full flags have dimension `n(n-1)/2`. The complete flag bundle is the type `(1, 2, …, n−1)`; partial and complete flags are both built here.

Here E finite locally free of rank n; strictly increasing admissible ranks; empty list is allowed.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Propositions 5.16–5.17, pp.61–62).

The API gives `flagBundle.projection`: The structure map of the flag scheme; `flagBundle.toGrassmann`: The ith flag step gives the quotient of rank `n-a_i`; the universal kernels are nested; `flagBundle.baseChange`: Flags and universal steps commute with arbitrary base change; `flagBundle.affinePoints`: For the free rank-n sheaf over `Spec R` and a strictly increasing admissible list a, points over the identity correspond to tuples of quotient-rank `n−aᵢ Grassmannian` data with nested kernels.

*Needs:* `coherentGrassmannian`, `grassmannSmoothness`, ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`.

**Checks.**

- `FlagTests.empty`: Flag(E;`[]`)≅S.
- `FlagTests.single`: Flag(E;`[a]`)≅`Gr_(n-a)(E)`.
- `FlagTests.nested`: For the free rank-three sheaf over a field, nonnested kernels of quotient ranks two and one are not the two components of any point of flagBundle with type `[1,2]`.

### 1.4 Relative very ampleness

Define `relativeVeryAmple`. An invertible L on X is very ample relative to `f:X→S` when there are a quasi-coherent E on S and an immersion `i:X→P_S(E)` over S with `L≅i*O(1)`. The immersion convention includes nonproper X. For quasi-compact f, the evaluation criterion requires f quasi-separated (so `f_*L` is quasi-coherent), surjective evaluation `f* f_*L→L`, and immersion of the complete classifying map into `P(f_*L)`. For quasi-compact f this property is local on S. It is stable under arbitrary base change without that hypothesis. If f is proper, a representing immersion is closed. Over `S = Spec k` it is very ampleness in the usual sense, and for quasi-compact `f` it implies relative ampleness in the sense of StableReduction Layer 2.

Here S and X arbitrary for the definition; quasi-compactness of f for locality on S and very ample⇒ample; quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness for the complete evaluation criterion.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/morphisms.pdf), §39, Definition 39.1, Lemmas 39.7–39.8, pp.86–89; tags 01VM,01VR,0B3F).

The API gives `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.of_embedding`: A specified immersion over S and pullback isomorphism witness relative very ampleness; `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.evaluation_criterion`: For quasi-compact quasi-separated f with quasi-coherent `f_*L` and epimorphic evaluation, relative very ampleness is equivalent to the canonical completeMap being an immersion; `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.closed_of_proper`: A witnessing immersion is closed when f is proper; `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.evaluation_epi`: For quasi-compact quasi-separated f, relative very ampleness makes the actual adjunction counit `f*f_*L→L` an epimorphism; `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.evaluationQuotient`: Given epimorphic evaluation, form the invertible quotient using the adjunction counit and L; `ProjectiveBundles.IsRelativelyVeryAmple.completeMap`: Classify the actual evaluation quotient, with the quasi-coherent pushforward supplied under quasi-compact/quasi-separated hypotheses.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, `integerTwists`, StableReduction Layer 2, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforward`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`.

**Checks.**

- `VeryAmpleTests.projectiveSpace`: `O(1)` on every `Pⁿ_S` is relatively very ample.
- `VeryAmpleTests.veronese`: `O(2)` on `P¹_k` is relatively very ample; the positive-power case differs from the globally generated trivial line.
- `VeryAmpleTests.trivialNotVeryAmple`: O on `P¹_k` is globally generated but not very ample.

Prove `amplePowersAndFixedTwists`. For finite-type `f:X→S` with quasi-compact S and f-ample A, all sufficiently high powers `A^m` are relatively very ample. If f is proper, their classifying embeddings are closed. If `X→S` is proper over a Noetherian S and B is any fixed invertible sheaf, `B⊗A^m` is relatively very ample for all sufficiently large m. For finitely many B, one bound works simultaneously; over affine S the embeddings may be into some finite `Pⁿ_S`.

Here Quasi-compact base for a global bound; finite type f. Coherence and properness for the fixed-twist application.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/morphisms.pdf), §40, Lemmas 40.4–40.5, pp.91–92; tags 01VT,01VU; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/morphisms.pdf), §40, Lemma 40.3 and proof, pp.90–91; Lemmas 40.4–40.5, pp.91–92; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/constructions.pdf), §13, Lemma 13.6, p.29).

For the proof, apply the local affine ampleness criterion and choose a maximum over a finite base cover; glue complete evaluation maps using the relative very-ampleness criterion; then relative Serre A makes `B⊗A^b` globally generated for large b. Tensoring a globally generated line with a fixed very ample power `A^c` is very ample by the Segre construction. Thus every `m≥b+c` gives the fixed-twist result.

*Needs:* `relativeVeryAmple`, `relativeSerre`, StableReduction Layer 2.

### 1.5 Hilbert polynomials and regularity

Prove `gradedPiecesFinite`. Let A be a Noetherian ring, B a finitely generated standard nonnegative graded A-algebra with `B₀=A`, and M a finitely generated graded B-module. Every `M_d` is finite over A and `M_d=0` for d sufficiently negative. For `B=A[x₀,…,x_n]`, its degree-d part is finite free of rank binomial(`n+d`,n) for `d≥0`, and is zero for `d<0`. These basis descriptions commute with arbitrary A-algebra extension.

Here Degree-one generators, finite generation of M, and nonnegative grading of B; M itself may have negative generator degrees.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/algebra.pdf), §58, Lemmas 58.5–58.6, pp.136–137; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/coherent.pdf), §8, Lemma 8.1, pp.16–17).

For the proof, choose finitely many homogeneous generators of B and M. Degree-d monomials times those generators form a finite spanning set. For the polynomial algebra, support-total-degree gives a genuine basis, counted by compositions of d; then use the homogeneous polynomial submodule; do not create a replacement polynomial carrier.

*Needs:* Mathlib `MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule`, Mathlib `SymmetricAlgebra`.

Prove `hilbertSerre`. For an Artinian ring A, a standard graded finite-type A-algebra B generated by e degree-one elements, and a finitely generated graded B-module M, each graded piece has finite A-length. The Laurent series `Σ_d length_A(M_d)T^d` equals `h(T)/(1-T)^e` for a Laurent polynomial h with integer coefficients. Consequently `d↦length_A(M_d)` agrees for d≫0 with a rational polynomial taking integer values at integers. Shift to a nonnegative grading, form the integer-length numerator and apply the `Polynomial.hilbertPoly` over ℚ; its characteristic-zero hypothesis is on ℚ rather than A; exact sequences add the polynomials.

Here Artinian A, finite graded M, standard degree-one grading; arbitrary positive weights require a different denominator and generally give a quasi-polynomial.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/algebra.pdf), §58, Proposition 58.7 and proof, pp.136–137, for the eventual polynomial; Atiyah–Macdonald, Introduction to Commutative Algebra, Chapter 11, Theorem 11.1, p.117, for the rational form of the series of a nonnegatively graded module, extended to negative degrees by the Laurent shift below).

For the proof, induct on the e generators using the exact sequence for multiplication by the last generator, including its kernel and cokernel. They are finite graded modules over `e−1` generators; A-length additivity yields `(1-T)H_M=H_coker−T H_kernel`; then after a finite shift, use the coefficient formula for `h/(1-T)^e` to obtain the eventual polynomial. Negative degrees contribute only a Laurent shift; finite lengths are proved before converting them to natural numbers. `Suggested.lean` states this as `ProjectiveParameterSpaces.hilbertSerre`, including finite lengths, vanishing in sufficiently negative degrees, the shifted integer Hilbert-series numerator and the eventual rational polynomial of degree less than e. Its integer grading allows negative generator degrees. Restricting scalars along the polynomial algebra on the e chosen generators covers the standard graded algebra B. Over a field, lengths are dimensions, giving the dimension-polynomial statement.

*Needs:* `gradedPiecesFinite`, Mathlib `Module.length`, Mathlib `Module.length_eq_add_of_exact`, Mathlib `Polynomial.hilbertPoly`, Mathlib `Polynomial.coeff_mul_invOneSubPow_eq_hilbertPoly_eval`.

Over a field, `ProjectiveParameterSpaces.hilbertSerre` gives the shared dimension-polynomial
interface of GroebnerGeometry `G4's` graded-module construction.
For a finite graded module over a standard polynomial ring over any field k, the coefficients
of its Hilbert series are the rational images of `Module.finrank k (ℳ n)`. After a graded
shift makes the series nonnegative, a presentation `p(T)/(1−T)^e` gives the eventual polynomial
`Polynomial.hilbertPoly p e` over ℚ. Mathlib's
`Polynomial.eq_hilbertPoly_of_forall_coeff_eq_eval` identifies any eventual dimension polynomial
with this one, independently of the chosen numerator and denominator presentation. If
`H_{M'}(T)=T^a H_M(T)`, the polynomials satisfy `P_M(t)=P_{M'}(t+a)`.
GroebnerGeometry `G2's` semigroup counts use this same
polynomial. The Artinian-length extension `hilbertSerre`, the sheaf-Euler comparison
`hilbertPolynomial`, and `familyHilbertPolynomials` are targets here. GroebnerGeometry's
polynomial minor and flag straightening supplies algebraic presentations; §1.3 constructs the
quotient-functor Grassmannians, flags and their Plücker geometry.

*Needs:* GroebnerGeometry G2 and G4; Mathlib `Polynomial.eq_hilbertPoly_of_forall_coeff_eq_eval`.

Define `hilbertPolynomial`. For a projective k-scheme X, an ample invertible L, and a coherent sheaf F, define `P_(F,L)∈Q[t]` by `P(m)=χ(X,F⊗L^m)` for every integer m, where χ is the finite alternating sum of cohomology dimensions. This agrees with the eventual section-dimension polynomial. Short exact sequences add P, tensoring F by `L^a` replaces `P(t)` by `P(t+a)`, and extension of k preserves P. If L is very ample, dim support F is the degree of P for nonzero F, and r! times its leading coefficient is its positive degree.

Here k a field; projective X and coherent F; ample L. For degree relative to an embedding take very ample L. The zero sheaf has zero polynomial and is treated separately.

([Alexander Grothendieck](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1960-1961__6__249_0.pdf), §2, exposé p.5 (collected p.253), before Theorem 2.1; [Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §2, pp.9–10, definitions preceding Lemma 2.1; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/algebra.pdf), §58, Proposition 58.7, p.137; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/varieties.pdf), §45, Lemmas 45.1–45.2 and Definition 45.10, pp.101–104; tags 0BEM,0BEN,0BEW).

The API gives `hilbertPolynomial.eval_euler`: For every integer m and any valid cohomological cutoff, evaluation at m equals the finite alternating Euler sum; `hilbertPolynomial.add`: A short exact sequence of coherent sheaves adds Hilbert polynomials; `hilbertPolynomial.twist`: Twisting by `L^a` translates the variable by a.

*Needs:* `hilbertSerre`, `serreGeneration`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, Tau Ceti `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.eulerCharBelow`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`, JacobianChallenge Layer B, `amplePowersAndFixedTwists`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 5, SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.3.

- `HilbertPolynomialTests.zero`: The zero sheaf has polynomial 0.
- `HilbertPolynomialTests.projectiveLine`: `O_P¹(a)` has polynomial `t+a+1`, not just its large-t values.
- `HilbertPolynomialTests.projectivePoint`: The structure sheaf of `Spec k` has polynomial 1.

Prove `familyHilbertPolynomials`. For projective `X→S` with S Noetherian, a relatively very ample L and coherent F, the geometric-fibre Hilbert polynomials form a finite set. If F is S-flat, the polynomial is locally constant on S. Without flatness, there is a finite stratification by reduced locally closed pieces on which the restriction is flat and the polynomial constant; this assertion is not universal flattening-stratum representability.

Here Noetherian includes quasi-compactness here. Coherent F; flatness only for local constancy on all of S.

([Alexander Grothendieck](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1960-1961__6__249_0.pdf), §2, exposé p.5 (collected p.253), before Theorem 2.1; [Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §4, Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2, pp.18–19).

For the proof, for flat F, coherent cohomology and base change or a finite complex computing cohomology make `χ(F_s(m))` locally constant for each m; finitely many evaluations determine its polynomial; then for general F, take finitely many generic flat opens of the irreducible components using generic flatness (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12), make their union into disjoint locally closed strata, and repeat on the closed complement by Noetherian induction. This yields finitely many flat finite-type families and hence finitely many polynomials.

*Needs:* `hilbertPolynomial`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, JacobianChallenge Layer C, StableReduction Layer 2.

Define `cmRegularity`. A coherent F on `Pⁿ_k` is m-regular, for an integer m, if `Hⁱ(Pⁿ,F(m−i))=0` for every `i>0`. Then F is r-regular for every `r≥m`; `Hⁱ(F(r))=0` for `r≥m−i` and `i>0`; `F(r)` is globally generated for `r≥m`; and `H⁰(F(r))⊗H⁰(O(1))→H⁰(F(r+1))` is surjective for every `r≥m`.

Here k any field; coherent sheaf on projective space; all positive cohomological degrees, with above-dimension vanishing.

([Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §2, unnumbered regularity definition preceding Lemma 2.1, p.9; Lemma 2.1 and proof, pp.10–11).

The API gives `ProjectiveBundles.IsCMRegular.monotone`: m-regular implies r-regular whenever `m≤r`; `IsCMRegular.vanish`: For `i>0` and `r≥m−i`, `Hⁱ(F(r))` vanishes; `IsCMRegular.multiplication`: For `r≥m`, multiplication of degree-r sections by linear forms is surjective.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, `serreGeneration`, `ProjectiveBundles.twistMultiplication`, JacobianChallenge Layer B.

**Checks.**

- `RegularityTests.structureSheaf`: `O_P`ⁿ is 0-regular.
- `RegularityTests.lineBundle`: On `P¹`, `O(a)` is m-regular iff `a+m≥0`; `O(-2)` is not 1-regular.
- `RegularityTests.zero`: The zero sheaf is m-regular for every integer m.
- `RegularityTests.pointSpace`: on `P⁰_k` every coherent sheaf is m-regular for every m, since there is no higher cohomology.

Prove `uniformQuotientRegularity` as the regularity specialization of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14's `hilbert_quot_schemes`. Fix a field k, a coherent E on `Pⁿ_k` and a numerical polynomial P. There is an integer `m₀` such that every quotient `E_K→F` on `Pⁿ_K` with Hilbert polynomial P, over every extension field `K/k`, has both F and its kernel `m₀`-regular in the sense of `ProjectiveBundles.IsCMRegular`. The same statement holds for a finite set of polynomials with a common maximum. There is no analogous uniform bound for arbitrary coherent sheaves with fixed P and no fixed quotient ambient E.

Here Fixed E and P; coherent quotient and kernel; no characteristic-zero hypothesis.

([Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §2, Theorem 2.3 and proof, pp.11–13, whose proof gives vanishing of `H¹(F(m))` once `m ≥ m₀ + h¹(F(m₀))`, and hence `(m₀ + h¹(F(m₀)) + 1)`-regularity; §3, Theorem 3.7, pp.16–17, and §5, Theorem 5.1, p.24, for cohomological base change and projective Quot; [Jarod Alper](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/moduli-versions/moduli-8-19-24.pdf), §1.3, Theorem 1.3.8 proof, pp.57–58, for the kernel estimate: if `J⊂O^p`, `t≥0` and `Hⁱ(J(t))=0` for `i≥2`, then `h¹(J(t)) = h⁰(J(t)) − P_J(t) ≤ p·binom(n+t,n) − P_J(t)`).

Use the projective k-scheme `Q = Quot^P_E` and its universal quotient `E_Q→U` supplied by `hilbert_quot_schemes`; Q is Noetherian and quasi-compact. Both U and its coherent kernel J are Q-flat, since `E_Q` is Q-flat and U is Q-flat. Apply `relativeSerre` and coherent cohomology and base change to U and J over Q. If all their fibre twists `r≥b` have vanishing positive cohomology, `m₀=b+n` makes `Hⁱ(F(m₀−i))` and `Hⁱ(ker(E_K→F)(m₀−i))` vanish for `1≤i≤n`; higher degrees vanish by dimension. This is the defining condition of `ProjectiveBundles.IsCMRegular`. Every extension-field quotient is a K-point of the same Q, so the bound is independent of K. An empty Q imposes no condition; take a maximum for finitely many P. These consequences and the comparison with our regularity predicate are proved here using the supplier's representing scheme and universal family.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 (`hilbert_quot_schemes`, projective Quot and universal quotient), `cmRegularity`, `hilbertPolynomial`, `relativeSerre`, JacobianChallenge Layer C, StableReduction Layer 2.

For `m≥m₀`, higher direct images vanish, `π_*F(m)` is finite locally free and commutes with arbitrary base change, evaluation is surjective, and multiplication `π_*F(m)⊗π_*O(1)→π_*F(m+1)` is surjective. Here Noetherian base for a global finite bound; flat F for locally free pushforward and arbitrary cohomological base change.

([Nitin Nitsure](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504590), §2, Theorem 2.3 and proof, pp.11–13, whose proof gives vanishing of `H¹(F(m))` once `m ≥ m₀ + h¹(F(m₀))`, and hence `(m₀ + h¹(F(m₀)) + 1)`-regularity; [Jarod Alper](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/moduli-versions/moduli-8-19-24.pdf), §1.3, Theorem 1.3.8 proof, pp.57–58, for the kernel h¹ estimate; [Alexander Grothendieck](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1960-1961__6__249_0.pdf), §2, Theorem 2.1 corrected by the 1962 erratum, exposé p.6 and erratum p.302).
