### 1.5a Hilbert functions

The Hilbert function of a graded module with finite pieces is `n ↦ Module.finrank k (ℳ n)` over a
field and `n ↦ Module.length A (ℳ n)` over an Artinian ring; both are Mathlib's, and no separate
carrier is introduced. The theorem `ProjectiveParameterSpaces.hilbertSerre` requires a finitely
generated integer-graded module over the standard graded polynomial ring, its direct-sum
decomposition and compatibility with homogeneous scalar multiplication. Over Artinian `A` the
coefficients are lengths over `A`, mapped to rational numbers; no
characteristic hypothesis is placed on `A`. (Stacks, Algebra, §58, Lemmas 58.5–58.6 and
Proposition 58.7, pp. 136–137.)

**Checks.**

- `HilbertFunctionChecks.zero`: the zero graded module has Hilbert function `0` and polynomial `0`.
- `HilbertFunctionChecks.constant`: `k[x]` has Hilbert function `1` in every nonnegative degree and `0` in every negative degree.
- `HilbertFunctionChecks.degreeTwo`: the degree-two piece of `k[x, y]` has dimension `3`.
- `HilbertFunctionChecks.cancelledDenominator`: the presentations `1/(1−T)` and
  `(1−T)/(1−T)²` for the Hilbert series of `k[x]` give the same rational polynomial, also
  when k has positive characteristic.
- `HilbertLengthChecks.dualNumbers`: over `k[ε]/ε²` the coefficient ring has length `2`.
- `HilbertLengthChecks.dualNumbersResidueField`: the residue field has length `1` as a module over
  the dual numbers acting through the augmentation.
- `HilbertLengthChecks.field`: `k` has length `1` as a `k`-module.
- `HilbertLengthChecks.zero`: the zero module has length `0` even over the zero ring.

### 1.6 Chow parameters and numerical boundedness

Define `chowParameters`. For an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, integers `0≤r≤n` and `D≥1`, construct the projective Chow coefficient scheme `Ch_(r,D)(Pⁿ_k)`, using the reduced closed locus of multihomogeneous associated forms of degree D in each of `r+1` hyperplane blocks. Its k-points are in bijection with effective pure r-cycles of degree D, with multiplicities; their Chow forms are unique up to scalar. Degree 0 is a single zero-cycle parameter. There is a closed universal support in Ch×`Pⁿ` whose geometric fibre has exactly the support of the corresponding cycle, as a set. Cycles supported in a fixed closed `Y⊂Pⁿ` give a closed coefficient locus. This construction does not assert a flat family of subschemes or representation of the cycle functor over arbitrary nonreduced bases.

Here Algebraically closed characteristic-zero field for this Chow construction; the boundedness theorem below does not use it and rests on the characteristic-free `boundedSupportParameters`. A pure cycle is a finite sum `Σ a_i[Z_i]` with `a_i>0`, `dim Z_i=r`; degree is `Σa_i deg Z_i`. AlgebraicCycle with natural coefficients stores the multiplicities at generic points.

([Wei-Liang Chow, B. L. van der Waerden](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN235181684_0113?tify={%22pages%22:[696]}), §1, Satz 1, pp.695–697; Satz 2, p.698; Satz 3, p.699; §2, p.700; [James Freitag, Wei Li, Thomas Scanlon](https://math.berkeley.edu/~scanlon/papers/differential-chow-varieties-22apr15.pdf), §3, Definition 3.1, pp.13–14; [Jarod Alper](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/moduli-versions/moduli-8-19-24.pdf), §1.4.5, p.64).

The API gives `chowParameters.cycle`: A geometric parameter determines its effective pure cycle, including multiplicities; `chowParameters.fromCycle`: The associated form gives the parameter of every effective pure cycle with the specified degree; `chowParameters.cycle_fromCycle`: Recover the cycle from its associated-form parameter; parameter equality is equivalent to cycle equality; `chowParameters.support`: A closed support subscheme of Ch×`Pⁿ`, with the stated geometric support equality.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, `gradedPiecesFinite`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle`, StableReduction Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `ChowTests.zeroDegree`: Degree 0 is a single parameter with cycle 0 and empty support.
- `ChowTests.hyperplanes`: `Ch_(n−1,1)(Pⁿ)` is the dual `Pⁿ`; for `n=1` these are points of `P¹`.
- `ChowTests.multiplicity`: Doubling a degree-one hyperplane gives multiplicity 2 and degree 2, even though its support equals that of the original hyperplane.

Prove `boundedSupportParameters`. Fix integers `0≤r≤n` and `D≥1`. Let `C_(r,D)` be the finite disjoint union, over multidegrees `a=(a_0,…,a_r)` with `0≤a_i≤D`, of the projective spaces over `Spec ℤ` of nonzero forms that are homogeneous of degree `a_i` in the i-th of `r+1` blocks of dual coordinates of `Pⁿ`. Let `W_(r,D)⊂C_(r,D)×_ℤ Pⁿ_ℤ` be the closed subscheme of pairs `(F,x)` such that F vanishes at every `(r+1)`-tuple of hyperplanes through x. Then `C_(r,D)` is projective over ℤ, and for every algebraically closed field K and every reduced closed subscheme `Y⊂Pⁿ_K`, equidimensional of dimension r and of degree at most D, there is `c∈C_(r,D)(K)` with `(W_c)_red=Y`. Base change along any `S→Spec ℤ` gives the same statement at the geometric points of S. The parameter c is not unique, W is not flat over `C_(r,D)`, and no cycle functor is represented.

Here Arbitrary characteristic, including mixed characteristic over `Spec ℤ`; K algebraically closed; Y reduced and pure of dimension r; the degree of Y is r! times the leading coefficient of its Hilbert polynomial, the convention of Grothendieck's Lemma 2.4.

([Alexander Grothendieck](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1960-1961__6__249_0.pdf), §2, Lemma 2.4 and the sentence introducing it, exposé p.7 (collected p.255), which states the boundedness over any Noetherian base and attributes it to the content of Chow coordinates; [Wei-Liang Chow, B. L. van der Waerden](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN235181684_0113?tify={%22pages%22:[696]}), §1, Satz 1, pp.695–697, for the associated form; Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Chapter I, Theorem 7.7, for the degree count of linear sections over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic).

For `n=0`, a nonempty reduced pure zero-dimensional `Y⊂P⁰_K` is `P⁰_K` itself. There are no hyperplanes through its point, so every allowed nonzero parameter form gives `W_c=P⁰_K` by the vacuous vanishing condition. For `n≥1`, first let Y be integral of degree d. The incidence `{(y,H_0,…,H_r): y∈Y∩H_0∩…∩H_r}` is a projective bundle over Y of dimension `r+(r+1)(n−1)`, and a general `(H_1,…,H_r)` cuts Y in finitely many points, so its image in `(Pⁿ∨)^(r+1)` is an irreducible hypersurface; let `F_Y` be a reduced equation. On a general line in the i-th block, with the other hyperplanes general, the zeros of `F_Y` are simple and correspond to the points of the general linear section of Y by the other r hyperplanes, so the i-th degree of `F_Y` is at most d by the Bézout count. If `x∈Y`, `F_Y` vanishes on all hyperplanes through x. If `x∉Y`, projection from x carries Y onto an r-dimensional closed subset of `P^(n−1)`, so a general linear space of codimension `r+1` through x misses Y and some tuple of hyperplanes through x has `F_Y≠0`. For reduced Y with components `Y_j` take `F=∏F_(Y_j)`, of multidegree at most Σdeg `Y_j≤D`, so `W_F=Y` as sets. Closedness of W: the tuples of hyperplanes through x form a projective subbundle of `Pⁿ×(Pⁿ∨)^(r+1)` over `Pⁿ`, and W is the zero locus of the direct image of the restricted universal form. No separability hypothesis enters, and no field of definition of F is asserted for Y.

*Needs:* `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle`, `ProjectiveBundles.projectiveBundle.projectiveSpaceCechComparison`, `gradedPiecesFinite`, `hilbertPolynomial`, StableReduction Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `BoundedSupportChecks.point`: `n=r=0` and `Y=P⁰_K` give `W_c=P⁰_K`, although the incidence scheme is empty; every allowed nonzero parameter form has this fibre.
- `BoundedSupportChecks.linear`: for a linear subspace Y of dimension r, the determinant pairing `r+1` hyperplanes with a basis of the cone over Y has multidegree `(1,…,1)` and `W_c=Y`, already reduced.
- `BoundedSupportChecks.degreeBound`: for a smooth conic `Y⊂P²` and `D=1` no parameter exists: a form vanishing at every pair of lines meeting on Y is divisible by the multidegree-(2,2) equation of that incidence hypersurface. The bound D is a hypothesis, not a convenience.
- `BoundedSupportChecks.inseparable`: for `n=1`, `r=0` and the binary form `X^p−tY^p` over `𝔽_p(t)`, `W_c` is a reduced point of degree p over `𝔽_p(t)` whose geometric fibre is one point of multiplicity p; its reduced geometric fibre has Hilbert polynomial 1. Reductions are taken after passage to an algebraic closure, not over the parameter field.

Prove `boundedDegreeHilbertPolynomials`. For a fixed projective complex scheme X with a fixed very ample embedding in `Pⁿ` and integers r,D, finitely many finite-type projective families contain all the reduced supports, and hence only finitely many Hilbert polynomials occur among reduced pure r-dimensional closed subschemes `Y⊂X` of degree at most D. More generally, as in Grothendieck's Lemma 2.4, the same finiteness holds in every characteristic for reduced equidimensional closed subschemes of the geometric fibres of a fixed projective family over a Noetherian base with a fixed relatively very ample embedding. Reducedness and purity are part of the assertion; the support construction does not record embedded structure.

Here Reduced pure dimension r; fixed embedding; geometric fibres in the family formulation; Noetherian projective ambient family.

([Alexander Grothendieck](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1960-1961__6__249_0.pdf), §2, Lemma 2.4, exposé p.7 (collected p.255); [Ziyang Gao, Tangli Ge, Lars Kühne](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/pmihes.26.pdf), §3.1, p.198; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/more-morphisms.pdf), §24, Lemmas 24.4,24.6, pp.68–70 and §26, Lemma 26.4, pp.75–76).

For the proof, a subscheme of a geometric fibre of the family is a subscheme of the corresponding `Pⁿ`, so by `boundedSupportParameters` every Y in question is the reduced geometric fibre `(W_c)_red` of `W_(r,D)` at a geometric point of the scheme `C_(r,D)×_ℤ S`, which is of finite type over the Noetherian S. It is therefore enough to show that the reduced geometric fibres of a closed subscheme of `Pⁿ` over a Noetherian parameter scheme lie in finitely many flat finite-type families; this needs no flat universal cycle functor. On an irreducible parameter component with generic field K, take the radical of the fibre after extension to an algebraic closure of K. Its finitely many generators and the finitely many equations expressing equality with the support are defined over one finite extension `K′/K`. In characteristic p this extension can have a purely inseparable part; it must not be suppressed. Over `K′` the resulting finite-presentation support is geometrically reduced. Spread it over a finite dominant cover of an open of the component, use generic flatness and shrink until its fibres are geometrically reduced. The defining equations of W and properness ensure that these fibres have the prescribed geometric supports; then every geometric point of that open lifts to the finite dominant parameter cover after passing to its algebraically closed residue field. The flat geometrically reduced fibre there is exactly the reduced subscheme with that support. Repeat on the proper closed complement. Noetherian induction produces finitely many finite-type flat families, including the positive-characteristic case. Their finitely many Hilbert polynomials give the bound. Embedded nilpotents would not be detected by this support construction and are explicitly excluded.

*Needs:* `boundedSupportParameters`, `familyHilbertPolynomials`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, `hilbertPolynomial`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4.

Prove `chowOpenAndEmbedding`. Let Y be a complex variety open and dense in its fixed projective closure Ybar. In the finite union Ch(Ybar,r,≤D), the cycles whose support meets Y form an open locus. This means at least one component meets Y; it differs from requiring every component to avoid the boundary. For two fixed projective embeddings of Ybar, a degree bound in one induces a degree bound in the other, separately for each r. Thus the collection of bounded-degree cycles is independent of the embedding up to change of the numerical bound.

Here Y locally closed; first replace Ybar by its closure so Y is open there. Fixed finite-type projective closure and fixed dimensions.

([Laura DeMarco, Niki Myrto Mavraki, Hexi Ye](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.17343v3), §2.5, p.10; [James Freitag, Wei Li, Thomas Scanlon](https://math.berkeley.edu/~scanlon/papers/differential-chow-varieties-22apr15.pdf), §3, Proposition 3.4, p.14; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/varieties.pdf), §45, Definition 45.3 and Lemmas 45.4–45.9 and Definition 45.10, pp.103–104).

For the proof, the complementary locus is the closed Chow locus of cycles supported in Ybar minus Y, obtained by the support-in-closed construction. Use its complement for the support-meets-open condition; then for very ample `L₁`,`L₂`, choose m so `A=L₁^m` tensor `L₂` inverse is very ample. The mixed intersection numbers of SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.3 are positive for ample factors, and multilinearity expands `(m c₁(L₁))^r=(c₁(L₂)+c₁(A))^r`. Every term is nonnegative, so `deg_L₂ Z≤m^r deg_L₁ Z` for each integral r-component. Add component multiplicities and reverse the roles for the other bound. No informal comparison of chosen hyperplanes is needed.

*Needs:* `chowParameters`, `amplePowersAndFixedTwists`, `hilbertPolynomial`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 5, SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.3.

Define `bigLineBundle`. An invertible sheaf `L` on a projective geometrically integral variety
`V` of dimension `d` over a field is big when there is `c > 0` with `h⁰(V, L^m) ≥ c·m^d` for all
sufficiently divisible `m > 0`; equivalently, some power `L^a` has a rational map birational onto its
image. For a projective morphism, bigness is a fibrewise condition. Ample sheaves are big; on a curve
a sheaf is big exactly when its degree is positive.

Here `V` projective and geometrically integral; the growth is along sufficiently divisible `m`.

([Esnault–Viehweg](https://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/esnault/books/esvibuch.pdf), Definition 5.3 and Properties 5.4, pp. 44–45).

The API gives `bigLineBundle.of_ample`: ample implies big; `bigLineBundle.pow_iff`: `L` is big iff
`L^a` is big for one, equivalently every, `a > 0`; `bigLineBundle.birational_iff`: the
section-growth and birational-system characterizations agree.

*Needs:* `hilbertPolynomial`, `amplePowersAndFixedTwists`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`.

**Checks.**

- `BigTests.curve`: on `P¹`, `O(1)` is big and `O` is not.
- `BigTests.notAmple`: on the blowup of `P²` at a point, the pullback of `O(1)` is big but not ample.
- `BigTests.product`: on `P¹ × P¹`, `O(1, 0)` is not big although it is globally generated.

Prove `bigFamilyBirationalBounds`. Let `f:X→S` be a flat projective family of geometrically integral complex varieties over a finite-type complex base and L an invertible sheaf whose restriction to each fibre is big. There are a,N,d such that for every fibre the complete linear system |`L_s^a`| gives a rational map birational onto its image, `h⁰(X_s,L_s^a)≤N`, and the image has degree at most d. Base points are allowed. These constants depend on the family, and this theorem does not assert that `L_s^a` is ample or that the map is a closed immersion. Bigness is `bigLineBundle`.

Here Fixed finite-type complex family; geometrically integral fibres and fibrewise bigness; no arbitrary numerical boundedness inference for big L.

([François Charles](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v184-n2-p04-p.pdf), §3, Lemma 3.6 and proof, p. 508; [Esnault–Viehweg](https://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/esnault/books/esvibuch.pdf), Definition 5.3 and Properties 5.4(d) with proof, pp. 44–45).

For the proof, first prove the section-growth-to-birational-system bridge on a geometrically integral projective fibre. Fix a very ample A. The restriction to an ample hyperplane has `h⁰(L^m|H)=O(m^(d−1))`: embed `L|H` into a fixed positive power of an ample line and use its Hilbert polynomial. The order-`m^d` growth of the big line then gives a nonzero section of `L^a⊗A`⁻¹ for some a. Multiplication by that section puts the very ample system of A inside |`L^a`|, so this rational map is birational. The same construction with its kth power proves birationality of |`L^(ka)`| for every `k>0`; then for a fixed a, stratify the finite-type base so `f_*L^a` is finite locally free and commutes with residue-field extension. The finite section coordinates define the relative rational map and its graph. Generic finiteness and degree one onto the image are constructible conditions, obtained by spreading the generic rational inverse and shrinking, followed by induction on the complement. Thus the locus where |`L_s^a`| is birational is constructible; then on an irreducible component all closed points lie in the countable union of these constructible loci, because every fibre is big. An irreducible finite-type variety over the uncountable field C cannot have its closed points covered by countably many proper closed subvarieties: a finite dominant map to an affine space and induction on its dimension prove this using lines with independently chosen coordinates. Consequently one locus is dense and contains an open. Use Noetherian induction on the closed complement, and choose a common multiple of the finitely many exponents. Every positive multiple of a birational complete system remains birational, so this exponent works on all strata; then upper semicontinuity bounds `h⁰` for the selected exponent over the quasi-compact base. Spread each graph and image, shrink to flat projective image families, and use their finitely many Hilbert polynomials to bound degree; induction covers the complements. Base points are retained throughout.

*Needs:* `familyHilbertPolynomials`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, JacobianChallenge Layer C, StableReduction Layer 2, `hilbertPolynomial`, `bigLineBundle`.

### 1.7 Determinantal and Frobenius loci

Define `rankLocus`. For a map `φ:E→F` of finite locally free sheaves, the rank≤r closed subscheme is defined locally by all `(r+1)`-minors, equivalently by the vanishing of `∧^(r+1)φ`. These ideals are independent of bases and glue, and their formation commutes with arbitrary base change. A T→S factors through the locus iff every pulled-back minor is zero in `O_T`, not merely zero at its geometric points. For a rank-a to rank-b map and r≥min(a,b), the locus is all of S.

Here Finite locally free domain and codomain; integer `r≥0`. The ideal convention includes zero-size and impossible-minor cases.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, graph charts and Plücker coordinates, pp.58–60).

The API gives `rankLocus.minor_mem`: Every selected `(r+1)`-minor lies in the defining ideal; `rankLocus.factor_iff`: A ring map kills the ideal iff it kills every selected minor; `rankLocus.baseChange`: The ideal of the base-changed matrix is the extended ideal.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Matrix.det`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`, ModularCurves §0G.

**Checks.**

- `RankLocusTests.oneByOne`: For `[t]` and `r=0` the ideal is `(t)`.
- `RankLocusTests.fullRankBound`: For r=min(a,b) there are no minors and the ideal is 0.
- `RankLocusTests.nilpotent`: For nonzero square-zero ε, the ideal `(ε)` is nonzero although every geometric rank test gives zero.

Define `incidenceLocus`. Let E have finite locally free rank n on S and `0≤a`,`b≤n`. In `Gr_(n−a)(E)×_S Gr_(n−b)(E)`, the locus `dim(U∩W)≥k` on geometric fibres has its canonical closed scheme structure: for `k≤a` it is rank(`U→E/W`)≤`a−k`, the vanishing of the `(a−k+1)`-minors, and for `k>a` it is the empty closed subscheme (unit ideal), the bound `a−k` being negative and never read as a truncated natural number. For `k=0` it is the full relative product; for k>min(a,b) it is empty (when `b<k≤a` because `U∩W⊂W` forces rank at least `a−b≥a−k+1` at every point, so the minor ideal is the unit ideal). The construction commutes with arbitrary base change. Over nonfields the rank-equation scheme, rather than the rank of a possibly nonflat intersection module, is the definition.

Here Admissible subbundle ranks a,b; locally free quotients; `k≥0`, with the empty closed subscheme for `k>a`.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Proposition 5.16, pp.61–62; graph coordinates pp.58–59).

The API gives `incidenceLocus.inclusion`: The inclusion into the relative product of the two Grassmann schemes; `incidenceLocus.isClosedImmersion`: The incidence inclusion retains the defining determinantal ideals; `incidenceLocus.baseChange`: The incidence scheme for `f*E` is isomorphic to the actual pullback of the incidence scheme over S, preserving its closed inclusion; `incidenceLocus.projection`: Compose the actual closed inclusion, the first relative-product projection and the Grassmannian structure map; `incidenceLocus.fieldPoints`: For the free rank-n sheaf over a field, points over the identity correspond to pairs of quotient kernels whose intersection has dimension at least k.

*Needs:* `coherentGrassmannian`, `rankLocus`, ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`.

**Checks.**

- `IncidenceTests.zeroBound`: `k=0` gives the entire relative product.
- `IncidenceTests.lines`: For two rank-one quotient kernels U,W in `k²`, a point of incidenceLocus of type `(n,a,b,k)=(2,1,1,1)` over `(U,W)` exists exactly when `U=W`.
- `IncidenceTests.impossible`: k>min(a,b) gives the empty scheme; for `(n,a,b,k)=(2,0,1,1)` the locus is empty although `U=0` makes `U→E/W` the zero map, which a truncated bound `a−k=0` would admit everywhere.

Define `frobeniusStableLocus`. On a characteristic-p scheme X with finite locally free E, write `F_X` for absolute Frobenius and let `Φ:F_X*E→E` be an `O_X`-linear map. On a Grassmann parameter scheme G carrying universal `U⊂E_G` and `Q=E_G/U`, equip the pulled-back bundle with the induced Frobenius-linear map, using the natural square `F_X∘π=π∘F_G`. The Frobenius-stable locus is the zero scheme of `F_G*U→F_G*E_G→E_G→Q`. It is a closed subscheme of G; a G-valued family factors through it exactly when this composite is the zero sheaf map. Absolute-Frobenius naturality gives arbitrary characteristic-p base-change compatibility. It is distinct from the O-linear invariant locus of ModularCurves §0G.

Here p prime; characteristic-p schemes and absolute Frobenius; locally free U and Q. Φ need not be invertible; an invertible Φ models the étale case.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Lemma 5.8, pp.58–59).

The API gives `frobeniusStableLocus.inclusion`: The zero-scheme inclusion into the parameter scheme; `frobeniusStableLocus.isClosedImmersion`: The inclusion is a closed immersion; `frobeniusStableLocus.equation`: After pulling back the universal subbundle and applying Φ, the quotient composite is zero; `frobeniusStableLocus.maximal`: Every morphism on which this pulled-back composite vanishes factors uniquely through the zero scheme; `frobeniusStableLocus.graphEquation`: In the rank-two line-graph chart, with Φ matrix `[[a,b],[c,d]]`, the zero-map equation is `c+d t^p-t(a+b t^p)=0`, since the Frobenius-pulled line has generator `(1,t^p)`.

*Needs:* `coherentGrassmannian`, ModularCurves §0G, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`, `rankLocus`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`, Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`.

**Checks.**

- `FrobeniusTests.zeroOperator`: For `Φ=0` the stable locus is the entire Grassmannian.
- `FrobeniusTests.identityChart`: On a line graph in rank two with semilinear identity coefficients, the equation is `t^p−t=0`.
- `FrobeniusTests.nonFixedCoefficient`: If `t^p≠t`, its graph is excluded even though the ordinary identity linear operator preserves it.

Prove `coefficientFrobeniusLattice`. For the arithmetic operation on `R((u))` that fixes every coefficient of R and sends u to `u^p`, a finite lattice cutoff expresses stability by the ordinary coefficient-linear composite `U→V→V/U`, after choosing a sufficiently large target cutoff. It is represented by the invariant (zero-map) locus of ModularCurves §0G, with relations for the changed u-exponents. This operation is not absolute Frobenius on R: the graph coefficient t is fixed, rather than sent to `t^p`. Determinantal bounds on the cutoff and nestedness use the rank and flag constructions separately.

Here Finite truncations with explicit source and target bounds ensuring τ maps source to target; base R has characteristic p for the arithmetic use but `τ|R`=id. No claim of a single cutoff representing all unbounded lattices.

([Ulrich Görtz](https://math.ug/alggeom3-ws2324/pdf/AG3-WS2324-Goertz-20240526.pdf), §5, Lemma 5.8 and Proposition 5.16, pp.58–59,61–62).

For the proof, describe τ on the finite monomial basis by `u^j↦u^(pj)`; its matrix entries are 0 or 1 and it is R-linear. If source and target truncations differ, use the corresponding two quotient Grassmannians and their zero-map incidence; then apply the O-linear invariant-locus construction of ModularCurves §0G when the same cutoff is preserved. Use larger target quotients otherwise; no new Grassmann representability is required.

*Needs:* ModularCurves §0G, `incidenceLocus`, `flagBundle`, `rankLocus`, Mathlib `Matrix.mulVecLin`.

**Checks.**

- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.zero`: the zero vector maps to zero.
- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.monomial`: for `p=3`, `N=3`, `j=2` and coefficient 5 over ℤ, the image is supported exactly at exponent 6 with coefficient 5. In general `p>0` keeps distinct source exponents distinct.
- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.nonFixedCoefficient`: when `t^p` differs from t, the constant coefficient is t, so this map differs from absolute Frobenius.

### 1.7a Finite coefficient transport

`ProjectiveBundles.coefficientFrobeniusCutoff R p N` is the coefficient-linear map from N coefficients to pN+1 coefficients obtained by placing coefficient j at exponent pj and summing if exponents coincide. It is an `R`-linear map, so additivity, scalar compatibility and the value on `0` are Mathlib's linear-map API; for every `p : ℕ` its value on a monomial is `ProjectiveBundles.coefficientFrobeniusCutoff_single`, which fixes the coefficient and changes the exponent. This finite linear map supplies the coefficient formula for `coefficientFrobeniusLattice`; it is separate from absolute Frobenius on the coefficient ring. At `p = 0` all source exponents map to degree zero, so the image coefficient is their sum; for `N = 0` the source is zero. The full lattice stability target uses a sufficiently large target cutoff and an actual quotient map. (The coefficient formula gives the proof directly; ModularCurves §0G supplies its zero-map locus.)

**Checks.**

- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.zero`: the zero vector maps to zero.
- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.monomial`: for `p=3`, `N=3`, `j=2` and coefficient 5 over ℤ, the image is supported exactly at exponent 6 with coefficient 5. In general `p>0` keeps distinct source exponents distinct.
- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.nonFixedCoefficient`: when `t^p` differs from t, the constant coefficient is t, so this map differs from absolute Frobenius.
- `CoefficientFrobeniusTests.collapsedExponents`: at `p=0`, the vector `(a,b)` with two source
  coefficients maps to the sole target coefficient `a+b`; the single-monomial formula still holds.

### Examples

The rank-zero bundle has empty projectivization. An invertible bundle has `P(L)=S` and `O(m)=L^m`, including negative m. For `E=O(1)⊕O` on `P¹`, the top direct image of `O(−2)` is `O(−1)`. On the quotient chart with rows `(1,0,a,b)` and `(0,1,c,d)`, the ordered minors are `(1,c,d,−a,−b,ad−bc)` and satisfy the alternating Plücker relation in every characteristic. Three collinear points in `P²` have ideal regularity 3; three noncollinear points have regularity 2, although both have Hilbert polynomial 3.

### Dependencies

Mathlib graded rings, projective spectra and the module Grassmannian; AlgebraicVectorBundles L0C (symmetric and exterior powers, determinants); SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.3 (relative Proj), §2.6 (projective-space cohomology and Serre vanishing), §4.12 (generic flatness) and §§5.3–5.4 (Chern classes, projective bundles of locally free sheaves); StableReduction Layer 2; ModularCurves §0G.

## Layer 2: Hom, Isom and coherent dévissage

### 2.1 Hilbert families and graph parameters

Define `hilbertFunctorAsQuot`. For `f : X → S` separated of finite presentation, `Hilb_{X/S}(T) = {closed Z ⊂ X_T finitely presented, flat and proper over T}`; the bijection `Hilb_{X/S} ≅ Quot_{O_X/X/S}`, `Z ↦ (O_{X_T} ↠ i_*O_Z)`, inverse "kernel = ideal of Z"; the degree-d subfunctor `Hilb^d` (`Z → T` finite locally free of rank d) and, for `X ⊂ Pⁿ_S`, the subfunctors `Hilb^P` of fixed fibrewise Hilbert polynomial.

The API consists of `HilbertFunctor.toQuot` sends Z to its structure-sheaf quotient; `HilbertFunctor.ofQuot` takes the closed subscheme cut out by the kernel, inverse to `HilbertFunctor.toQuot`; `HilbertFunctor.pullback` base-changes the closed family and its quotient; `HilbertFunctor.degree` is the locally constant rank for finite locally free families.

**Checks.**

- `HilbertFunctorTests.degreeZero` `Hilb⁰ = S`
- `HilbertFunctorTests.affineLineNotProper` `A¹_T ⊂ A¹_T` is not a point of `Hilb_{A¹/S}`, so dropping properness changes the functor
- `HilbertFunctorTests.twoPointsOnLine` `Hilb²_{P¹/k} = P²`.
(Stacks, Section 99.9 (tag 0CZX), Lemma 99.9.2 (tag 0D00).)
*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`.

Prove `hilbertDegreeOneAndNonFlatBase`. For `f : X → S` separated of finite presentation, `Hilb¹_{X/S}` is represented by X with universal family the diagonal `X → X ×_S X` (an isomorphism onto its image, hence flat): a degree-one `Z ⊂ X_T` gives a unit map `O_T → q_*O_Z` with `q_*O_Z` locally free of rank 1. On each residue field this is the unit map into a nonzero one-dimensional algebra and is an isomorphism; its determinant is therefore a unit locally, so the map is an isomorphism, so Z is the graph of a section `T → X_T`, `i.e`. a morphism `T → X` over S. Consequently, for `S = Spec k[ε]/(ε²)` and `X = Spec k` its closed point, `Hilb¹_{X/S} = X` has flat universal family while `X → S` is not flat (k is not flat over `k[ε]`); so flatness of the universal family over Hilb, which holds by definition of the functor, never implies flatness of `Hilb_{X/S} → S`, even for a closed immersion `X → S` of finite presentation.
(Stacks, Lemma 99.9.2 (tag 0D00) (`Hilb = Quot`) and Lemma 10.16.4 (tag 05G8) (a surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism); the degree-one representability additionally uses the preceding fibrewise unit-map argument and has no Stacks number.)
*Needs:* §2.1.

Prove `homAndIsomSchemes`. Let S be locally Noetherian, `X → S` projective flat and `Y → S` quasi-projective. (i) `T ↦ Hom_T(X_T,Y_T)` is represented by an open subscheme `Hom_S(X,Y) ⊂ Hilb_{X×_SY/S}`, the locus of `Z ⊂ X_T ×_T Y_T` with `pr_1 : Z → X_T` an isomorphism; it is a disjoint union over Hilbert polynomials of quasi-projective S-schemes, commutes with base change, and carries identity, composition and evaluation `X ×_S Hom_S(X,Y) → Y`. (ii) If also `Y → S` is projective flat, the isomorphisms form an open subscheme `Isom_S(X,Y) ⊂ Hom_S(X,Y)`, with inverse `Isom_S(X,Y) ≅ Isom_S(Y,X)`, composition and base change. When `Y → S` is projective flat, (i) and (ii) are the Hom and Isom schemes of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14's `hilbert_quot_schemes`, which are imported with their universal families and base change and are not rebuilt; the extension proved here is (i) for a quasi-projective target. For an open immersion `Y ⊂ Ȳ` into a projective flat S-scheme, `Hom_S(X,Y)` is the open subscheme of the §4.14 scheme `Hom_S(X,Ȳ)` where the universal morphism avoids `Ȳ\Y`: remove the proper image of the inverse image of that closed complement in `X×_S Hom_S(X,Ȳ)`. For a locally closed immersion, first impose the closed factorization condition through the scheme-theoretic closure of Y, then the open avoidance condition inside that closure. This gives a locally closed Hom subscheme, compatibly with evaluation, composition and base change; a closed target gives a closed Hom subscheme. The cited openness argument applies to the projective projection from the universal graph between proper flat families. A general proper morphism is not covered by that projectivity-based source argument. Checks: `Hom_S(S,Y) = Y`, `Hom_S(X,S) = S`; `Hom_k(Spec k[ε],Y)` is the tangent scheme `Spec Sym Ω_{Y/k}` for Y smooth; for `Y = A¹_k ⊂ P¹_k` and `X = P¹_k`, `Hom_k(X,Y)` is the open locus of constant maps to `A¹` in `Hom_k(P¹,P¹)`, a copy of `A¹_k`. `HomTargetChecks.closedPoint`: for `X=Spec k` and `Y={0}⊂P¹_k`, the Hom locus is the closed point `{0}`, which is not open. `HomTargetChecks.openLine`: for `X=Spec k` and `Y=A¹_k⊂P¹_k` it is the open `A¹_k`. `HomTargetChecks.locallyClosed`: for `X=Spec k` and `Y=A¹_k×{0}⊂P¹_k×P¹_k` it is open in the closed fibre `P¹_k×{0}` and is not open in the ambient product.
(Nitsure, Theorems 6.5–6.6, pp. 30–31, with the evaluation, inverse and composition maps supplied by the graph functor.)
*Needs:* §2.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 (`hilbert_quot_schemes`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.8.

### 2.1a Nonflat test points

The scheme map `Spec k → Spec k[ε]/ε²` induced by the augmentation is a closed immersion and is not flat. It is a test input for graph and Hilbert constructions: the universal family is flat over its parameter, which does not require that parameter to be flat over the original base. (The augmentation formula and the tensor test: the nonzero ideal `(ε)` injects into `k[ε]/ε²`, while its inclusion becomes zero after tensoring with k.)

**Checks.**

- `HilbertTests.universalFlat`: the universal family is flat over the Hilbert parameter scheme.
- `HilbertTests.nonflatParameter`: the dual-number closed point is a valid degree-one parameter although its map to the base is not flat.
- `HilbertTests.augmentation`: the augmentation kills ε and preserves 1, fixing its direction and distinguishing it from an isomorphism.

### 2.2 Automorphisms and bounded quotients

Prove `automorphismGroupScheme`. For S locally Noetherian and `X → S` projective flat, `Aut_S(X) := Isom_S(X,X)` is a group scheme over S, locally of finite type (a disjoint union of quasi-projective S-schemes), acting on `Hom_S(X,Y)` and `Hom_S(Y,X)`; `Aut_S(Pⁿ_S) = PGL_{n+1,S}`; `Aut_k(E)` for an elliptic curve contains E acting by translation and is not finite; finiteness and unramifiedness are asserted only for stable curves, by SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.15.
(Nitsure, Theorems 6.5–6.6, pp. 30–31, together with the group operations on Isom and SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.15's `isom_stable_curves`.)
*Needs:* §2.1 (`homAndIsomSchemes`, with its composition and inverse maps), SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.13.

Prove `quotIntoGrassmannian`. Let S be Noetherian, `X = Pⁿ_S`, `E = O_X(−a)^{⊕p}`, P a polynomial and `m_0 = m_0(n,p,P,a)` from §1.5. Increase `m_0` to at least a. For `m ≥ m_0` every T-point of `Quot^P_{E/X/S}` (T-flat quotient `E_T ↠ Q` with fibrewise Hilbert polynomial P) satisfies `Rⁱπ_{T*}Q(m) = 0 (i ≥ 1)`, `π_{T*}Q(m)` locally free of rank `P(m)`, `π_{T*}E_T(m) ↠ π_{T*}Q(m)`, and Q is recovered from the subsheaf of `E_T(m)` generated by `π_{T*}K(m)`. Hence `Q ↦ (π_{T*}E_T(m) ↠ π_{T*}Q(m))` is a monomorphism of functors `Quot^P_{E/X/S} → Gr(P(m), π_*E(m))` with `π_*E(m) = Sym^{m−a}(O^{n+1})^{⊕p}` locally free. SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 owns the representability of Quot, including its own regularity bound and Grassmannian embedding, and imports nothing from this roadmap; this theorem is the explicit form of that embedding for the bound `m_0` of `uniformQuotientRegularity`, and identifies the representing scheme of §4.14 with a closed subscheme of this Grassmannian. It is not an input to §4.14.

Assume S Noetherian; E a finite sum of twists of O (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 reduces general coherent E to this case).
(Nitsure, §5, Grassmannian embedding in the proof of Theorem 5.2, p. 26; Theorem 2.3, pp. 11–12.)
*Needs:* §1.3, §1.5, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14.
`QuotBoundTests.nonnegativeDegree` has `m−a ≥ 0`, so `Sym^{m−a}` and `P(m)` specify genuine finite ranks; the empty-quotient case has `P = 0` and Grassmannian rank zero.

### 2.3 Coherent dévissage

Prove `coherentDevissage`. Let X be Noetherian and P a property of coherent `O_X`-modules such that (0) the zero sheaf has P, (1) in any short exact sequence of coherent sheaves, if two terms have P so does the third, and (2) for every integral closed `Z ⊂ X` with generic point ξ there is a coherent G with `Supp G = Z`, `m_ξG_ξ = 0`, `dim_{κ(ξ)}G_ξ = 1` and `P(G)`. Then P holds for every coherent sheaf on X. Variant: (1) may be weakened to closure under extensions plus "`F^{⊕r}` has `P ⇒ F` has P" if (2) is strengthened to the ideal-subsheaf condition of the cited variant; (0) is kept in both forms. Hypothesis (0) follows from (1) and (2) when X is nonempty (apply (1) to `0 → G → G → 0 → 0` for any G supplied by (2)) and is needed only for the empty scheme, where (1) and (2) are vacuous; the cited lemmas omit it.
Checks: for `X = ∅` and P identically false, (1) and (2) hold and P fails on the zero sheaf, so (0) cannot be dropped; for `X = Spec k` and P = "finite-dimensional of even dimension", (0) and (1) hold but (2) fails for `G = k`, and P indeed fails for k; for `X = Spec k` and P = "finite-dimensional", all three hypotheses hold and the conclusion is the finiteness of every coherent sheaf.
(Stacks, Lemma 30.12.6 (tag 01YI); Lemma 30.12.8 (tag 01YM); Lemma 30.12.3 (tag 01YF).)
*Needs:* Mathlib `IsNoetherianRing` (Noetherian induction). The same induction gives the dévissage for algebraizability of AdicSpacesPartIII F0.7 (*existence-devissage*).

Prove `devissageViaChow`. Let X be proper over a Noetherian S and P as in §2.3(0)–(1). Suppose that for every integral closed `Z ⊂ X` there are a proper surjective `π : Z' → Z` with `Z'` projective over S and π an isomorphism over a dense open of Z, and L relatively very ample on `Z'`, such that P holds for `(Z → X)_*π_*L^{⊗n}` for some n with `Rⁱπ_*L^{⊗n} = 0 (i ≥ 1)`. Then P holds for every coherent sheaf on X. Chow's lemma supplies `(Z',π,L)` for each Z and relative Serre vanishing supplies n; `G := π_*L^{⊗n}` has support Z and generic stalk `κ(ξ)` because π is an isomorphism near ξ. This is the mechanism of the proofs of proper GAGA and of coherence of higher direct images under proper morphisms. Check: for `X = ∅` there is no Z and the conclusion is exactly hypothesis (0).
(Stacks, Proposition 30.19.1 `(02O5)`, Lemma 30.18.1 (0200) and Lemma 30.12.6 (01YI); SGA 1, XII, Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.3 and Theorem 4.4, retyped pp. 247–251. ComplexComparisonPartII §C1.9 states the complex proper comparison and its `Ext¹` correction.)
*Needs:* §2.3, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6.

### Examples

The degree-one Hilbert functor is X. For the closed point `Spec k → Spec k[ε]/(ε²)`, its universal family is flat over the parameter while the parameter map is not flat. The graph openness argument uses a projective source.

### Dependencies

Layer 1; SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12 (Chow's lemma) and §4.14 (Hilbert and Quot schemes). The dévissage criterion is used by the nonarchimedean proper comparison of §7.4 and the complex proper comparison of ComplexComparisonPartII §C1.9.

## Layer 3: effective descent and finite-source restriction

### 3.1 Pullback coherence and fpqc descent

SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 owns the quasi-coherent pseudofunctor `Descent.qcohPseudofunctor` and
the theorem `qcoh_fpqc_descent` that it is a stack for the fpqc topology. `quasicoherentPseudofunctor`
and `fpqcQuasicoherentDescent` below are aliases of those two declarations (`abbrev` and `alias` in
Lean), not second constructions, and `spaceQuasicoherentModules` is an alias of §1.11's `Spaces.QCoh`.
The faithful, full and effective statements below are read off from `qcoh_fpqc_descent` in the
covering-family form that the algebraic-space descent `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent` uses. What this
roadmap adds is the API of these aliases, the affine overlap and coalgebra presentations (§§3.2–3.3),
the descent of finite presentation and of finite local freeness, and the extension to algebraic
spaces.

Define `quasicoherentPseudofunctor` as SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1's `Descent.qcohPseudofunctor`: the scheme-module pullback functors restricted to the full subcategories of the IsQuasicoherent predicate, a Cat-valued pseudofunctor on Schemeᵒᵖ with the sheaf-module unit and composition constraints restricted to these subcategories. Quasi-coherent modules retain arbitrary module morphisms; the fibres are not groupoids. The API below is added here.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T), Proposition 35.5.2; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01BG), Lemma 17.10.4).

The API gives `QCohPseudofunctor.fibre`: The fibre at X is the full subcategory defined by IsQuasicoherent; `QCohPseudofunctor.map`: The arrow map is the restriction of `Scheme.Modules.pullback`; `QCohPseudofunctor.affine`: The affine comparison through tildeEquiv identifies arrow maps with extendScalars; `QCohPseudofunctor.map_forget`: Forgetting the quasi-coherent property after the restricted pullback is naturally isomorphic to forgetting first and applying the `Scheme.Modules.pullback`.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentSheaf.pullback`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackId`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pseudofunctor_associativity`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pseudofunctor_left_unitality`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pseudofunctor_right_unitality`.

**Checks.**

- `QCohPseudoTests.identity`: The unit map is the pullbackId restricted to the full subcategory.
- `QCohPseudoTests.infiniteModule`: The direct sum of countably many copies of R on `Spec R` is included even though it is not finitely generated when R is a field.
- `QCohPseudoTests.nonInvertibleArrow`: Multiplication by 2 on `O_SpecZ` is a fibre morphism, and is not an isomorphism; the category is not truncated to its core.
- `AffinePullbackTests.nonflat`: along `ℤ → ℤ/2`, multiplication by `2` on `O_{Spec ℤ}` is a monomorphism whose pullback is the zero endomorphism of the nonzero sheaf `O_{Spec 𝔽₂}`; pullback is right exact, not exact.

Define `moduleDescentCoaction`. For every commutative ring map `R→A`, tensor-overlap module descent is equivalent to the existing scalar-extension comonad coalgebras, preserving the underlying A-module and every morphism. The all-test-object DescentData category is identified with this presentation through Mathlib’s existing chosen-pullback descent equivalence and the module-specific coordinate comparison. The coaction is `d(n)=θ(n⊗1)`; the reverse transition and its inverse are the specified coaction-transition maps. No flatness is required for these presentation comparisons.

Here Commutative rings R,A in one universe and an arbitrary ring map `R→A`. Modules and their morphisms are arbitrary; faithful flatness is needed only for the following effective-descent theorem.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023N), Proposition 35.3.9, equalizer formula and cocycle calculation).

The API gives `ModuleDescentCoalgebra.equivalence`: An equivalence preserving the underlying A-module and its maps; `ModuleDescentCoalgebra.coaction`: The coaction sends n to `θ(n⊗1)`; `ModuleDescentCoalgebra.canonical`: The canonical datum on `A⊗R M` becomes the comparison coalgebra of M.

*Needs:* `overlapCoalgebraEquivalence`, `ModuleDescentBridge.overlap_comparison_canonical`, Mathlib `CommRingCat.moduleCatExtendScalarsPseudofunctor`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`, `moduleDescentCoalgebra`.

**Checks.**

- `ModuleCoalgebraTests.identity`: For `R=A`, descent and coalgebras are equivalent to ModuleCat R.
- `ModuleCoalgebraTests.product`: For the diagonal `R→R×R` the transition identifies the two component modules and recovers one R-module.
- `ModuleCoalgebraTests.cocycle`: Arbitrary pairwise invertible maps that fail the triple-overlap equation do not define a coalgebra.

Prove `affineModuleDescentEquivalence`. For a faithfully flat commutative ring map `R→A`, Mathlib's canonical functor ModuleCat R→affine ModuleCat DescentData for the singleton `f.op` is an equivalence. Under the tensor-overlap comparison its inverse is `M={n∈N | 1⊗n=θ(n⊗1)}`. The comparison `A⊗R M→N` is `a↦(m↦a m)` and is an isomorphism of the descent data, not merely of modules.

Here Commutative rings R,A in one fixed universe, a specified ring map `f:R→A` with f faithfully flat, and arbitrary R- and A-modules with all module morphisms. No Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023N), Proposition 35.3.9(1)–(3)).

For the proof, use the comonadicExtendScalars and the canonical comparison; transfer IsEquivalence through the specified descent/coalgebra equivalence; then identify the inverse and its counit by `descentEqualizerModuleCoordinates`, including the right-adjoint uniqueness transport; then keep the unit/counit and every module-map naturality square; faithful flatness is used here, after the arbitrary-map presentation equivalences.

*Needs:* `moduleDescentCoaction`, Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`, `moduleCanonicalComparison`, `descentEqualizerModuleCoordinates`.

Prove `affineFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`. For a finite standard fpqc covering {Ui→S} of an affine scheme S, the canonical functor from QCoh(S) to descent data for the cover is an equivalence.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023S), Lemma 35.5.1 and proof).

For the proof, replace the finite affine cover by its finite disjoint union, which is affine; its ring is the finite product of the component rings, and the resulting ring map is faithfully flat by flatness and joint surjectivity; then use tildeEquiv and its tensor pullback comparisons to identify the module descent of `affineModuleDescentEquivalence` with the sheaf descent of `qcoh_fpqc_descent` for this cover, comparing finite-family and disjoint-union descent data with their morphisms and cocycles. This is the affine module presentation of the §1.1 theorem, not a second proof of it.

*Needs:* `quasicoherentPseudofunctor`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.tildeFunctorCompPullbackIso`, `affineModuleDescentEquivalence`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (`qcoh_fpqc_descent`), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFaithful`. For an arbitrary fpqc cover {Ui→S} and maps a,`b:M→N` between quasi-coherent modules on S, equality of all pullbacks implies `a=b`.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T), Proposition 35.5.2, faithfulness proof).

For the proof, the covering family generates a covering sieve of the fpqc topology, and the canonical functor to descent data for the family factors through descent data for that sieve; faithfulness is the faithfulness part of `qcoh_fpqc_descent` for this sieve.

*Needs:* `quasicoherentPseudofunctor`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (`qcoh_fpqc_descent`).

Prove `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFull`. For an arbitrary fpqc cover {Ui→S}, every compatible family of maps `f_i:M`|Ui→N|Ui is the pullback of a unique map `M→N`.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T), Proposition 35.5.2, fullness proof).

For the proof, pass from the covering family to the covering sieve it generates, where a compatible family of maps over the family determines a compatible family over the sieve because the members of the sieve factor through some Ui and the compatibility is over Ui×S Ui′; fullness is the fullness part of `qcoh_fpqc_descent` for this sieve, and uniqueness is `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFaithful`.

*Needs:* `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFaithful`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (`qcoh_fpqc_descent`).

Prove `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentEffective`. Every quasi-coherent module descent datum on an arbitrary fpqc covering {Ui→S} is effective, with a specified isomorphism from the canonical datum of the glued sheaf to the original datum.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T), Proposition 35.5.2, effectivity proof and final omitted verification).

For the proof, extend a descent datum on the family to the covering sieve it generates, by pulling back along a chosen factorization through some Ui and using the cocycle to make the result independent of that choice; effectivity is the essential surjectivity part of `qcoh_fpqc_descent` for this sieve, and the specified comparison isomorphism is its counit restricted back to the family.

*Needs:* `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFull`, `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFaithful`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (`qcoh_fpqc_descent`).

Prove `fpqcQuasicoherentDescent`. For every scheme S and every fpqc covering {Ui→S}, the canonical functor QCoh(S)→`QCohPseudofunctor.DescentData`(Ui→S) is an equivalence. There is no Noetherian, coherence, finite-generation, finite-presentation, separatedness or smoothness condition.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T), Proposition 35.5.2).

For the proof, this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1's `qcoh_fpqc_descent`, declared here as an alias in the covering-family form: combine the three preceding statements for the same canonical functor, retaining the datum comparison as the counit.

*Needs:* `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFaithful`, `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentFull`, `fpqcQuasicoherentDescentEffective`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (`qcoh_fpqc_descent`).

Prove `finitePresentationModuleDescent`. If S is faithfully flat over a commutative ring R and `S⊗R M` is a finitely presented S-module, then M is finitely presented over R. Mathlib has the finitely generated case and the case of algebras.

Here S is a faithfully flat commutative R-algebra; M is an arbitrary R-module; no Noetherian hypothesis.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05B0), Lemma 35.7.3, affine case).

For the proof, use the finite-generation descent to choose a finite free surjection `Rⁿ→M`; then flat scalar extension identifies `S⊗R ker` with the kernel of `Sⁿ→S⊗R M`; then finite presentation of `S⊗R M` makes this extended kernel finite by the kernel criterion; then descend finite generation of the kernel and apply the same criterion over R.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, Mathlib `Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker_iff`, Mathlib `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat`.

Prove `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`. For a quasi-coherent module M and an fpqc cover, if the pulled modules are finite locally free, then M is finite locally free. If their rank is the same fixed finite r, the descended module has rank r. In particular invertibility descends. This is not a descent theorem for arbitrary infinite-rank locally free modules.

Here An fpqc covering and a quasi-coherent module; A finite rank r is specified when rank preservation is asserted.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05B2), Lemma 35.7.6 and proof).

For the proof, work on affine standard fpqc refinements, as in the general module-descent proof; then descend finite presentation and flatness, then use the theorem to obtain finite projectivity; then use the finite-projective/local-free comparison; ranks agree after the residue-field extensions at points above every base point; then apply rank 1 to the invertible-sheaf predicate.

*Needs:* `finitePresentationModuleDescent`, Mathlib `Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`, Mathlib `Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `spaceQuasicoherentModules` as SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11's `Spaces.QCoh`: for an algebraic space X, the full category of sheaves of modules on its small étale ringed site satisfying the sheaf-of-modules quasi-coherence predicate. No second carrier is introduced; the chart API below is added here. The category is equivalent to compatible quasi-coherent modules on its scheme étale charts, with specified pullback isomorphisms and composition equations (§1.11's `QCoh.presentationEquiv` for a presentation).

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03G5), Definition 66.29.1 and Lemma 66.29.3).

The API gives `SpaceQCoh.chart`: Restriction to a scheme étale chart is quasi-coherent; `SpaceQCoh.transition`: A chart morphism gives a specified pullback isomorphism with unit/composition coherence; `SpaceQCoh.schemeEquivalence`: For a scheme X the category agrees with the ordinary quasi-coherent category.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11 (`Spaces.QCoh`, `QCoh.presentationEquiv`, `QCoh.ofSchemeEquiv`), Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`, `quasicoherentPseudofunctor`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `SpaceQCohTests.affine`: For `Spec R`, composition with the existing tildeEquiv identifies this category with ModuleCat R.
- `SpaceQCohTests.identity`: The identity atlas of a scheme recovers its existing quasi-coherent modules.
- `SpaceQCohTests.infiniteModule`: Infinite free modules are allowed on every chart; this is not a coherent-only category.

Prove `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`. For any fpqc covering {Xi→X} of algebraic spaces, the canonical functor QCoh(X)→descent data is an equivalence, retaining all module maps and allowing arbitrary quasi-coherent modules.

Here Schemes and quasi-coherent modules in specified universes; no Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-presentation hypotheses.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04W8), Proposition 74.4.1, steps1–7).

For the proof, choose scheme étale charts Tij→Xi. The composite family {Tij→X} is an fpqc refinement of {Xi→X}; preserve the pulled original datum and the comparison to its restrictions; then for every scheme `U→X` in the small étale site, the representable diagonal of X makes `U×X` Tij a scheme. Apply the scheme descent theorem to the fpqc cover {`U×X` Tij→U}. Do not apply a theorem about scheme covers directly to `U×X` Xi before replacing Xi by its scheme charts; then full faithfulness makes the descended modules functorial in the input datum and supplies the comparisons for chart maps; then faithfulness verifies their unit and composition equations; glue them as a sheaf on the ringed étale site; then compare both composites with identity on objects and morphisms by the same chartwise full faithfulness.

*Needs:* `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, `fpqcQuasicoherentDescent`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `moduleOverlapDatum`. ModuleOverlapDatum(f) has an S-module N and an `S⊗R S`-linear isomorphism `θ:N⊗R S→S⊗R N` satisfying `θ12∘θ01=θ02` on the triple tensor product. On `N⊗R S` the two scalar factors act on N and S respectively; on `S⊗R N` they act on S and N respectively. θij is extension along the insertion map `p_ij:S⊗R S→S⊗R S⊗R S`, using the tensor associators.

Here Commutative rings R,S in one fixed universe and an arbitrary ring homomorphism `f:R→S`; N is an arbitrary S-module. No faithful-flatness, finite-generation or Noetherian assumption.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023F), Definition 35.3.1 and the paragraph defining φij).

### 3.2 Tensor overlap and coalgebra comparison

Throughout this topic, Commutative rings R,S in one fixed universe and an arbitrary ring homomorphism `f:R→S`; N is an arbitrary S-module. No faithful-flatness, finite-generation or Noetherian assumption..

For the proof, read the toComonad fields: toFunctor=U⋙L, ε=the adjunction counit, `Δ=L` applied to the unit at `U(N)`; then evaluate the existing unit and scalar-extension map on a pure tensor to obtain `Δ(s⊗n)=s⊗(1⊗n)`; then evaluate the existing counit to obtain `s·n`, then unfold the existing `Coalgebra.counit`, coassoc and `Hom.h` equations; then use tensor universal properties to extend these formulas to all elements.

*Needs:* Mathlib `ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.toComonad`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Comonad.Coalgebra`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Comonad.Coalgebra.Hom`, Mathlib `ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj_unit_app_apply`, Mathlib `ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.Counit.map`, Mathlib `ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.map_tmul`.

Prove `overlapDiagonal`. For a ModuleOverlapDatum(f), let `p:N→N` be the pullback of θ along multiplication `μ:S⊗R S→S`, using the two tensor unit identifications. Equivalently `p(n)`=εN(`θ(n⊗1)`). Then p=idN. This holds for any f, even if f is not faithfully flat.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023F), Lemma 35.3.2, full proof of σ00∘δ11=id).

For the proof, base change of the overlap isomorphism along μ shows that p is an isomorphism; no flatness is used to preserve an isomorphism; then evaluate the cocycle on `n⊗1⊗1` and multiply the two S coefficients into the N factor: if `θ(n⊗1)`=Σai⊗ni and θ(ni⊗1)=Σaij⊗nij, obtain Σai aij nij=Σai ni; then because p is S-linear, the left side is `p(p(n))` and the right side is `p(n)`; hence `p²=p`; then cancel the invertible p to get p=id. The finite sums abbreviate equality of tensor-induced linear maps, not chosen coordinates.

*Needs:* `moduleOverlapDatum`, `ModuleDescentBridge.tensor_comonad_coordinates`.

Define `overlapToCoalgebra`. For an arbitrary f and overlap datum `(N,θ)`, `dθ(n)=θ(n⊗1)` is S-linear for the first-factor action and defines an object of the existing `Comonad.Coalgebra G`. The counit law is overlap diagonal normalization; the coassociativity law is the triple cocycle evaluated at `n⊗1⊗1`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023F), Definition 35.3.1; Lemma 35.3.2, δ11 and the cocycle equality).

The API gives `ModuleOverlapDatum.toCoalgebra`: Constructs the coalgebra on the same S-module N; `ModuleOverlapDatum.toCoalgebra_coaction`: The coaction at n is `θ(n⊗1)`; `ModuleOverlapDatum.toCoalgebra_module`: Forgetting the coalgebra returns the datum's underlying ModuleCat S object.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023F), Definition 35.3.1 and Lemma 35.3.2, tensor-linearity and displayed coaction).

The right side becomes s⊗Σai ni=`s⊗n`; then tensor extensionality proves the two map equalities on all elements; the preceding bilinearity checks prove these operations respect balancing. The abbreviation `ModuliDescent.P` is `Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type`, at the fixed scheme universe. Its objects, restriction maps and natural transformations are the existing presheaf operations. The relative Hom and restriction checks below compute their identity-source, empty-source and two-point values in this carrier.

### 3.3a Signatures of the descent carriers

The affine presentation uses Mathlib's extension-of-scalars pseudofunctor reindexed by affine
scheme arrows, `AffineModuleDescent.affineModulePullback`, with the effective descent theorem
`AffineModuleDescent.faithfullyFlatDescent`. These and the quasi-coherent pseudofunctor of §3.1, the
singleton descent category `AffineModuleDescent.SingletonDescentData f` and the coalgebra category
`AffineModuleDescent.ScalarExtensionCoalgebra f` (Mathlib's `Comonad.Coalgebra` for restriction
followed by extension of scalars), the comparisons `AffineModuleDescent.forgetDescentData`,
`AffineModuleDescent.coalgebraEquivalence`, `AffineModuleDescent.coalgebraEquivalenceForget` and
`AffineModuleDescent.canonicalComparison` (§§3.2–3.3), and the relative Hom and Weil restriction
presheaves of §3.4 with their structure maps, universal properties and functoriality are targets
with the following intended signatures. The value of `ModuliDescent.relativeHom f x hf` at `T` is
the set of pairs of a point `a ∈ B(T)` and a section `b ∈ X(T ×_B Z)` over `a`, and its restriction
maps precompose with the canonical fibre maps; `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction f hf z` is the same
with `b` a section of `z` over `T ×_B Z`. The coalgebra presentations hold for every ring map;
`AffineModuleDescent.faithfullyFlatDescent` needs faithful flatness. (Mathlib `DescentData`,
`DescentData'.descentDataEquivalence`, `ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj`, `Comonad.comparison`;
the tensor-overlap construction of §3.2.)

```lean
open _root_.AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable def QCohPseudofunctor : LocallyDiscrete Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat

namespace AffineModuleDescent

open CategoryTheory Opposite

noncomputable section

variable {R A : Type uD} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]

abbrev SingletonDescentData (f : R →+* A) :=
  affineModulePullback.DescentData
    (fun (_ : PUnit) ↦ (CommRingCat.ofHom f).op)

abbrev ScalarExtensionCoalgebra (f : R →+* A) :=
  (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj f).toComonad.Coalgebra

def forgetDescentData (f : R →+* A) : SingletonDescentData f ⥤ ModuleCat.{uD} A

def coalgebraEquivalence (f : R →+* A) :
    SingletonDescentData f ≌ ScalarExtensionCoalgebra f

def coalgebraEquivalenceForget (f : R →+* A) :
    (coalgebraEquivalence f).functor ⋙
      Comonad.forget (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj f).toComonad ≅
    forgetDescentData f

def canonicalComparison (f : R →+* A) :
    affineModulePullback.toDescentData
        (fun (_ : PUnit) ↦ (CommRingCat.ofHom f).op) ⋙
      (coalgebraEquivalence f).functor ≅
    Comonad.comparison (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj f)

end

end AffineModuleDescent

noncomputable section

namespace ModuliDescent

variable {B Z X : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (f : Z ⟶ B) (x : X ⟶ B)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)

def relativeHom : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)

def relativeHomToBase : relativeHom f x hf ⟶ B

def relativeHomHomEquiv {V : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (v : V ⟶ B) :
    { c : V ⟶ relativeHom f x hf // c ≫ relativeHomToBase f x hf = v } ≃
      { b : pullback v f ⟶ X // b ≫ x = pullback.fst v f ≫ v }

def relativeHomMap {X' : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (x' : X' ⟶ B) (m : X ⟶ X') (hm : m ≫ x' = x) :
    relativeHom f x hf ⟶ relativeHom f x' hf

variable (z : X ⟶ Z)

def weilRestriction : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)

def weilRestrictionToBase : weilRestriction f hf z ⟶ B

def weilRestrictionHomEquiv {V : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (v : V ⟶ B) :
    { c : V ⟶ weilRestriction f hf z // c ≫ weilRestrictionToBase f hf z = v } ≃
      { b : pullback v f ⟶ X // b ≫ z = pullback.snd v f }

def weilRestrictionMap {X' : (Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (z' : X' ⟶ Z) (m : X ⟶ X') (hm : m ≫ z' = z) :
    weilRestriction f hf z ⟶ weilRestriction f hf z'

end ModuliDescent

end
```

**Checks.**

- `ModuleNativeChecks.object`: the canonical descent object corresponds to the scalar-extension coalgebra with the unit coaction.
- `ModuleNativeChecks.roundtrip`: an arbitrary overlap datum is recovered after conversion to a coalgebra and back.
- `ModuleNativeChecks.arrows`: extension of every module map, including a zero or noninvertible map, is the underlying map of canonical descent.
- `ModuleCoalgebraChecks.counit`: the coaction followed by the counit is the identity (Mathlib's `Comonad.Coalgebra.counit`).
- `ModuleCoalgebraChecks.coassociativity`: the two iterated coactions agree (Mathlib's `Comonad.Coalgebra.coassoc`).
- `ModuleCoalgebraChecks.arrows`: a coalgebra morphism intertwines coactions; the morphisms are not restricted to isomorphisms.

### 3.4 Relative Hom and Weil restriction

Define `ModuliDescent.relativeHom`. For scheme-representable `f:Z→B` and `x:X→B`, define `Mor_B(Z,X)(T)` to be pairs consisting of a point a in `B(T)` and a morphism `b:T×_B Z→X` satisfying `x∘b=f∘pr_Z`. Restriction along `g:T′→T` keeps `a|T′` and precomposes b with the canonical fibre map. Retain the projection to B. The representing scheme of `T×_B Z` is a choice; replacing it gives a canonical natural isomorphism.

Here Fix a universe of schemes. Algebraic spaces are the fppf sheaves of SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.3–1.4; The source `f:Z→B` is representable by schemes. This includes every finite locally free map of algebraic spaces.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §10, formula (10.0.2), Lemma 10.1 (05Y2, 05Y3), pp.14–15).

The API gives `ModuliDescent.relativeHomToBase`: The projection sends `(a,b)` to a and is natural on schemes; `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_points`: Evaluation at T identifies points with precisely the pairs in the definition; `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_map_points`: For `g:T′→T` and the unique fibre map `h:Z_T′→Z_T`, restriction sends `(a,b)` to `(a|T′,b∘h)`. Both maps to Z and to T must commute; `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_ext`: Two points coincide when their base points coincide and their maps b coincide after transport between the chosen fibres; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomHomEquiv`: For any presheaf V with `v:V→B`, maps `V→Mor_B(Z,X)` over B are naturally equivalent to maps `V×_B Z→X` over B. In objects over B, relative Hom is right adjoint to `V↦V×_B Z`, with that product regarded over B; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomHomEquiv_points`: For a scheme test T and a point `(a,b)`, the universal-property equivalence sends its Yoneda morphism to b, after precomposition with the canonical isomorphism from the chosen scheme `Z_T` to the presheaf pullback. This evaluation equation fixes the actual equivalence, rather than an arbitrary bijection of the same Hom sets; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomMap`: An actual target morphism over the relevant base induces postcomposition, retaining the base point; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomMap_points`: On a point `(a,b)`, target postcomposition with m gives exactly `(a,m∘b)`; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomMap_id`: The map induced by the identity target morphism is the identity; `ModuliDescent.relativeHomMap_comp`: The map induced by m followed by `m′` equals the composite of their induced maps, with the given base triangles transported.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable.pullback`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable.isPullback`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.yonedaEquiv`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.8.

**Checks.**

- `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_identity`: For `Z=B` and f the identity, `Mor_B(B,X)` is canonically X over B.
- `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_empty`: For Z the empty scheme presheaf, `Mor_B(Z,X)` is canonically B, even if X is empty.
- `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_split_two`: For B a scheme and `Z=B` disjoint union B, `Mor_B(Z,X)` is canonically `X×_B X`; two independent maps are retained.

Prove `ModuliDescent.finiteSourceEtaleSections`. Let `p:Z→U` be finite locally free between schemes and `w:W→Z` etale, with W an algebraic space. The sheaf of sections of `W_T→Z_T` is an algebraic space etale over U. If w is surjective its projection to U is surjective in the etale topology. No separatedness of `W→Z` is required in the conclusion.

Here U and Z are schemes; p is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation; W is an algebraic space, and w is etale; w is surjective only for the final assertion.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §9, Lemmas 9.1–9.2 (05XQ, 05XR), pp.12–14; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-more-groupoids.pdf), §12, Proposition 12.11 (04QH), p.19, with Lemmas 12.1, 12.7–12.10, pp.14–18; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-more-morphisms.pdf), §49, Lemma 49.6 (05XD), p.122).

For the proof, for separated etale `W→Z`, identify a section with its open and closed image inside `W_T`. Use the finite-part sheaf and the open locus where its map to `Z_T` is an isomorphism. For the finite open subspace `Z′` of `W_T`, its map to T is flat and locally of finite presentation because it is open in `W_T` and `W_T→Z_T→T` has those properties; finiteness makes it universally closed. The target `Z_T→T` is finite, hence closed, separated and locally of finite type. These are exactly the hypotheses of 05XD; then for general W, choose a separated scheme etale atlas `W′→W`. Sections of `W′` give a representable-by-spaces etale cover of the section sheaf: its fibre over a section is the separated case for `W′_T×_{W_T}Z_T`; then surjectivity follows by splitting the finitely many source-fibre points after an etale neighbourhood of U (05XQ). Apply Artin's bootstrap (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17) and étale locality on the source.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.8, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_algebraicity`. For algebraic spaces `Z→B` and `X→B` with `Z→B` finite locally free, `Mor_B(Z,X)` is an algebraic space. Its points and structural map are those of `ModuliDescent.relativeHom`. There is no finite-presentation, separatedness, affineness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on X.

Here B, Z and X are algebraic spaces; `Z→B` is finite locally free; finite flat alone without local finite presentation is not the convention.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §10, Lemma 10.3 and Proposition 10.4 (05Y5, 05Y7), pp.15–16; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/more-morphisms.pdf), §68, Lemmas 68.1–68.2 (05Y6, 0BL3), pp.208–209).

For the proof, the functor is an fppf sheaf by gluing the base map and then the relative morphism. Work etale locally on B to make B affine and Z finite free; then choose an etale atlas `X′→X` that is a disjoint union of affine schemes. For a point represented by `b:Z_T→X`, the pullback of `Mor_B(Z,X′)→Mor_B(Z,X)` is the section space for `Z_T×_X X′→Z_T`; `ModuliDescent.finiteSourceEtaleSections` proves etale representability by spaces and surjectivity; then for a finite collection of atlas components the target disjoint union is affine; its relative morphism space is represented by the arbitrary-algebra affine Weil restriction of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1. Maps landing in that finite union form an open subfunctor: the complement projects closed under the finite map `Z_T→T`; then on affine scheme tests T the finite source `Z_T` is quasi-compact, so a finite collection of components suffices. These open pieces therefore cover as sheaves. Glue their representers and apply Artin bootstrap to the etale cover, then descend from the etale base chart. The atlas-component index and its finite subsets stay in the fixed universe; each arbitrary-generator affine representer also stays there. Thus the covering coproduct meets the same size bounds as the source proof, 05Y7 footnote 3, p.16; no unrestricted larger-universe atlas is silently assumed.

For the proof, for `T→B′` identify `T×_{B′}Z′` with `T×_B Z` and maps into `X′` over `Z′` with maps into X over Z; then give both inverse transformations explicitly and verify their pointwise roundtrips; then all naturality, unit and composition equations follow from preservation of the same section b and the uniqueness clause of the evaluation property.

*Needs:* `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction`, `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_isSheaf`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.8.

Prove `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_cartesian`. Postcomposition with `z:X→Z` gives `Mor_B(Z,X)→Mor_B(Z,Z)`, where X is viewed over B. The identity section of Z gives `B→Mor_B(Z,Z)`. The resulting square with `Res_{Z/B}(X)`, its inclusion into `Mor_B(Z,X)` and its projection to B is cartesian as presheaves and fppf sheaves. All four maps are fixed by evaluation, and the square is natural under arbitrary base change.

Here `X→Z→B` are morphisms of algebraic spaces with `Z→B` scheme-representable.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §11, Lemma 11.4 (05YE), p.18).

For the proof, evaluate the square at T. A point in its fibre product is a pair `(a,b)` whose composite `z∘b` equals the identity section on `Z_T`; then this is exactly the defining equality for restriction; build inverse transformations with the same a and b; then use pointwise limits of presheaves and the fact that sheaf fibre products use these limits.

*Needs:* `ModuliDescent.relativeHom`, `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction`, `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_isSheaf`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.8.

Prove `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_algebraicity`. For morphisms `X→Z→B` of algebraic spaces, if `Z→B` is finite locally free, `Res_{Z/B}(X)` is an algebraic space. Its structural map, functorial evaluation and arbitrary-base-change comparison are the previously specified ones. No hypothesis of affineness, finite presentation, separatedness or quasi-compactness is imposed on X.

Here `Z→B` is finite locally free; it need not be surjective and may have rank zero on components.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §11, Proposition 11.5 (05YF), p.18).

For the proof, apply algebraicity of relative morphisms to `Mor_B(Z,X)` and `Mor_B(Z,Z)`; then use `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_cartesian` and closure of algebraic spaces under fibre products; then identify the represented sheaf with `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction` by the specified evaluation map, then carry base change across that identification.

*Needs:* `ModuliDescent.relativeHom_algebraicity`, `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_cartesian`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.8.

### 3.5 Geometric comparisons and polarized descent

Prove `ModuliDescent.affineRestrictionComparison`. On the domain of ModularCurves §0F (`Z/B` finite locally free schemes and `X/Z` affine finitely presented), the representing scheme of ModularCurves §0F, embedded into the algebraic spaces of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.4, is canonically isomorphic over B to `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_algebraicity`. On the affine-base arbitrary-algebra domain of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1 the same comparison uses its representing algebra. Both are determined by the common map `b:Z_T→X`. The comparisons agree where both suppliers apply, preserve target morphisms and commute with all base-change maps and their unit/composition equations.

Here the hypotheses of ModularCurves §0F and of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1 are retained; For the unrestricted affine coordinate reduction use the arbitrary-algebra representing algebra of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1, not only the finitely presented case of ModularCurves §0F.

(ModularCurves §0F, affine Weil restriction paragraph; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/criteria.pdf), §11, definition and Lemma 11.2 (05Y9–05YC), pp.16–17; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/more-morphisms.pdf), §68, Lemmas 68.1–68.2 (05Y6, 0BL3), pp.208–209).

For the proof, read the two representing properties as natural bijections into the same test-section set; then compose the bijections to construct the unique Yoneda isomorphism preserving the evaluation section; then prove the overlap and base-change equations by evaluation uniqueness; preserve Spec contravariance when comparing the ring-side adjunction.

*Needs:* `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_algebraicity`, `ModuliDescent.weilRestriction_baseChange`, ModularCurves §0F, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1 (*weil-restriction-representing-algebra*), ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1 (*weil-restriction-base-change*).

Prove `ModuliDescent.finiteQuotientComparison`. Let `R⇉U` be an equivalence relation of schemes in ModularCurves §0C’s affine or invariant-affine-cover effective finite locally free quotient domain. Let `q:U→Q_MC` be its supplied quotient, with q faithfully flat locally of finite presentation and `R≅U×_{Q_MC}U`. The fppf quotient sheaf `U/R` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.5) is canonically `h_{Q_MC}`, with the same map from U. This is natural for maps of effective relations and commutes with base changes for which the construction of ModularCurves §0C applies. When s,t are also etale this identifies the étale-relation quotient of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.6. For a free finite constant group action with the required invariant affine cover it identifies the torsor quotient. No such sheaf-quotient comparison is asserted for actions with stabilizers.

Here the relation is effective, with its actual kernel-pair identification and fppf cover q, as supplied by ModularCurves §0C; General finite locally free relations need not be etale. The comparison uses the fppf quotient sheaf and the scheme of ModularCurves §0C, not the etale quotient theorem alone.

(ModularCurves §0C, finite quotients and torsors; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces.pdf), §9, Lemma 9.1 (0262), p.12, presentation by a quotient sheaf; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/groupoids.pdf), §20, Definition 20.1 (02VG), p.39; Lemma 20.3 `(03C5)`, pp.39–40).

For the proof, the fppf cover q is locally surjective as a sheaf map and its kernel pair is `h_R`. Thus `h_Q` is the coequalizer sheaf of `h_R⇉h_U`; then use the universal property of the quotient sheaf (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.5) to obtain the unique isomorphism preserving q; then morphisms of relations and allowed base changes commute by this uniqueness; on the etale subdomain use the same coequalizer to identify the etale quotient.

*Needs:* ModularCurves §0C, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.5, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.6.

Prove `ModuliDescent.coherentPresentationDescent`. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space, `U→X` an etale surjective scheme presentation and `R=U×_X U` with source and target s,t. Restriction induces an equivalence between coherent `O_X`-modules and pairs consisting of a coherent module M on U and an isomorphism `t* M≅s* M` satisfying the diagonal and triple-overlap equations. Morphisms are all module maps commuting with this isomorphism, including zero and noninvertible maps. The equivalence is exact, independent of the presentation, and natural under base changes `X′→X` for which `X′` is locally Noetherian. Invertible modules give the rank-one restriction of the specified finite locally free equivalence.
