Here X is locally Noetherian in the sense that one, hence every, etale scheme atlas is locally Noetherian; Coherent means the existing small-etale-site module notion; on this class it equals quasi-coherent finite type and quasi-coherent finite presentation; No claim of coherence under arbitrary change to a non-Noetherian target is made. Finite presentation, not coherent terminology, is the invariant used there.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), §4, Proposition 4.1 (04W8), pp.3–4; §6, Lemmas 6.2–6.4 (060V–060X), pp.5–6; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-cohomology.pdf), §12, Lemmas 12.2–12.3 (07UB, 07UC), p.19).

For the proof, use the equivalence between QCoh(X) and modules on the étale presentation (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11), and the specified full fpqc descent comparison; do not rebuild quasi-coherent descent. Use the fpqc cover and `U×_X X_i` in step 4 of 04W8, as required by that proof; an arbitrary fpqc cover is retained; then apply 07UB on the locally Noetherian charts. Finite presentation descends by the specified finite-presentation theorem, so the equivalence restricts to coherent objects in both directions; then etale pullback is exact, and the coherent category is abelian (07UC). The equivalence therefore preserves kernels and cokernels; then use a common refinement of two presentations; full faithfulness fixes its natural comparisons and the triple-refinement coherence. Base change preserves finite presentation, and 07UB identifies coherence when the new space is locally Noetherian.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.10, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11, `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`, `finitePresentationModuleDescent`, `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`.

Prove `ModuliDescent.polarizedDescentComparison`. For an fppf cover `S′→S` of schemes, let `Y′→S′` be proper finitely presented with a relatively ample invertible sheaf `L′`. Give an isomorphism of `Y′` over `S′×_S S′` satisfying the identity and triple cocycle, and a specified lift identifying the two pullbacks of `L′` satisfying its own identity and triple cocycle. Then `(Y′,L′)` descends to a pair `(Y,L)` over S, Y proper and finitely presented over S with L relatively ample, with an identification of the pullback pair with `(Y′,L′)`; this general-base descent is proved here. On the domain of the polarized projective relative curves of ModularCurves §0E or the étale-polarized schemes of StableReduction Layer 2, their supplied descended pair is uniquely isomorphic to this pair by an isomorphism whose pullback is the specified identity. These comparisons preserve polarized morphisms and sections, and satisfy refinement and arbitrary-base-change coherence. The line-bundle cocycle is data, not inferred from invariance of an isomorphism class of `L′`.

Here the base cover is fppf; all object and line-bundle cocycle identifications are supplied explicitly; The pair is proper finitely presented and relatively polarized. Projectivity is asserted in the local-on-base convention of StableReduction Layer 2, with relatively ample L and properness; For the StableReduction comparison the cover is étale; for the ModularCurves comparison the object is a relative curve in the class of ModularCurves §0E.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), §13, Lemma 13.1 (0D3C), pp.21–22; §23, Lemma 23.1 (0ADT), pp.35–36; ModularCurves §0E, effective descent of polarized projective relative curves; StableReduction Layer 2, effective etale descent of polarized schemes).

For the proof, descend the underlying algebraic space by SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2 and the invertible module by `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent` and `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`, using the specified lift of the object cocycle to `L′`; then fpqc locality of relative ampleness (0D3C) makes the descended space a scheme over S; properness and finite presentation descend independently. Then full faithfulness of object and module descent gives the unique comparison between any two descended pairs with the given local identity; it preserves the polarization map and all compatible morphisms and sections; then pull back the local identity under refinement or base change. Uniqueness identifies the resulting comparison with the directly constructed one, giving unit and composition coherence.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, ModularCurves §0E, StableReduction Layer 2.

Prove `ModuliDescent.finiteModuliDescentComparison`. For an fppf cover `S′→S` and a finite locally free group scheme `G′/S′` with descent datum by group isomorphisms, take the descended finite locally free group `G/S` of ModularCurves §0E. If one also supplies a compatible finite locally free closed subgroup `H′→G′`, a compatible torsor under `G′`, and a finite tuple of compatible sections and morphisms of these objects satisfying specified equations, compare the simultaneous descent of ModularCurves §0E with descent of algebraic spaces and of quasi-coherent modules (SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.2, 1.11). There is a unique isomorphism of the descended tuples preserving the specified local identifications, the group operations, subgroup immersion, torsor action, sections and all the equations. It commutes coherently with arbitrary base change and with forgetting any of the extra data. This stage supplies the comparison, not a second construction of any finite flat group or level-structure moduli scheme.

Here Every scheme declared finite locally free is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation over its base; Descent isomorphisms commute with the multiplication, identity, inverse and all supplied structure maps; the triple cocycle is part of the datum; A torsor is an fppf torsor in the sense of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.15; a subgroup includes its actual closed immersion. No abelian dual or polarizing isogeny is introduced here.

(ModularCurves §0E, descent of finite locally free schemes, groups, torsors, subgroups and level structures; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), §4, Proposition 4.1 `(04W8)`, pp.3–4; §6, Lemma 6.4 `(060X)`, p.6; §23, Lemma 23.1 (0ADT), pp.35–36).

For the proof, use ModularCurves §0E for the group, subgroup, torsor and section descent. View these schemes through the fully faithful embedding of schemes into algebraic spaces (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.4); then the descended spaces of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2 agree with these schemes by full faithfulness of descent. Transport the operations and maps through the unique isomorphisms; then check every equation on the fppf cover, where the comparison is the identity; faithfulness reflects it globally. For subgroup properties and finite local freeness use their supplied descent interfaces; then the same local-identity characterization proves compatibility with forgetting data and arbitrary base change.

*Needs:* ModularCurves §0E, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2, `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`.

### Examples

For multiplication by 2 on Z, pulling back the inclusion `2Z→Z` to `Z/2` makes the map zero; arbitrary base change is not an effective descent equivalence. Faithfully flat extension of scalars retains every module map. For an empty finite étale source relative Hom is the base, and for a split two-point source it is the square of the target over the base.

### Dependencies

Tau Ceti's quasi-coherent pullback and tilde comparison (`TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentSheaf.pullback`, `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.tildeFunctorCompPullbackIso`); Mathlib module descent and comonadicity; SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 (quasi-coherent descent), §§1.2–1.11 (algebraic spaces, their étale sites and quasi-coherent modules) and §1.17 (Artin's bootstrap); ModularCurves §§0C, 0E and 0F; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a.1.

## Layer 4: gerbes, bands and profinite stages

### 4.1 Gerbes and relative locality

Throughout this topic, A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres..

Define `IsGerbe`. For `F : C`ᵒᵖ → Cat a pseudofunctor, IsGerbe(F,J) extends the IsStack predicate, asserts every fibre arrow invertible, and asserts local nonemptiness and local isomorphism of every pair of objects. Formulate locality by covering sieves: for each U choose `R∈J(U)` with a fibre object over every arrow `V→U` in R.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Definition 8.11.1; [Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, p.122).

The API gives `IsGerbe.toIsStack`: A gerbe is an instance of the `F.IsStack J`; `IsGerbe.isIso_hom`: Every morphism in every fibre is invertible; the IsStack predicate alone does not impose this groupoid condition; `IsGerbe.locallyNonempty`: Each U has a J-covering sieve on which the fibre categories are nonempty; `IsGerbe.locallyIsomorphic`: Each pair of fibre objects becomes isomorphic on a J-covering sieve; `IsGerbe.equivalence_iff`: A pseudonatural equivalence over C preserves and reflects IsGerbe; `GerbeSampleAPI.classifyingNeutral`: For an abelian sheaf A on the chosen site with terminal object S, BA is a neutral A-gerbe and its class in derived `H2(S,A)` is zero; `GerbeSampleAPI.rootClass`: For algebraically closed k, `n>1` invertible in k, the nth-root gerbe of `O(1)` on `P1_k` has derived Kummer class `δ([O(1)])` and has no global object; `GerbeSampleAPI.localNotNeutral`: For algebraically closed k and `n≥2` invertible in k, `RootGerbe_n(O(1))` is locally nonempty but not neutral; an nth root would have degree `1/n`; `GerbeSampleAPI.derivedClassification`: For a fixed abelian sheaf A on the chosen site with terminal object and the stated derived-H1 and injective-neutralization inputs, band-preserving equivalence classes of A-gerbes correspond to derived `H2(A)`; the zero class is exactly the neutral class; `GerbeSampleAPI.pullbackClass`: For the geometric morphism and exact inverse-image/cohomology comparison in `classSitePullback`, pullback carries A-bandings to `f* A`-bandings and carries the gerbe class to its change-of-site pullback class; `GerbeSampleAPI.neutralSelfEquivalences`: For a neutral A-gerbe with a chosen neutralization, band-preserving self-equivalences and invertible modifications form a groupoid equivalent to the groupoid of A-torsors and equivariant isomorphisms; composition corresponds to contracted product; `GerbeSampleAPI.compatibleLimit`: For the specified small cofiltered finite-gerbe diagram and coherent presentation, an object of its fpqc 2-limit over T consists of finite-stage objects and compatible transition isomorphisms with unit/composition laws; arrows are compatible families, not only isomorphism classes; `GerbeSampleAPI.profiniteNotFinitePresentation`: Over a field k, the fpqc classifying gerbe of `G=lim_m (Z/m!Z)_k` is a profinite étale gerbe but not an algebraic stack of finite presentation: its trivial-object stabilizer G is not of finite type.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsPrestack`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeTests.classifying`: The classifying stack BA of any sheaf of groups (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21) is a gerbe.
- `GerbeTests.twoComponents`: On the one-point site with only the maximal cover, the discrete groupoid on two objects is a stack but not a gerbe.
- `GerbeTests.rootNotNeutral`: For algebraically closed k and `n>1` invertible in k, the nth-root gerbe of `O(1)` on P1 is a gerbe with no global object.
- `GerbeSampleTests.classifyingNeutral`: For an abelian sheaf A on the chosen site with terminal object S, BA is a neutral A-gerbe and its class in derived `H2(S,A)` is zero.
- `GerbeSampleTests.rootClass`: For algebraically closed k, `n>1` invertible in k, the nth-root gerbe of `O(1)` on `P1_k` has derived Kummer class `δ([O(1)])` and has no global object.
- `GerbeSampleTests.derivedClassification`: For a fixed abelian sheaf A on the chosen site with terminal object and the stated derived-H1 and injective-neutralization inputs, band-preserving equivalence classes of A-gerbes correspond to derived `H2(A)`; the zero class is exactly the neutral class.
- `GerbeSampleTests.pullbackClass`: For the geometric morphism and exact inverse-image/cohomology comparison in `classSitePullback`, pullback carries A-bandings to `f* A`-bandings and carries the gerbe class to its change-of-site pullback class.
- `GerbeSampleTests.neutralSelfEquivalences`: For a neutral A-gerbe with a chosen neutralization, band-preserving self-equivalences and invertible modifications form a groupoid equivalent to the groupoid of A-torsors and equivariant isomorphisms; composition corresponds to contracted product.
- `GerbeSampleTests.compatibleLimit`: For the specified small cofiltered finite-gerbe diagram and coherent presentation, an object of its fpqc 2-limit over T consists of finite-stage objects and compatible transition isomorphisms with unit/composition laws; arrows are compatible families, not only isomorphism classes.
- `GerbeSampleTests.profiniteNotFinitePresentation`: Over a field k, the fpqc classifying gerbe of `G=lim_m (Z/m!Z)_k` is a profinite étale gerbe but not an algebraic stack of finite presentation: its trivial-object stabilizer G is not of finite type.

Prove `IsGerbe.equivalence_iff`. If `E:F≃G` is an equivalence over `(C,J)`, IsGerbe(F,J) iff IsGerbe(G,J).

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.2).

For the proof, transport `Pseudofunctor.IsStack` along the equivalence; then apply fibre equivalences to local objects and local isomorphisms in both directions.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Define `relativeGerbe`. For a morphism `F:X→Y` of stacks in groupoids, IsRelativeGerbe(F) means objects of Y lift locally up to isomorphism and, for x,`x′` over U, every isomorphism `F(x)→F(x′)` locally lifts to `x→x′`. Equivalently, after replacing X by the equivalent iso-comma stack over Y, its projection is a gerbe on the site of Y. Mere local essential surjectivity is insufficient.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.3 and Definition 8.11.4).

The API gives `IsRelativeGerbe.localLift`: Every target object admits local lifts up to isomorphism; `IsRelativeGerbe.isom_epi`: Every induced map of Isom sheaves is locally surjective; `IsRelativeGerbe.rectification_iff`: The iso-comma projection is a gerbe iff the two local lifting conditions hold.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21.

**Checks.**

- `RelativeGerbeTests.identity`: The identity of any stack is a relative gerbe.
- `RelativeGerbeTests.classifying`: For the trivial action, `[S/G]→S` is a relative gerbe for a sheaf of groups G.
- `RelativeGerbeTests.subgroup`: On an algebraically closed field, BH→BG for a proper subgroup `H<G` of finite constant groups is locally essentially surjective but not a relative gerbe.

Prove `relativePullback`. In a 2-cartesian square `X′→X` over `Y′→Y`, if `X→Y` is a relative gerbe, so is `X′→Y′`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.5).

For the proof, write objects as triples `(y′,x,α)`; then lift `y′` locally by lifting its image in Y; retain α; then lift a target isomorphism through the Isom-sheaf epimorphism for `X→Y`.

*Needs:* `relativeGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21.

Prove `relativeComposition`. The composite of two relative gerbe morphisms is a relative gerbe.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.6).

For the proof, lift objects twice and compose covering sieves; then lift isomorphisms twice and refine the two covers by transitivity of J.

*Needs:* `relativeGerbe`.

Prove `relativeDescent`. If `Y′→Y` is locally essentially surjective and `X×Y Y′→Y′` is a relative gerbe, then `X→Y` is a relative gerbe.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.7).

For the proof, first lift a target object to `Y′` and then to the relative gerbe; then for a target isomorphism choose one local `Y′` object, form the two iso-comma objects, and lift its identity.

*Needs:* `relativeGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21.

### 4.2 Bandings and band-preserving equivalences

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres.

Define `AbelianBanding`. For an abelian sheaf A on `(C,J)` and a gerbe F, an A-banding consists of group isomorphisms `b(U,x):A(U)`→AutF(U)(x) for all U and x, compatible with restriction along every `V→U` and conjugation along every isomorphism `x→y`. Equivalently these define isomorphisms `A|U≅Aut(x)` of sheaves on `C/U` compatible with isomorphisms and cartesian pullbacks.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1 and Remark 31.2, p.122; [Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), Definition 2.6(ii), p.515).

The API gives `AbelianBanding.autEquiv`: For every U,x there is `A(U)≃Aut(x)` as groups; `AbelianBanding.pullback`: mapAut of restriction sends `b(U,x)(a)` to `b(V,x|V)(a|V)`; `AbelianBanding.conjugation`: Conjugation by `x≅y` sends `b(U,x)(a)` to `b(U,y)(a)`; `AbelianBanding.ext`: Two bandings are equal if their sectionwise automorphism equivalences agree for every U,x,a.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.sheafHom`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut`.

**Checks.**

- `BandMorphismTests.nonidentity`: a band-preserving transformation sends the band automorphism of a nonidentity coefficient to the band automorphism of the same coefficient, so it stays nonidentity.
- `BandingTests.zero`: If `A(U)` is trivial, an A-banding makes every `Aut(x)` trivial.
- `BandingTests.conjugation`: Changing a local trivialization by an object isomorphism leaves the identified element of A unchanged.
- `BandingTests.nonabelian`: The constant S3 automorphism group cannot have a fixed-sheaf banding satisfying conjugation compatibility with every automorphism.

Prove `banded_aut_commute`. For an A-banded gerbe every `Aut(x)` is commutative; equivalently `b(a)b(a′)=b(a′)b(a)`.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Remark 31.2, p.122).

For the proof, transport commutativity through b; alternatively specialize conjugation compatibility to `y=x` and arbitrary object automorphisms.

*Needs:* `AbelianBanding`.

Prove `banding_iso_independent`. In any category D, if `Aut(x)` is commutative and e,`e′:x≅y` are actual isomorphisms, the group equivalences `Aut.autMulEquivOfIso(e)` and `Aut.autMulEquivOfIso(e′)` are equal. Applied in every restricted fibre of an abelian-inertia gerbe, these equalities identify its automorphism sheaves independently of the chosen object isomorphism. No band is chosen.

Here D is a category in fixed object and morphism universes; x,y are its objects, e,`e′` are actual isomorphisms `x≅y`, and `a*b=b*a` for every a,b in `Aut(x)`; The automorphism-sheaf specialization uses a gerbe with abelian inertia on a specified site, applying the categorical statement after every base restriction. Gerbe, groupoid and site assumptions are not needed for the categorical lemma itself.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8, first part).

The API gives `GerbeAutTransport.conjugation_independent`: In any category, commutativity of `Aut(x)` makes conjugation through any two x-to-y isomorphisms equal; `GerbeAutTransport.map_conjugation`: A functor maps conjugation through e to conjugation through its actual mapIso(e); `GerbeAutTransport.map_conjugation_hom`: On hom arrows the preceding functoriality equation is the exact map of `e.inv` followed by `a.hom` followed by `e.hom`.

For the proof, in the Aut group the ratio of e and `e′` is an automorphism of x; its inner conjugation fixes every a by the stated commutativity; then unfold the conjugation equivalence and apply isomorphism cancellation and function extensionality. Retain Mathlib’s reversed multiplication/composition convention; then apply this categorical identity in each restriction fibre for the gerbe sheaf corollary. It does not prove descent, arbitrary-base band gluing or evaluation surjectivity; those are separate targets.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso`.

Define `intrinsicAbelianBand`. If every automorphism sheaf of a gerbe is abelian, glue these sheaves through their choice-independent local conjugation maps to an abelian sheaf A on C with an A-banding of the gerbe. The intrinsic sheaf is canonical up to unique compatible sheaf isomorphism; an identification with a preselected A remains additional data.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8).

The API gives `IntrinsicBand.autIso`: The intrinsic band restricted to U is `Aut(x)` for every x over U; `IntrinsicBand.pullback`: Restricting the intrinsic band to V gives the intrinsic band of the restricted gerbe; `IntrinsicBand.unique`: Compatible automorphism-sheaf identifications determine the intrinsic band up to unique isomorphism.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, `banding_iso_independent`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `IntrinsicBandTests.BA`: The intrinsic band of BA for abelian A is A.
- `IntrinsicBandTests.trivial`: The intrinsic band of a terminal groupoid-valued stack is the zero abelian sheaf.
- `IntrinsicBandTests.unfixed`: An isomorphism of the intrinsic band with A does not identify two A-bandings differing by a nontrivial automorphism of A as band-preserving objects.

Define `BandPreserving`. For A-banded gerbes (F,bF),(G,bG), a band-preserving morphism is a StrongTrans `η:F→G` such that ηU.mapAut(bF(U,x)`(a)`)=bG(U,ηU(x))`(a)` for all U,x,a. Its morphisms are the modifications; their components are isomorphisms since G has groupoid fibres. Band preservation is a property of η, not another general natural-transformation carrier.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, p.122; [Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1, p.515).

The API gives `BandPreserving.map_band`: The component mapAut commutes with the two chosen band equivalences; `BandPreserving.id`: The identity transformation is band-preserving; `BandPreserving.comp`: Composites of band-preserving transformations preserve the same fixed band; `BandPreserving.modificationGroupoid`: Compatible modifications are morphisms of a groupoid, with componentwise inverse.

*Needs:* `AbelianBanding`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.Modification`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut`.

**Checks.**

- `BandMorphismTests.identity`: The identity of BA preserves its canonical band.
- `BandMorphismTests.inversion`: For the constant band `Z/3Z`, the self-equivalence induced by `a↦−a` preserves the underlying gerbe but does not preserve the fixed band.
- `BandMorphismTests.modifications`: For BA over an algebraically closed point and A constant `Z/3Z`, the identity band-preserving equivalence has three automorphisms as a transformation, not one.

Define `isomTorsor`. For x,y over U in an A-banded gerbe, the existing sheafHom(x,y) is the sheaf `Isom(x,y)`, since every arrow is invertible. It is an `A|U`-torsor with `p·a=b_y(a)∘p`. In the abelian setting this also equals `p∘b_x(a)`. It is locally nonempty and the torsor comparison `Isom(x,y)×A|U→Isom(x,y)×Isom(x,y)`, `(p,a)↦(p,p·a)`, is an isomorphism of sheaves.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.3 and Remark 31.5, pp.122–123).

The API gives `Gerbe.isomTorsor`: The Hom sheaf of x,y carries the indicated `A|U`-torsor structure; `Gerbe.isomTorsor_action`: `p·a` is postcomposition with `b_y(a)`, also precomposition with `b_x(a)`; `Gerbe.isomTorsor_pullback`: Restriction to V identifies this torsor with `Isom(x|V,y|V)`, respecting the action.

*Needs:* `AbelianBanding`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.sheafHom`, `BandedIsom.principalSheafIso`, `BandedIsom.hom_localNonempty`.

**Checks.**

- `IsomTorsorTests.self`: `Isom(x,x)` is the trivial `A|U`-torsor through the band, with identity corresponding to zero.
- `IsomTorsorTests.emptySections`: A nontrivial A-torsor P in BA need not have `Isom(A,P)(U)` nonempty, although the Isom sheaf is a torsor.
- `IsomTorsorTests.composition`: Composing `p·a` with an isomorphism `y→z` gives the transported isomorphism acted on by the same a.

Prove `band_morphism_full_faithful`. A band-preserving morphism of A-gerbes induces isomorphisms of their Isom sheaves; hence each fibre functor is fully faithful.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.3, full-faithfulness proof, p.122).

For the proof, in order: (1) the StrongTrans naturality isomorphisms, transported to the target pullbacks `G(f)(η_U x)` and `G(f)(η_U y)` on every deeper slice, define a morphism of sheaves `Isom_F(x,y)→Isom_G(ηx,ηy)` (`GerbeMorphismPullback.homSheafIso`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.preimageIso_restrict`); (2) band preservation makes it A-equivariant, and it is injective by `BandedMorphism.faithful`; (3) on a cover where `Isom_F(x,y)` has a section it is a map of trivial A-torsors given by translation, hence a local bijection (`BandedMorphism.locallyIsomEquiv`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.locallyIsomEquiv`), so it is an isomorphism of sheaves; (4) evaluating its inverse on sections over U gives fullness of `η_U` (`BandedMorphism.full`). The version with independently sized coefficient universes is transported through `universeNormalizedGerbe`.

*Needs:* `BandPreserving`, `isomTorsor`, `BandedMorphism.faithful`, `BandedMorphism.locallyIsomEquiv`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.locallyIsomEquiv`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.preimageIso_restrict`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.homSheafIso`, `BandedMorphism.full`.

Prove `band_morphism_essential_surjective`. A band-preserving morphism `η:F→G` between A-gerbes is essentially surjective on every fibre.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.3, essential-surjectivity proof, pp.122–123).

For the proof, for `z∈G(U)` locally choose `y∈F` and an isomorphism `η(y)≅z`; then full faithfulness uniquely lifts the descent isomorphisms of z to those of y and reflects their cocycle condition; then effective descent in F gives an object over U; morphism descent in G gives its image isomorphism to z; then form the local-image covering sieve, reflect the DescentData equations through full faithfulness, descend the source object, and descend its image isomorphism. The normalized coefficient version transports through universeNormalizedGerbe.

*Needs:* `BandPreserving`, `band_morphism_full_faithful`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.isEquivalence_toDescentData`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.global_preimage`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentEssSurj`.

Prove `band_morphism_equivalence`. Every band-preserving morphism of A-gerbes is a pseudonatural equivalence over the site, with a band-preserving inverse. For every site object U the component functor `η_U` is an equivalence of fibre categories. The pseudonatural inverse is `CoherentInverse.inverse` (§4.21), with band preservation given by `GerbeBandEquivalence.inverse_preserving`.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.3).

For the proof, the fixed-band Hom-sheaf isomorphism proves actual fibrewise full faithfulness; object descent proves actual essential surjectivity. The CoherentInverse construction of §4.21 assembles the chosen component inverses into a StrongTrans, its unit and counit modifications and both triangle identities. Restriction coherence is obtained by lifting the naturality squares through full faithfulness. The inverse-band equations show that this inverse preserves the band, independently of the chosen comparisons.

*Needs:* `band_morphism_full_faithful`, `band_morphism_essential_surjective`, `BandPreserving`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentIsEquivalence`, `GerbeBandEquivalence.inverse_preserving`, `GerbeBandEquivalence.modificationIso_iff`, `GerbeBandEquivalence.unit_band`, `GerbeBandEquivalence.counit_band`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

### 4.3 Neutralizations and derived classification

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: A fixed arbitrary site `(C,J)` and its terminal sheaf, with compatible site, stack and coefficient universes after the normalization described in §4.20; groupoid-valued stacks and an actual abelian sheaf A. Enough injectives, Ext and connecting maps are Mathlib's, with the torsor comparison of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3. The slice restriction, injective torsor/gerbe neutrality and band-change constructions are proved in §4.20. A terminal object of C is not required.

Define `classifyingAbelianGerbe`. For an abelian sheaf A, specialize the groupoid quotient stack of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21 to BA, the stack of A-torsors with equivariant isomorphisms. Identify `Aut(P)` with `A|U` through translations, which is independent of a local trivialization since A is commutative. This supplies its canonical band. The trivial torsor provides a global object over a terminal site object S.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.4, p.123; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06PD), Lemma 78.27.2).

The API gives `ClassifyingGerbe.band`: BA carries the canonical A-banding; `ClassifyingGerbe.trivial`: The trivial A-torsor is a global object of BA; `ClassifyingGerbe.autIso`: `Aut(P)≅A|U` as sheaves, compatible with pullbacks and conjugation.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, `AbelianBanding`.

**Checks.**

- `ClassifyingGerbeTests.zero`: B0 is equivalent to the terminal groupoid-valued stack.
- `ClassifyingGerbeTests.point`: For algebraically closed k and A constant `Z/3Z`, BA(k) has one isomorphism class with automorphism group `Z/3Z`.
- `ClassifyingGerbeTests.inertia`: BA for nonzero A is not equivalent to the sheaf of its isomorphism classes.

Define `Neutralization`. For any site object S and `Cat`-valued pseudofunctor F, this carrier records an object `x∈F(S)`. For an A-gerbe its morphisms are the fibre isomorphisms. When S is a chosen terminal object, write `IsNeutral F S hS` for nonemptiness of this groupoid, retaining the terminal-object witness hS. A neutralization over a terminal object induces an equivalence F≃BA preserving the band. Distinct neutralizations need not be uniquely isomorphic.

Here the carrier permits any S; the neutrality assertion and the equivalence with BA require a fixed terminal object S and an A-banded gerbe F.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Remark 31.5, p.123).

The API gives `Neutralization.obj`: A neutralization gives an object of `F(S)`; `Neutralization.isNeutral`: For a specified terminal object S, with its terminal-object witness retained, F is neutral iff `F(S)` is nonempty, equivalently iff its groupoid of neutralizations is nonempty. A section over an arbitrary nonterminal site object asserts only neutrality on its slice; `Neutralization.pullback`: A neutralization restricts to a neutralization on every slice site.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, `AbelianBanding`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal`.

**Checks.**

- `NeutralizationTests.BA`: The trivial A-torsor neutralizes BA.
- `NeutralizationTests.root`: The nth-root gerbe of `O(1)` on P1 has no neutralization for `n>1` invertible in the algebraically closed ground field.
- `NeutralizationTests.nonterminal`: on the two-object discrete site with the minimal topology
  and the constant `B(C₃)` diagram, `Neutralization F (Discrete.mk true)` is nonempty, but
  neither site object has an `IsTerminal` witness. This fibre object alone does not supply
  the witness required by `IsNeutral`; neutrality over the terminal sheaf is a separate condition.

Prove `neutralizationEquivalence`. For `x∈F(S)`, the functor `y↦Isom(x|U,y)` is a band-preserving equivalence F≃BA; its quasi-inverse twists x by the A-torsor, with descent.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres; The site has a chosen terminal object S; the neutralization x is an object of `F(S)`.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Remark 31.5, p.123).

For the proof, the Isom construction is pseudonatural and respects the chosen band; then apply the band-morphism-equivalence theorem; then describe the inverse by trivializing the torsor locally and descending x with its torsor transition automorphisms.

*Needs:* `Neutralization`, `isomTorsor`, `classifyingAbelianGerbe`, `band_morphism_equivalence`.

Prove `neutralSelfEquivalences`. For an A-gerbe with a neutralization x, its groupoid of band-preserving self-equivalences is equivalent to the groupoid of A-torsors on the base. A torsor P acts on BA by `Q↦Q⊗A P`. An equivariant isomorphism `P≅P′` corresponds to an invertible modification. Composition corresponds to contracted product, and the identity to the trivial torsor.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres; The site has a chosen terminal object S; the neutralization x is an object of `F(S)`.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1, p.515; [Lawrence Breen](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__225__1_0.pdf), Proposition 2.14, p.56).

For the proof, in order: (1) conjugate along the neutralization equivalence F≃BA (`neutralizationEquivalence`), so that it suffices to treat BA; (2) a band-preserving self-equivalence Φ of BA determines the A-torsor `P_Φ=Φ(A)`, and on a cover trivializing a torsor Q the comparison `Φ(Q)≅Q×ᴬP_Φ` is independent of the trivialization because Φ preserves the band, and is compatible with restriction (`BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_restriction`); (3) for two such Φ,Ψ the fibre Hom sheaf of modifications `Φ⇒Ψ` (`BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheafFunctor`) is an A-torsor, locally nonempty with a freely transitive action compatible with restriction (`BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheaf_locallyNonempty`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_freeTransitive`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_restriction`); (4) evaluation at A identifies it, equivariantly and naturally in modifications, with the Isom sheaf of torsors `P_Φ≅P_Ψ`, using the self-gerbe transport, its base change and endpoint comparisons (`BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor_parallel`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_transport`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeNatIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeTransport_square`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportIso_self`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointBaseChange_square`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportNatIso`); taking global sections gives full faithfulness of `Φ↦P_Φ` on the groupoid `BandedMorphism.groupoid`; (5) every torsor P arises from the band-preserving self-equivalence `Q↦Q`×ᴬP, giving essential surjectivity; `(6) Φ∘Ψ` goes to `P_Ψ×ᴬP_Φ` and the identity to the trivial torsor, and the inverse equivalence with its unit and counit is assembled by `CoherentInverse` (§4.21).

*Needs:* `neutralizationEquivalence`, `BandPreserving`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, `BandedMorphism.groupoid`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_restriction`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheafFunctor`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheaf_locallyNonempty`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_freeTransitive`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_restriction`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomTransportIsoEquiv_modification`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor_parallel`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_transport`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeNatIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeTransport_square`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportIso_self`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointBaseChange_square`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportNatIso`.

Define `changeBand`. For a homomorphism `u:A→B` and an A-gerbe F, extend each `Isom(x,y)` by the contracted product with B; glue composition using the abelian band equation, then apply the stackification of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18. The resulting `u_*F` is a B-gerbe with a u-compatible morphism `F→u_*F`. It is universal for u-compatible morphisms from F to B-gerbes, at the level of morphism groupoids.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Theorem 31.7, reverse construction, p.126; [James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9).

The API gives `Gerbe.changeBand`: Produces the B-gerbe `u_*F` and its u-compatible map; `Gerbe.changeBand_lift`: Composition with `F→u_*F` is an equivalence on groupoids of band-compatible morphisms; `Gerbe.changeBand_comp`: `v_*(u_*F)≃(v∘u)_*F` coherently, and `id_*F≃F`.

*Needs:* `isomTorsor`, `BandPreserving`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

**Checks.**

- `ChangeBandTests.identity`: Extension along `id_A` recovers F preserving its band.
- `ChangeBandTests.BA`: Extension sends BA to BB with the induced map on torsors.
- `ChangeBandTests.zero`: Extension to the zero band gives a gerbe equivalent to the terminal stack.

Define `liftingGerbe`. For a short exact sequence `0→A→B→D→0` of abelian sheaves and a D-torsor P, Lift(P)`(U)` is the groupoid of pairs `(Q,α)`, where Q is a B|U-torsor and `α:Q×B D≅P|U` is an equivariant isomorphism. Arrows are B-torsor isomorphisms commuting with α. This is an A-gerbe: the stack is a 2-fibre product of the torsor stacks of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.15; local triviality of P gives local objects; the kernel A gives its band. The sheaf epimorphism `B→D`, not surjectivity on all section groups, supplies local isomorphisms.

Here A short exact sequence in the category of abelian sheaves on the specified site; P is a D-torsor, with arrows retained.

([James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2, p.9; [Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Remark 31.8, p.127).

The API gives `LiftingGerbe.obj`: A B-torsor Q and an isomorphism `Q×B D≅P` give an object; `LiftingGerbe.autIso`: Automorphisms of `(Q,α)` form the sheaf A, through the kernel inclusion; `LiftingGerbe.neutral_iff`: Lift(P) is neutral iff P is the pushforward of a B-torsor; `LiftingGerbe.pullback`: Restriction of Lift(P) is equivalent to the lifting gerbe of the restricted exact sequence and torsor.

*Needs:* `classifyingAbelianGerbe`, `relativeGerbe`, `AbelianBanding`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21.

**Checks.**

- `LiftingGerbeTests.trivial`: Lift of the trivial D-torsor is a neutral A-gerbe.
- `LiftingGerbeTests.surjectiveSheaf`: The Kummer sequence with n invertible is locally exact even when units are not all nth powers in the global section ring.
- `LiftingGerbeTests.zeroKernel`: If `A=0`, a lifting gerbe of P is equivalent to the terminal stack because `B→D` is an isomorphism.

Prove `injectiveBoundaryBijection`. For `0→A→I→D→0` short exact with I injective, the connecting map `δ:H1(D)→H2(A)` is an isomorphism of abelian groups. This is derived `Sheaf.H`, not Čech H2.

Here HasSheafify and HasExt for the chosen abelian-sheaf category; I is injective and the sequence is short exact.

([James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9, proof of (i)).

For the proof, positive-degree Ext into I vanishes by the injective lemma; then exactness at `H1(D)` gives injectivity of δ and exactness at `H2(A)` gives surjectivity.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.eq_zero_of_injective`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.δ`, Tau Ceti `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.exact_map_δ`, Tau Ceti `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.exact_δ_map`.

Define `torsorRepresentativeOfClass`. On the chosen site with terminal object S and the stated cohomology and torsor-comparison inputs, choose a monomorphism `A→I` into an injective abelian sheaf and let D be its cokernel. For `α∈H2(A)`, take the inverse dimension-shift class in `H1(D)`, choose a D-torsor representing it, and construct Lift(P). This constructs an A-gerbe for α, with the choice of P irrelevant up to band-preserving equivalence. Enough injectives, cokernel exactness and the derived-H1 torsor comparison are inputs, not assumptions that every section of D lifts globally.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes, a chosen terminal object S and its `Limits.IsTerminal` witness; all stacks have groupoid fibres; HasSheafify and HasExt for the chosen abelian-sheaf category, with coefficient/site universes compatible with the connecting maps `Sheaf.H.δ`; Enough injectives in the abelian sheaf category, short exactness of cokernels, and the natural comparison of torsors with derived H1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3).

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Theorem 31.7, p.126; [James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9).

The API gives `Gerbe.ofH2`: A derived H2 class produces an A-gerbe through an injective embedding and a lifting torsor; `Gerbe.ofH2_equiv`: Isomorphic representative D-torsors give equivalent A-gerbes; `Gerbe.ofH2_zero`: The zero class produces a gerbe equivalent to BA.

*Needs:* `injectiveBoundaryBijection`, `liftingGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `H2RepresentativeTests.zero`: Choose P the trivial D-torsor for `α=0`; its trivial B-lift neutralizes Lift(P).
- `H2RepresentativeTests.changeTorsor`: An isomorphism `P≅P′` induces an equivalence of lifting gerbes, respecting the chosen band.
- `H2RepresentativeTests.nonzero`: A nonzero Kummer boundary `δ(O(1))` on P1 cannot be represented by a neutral root gerbe.

Prove `injectiveGerbeNeutral`. On a site with terminal object S and the slice-site injective restriction and Čech-acyclicity inputs below, every gerbe banded by an injective abelian sheaf I has an object over S.

Here the site has a terminal object and the covers and slices stated above; I is injective in the abelian-sheaf category.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Lemma 31.6 and Theorem 31.7, pp.123–126; [James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9, (i″)).

For the proof, choose local objects on a covering of S; then the I-torsors of isomorphisms on pairwise overlaps are trivial because restriction of I is injective and derived H1 computes torsors; then choose overlap isomorphisms; their failure to satisfy the cocycle is a Čech 2-cocycle valued in I; then čech cohomology of injectives vanishes for this cover, so correct the chosen isomorphisms by a 1-cochain; then effective stack descent gives the global object.

*Needs:* `isomTorsor`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.isEquivalence_toDescentData`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.2.

Define `classOfGerbe`. On the chosen site with terminal object S and the stated injective-neutralization inputs, for an A-gerbe F, choose an injective embedding `A→I` and neutralize the I-gerbe obtained by extension of band. For a neutralizing object z, let Pz be the sheaf of isomorphism classes of pairs `(x,φ)` with `x∈F(U)` and `φ:z|U≅u_*x`; quotient arrows are isomorphisms in F commuting with φ. This is a D=I/A-torsor. Define class(F)=δ([Pz])∈`H2(A)`, with δ the connecting map and the contraction convention fixed above.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Theorem 31.7, reverse map, p.126).

The API gives `Gerbe.class`: The class is an element of the derived `H2(A)`; `Gerbe.class_equivalence`: A band-preserving gerbe equivalence leaves the class unchanged; `Gerbe.class_changeNeutralization`: Changing z changes Pz by an I-torsor pushforward, whose δ-image is zero.

*Needs:* `changeBand`, `injectiveGerbeNeutral`, `injectiveBoundaryBijection`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeClassTests.BA`: The canonical neutral object gives class(BA)=0.
- `GerbeClassTests.lift`: The class of Lift(P) is `δ([P])` for the fixed short exact sequence.
- `GerbeClassTests.banding`: Changing a chosen band by a coefficient automorphism applies that automorphism to the H2 class; band choices are not silently forgotten.

Prove `classChoiceIndependent`. The derived class of an A-gerbe is independent of the injective embedding `A→I` and the chosen neutralization of `u_*F`. This uses the same terminal site and cohomology, torsor-comparison and injective-neutralization hypotheses as `classOfGerbe`.

([Martin Olsson (lectures); Anton Geraschenko, Tony Várilly, Ed Carter, Anne Shiu and class contributors (notes)](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Theorem 31.7, p.126).

For the proof, changing a neutralization translates Pz by an I-torsor pushforward; exactness kills its boundary; then compare two injective embeddings in a common injective embedding and transport quotient torsors; then naturality of the connecting maps identifies the two derived classes.

*Needs:* `classOfGerbe`, `neutralSelfEquivalences`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.δ_naturality`.

Prove `h2Classification`. For a fixed abelian sheaf A on the chosen site with terminal object, band-preserving equivalence classes of A-gerbes are naturally in bijection with the derived `H2(A)`. The class and lifting-gerbe constructions are inverse. The zero class is precisely the neutral class. Equivalence fixes the A-banding.

([James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9, (i); [Lawrence Breen](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__225__1_0.pdf), (2.13.4), Proposition 2.14, pp.55–56).

For the proof, compare F with the lifting gerbe of its quotient torsor by a band-preserving map, hence an equivalence; then for a lifted gerbe, identify its quotient torsor and compute the boundary class; then use both identities to descend the maps to equivalence classes and establish bijectivity; then a lift of the trivial torsor supplies a neutralization; conversely a neutralization identifies F with BA.

*Needs:* `torsorRepresentativeOfClass`, `classOfGerbe`, `classChoiceIndependent`, `neutralizationEquivalence`, `band_morphism_equivalence`.

Define `rootGerbe`. For a scheme X, an invertible sheaf L and `n>0` invertible on X, `RootGerbe_n(L)(T)` consists of line bundles M on T and isomorphisms `φ:M⊗n≅L|T`, with arrows ρ satisfying `φ=ψ∘ρ⊗n`. It is the lifting gerbe for 1→μn→Gm→Gm→1 and the Gm-torsor of L, hence a μn-gerbe. No section of L is part of the data. The root stack of a line bundle with a section is a different construction owned by FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII:key/root-stacks.

Here X is a scheme; n is a positive integer invertible on X; L is an invertible sheaf, with no chosen section.

([Elena Andreini, Yunfeng Jiang and Hsian-Hua Tseng](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0907.2087v2), §2.2 Definition 2.2 and Remark 2.4, p.5; [Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.3 p.519).

The API gives `RootGerbe.obj`: A pair `(M,φ:M⊗n≅L)` gives an object; `RootGerbe.band`: An automorphism is scalar multiplication by a μn section; `RootGerbe.pullback`: `RootGerbe_n(L)×X T≃RootGerbe_n(L|T)`, respecting its band.

*Needs:* `liftingGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `RootGerbeTests.one`: For `n=1` the root gerbe is equivalent to X.
- `RootGerbeTests.trivialLine`: The root gerbe of `O_X` is equivalent to `B_Xμn` using its trivial nth root.
- `RootGerbeTests.noSection`: For `n>1` the root gerbe has μn inertia at every geometric point, whereas a divisor root stack has trivial inertia outside the divisor.

Prove `rootGerbeClass`. For X, L and n on the small étale site specified below, class(`RootGerbe_n(L)`)=`δ([L])` in derived `H2(Xét,μn)`, with δ the connecting map of the Kummer sequence and with the same sign convention as the lifting-gerbe construction.

Here X is a scheme, L an invertible sheaf on X, and n a positive integer invertible on X; Use the small étale site of X with terminal object X and its terminality witness; the cohomology and injective-neutralization inputs of `h2Classification` apply to this site; The étale Kummer short exact sequence, the equivalence of line bundles with Gm-torsors and the comparison derived-H1(Gm)=`Pic(X)` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11) retain the band orientation and the δ convention.

([Elena Andreini, Yunfeng Jiang and Hsian-Hua Tseng](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0907.2087v2), Definition 2.2, Remark 2.4, p.5; [Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.3 p.519).

For the proof, identify the root gerbe with the Kummer lifting gerbe; then use the lifting-gerbe boundary identity from the classification route; check the band orientation and δ sign.

*Needs:* `rootGerbe`, `h2Classification`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.δ`.

Prove `rootO1Nonneutral`. Let k be algebraically closed and `n>1` invertible in k. `RootGerbe_n(O(1))` on `P1_k` is locally nonempty, but has no global object and its derived Kummer class is nonzero. For `n = 1` it is neutral; for `n = 2` in characteristic different from 2 its class is degree 1 modulo 2, while `O(2)` has the root `O(1)` and gives class zero. These fix the Kummer boundary normalization.

Here k algebraically closed; `n>1` and n invertible in k; The degree API of JacobianChallenge Layer A on P1 includes degree(`O(1)`)=1 and degree(`M⊗n`)=n·degree(M).

([Elena Andreini, Yunfeng Jiang and Hsian-Hua Tseng](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0907.2087v2), §2.2 Definition 2.2; [James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9, boundary-gerbe neutrality).

For the proof, a global pair `(M,φ)` would give `n·deg(M)=deg(O(1))=1`; then degree takes integral values and tensor powers multiply it by n, so `n>1` makes this impossible; then the lifting boundary class vanishes exactly when a global nth root exists.

*Needs:* `rootGerbe`, `rootGerbeClass`, `h2Classification`, JacobianChallenge Layer A.

Prove `classCoefficientMap`. For `u:A→B`, class(`u_*F`)=`H2(u)`(class(F)), where `H2(u)` is the same-site coefficient map. Both class constructions use the same terminal site and the hypotheses of `classOfGerbe` and `classChoiceIndependent`.

([James S. Milne](https://jmilne.org/math/Books/ECpup4.pdf), IV §2 p.9, coefficient homomorphism).

For the proof, compare injective embeddings and quotient torsors for u; then apply naturality of the connecting maps and independence of choices.

*Needs:* `changeBand`, `classOfGerbe`, `classChoiceIndependent`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.map`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.δ_naturality`.

Prove `classSitePullback`. For a geometric morphism of the chosen sheaf topoi induced by base change `T→S`, with exact inverse-image functor on abelian sheaves and the derived global-cohomology comparison, pullback carries an A-banding to an `f* A`-banding and class(`f*F`)=f*(class(F)).

Here Both specified sites have fixed universes and chosen terminal objects with terminality witnesses; their cohomology, torsor-comparison and injective-neutralization inputs satisfy `h2Classification`; The geometric morphism induced by `T→S` has exact inverse image on abelian sheaves and the derived global-cohomology comparison of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.1, natural for short exact sequences and connecting maps; The A-banding is fixed on the source gerbe and the target band is its inverse image; all stack fibres are groupoids.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2 Definition 2.6(ii), p.515; [Lawrence Breen](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__225__1_0.pdf), Proposition 2.14 and (2.13.4)).

For the proof, transport the band equations through exact inverse image; then pull back the torsor lifting square and identify the resulting lifting gerbe; then use the derived-cohomology base-change naturality supplied by the change-of-site construction.

*Needs:* `relativePullback`, `AbelianBanding`, `h2Classification`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2.

### 4.4 Coherent finite-stage gerbes

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres.

Define `finiteEtaleGerbe`. A finite étale gerbe over k is a fpqc gerbe admitting a flat presentation `R⇒U` with both U and R finite étale k-schemes. Equivalently it is a finite gerbe whose base change to a separable splitting extension is BG for a finite étale group scheme G.

Here k is a field; Quotient stacks and algebraic-space diagonals are those of SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.19–1.21.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), §4 Definition 4.1, p.7; [Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), §2 p.133 and Lemma 2 p.135).

The API gives `FiniteEtaleGerbe.presentation`: There is a presentation by a finite étale groupoid `R⇒U`; `FiniteEtaleGerbe.baseChange`: Any field extension preserves finite étale gerbes; `FiniteEtaleGerbe.autFiniteEtale`: Every object over a field extension has finite étale automorphism group scheme.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `FiniteGerbeTests.trivial`: `Spec(k)`, with the trivial group, is a finite étale gerbe.
- `FiniteGerbeTests.constant`: BG for a finite constant group G is a finite étale gerbe, including nonabelian G.
- `FiniteGerbeTests.muP`: In characteristic p, Bμp is a finite fppf gerbe but is not a finite étale gerbe.

Define `GerbeLimitFamily`. For a small index category `I` and a `Cat`-valued pseudofunctor `Φ` on `I`, a compatible family consists of objects `x_i∈Φ(i)` and isomorphisms `θ_a:Φ(a)(x_j)≅x_i` for each `a:j→i`, with unit and composition equations using the pseudofunctor constraints. A morphism is a family of component arrows commuting with every `θ_a`. For a diagram of fpqc stacks Γ evaluated at T, these form its 2-limit fibre; its arrows are isomorphisms because the stage fibres are groupoids. The affine-gerbe applications use cofiltered index categories, in particular cofiltered posets.

Here `I` is any small ordinary category; the compatible-family carrier imposes no cofilteredness or groupoid hypothesis. For geometric stack fibres use the specified site `(C,J)` with fixed object and morphism universes and groupoid fibres. The separate Boolean 2-category model additionally needs index 2-arrow coherence.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), §3 Definitions3.2–3.5, pp.4–6).

The API gives `GerbeLimitFamily.component`: The family has an object xi at each index; `GerbeLimitFamily.transition`: Each index arrow has a specified transition isomorphism satisfying the coherence laws; `GerbeLimitFamily.hom_ext`: Two compatible-family arrows are equal iff all their component arrows agree; `GerbeLimitFamily.pullback`: A supplied strong transformation `η:Φ⇒Ψ` between same-universe index diagrams induces a functor on compatible families, applying η at every component and using its naturality isomorphisms on transitions. Site restriction `T′→T` must first supply this strong transformation; that geometric diagram and its coherence are the subject of §4.23; `GerbeLimitFamily.category`: Compatible component arrows form a category with componentwise identity and composition; its Hom type is the displayed compatibility-square carrier; `GerbeLimitFamily.evaluation`: Evaluation at i is a functor to `Φ(i)`, taking objects and arrows to their i-components; `GerbeLimitFamily.isIso_of_components`: A compatible-family arrow is invertible when every component is invertible; its inverse is the componentwise inverse in the same category; `GerbeLimitFamily.pullback_component`: The i-component of the family induced by η is exactly `η_i(x_i)`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.Modification`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SingleObj.category`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SingleObj.groupoid`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Skeleton`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeLimitFamily.singletonEquivalence`: For any pseudofunctor on LocallyDiscrete(Discrete PUnit), its compatible-family category is equivalent to the sole fibre, including the pseudofunctor unit constraint.
- `LimitFamilyTests.identityTower`: For a nonempty cofiltered ordinary index category and the constant identity diagram SingleObj G, with G a group, its compatible-family category is equivalent to SingleObj G. This retains G automorphisms. The corresponding BA(T) formulation additionally requires the geometric classifying-stack fibre comparison.
- `LimitFamilyTests.classesInsufficient`: For the singleton constant diagram SingleObj(Multiplicative(ZMod 3)), compatible families are nonempty, their Skeleton is a subsingleton, and every object has exactly three endomorphisms. Passing only to the singleton set of isomorphism classes loses those arrows. Comparing this model to `B(C3)` over an algebraically closed point is a separate geometric input.

Prove `limitStackDescent`. The compatible-family construction for a small diagram of fpqc stacks is an fpqc stack in groupoids.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), Following Definition 3.5, p.6).

For the proof, descend every component object through its stack equivalence to descent data; then descend transition isomorphisms by Hom-sheaf descent; their unit and composition equations can be checked locally; then descend compatible morphisms componentwise, retaining the transition commuting squares.

*Needs:* `GerbeLimitFamily`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.isEquivalence_toDescentData`.

Prove `nonemptyAffineLimitGerbe`. For a cofiltered system of affine fpqc gerbes over a field, if its compatible-family stack has an object over some nonempty k-scheme X, then the 2-limit is an affine fpqc gerbe. This assumption is not a k-rational neutralization and is not suppressed.

Here Small cofiltered system of affine fpqc gerbes over k; A compatible object exists over a nonempty k-scheme X; Inverse limits of affine faithfully flat schemes in this field-gerbe situation are affine faithfully flat.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), Remark 3.6 and Proposition 3.7, p.6).

For the proof, for two compatible objects, their Isom functor is the inverse limit of the affine finite-stage Isom schemes; then the inverse-limit affines and faithful-flatness input makes this Isom scheme affine faithfully flat, giving local isomorphisms; then choose a point of the nonempty k-scheme X and restrict the compatible object to `Spec L` for its residue field L. The field extension `L/k` is faithfully flat. For any affine test scheme with a compatible object, the fibre product with `Spec L` is the affine faithfully flat Isom limit over its base change to L. Thus `Spec L`→lim Γ gives the required fpqc chart and local objects; no k-rational object is inferred.

*Needs:* `GerbeLimitFamily`, `limitStackDescent`, `IsGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `profiniteEtaleGerbe`. A profinite étale gerbe over k is a fpqc gerbe with a specified presentation, up to coherent equivalence, as the compatible-family 2-limit of a small cofiltered system of finite étale gerbes. Its data include the transition functors, coherence and comparison equivalence.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), Definition 4.6, p.8; [Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), §2 p.133).

The API gives `ProfiniteEtaleGerbe.projection`: There is a morphism to each finite stage, with transition 2-isomorphisms; `ProfiniteEtaleGerbe.objectEquiv`: The fibre over T is the groupoid of compatible finite-stage objects and arrows; `ProfiniteEtaleGerbe.cofinal`: A cofinal reindexing of the presentation yields an equivalent compatible-family gerbe; all coherence is transported.

*Needs:* `finiteEtaleGerbe`, `GerbeLimitFamily`, `nonemptyAffineLimitGerbe`.

**Checks.**

- `ProfiniteGerbeTests.finite`: A finite étale gerbe is a profinite étale gerbe via a singleton presentation.
- `ProfiniteGerbeTests.identity`: The constant identity presentation recovers the original finite gerbe and its automorphism groupoid.
- `ProfiniteGerbeTests.zHat`: The fpqc classifying gerbe `B(Z_hat)` is profinite étale but is not an algebraic stack of finite presentation.

Define `locallyFull`. For affine fpqc gerbes Γ,Δ over a field k, a morphism `f:Γ→Δ` is locally full if for every extension `ℓ/k` and every `x∈Γ(ℓ)`, `Autℓ(x)→Autℓ(f(x))` is faithfully flat as a morphism of group schemes. This is not surjectivity of ℓ-valued points. For finite étale groups after separable splitting it becomes surjectivity of the finite geometric group homomorphism.

Here Γ and Δ are affine fpqc gerbes over k; f is a morphism of gerbes; no fixed abelian band is assumed.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Definition 3.4, Remarks 3.5–3.7, p.8).

The API gives `LocallyFull.autFaithfullyFlat`: Every induced automorphism-group map has faithful flatness; `LocallyFull.classifying_iff`: BG→BH is locally full iff `G→H` is faithfully flat; `LocallyFull.baseChange`: The property is preserved by every field extension.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, `relativeGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `LocallyFullTests.identity`: The identity of an affine gerbe is locally full.
- `LocallyFullTests.square`: Over R, the square map Gm→Gm is faithfully flat but its map `R×→R`× misses every negative element; point surjectivity is not the definition.
- `LocallyFullTests.subgroup`: For a proper subgroup H of a finite constant G, BH→BG is faithful but not locally full.

Prove `locallyFullIsomEpi`. For affine fpqc gerbes over a field, f is locally full iff every `IsomΓ(x,y)→IsomΔ`(fx,fy) is an epimorphism of fpqc sheaves.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.10(1)⇔(2), pp.9–10).

For the proof, locally trivialize the Isom torsors and reduce their map to the induced automorphism-group map; then for general affine test schemes, take an fpqc cover on which the objects come from one field-extension object; then use faithful flatness iff an affine-group morphism is an fpqc cover.

*Needs:* `locallyFull`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `locallyFullRelative`. A morphism of affine fpqc gerbes is locally full iff it is a relative gerbe. A faithful locally full map is an equivalence.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.10(2)⇔(3), Remark 3.7).

For the proof, objects lift locally because both source and target are gerbes and the source is locally nonempty; then the Isom-epimorphism condition is exactly relative local morphism lifting; then if also faithful, the Isom maps are monomorphisms and epimorphisms, hence isomorphisms; descend the local equivalence.

*Needs:* `locallyFullIsomEpi`, `relativeGerbe`, `relativeDescent`.

Prove `locallyFullLimit`. Let `Γ→lim_iΔi` be a morphism of affine fpqc gerbes. If each Γ→Δi is locally full, then `Γ→lim_iΔi` is locally full.

Here A field k and a small nonempty cofiltered index category (or cofiltered poset), so the coordinate-ring diagram is filtered after taking opposites; Both Γ and the compatible limit are already affine fpqc gerbes; The affine-group Hopf-algebra faithful-flatness criterion is supplied.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.11, p.10).

For the proof, after choosing an object over a field extension, write the stabilizer H of the limit as lim Hi; then its coordinate Hopf algebra is `colim ℓ`[Hi]; then each ℓ[Hi]→`ℓ[G]` is injective by faithful flatness; a filtered colimit element maps to zero only if its finite-stage representative is zero; then the Hopf-algebra criterion for affine group morphisms converts this injection to faithful flatness.

*Needs:* `locallyFull`, `nonemptyAffineLimitGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`.

Define `zHatGerbe`. Over a field k, let `G=lim_m (Z/m!Z)_k` as affine group schemes, with the quotient transition maps. Its fpqc torsor stack BG is an fpqc gerbe and is presented as the 2-limit of `B(Z/m!Z)_k`. A compatible family of finite torsors yields a G-torsor by affine inverse limit with its action; the torsor comparison and local triviality must be verified in the fpqc topology.

([Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), §2 p.133; [Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.1260v5), §3 Remark 3.6, Definition 4.6).

The API gives `ProfiniteIntegersGerbe.finiteProjection`: Each quotient `G→Z/m`!Z induces BG→`B(Z/m!Z)`; `ProfiniteIntegersGerbe.trivial`: The trivial G-torsor neutralizes BG over k; `ProfiniteIntegersGerbe.aut`: The automorphism group scheme of the trivial object is G.

*Needs:* `GerbeLimitFamily`, `profiniteEtaleGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `ZHatGerbeTests.finiteLevel`: At each finite level the stabilizer is the finite étale group `Z/m`!Z.
- `ZHatGerbeTests.compatibleArrows`: An automorphism of the compatible trivial object is a compatible family of finite residues, that is G.
- `ZHatGerbeTests.notFinitePresentation`: BG is not an algebraic stack of finite presentation because G is not of finite type.

Prove `zHatNotFiniteType`. The affine k-group `G=lim_m (Z/m!Z)_k` is not of finite type over k.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.1(4)–(6), pp.5–7).

For the proof, its coordinate ring is the union of the finite-dimensional rings `k^(Z/m!Z)`, with injective transition maps; then every finite list of algebra generators would lie in one finite stage and therefore generate a finite-dimensional subalgebra; then larger finite stages have arbitrarily many nonzero orthogonal idempotents, which are linearly independent and remain nonzero in the colimit; then this contradicts generation by that finite-dimensional subalgebra.

*Needs:* `zHatGerbe`.

Prove `zHatNotAlgebraicFp`. The fpqc gerbe `B(Z_hat)_k` is not an algebraic stack of finite presentation. In fact its affine-gerbe stabilizer criterion excludes algebraicity.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.1(3)⇒(5), pp.5–6).

For the proof, if this affine gerbe were algebraic, BV19 Proposition 3.1 would make its automorphism group at the trivial object finite type; then that group is G, contradicting the explicit coordinate-ring computation.

*Needs:* `zHatNotFiniteType`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

### 4.5 Self-equivalences, affine images and twisted inertia

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: A specified site `(C,J)`, with fixed object and morphism universes; all stacks have groupoid fibres.

Prove `selfEquivalenceIsomTransport`. Let η be a band-preserving self-equivalence of an A-gerbe F. For an isomorphism `φ:x→y`, the map `Isom(x,ηx)→Isom(y,ηy)`, `p↦η(φ)∘p∘φ`⁻¹, is an A-torsor isomorphism independent of φ. These maps compose and commute with restrictions.

Here An A-gerbe on the chosen site; η is band-preserving, with its actual strong-transformation coherence.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1, p.515).

For the proof, replacing φ by `φ∘a` changes `η(φ)` by the matching band automorphism `η(a)`; band preservation and the band conjugation equation move `η(a)` past p and cancel a⁻¹, so the map is independent of φ; functoriality of η gives compatibility with composition, and the strong naturality of η gives the restriction comparison (`BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_restriction`).

*Needs:* `BandPreserving`, `isomTorsor`, `banding_iso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_restriction`.

Define `selfEquivalenceTorsor`. For a band-preserving self-equivalence η of any A-gerbe F, choose local objects x and glue the A-torsors `Isom(x,ηx)` using their choice-independent transport maps. The resulting A-torsor Pη is defined globally without a neutralization of F. Invertible modifications `η⇒η′` induce equivariant isomorphisms `Pη≅Pη′`.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1, p.515; [Lawrence Breen](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__225__1_0.pdf), Proposition 2.14, p.56).

The API gives `GerbeSelfEquivalence.torsor`: Associates a global A-torsor Pη to η; `GerbeSelfEquivalence.torsor_local`: For any local object x, Pη restricts to `Isom(x,ηx)`; `GerbeSelfEquivalence.torsor_map`: A modification induces a torsor isomorphism, with identity and composition laws.

*Needs:* `selfEquivalenceIsomTransport`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheafFunctor`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSheaf_locallyNonempty`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_freeTransitive`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomSectionAction_restriction`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomTransportIsoEquiv_modification`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafObjectFunctor_parallel`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomSheafTransport_transport`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeNatIso`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomBaseChangeIso_equivariant`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeTransport_square`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfHomBaseChangeNatIso_comp`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportIso_self`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointBaseChange_square`, `BandedMorphism.fibreHomEndpointTransportNatIso`.

**Checks.**

- `SelfEquivalenceTorsorTests.identity`: For η=id, Pη is the trivial A-torsor, even if F has no global object.
- `SelfEquivalenceTorsorTests.neutral`: For a chosen neutralization this agrees with evaluating the induced equivalence of BA on its trivial torsor.
- `SelfEquivalenceTorsorTests.nonNeutralRoot`: The identity of the nonneutral μn-root gerbe of `O(1)` still gives the trivial μn-torsor; this construction cannot require a global root.

Prove `allSelfEquivalences`. For any A-gerbe F, the groupoid of band-preserving self-equivalences is equivalent to the groupoid of A-torsors. The functor is `η↦Pη`; its inverse twists local objects by a torsor and descends them. Modifications correspond to equivariant isomorphisms. The assertion holds without a chosen neutralization.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1 p.515; [Lawrence Breen](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__225__1_0.pdf), Proposition 2.14).

For the proof, in order: (1) on a cover with local objects, apply `neutralSelfEquivalences` on each member; (2) the choice-independent transport of `selfEquivalenceIsomTransport` glues the local functors `η↦Pη` and the local inverses that twist local objects by a torsor, together with their units and counits, by descent of modifications in the groupoid `BandedMorphism.groupoid`; (3) descent of modifications makes the glued functor fully faithful, and object descent in F descends the twisted local objects, giving essential surjectivity; (4) the inverse equivalence with its unit and counit is assembled by `CoherentInverse` (§4.21).

*Needs:* `selfEquivalenceTorsor`, `neutralSelfEquivalences`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, `BandedMorphism.groupoid`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_independent`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportNatIso_restriction`.

Define `quotientGerbeTransgression`. Let a finite constant group Γ act on Y, let A be a commutative band on the chosen site, and let α be an A-gerbe with Γ-equivariant structure ηγ and its unit/composition modifications. On each fixed locus Yγ, ηγ becomes a self-equivalence, hence determines an A-torsor Pγ. The centralizer `CΓ(γ)` acts coherently on Pγ; descend it to `[Yγ/CΓ(γ)]`. The sum over conjugacy representatives gives the torsor on `I[Y/Γ]`.

Here Finite constant Γ; the quotient and its inertia fixed-locus decomposition are supplied; A is μr with r invertible or Gm for the paper’s étale applications; the site and topology are fixed; An actual Γ-equivariant A-banding and its coherent modifications are given.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1 p.515).

The API gives `GerbeTransgression.component`: The restriction to `[Yγ/CΓ(γ)]` is the descended Pγ; `GerbeTransgression.conjugation`: Conjugate γ give canonically equivalent torsors through equivariant coherence; `GerbeTransgression.pullback`: Equivariant base changes preserving the band commute with the construction.

*Needs:* `allSelfEquivalences`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, `quotientInertiaComponents`.

**Checks.**

- `TransgressionTests.identity`: The identity inertia component gets the trivial A-torsor through ηe and its unit modification.
- `TransgressionTests.trivialEquivariance`: A neutral gerbe with trivial Γ-equivariant structure gives trivial component torsors.
- `TransgressionTests.modification`: An isomorphism of coherent equivariant gerbes induces an isomorphism of the descended inertia torsors, not merely equality of H1 classes.

Prove `quotientInertiaComponents`. For a finite constant group Γ acting on Y, `I[Y/Γ]≃⊔_[γ] [Yγ/CΓ(γ)]`, where one representative is chosen from each conjugacy class and Yγ is the fixed-point sheaf (with representability whenever supplied). Changing representatives gives the canonical equivalent description. No tameness or invertibility of |Γ| is required for this groupoid formula.

Here Γ is a finite constant group acting on the sheaf Y; For a separated scheme Y the fixed-point sheaf Yγ is the equalizer of the identity and γ, a closed subscheme.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), §2.2.1, p.515).

For the proof, locally trivialize the Γ-torsor of a quotient-stack object; then an automorphism is then `γ∈Γ` fixing its image y in Y; then changing the trivialization acts by simultaneous conjugation on γ and translation on y; then decompose this action groupoid by conjugacy classes, identifying the remaining stabilizer with `CΓ(γ)`, and descend the equivalence.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 (`inertia`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21.

Define `canonicalAffineFactorization`. For `f:Γ→Δ` between affine fpqc gerbes over k, a canonical factorization consists of an affine fpqc gerbe E, maps `g:Γ→E` and `h:E→Δ`, an invertible modification `h∘g≅f`, proof that g is locally full, and proof that h is faithful on all fibre groupoids. Equivalence of such data includes the compatible modification over Δ.

Here Γ and Δ are affine fpqc gerbes over a field k.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Definition 3.8, p.8).

The API gives `AffineGerbeFactorization.sourceMap`: The first map g is locally full; `AffineGerbeFactorization.targetMap`: The second map h is faithful; `AffineGerbeFactorization.factorIso`: The composite `h∘g` is identified with f by an invertible modification.

*Needs:* `locallyFull`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.Modification`, Mathlib `MonoidHom.toFunctor`.

**Checks.**

- `CanonicalFactorTests.identity`: The identity has `E=Γ` and both maps identity.
- `CanonicalFactorTests.kernel`: For a group morphism `G→H` the neutral factor is `B(G/ker f)`→BH.
- `CanonicalFactorTests.notTarget`: The inclusion `B1→B(C2)` cannot have `E=B(C2)`, because its first map is not locally full. With trivial stabilizer kernel the actual middle gerbe is B1; at the trivial object the quotient source Isom sheaf has one arrow while the final-target Isom sheaf has two. The SingleObj PUnit→SingleObj(Multiplicative(ZMod 2)) fixture is faithful but not full and has these Hom cardinalities; its geometric comparison remains required.

Prove `canonicalFactorizationUnique`. Two canonical factorizations of the same `f:Γ→Δ` have equivalent middle affine gerbes over Δ, compatibly with the maps from Γ.

Here Two canonical factorizations of an affine-gerbe morphism over a field.
