([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.9, uniqueness proof, pp.8–9).

For the proof, both first maps kill precisely the stabilizer kernel K of f because the second maps are faithful; then local fullness of the first maps identifies each middle-gerbe sheaf `Isom_E`(gx,gy) with `Isom_Γ(x,y)`/Kx. Faithfulness of the second maps embeds it in `Isom_Δ`(fx,fy), and does not make that embedding surjective; then identify both middle gerbes with the quotient presentation and obtain the equivalence with its compatibility modifications.

*Needs:* `canonicalAffineFactorization`, `affineNormalQuotient`.

Prove `finiteEtaleImage`. For a profinite étale fpqc gerbe Γ over k and a morphism `Γ→Δ` to a finite étale gerbe, its canonical affine factor E is finite étale, and `Γ→E` is locally full. The faithful map `E→Δ` is representable.

Here Γ has the fpqc profinite presentation, with the nonemptiness requirement satisfied; Δ is finite étale over k.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.9 with §3 faithfulness criterion, pp.8–9; [Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), Lemma 2 proof, p.135).

For the proof, after a splitting field extension, identify the middle stabilizer with the image of a profinite étale group in a finite étale group; then it is a subgroup of a finite constant group after separable splitting, hence finite étale; then descend the finite étale image and its classifying presentation to k; then faithfulness is representability for these finite-type gerbes, by the stabilizer criterion.

*Needs:* `profiniteEtaleGerbe`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, `canonicalAffineFactorization`, `affineNormalQuotient`.

Prove `locallyFullFinitePresentation`. Every profinite étale fpqc gerbe Γ has a cofinal finite étale presentation Γ≃lim `E_i` with each projection `Γ→E_i` locally full. The presentation and comparison include the transition isomorphisms and their coherence.

Here A nonempty profinite étale fpqc gerbe over k; The cofinal pseudodiagram comparison below.

([Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), Lemma 2 proof, p.135; [Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.9).

For the proof, replace each finite stage of a chosen presentation by the finite étale image of Γ in that stage; then for finitely many stages, take the image into their product to obtain a common refinement; then retain the original compatibility two-morphisms when factoring maps through the images; uniqueness gives the corresponding compatible refinements; then show that compatible objects and arrows for the image stages recover those of the original presentation, using the cofinal comparison for the chosen pseudodiagram; then the locally full source projections are supplied by their canonical factorizations.

*Needs:* `finiteEtaleImage`, `canonicalFactorizationUnique`, `GerbeLimitFamily`, `locallyFullLimit`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `relativeProfiniteGerbeFiniteStages`. Let `f:Γ→Δ` be a locally full map of profinite étale fpqc gerbes over k. Choose synchronized cofinal finite presentations Γ≃lim `E_i` and Δ≃lim `D_i` with locally full projections and maps `E_i→D_i`. Each `E_i→D_i` is a proper étale relative gerbe. For any scheme `C→Δ` the pullback `Γ×Δ C→C` is the compatible two-limit of `E_i×D_i C→C`, each a proper étale relative gerbe.

Here the synchronized finite-stage construction, cofinal product-image comparison and joint object/arrow/modification descent of §4.23; a scheme C mapping to the resulting limit gerbe Δ.

([Giulio Bresciani](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6.pdf), Lemma 2 and proof, p.135).

For the proof, refine the two finite systems so each target finite map factors through a source finite stage; replace that stage by its image, retaining the triangle modification; then the composite `Γ→D_i` is locally full. On stabilizers, its coordinate map factors through that for `E_i→D_i`; injectivity of the composite gives injectivity of the latter, hence local fullness; then apply the criterion `relativeGerbe`. After a common splitting field extension, the map is a finite étale band gerbe; descend properness and étaleness; then pull back along `C→D_i` and apply base-change stability; then compare the compatible two-limit with `Γ×Δ C`, retaining both pseudodiagram and pullback coherence.

*Needs:* `locallyFullFinitePresentation`, `locallyFullRelative`, `relativePullback`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `finiteQuotientPresentation`. For a Deligne–Mumford stack X, a finite quotient presentation is an algebraic space Y, an action of a finite constant group Γ which is generically fixed-point free, and an equivalence `X≃[Y/Γ]`. A finite abelian quotient presentation additionally requires Γ abelian.

Here X is Deligne–Mumford, and Y is an algebraic space over its base.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), Definition 2.1, p.512).

The API gives `FiniteQuotientPresentation.equivalence`: The specified stack equivalence to the action quotient; `FiniteQuotientPresentation.genericFree`: The Γ action is free on the specified dense open; `FiniteAbelianQuotientPresentation.toFinite`: An abelian presentation forgets to a finite quotient presentation.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `FiniteQuotientTests.trivial`: An algebraic space has a presentation by the trivial group.
- `FiniteQuotientTests.sign`: The sign action of `Z/2Z` on A1 in characteristic different from 2 is generically free, though inertia at 0 is nontrivial.
- `FiniteQuotientTests.trivialAction`: The displayed trivial nontrivial-group action on a nonempty Y is not generically free and does not give a presentation of this prescribed kind.

Prove `commutingQuotientExchange`. If fppf group schemes G1,G2 over S act on the S-scheme N through commuting actions, then `[[N/G1]/G2]≃[N/(G1×G2)]≃[[N/G2]/G1]` as S-stacks. These are equivalences of groupoids over every test scheme T, natural in T.

Here G1,G2 are fppf S-group schemes; The two actions commute; no interchange is claimed for unrelated noncommuting actions.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), Lemma 4.7 and proof, p.540).

For the proof, a double-quotient object over T is a G2-torsor `P→T` and a G2-equivariant G1-torsor `Q→P` with its map to N; then descend Q along `P→T` to a G1-torsor `P′→T` using its G2-equivariant structure; then identify `Q≃P×_T P′` and retain the original `(G1×G2)`-equivariant map from this product to N. A G2-equivariant map to a nontrivial G2-space need not descend to `P′→N`; then this description is symmetric in G1,G2 and includes isomorphisms, yielding the natural equivalences.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `torsorTwistSpace`. For a commutative étale S-group scheme Γ, an S-scheme N with Γ-action and a Γ-torsor T, the anti-diagonal action on `N×S T` is free and its quotient `N_T=(N×S T)/Γ` is an algebraic space. The action through T descends to a Γ-action on `N_T`. This construction depends on the torsor and its arrows, not on a bare symbol representing its H1 class.

Here Γ is a commutative étale S-group scheme; T is an actual étale Γ-torsor.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), Definition 4.5, p.539).

The API gives `TorsorTwist.quotient`: The quotient is an algebraic space with its descended Γ-action; `TorsorTwist.trivial`: A chosen trivialization of T identifies `N_T` with N equivariantly; `TorsorTwist.mapTorsor`: A Γ-torsor isomorphism `T≅T′` induces a Γ-equivariant space isomorphism `N_T≅N_T′`.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `TwistTests.trivial`: For `Γ=1` the twist is N.
- `TwistTests.freeTorsor`: For `N=Γ` with its regular action, the twist is equivariantly the torsor T.
- `TwistTests.arrows`: An automorphism of T can act nontrivially on `N_T`; quotienting the construction to a set of H1 classes loses these arrows.

Prove `torsorTwistQuotientEquivalence`. Under the torsor-twist hypotheses, `[N/Γ]≃[N_T/Γ]` over S, retaining the groupoids of objects and their arrows.

Here the commutative étale Γ and actual torsor of the preceding construction.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8.pdf), Lemma 4.6 and proof, p.539).

For the proof, express the right side as the double quotient of `N×S T` by the anti-diagonal and residual Γ actions; then exchange the two commuting quotients; then use `[T/Γ]≃S` and the canonical triviality of the inner action on `[N/Γ]`, with its actual coherence modification; then check the resulting equivalence under change of torsor trivialization.

*Needs:* `torsorTwistSpace`, `commutingQuotientExchange`.

Prove `twistedGroupActionQuotient`. Let A,B be smooth group algebraic spaces over S, with A acting on B by automorphisms and compatible A and B actions on an algebraic space X. For an A-torsor ρ, let `Xρ=X×Aρ` and `Bρ=B×Aρ`. Then `[(X×Sρ)/(B⋊A)]≃[Xρ/Bρ]` naturally in the torsor and equivariant maps.

Here Smooth group algebraic spaces A,B over S with the specified semidirect-action compatibility; ρ is an A-torsor.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Construction5.1, p.26).

For the proof, trivialize ρ in the fppf topology; then over the trivialization, quotient first by A, identifying Xρ and Bρ with X and B; then identify the remaining B action, transported through A, with the descended action of Bρ; then descend the quotient equivalence and its arrow maps; the transition cocycle is exactly the given A action on B and compatibility with the B action on X.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `TwistedInertia.finiteStagePairs`. For a perfect field k of characteristic p, a positive
integer n prime to p and an fppf stack in groupoids X over k, construct the stack whose objects
over a k-scheme T are pairs `(x, α)`, with `x ∈ X(T)` and a homomorphism of fppf sheaves of groups
`α : μ_n,T → Aut_T(x)`. An arrow is an isomorphism `u : x → y` with
`α_y = Ad_u ∘ α_x`. Retain every homomorphism, including the trivial one. Pullback along `T′ → T`
uses X's restriction and the canonical pullback comparison for automorphism sheaves; its unit and
composition isomorphisms come from X. Prove descent for objects, homomorphisms and intertwining
arrows: descend x in X and then descend α in the automorphism sheaf.

Here the site is the big fppf site of k-schemes, with fixed universes. No representability or
finiteness hypothesis on X's diagonal is needed for this construction.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Definition
2.9 and the proof of Lemma 2.10, pp.9–10; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02ZP),
Lemma 8.9.1, for stackification.)

The API gives `TwistedInertia.finiteStageProjection`, forgetting α, and
`TwistedInertia.mappingStackComparison`: an equivalence with the internal mapping stack
`T ↦ Hom_T(Bμ_n,T, X_T)`, whose arrows are invertible modifications. Construct this
test-scheme pseudofunctor here from the supplier's categories of strong transformations; its
restriction is base change and its coherence comes from pullback. The equivalence sends a map to
its value on the trivial torsor and the induced μ_n-action. Conversely, for a μ_n-torsor P on U,
descend `x|_P` along the action α; this defines the map on all torsors and arrows. Prove naturality
under every change of test scheme and compatibility with evaluation at the trivial torsor.
`TwistedInertia.finiteStageFibre` identifies the 2-fibre over a specified `x : T → X` with the
sheaf `Hom_T-grp(μ_n,T, Aut_T(x))`, viewed as a discrete stack on T's fppf site. The fibre data
include an identification of the evaluated object with x, so its arrows preserve α and have no
residual stabilizers.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.20–1.21 (strong transformations, automorphism sheaves,
classifying stacks and torsor descent), SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.9 (`μ_n`).

**Checks.**

- `TwistedInertiaTests.stageOne`: for n = 1, the pair stack and `Hom(Bμ_1, X)` are equivalent to X,
  and their evaluation fibre at each specified x is terminal.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.splitCyclicStage`: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p,
  for a prime ℓ different from p and `X = B(C_ℓ)`, stage ℓ has ℓ isomorphism classes, each with
  automorphism group `C_ℓ`; the fibre at the trivial torsor consists of ℓ discrete objects.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.torsorDescent`: for `X = Bμ_n` and the identity homomorphism at the trivial
  torsor, the inverse mapping-stack comparison sends any μ_n-torsor P to P, including a nontrivial
  torsor, rather than to the trivial torsor.

Define `primeToPTwistedInertia`. For an fppf stack in groupoids X over a perfect field k of
characteristic p, let `μ̂ = lim_(n,p)=1 μ_n`, with transition `μ_mn → μ_n` given by the mth power.
`TwistedInertia.inflation` sends `(x, α)` at stage n to `(x, α ∘ (−)^m)` at stage mn and leaves
its intertwining arrow unchanged. Prove its full faithfulness using that `μ_mn → μ_n` is an
epimorphism of fppf sheaves, its compatibility with restriction, and its unit and composition
coherence. Under `TwistedInertia.mappingStackComparison` this is precomposition by
`Bμ_mn → Bμ_n`.

Construct `TwistedInertia.filteredPrestack` objectwise: objects are stage pairs `(n, x, α)`;
arrows between two such objects are intertwining arrows at a common divisible stage, identified
when they agree after a further inflation. Specify composition at a common refinement, independence
of refinement, restriction functors and their pseudofunctor constraints. Its groupoid fibres and
Hom-sheaf descent are part of the construction. Define Iμ̂X by the supplier's fppf stackification
of this pseudofunctor. Prove `TwistedInertia.twoColimitComparison`: for every fppf stack Y,
maps `Iμ̂X → Y` and modifications are equivalent to compatible stage maps with their invertible
transition modifications and unit/composition coherence. Thus this is the two-colimit of the
finite-stage mapping stacks among fppf stacks. This system and its comparisons are owned here;
SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18 supplies stackification and its 2-universal property.

Here k is perfect of characteristic p; n ranges over all positive integers prime to p ordered by
divisibility. All maps `Bμ_n → X` are retained. No algebraic finite-presentation assertion for the
two-colimit is included.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), §2.4 setup
and Definition 2.9, p.9; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02ZP), Lemma 8.9.1.)

The API gives `TwistedInertia.project`: the projection induced by the finite-stage projections;
`TwistedInertia.finiteStage`: the compatible maps from each stage into Iμ̂X;
`TwistedInertia.fibre`: for a specified `x : T → X`, the 2-fibre of the projection is the discrete
stack of the fppf sheafification of `colim_(n,p)=1 Hom_T-grp(μ_n,T, Aut_T(x))`. Prove this
identification compatibly with change of T and x. Conjugating arrows occur in the total stack of
pairs as x varies; they are not automorphisms in this relative fibre.

*Needs:* `TwistedInertia.finiteStagePairs`, `TwistedInertia.mappingStackComparison`,
`TwistedInertia.finiteStageFibre`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18 (stackification and its
2-universal property).

**Checks.**

- `TwistedInertiaTests.space`: For an algebraic space regarded as a stack, Iμ̂`X≃X`.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.zeroHom`: The trivial homomorphism is retained; the definition is not the representable cyclotomic inertia substack.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.pGroup`: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, all
  homomorphisms `μ_n → C_p` with n prime to p are trivial. The projection `Iμ̂B(C_p) → B(C_p)`
  is an equivalence and its 2-fibre at a specified torsor is terminal, while the total stack retains
  its `C_p` automorphisms. The conjugation groupoid of the trivial homomorphism is `B(C_p)`,
  so it cannot describe that relative fibre.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.frobeniusDirection`: on the fifth roots of unity over `𝔽₂`, arithmetic Frobenius acts by the exponent 2 and its inverse by 3, which differ at a generator; this fixes the direction of the Frobenius action. Over `𝔽₂` a homomorphism from `μ₃` to the constant group `ℤ/3` that intertwines the square Frobenius with the identity is trivial, whereas over `𝔽₄` the fourth-power Frobenius is the identity on `μ₃` and every such homomorphism is equivariant.

Prove `TwistedInertia.finiteFieldComparison`. For an fppf stack in groupoids X over `𝔽_q` with
diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and of finite presentation, identify
`TwistedInertia.finiteStagePairs(n)(𝔽_q)` with the groupoid of pairs `(x, α_n)`, where
`x ∈ X(𝔽_q)` and `α_n : μ_n(𝔽_qbar) → Aut(x_𝔽_qbar)` is Galois-equivariant; arrows are rational
isomorphisms intertwining the geometric homomorphisms. Prove compatibility with inflation and
evaluation in X. Also prove that the functor from the filtered groupoid of these rational stage
objects to `Iμ̂X(𝔽_q)` is an equivalence, including full faithfulness on rational arrows.

Here q is a power of p and n is positive and prime to p. All the diagonal hypotheses are retained
in the filtered and continuous-homomorphism comparisons.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Lemma
2.10(a) and proof, pp.9–10; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02ZP), Lemma 8.9.1.)

For the proof, finite étale splitting of μ_n and Galois descent identify its sheaf homomorphisms
with equivariant geometric homomorphisms; descent of X's Isom sheaves identifies the arrows.
An object of the stackification is fppf-locally a finite-stage object. Over a finite field, a
nonempty finite-type member of such a cover has a point over a finite field extension. Pull back
to that finite étale cover and use the fully faithful inflations to descend its finite-stage
object and intertwining descent arrows at the same stage. This proves the rational-point
comparison through stackification. The finite-presentation diagonal ensures that the geometric
automorphism and Isom data descend to finite extensions, so the Galois comparison uses finite
étale descent: choose étale scheme charts of these algebraic spaces and apply finite-presentation
limit factorization to their affine charts.
For geometric points with discrete target, continuity is equivalent to factoring through some
finite μ_n; equivariance then gives the corresponding rational sheaf homomorphism.

*Needs:* `TwistedInertia.finiteStagePairs`, `TwistedInertia.mappingStackComparison`,
`TwistedInertia.inflation`, `TwistedInertia.filteredPrestack`, `primeToPTwistedInertia`,
SchemeAndStackFoundations §§0.9, 1.18 (limits and stackification), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1
(finite étale Galois descent and Isom sheaves).

**Checks.**

- `TwistedInertiaTests.nonsplitStage`: at stage 3 over `𝔽₂`, for the trivial object of `B(C₃)`,
  the only equivariant homomorphism is trivial; over `𝔽₄`, the relative fibre has three objects.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.rationalCentralizer`: for the identity `μ₃ → μ₃` at the trivial object of
  `Bμ₃` over `𝔽₂`, the rational pair has trivial automorphism group, although the geometric
  centralizer has three elements.
- `TwistedInertiaTests.finiteFieldStackification`: at stage 1 for `X = B(C₃)` over `𝔽₂`, all
  three rational torsor classes and their rational arrows survive the filtered comparison; objects
  are not restricted to the trivial torsor.

Prove `twistedInertiaFiniteField`. For X/Fq with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and of finite presentation, Iμ̂X(Fq) is equivalent to the groupoid of pairs `(x,α)`, with `x∈X`(Fq), a continuous homomorphism `α:μ`̂(Fqbar)→`Aut(x_Fqbar)` for the discrete topology, and Frobenius equivariance `φα=αφ`. An arrow is an Fq-isomorphism of objects intertwining α. The domain Frobenius acts by qth power. For `μ₅` over `F₂` the exponent is 2 modulo 5, whereas inverse Frobenius has exponent 3; the identity map from `μ₅` to itself intertwines the two q-power actions and does not intertwine q-power with inverse q-power. For a constant `C₃` target over `F₂` equivariance forces `α = 0`; over `F₄` there are three homomorphisms from `μ₃` to `C₃`.

Here X is an fppf stack in groupoids over Fq with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and
of finite presentation; `TwistedInertia.finiteFieldComparison` supplies the finite-stage and
stackification comparisons as targets of this roadmap.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Lemma 2.10(a) and proof, pp.9–10).

For the proof, apply `TwistedInertia.finiteFieldComparison` and pass to the prime-to-p system,
using its continuous-homomorphism comparison. Equivariance for arithmetic Frobenius is equivalent
to equivariance for the Galois group because the source is profinite, the target is discrete and
the arithmetic Frobenius powers are dense.

*Needs:* `primeToPTwistedInertia`, `TwistedInertia.finiteFieldComparison`.

Prove `twistedInertiaGenerator`. For a chosen profinite generator ξ of μ̂(Fqbar), the preceding groupoid is equivalent to pairs `(x,a)` in ordinary inertia with x defined over Fq and `φ(a)=a^q`. The finite-presentation hypothesis makes a finite-order geometric automorphism; the displayed equation forces its order prime to p, so it uniquely determines the continuous homomorphism α with `α(ξ)=a`.

Here the hypotheses of the finite-field case; A choice of profinite generator, explicitly part of the comparison.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Lemma 2.10(b) and proof, pp.9–10).

For the proof, any geometric point of a finite-type automorphism group scheme descends to a finite field, and its group of rational points is finite; then choose a power `φ^r` fixing a; then `a=a^(q^r)`, so its order divides `q^r−1` and is prime to p; then a prime-to-p finite-order a defines the unique continuous homomorphism from μ̂ sending ξ to a; then the equation gives Frobenius equivariance and the conjugating arrows agree.

*Needs:* `twistedInertiaFiniteField`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 (`inertia`), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `twistedInertiaAutomorphisms`. For a rational twisted-inertia object `(x,a)`, its automorphism group is {`β∈Aut_X`(Fq)`(x) | aβ`=βa}. The rationality condition on β cannot be dropped.

Here A rational object of the finite-field twisted-inertia groupoid.

([Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss and Paul Ziegler](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.06739v2), Lemma 2.10(c), equation(10), p.10).

For the proof, an arrow of the pair groupoid is a rational isomorphism of x intertwining the homomorphism; then intertwining its generator value is equivalent to intertwining the whole continuous homomorphism.

*Needs:* `twistedInertiaGenerator`.

### 4.6 Intrinsic centre sections and descended bands

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C is a fixed small category with topology J; F is the existing Cat-valued pseudofunctor. Gerbe and abelian-inertia assumptions are imposed only where stated. All coefficient sheaves use one fixed universe large enough for the indexed family.

Define `IntrinsicBandSections`. Define ZF(U) as the subgroup of the product over V and `f:V→U` of units of the CatCenter(`F(V)`) whose components satisfy `F(g)(z(V,f)x)=z(W,g≫f)(F(g)x)` for every `g:W→V` and object x over V. Each unit is an invertible natural endomorphism of the identity of the fibre.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8, final omitted varying-U step).

The API gives `IntrinsicBandSections.val`: A section specifies a unit of CatCenter(`F(V)`) for every arrow `V→U`; `IntrinsicBandSections.compatible`: The central family commutes with every pullback functor on every object; `IntrinsicBandSections.ext`: Equality of all component automorphisms implies equality of sections; `IntrinsicBandSections.commGroup`: The subgroup has pointwise group operations and a commutative group structure specified from centrality; `IntrinsicBandSections.mk`: For U, a family `z(V,f)` of units of CatCenter(`F(V)`) satisfying the vertical compatibility equation for every `f:V→U`, `g:W→V` and x over V determines a section in ZF(U). No topology, gerbe, chosen object or abelian-inertia assumption is needed; `IntrinsicBandSections.val_mk`: For every V and `f:V→U`, the component of mk(z,hz) is `z(V,f)`; the compatibility witness does not change this component; `IntrinsicBandSections.val_one`: For every `f:V→U`, the component of the identity section is the identity unit of CatCenter(`F(V)`); `IntrinsicBandSections.val_mul`: For s,t in ZF(U), val(`s t`,V,f)=val(s,V,f) val(t,V,f) with the categorical-center multiplication; `IntrinsicBandSections.val_inv`: For s in ZF(U), val(s inverse,V,f)=val(s,V,f) inverse.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CatCenter`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CatCenter.naturality`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CatCenter.mul_app`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut`.

**Checks.**

- `BandCenterTests.C3`: On the one-object point-site gerbe `B(C3)`, there are three central sections, with evaluation recovering all of C3.
- `BandCenterTests.identity`: For the terminal fibre groupoid, the group of compatible central sections is trivial.
- `BandCenterTests.S3`: For `B(S3)` on a point, sections form the trivial center of S3, rather than all six automorphisms. Thus evaluation onto inertia fails without abelian inertia.
- `BandLocalityTests.cover`: For a gerbe on an arbitrary site, equality of central-section restrictions on a covering sieve forces equality of the original sections; no terminal object or fibre products are needed.
- `BandLocalityTests.disconnected`: On the point site, the stack given by a disjoint union of two one-object C3 groupoids is not a gerbe: the objects in different components are not locally isomorphic. Its central-section group is `C3×C3` of order9, and evaluation at the first object is projection to C3, not injective. The pair projection proves this coordinate consequence, not a complete point-site fixture.
- `BandLocalityTests.singleReduction`: In the specified `C4→C2→C2` restriction chain, the single reduction `C4→C2` sends both 0 and 2 to 0, so it is not injective. A single arbitrary arrow must not be treated as a covering-sieve equality test. The actual `ZMod.castHom` reduction is used; no topology making that arrow a cover is asserted.

Prove `bandCenterExt`. If s,t∈ZF(U) have the same evaluated automorphism at every `V→U` and every object x over V, then `s=t`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8, final omitted varying-U step).

For the proof, the hom components determine the natural transformation by existing `CatCenter.ext`; then units equality follows from equality of their values; product equality is function extensionality; subgroup proof fields are irrelevant.

*Needs:* `IntrinsicBandSections`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CatCenter.ext`.

Prove `bandCenterCommute`. For arbitrary F and U, `s t=t s` in ZF(U). The product is pointwise categorical-center multiplication, with the specified reversed categorical composition convention.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8, final omitted varying-U step).

For the proof, apply componentwise extensionality; then the existing commutativity of the categorical center gives equality of each unit value; no abelian-inertia assumption is needed for central sections themselves.

*Needs:* `bandCenterExt`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CatCenter.mul_app`.

Define `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict`. For `f:V→U` define `r_f`:ZF(U)→ZF(V) by `(r_f s)(W,a)=s(W,a≫f)`. This is a group homomorphism preserving the vertical compatibility equations. Its restriction identities come from base-category identity and associativity, without a choice of fibre pullback object.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Lemma 8.11.8, final omitted varying-U step).

The API gives `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict`: The map `r_f` is reindexing by composition with f; `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict_apply`: `(r_f s)(W,a)=s(W,a≫f)`; `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict_id`: `r_id` is the identity; `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict_comp`: For `g:W→V`, `r_g∘r_f=r_(g≫f)`.

*Needs:* `IntrinsicBandSections`, `bandCenterExt`.

Define `bandCenterEvaluation`. For `a:V→U` and `x∈F(V)`, evaluation `ev_(a,x)`:ZF(U)→`Aut(x)` applies the existing unitsEndEquivAut at the identity functor and then its natural-isomorphism component at x. ### 4.6a Compatible centre carriers

`intrinsicBandSectionSubgroup F U` is the subgroup of slice-indexed centre units satisfying all restriction equations, and `IntrinsicBandSection F U` is its section carrier. Evaluation underlying `IntrinsicBandSections.evalEquiv` is bijective for a gerbe with commutative inertia. The carriers have the intended signatures of §4.24. Its API `IntrinsicBandSections.commGroup`, `IntrinsicBandSections.restrict`, `IntrinsicBandSections.eval` gives commutative pointwise composition, reindexing along a slice arrow, and evaluation at an object. `IntrinsicBandSections.pullbackArrow` names the composite slice arrow used by that reindexing. The presheaf `IntrinsicBandSections.presheaf` packages these groups and restriction maps. With gerbe locality and commutative inertia, `IntrinsicBandSections.evalEquiv` identifies the compatible family with the automorphism group of a chosen object over U, evaluated at the identity arrow of U. The subgroup and its commutativity do not require gerbe locality; bijectivity of evaluation does. (The endomorphism interchange calculation, followed by Hom-sheaf descent in §§4.6–4.7.)

The intrinsic band has the further API: `IntrinsicBandSections.eval_surjective` (for a gerbe whose
automorphism groups are commutative, evaluation at an object over `U` is surjective; with
`IntrinsicBandSections.eval_injective` it gives the group isomorphism `IntrinsicBandSections.evalEquiv`,
computed by `IntrinsicBandSections.evalEquiv_apply`); `IntrinsicBandSections.coefficient_naturality`
(the automorphisms specified by a banding commute with every fibre arrow);
`IntrinsicBandSections.coefficientCenter_restrict` (the central unit of a band coefficient restricts by
the band pullback equation); `IntrinsicBandSections.fromBanding_ext` (a compatible central family is
the one induced by a band coefficient when all its evaluations are the band automorphisms of that
coefficient); `IntrinsicBandSections.fromBanding_ne_of_aut_ne` (bandings whose automorphisms differ at
some coefficient and object give different central families; no quotient by coefficient symmetries is
taken); `IntrinsicBandSections.band_unique` (for an `A`-banded gerbe there is a unique isomorphism
`A ≅ IntrinsicBandSections.sheaf F J` compatible with evaluation, glued even where `F(U)` is empty);
and `IntrinsicBandSections.centerFamily_congr` (a family indexed by a covering sieve depends only on
the arrow, not on the proof that it lies in the sieve).

**Checks.**

- `BandCenterTests.C3`: On the one-object point-site gerbe `B(C3)`, there are three central sections, with evaluation recovering all of C3.
- `BandCenterTests.identity`: For the terminal fibre groupoid, the group of compatible central sections is trivial.
- `BandCenterTests.S3`: For `B(S3)` on a point, sections form the trivial center of S3, rather than all six automorphisms. Thus evaluation onto inertia fails without abelian inertia.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.composition`: successive restriction equals restriction along the composite slice arrow.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.conjugation`: changing the object transports evaluation by conjugation.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.coefficient`: the nonidentity cyclic-three coefficient survives evaluation.

### 4.7 Cover comparison and conjugation

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C is a fixed small category with Grothendieck topology J; F is the Cat-valued pseudofunctor, and every automorphism group of every fibre object is commutative. All indexed families use sufficiently large fixed universes; Fix U and actual objects x,y in `F(U)`. R is a sieve on U, indexed by its `R.arrows.category`, and `e_i:F(i)^*x ≅ F(i)^*y` is given at each of its arrows. The choices `e_i` need not form an isomorphism of descent data. No terminal object, fibre products, chosen coefficient sheaf, banding or global neutrality assumption is made; F satisfies the existing IsPrestack J condition, and R belongs to `J(U)`. Only morphism descent is used; object-effectivity and groupoid fibres are not additional hypotheses.

Prove `IntrinsicBandSections.coverTransition`. Let R be any sieve on U. For each arrow i:`V_i`→U in its arrow category take `z_i`∈ZF(`V_i`), with `r_g(z_j)=z_i` for every arrow `g:i→j` in that category. Fix `x∈F(U)`. For every common test object Y and arrows `f:Y`→`V_i`,`g:Y→V_j` with f≫`i=g`≫`j=q`, the two pulled-back evaluated homs commute with the actual transition of the canonical descent datum of x. No cover, prestack, groupoid or abelian-inertia assumption is needed.

### 4.8 Constant, connected and varying restriction fixtures

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C is an arbitrary category and `P:C` opposite to CommGrpCat is an actual presheaf; it need not be constant. Fibres are the existing SingleObj categories, with actual coefficient homomorphisms and coherence; The generic section equivalence uses no topology or terminal object. Stack and gerbe assertions use exactly the bottom topology. Presheaf/sheaf isomorphisms explicitly require a small base B:Type; coefficient groups retain their own universe; The finite fixtures use opposite Fin3 and opposite (Fin3 plus Fin3), with C4 to C2 reduction followed by the C2 identity; no higher-topology, nonneutral or derived-H2 assertion follows.

Define `BandedIsom.act`. For `p:x≅y` and a in the multiplicative tag of `A(U)`, act(p,a) is p followed by the actual band automorphism `b_y(a)`. No global isomorphism or neutralization is chosen.

Here An arbitrary specified site `(C,J)`, an actual Cat-valued pseudofunctor F with the existing IsGerbe condition, and a specified AbelianBanding of F by the abelian sheaf A. No bottom-topology, finite, terminal-object or neutralization hypothesis is imposed; The coefficient and fibre-hom types use the same explicit universe `v′` for these sheaves; object and base universes are arbitrary. UniverseNormalizedGerbe supplies the independently sized comparison; All arrows and restriction maps are those of the existing categories. Global nonemptiness is required only by the section-torsor constructor; a chosen anchor is required only by coordinateEquiv.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, Lemma 31.3 and Remark 31.5, PDF pp.122–123; library deductions specified here).

The API gives `BandedIsom.act_one`: act(p,1)=p; multiplicative one is additive zero; `BandedIsom.act_mul`: act(p,`a*c`)=act(act(p,c),a), retaining the reversed-composition convention for automorphisms; `BandedIsom.act_precompose`: Postcomposition of p with `b_y(a)` equals precomposition with `b_x(a)`, using the stored conjugation equation.

*Needs:* `AbelianBanding`.

**Checks.**

- `BandedIsom.Tests.zeroAction`: The additive-zero coefficient fixes an arbitrary actual isomorphism.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.actionOrder`: Two successive actions use the automorphism multiplication order.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.precomposition`: Postcomposition and precomposition use the same band coefficient.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.composition`: Composition with y to z preserves the same action coefficient.

### 4.8a Fixture indexing and restriction maps

`BandFixtures.constantDiagram C G` is the constant category-valued pseudofunctor. Its API uses `constantSection`, `constantSectionsEquiv` and fibre evaluation to compare compatible central families with centre units. `BandFixtures.Fibre I G` is the product of the discrete groupoid on I and BG. `ConnectedBandFixtures.ConnectedFibre I G` uses the codiscrete groupoid instead, with a chosen index for any assertion requiring nonemptiness. Their APIs are `componentCenterEquiv`, `componentSectionsEquiv`, `connectedCenterEquiv`, `connectedSectionsEquiv`; disconnected centres have one coordinate per component, whereas the connected fixture has one central coordinate. (Direct category and centre calculations in §4.8.)

**Checks.**

- `BandCenterTests.C3`: On the one-object point-site gerbe `B(C3)`, there are three central sections, with evaluation recovering all of C3.
- `BandCenterTests.identity`: For the terminal fibre groupoid, the group of compatible central sections is trivial.
- `BandPointTests.mixedDisconnectedCardinality`: on the point site, `B(C₃)`⊔`B(C₃)` has nine sections, and `B(S₃)`⊔`B(C₃)` has three. Both fail gerbe local isomorphism, so neither satisfies the gerbe hypotheses of the cardinality examples.
- `ConnectedBandTests.cardinality`: The actual compatible-section type for that two-object C3 gerbe has exactly three elements.

`RestrictionBandFixtures.reduction` is `C₄→C₂`. `RestrictionBandFixtures.chainGroups` is `C₄→C₂→C₂`; `RestrictionBandFixtures.ChainSite` is the opposite three-object chain; `RestrictionBandFixtures.chainPresheaf` and `RestrictionBandFixtures.chainF` are its group presheaf and one-object groupoid pseudofunctor. `RestrictionBandFixtures.U₀`, `RestrictionBandFixtures.U₁`, `RestrictionBandFixtures.U₂` name its three objects and `RestrictionBandFixtures.f₀₁`, `RestrictionBandFixtures.f₁₂`, `RestrictionBandFixtures.f₀₂` the reduction arrow, identity restriction arrow and their composite. The API `chain_generator_restrict`, `chain_generator_comp`, `chain_two_killed` computes their actual coordinate maps. `RestrictionBandFixtures.TwoChainSite` is the disjoint union of two such sites; `RestrictionBandFixtures.twoChainPresheaf` and `RestrictionBandFixtures.twoChainF` repeat the construction on both components. Their API `twoChains_no_terminal`, `twoChains_sections_equiv`, `twoChains_gerbe` proves the absence of a terminal object, the sectionwise band computation and gerbe locality. Each indexing abbreviation is determined by these objects, arrows and composite computations; it introduces no additional carrier. (Direct finite-category and cyclic-group calculations.)

**Checks.**

- `RestrictionBandTests.sheafRestrictionGenerator`: The additive band-sheaf restriction sends the C4 generator section to the C2 generator section.
- `RestrictionBandTests.restrictionNotInjective`: The actual compatible-section restriction is not injective.
- `RestrictionBandTests.noTerminal`: No object of the actual two-chain site is terminal.
- `RestrictionBandTests.leftChainSourceCard`: The actual section type at the left C4 source has four elements.
- `RestrictionBandTests.rightChainTargetCard`: The actual section type at the right C2 target has two elements.
- `RestrictionBandTests.terminalFreeGerbe`: The actual two-chain varying diagram is a gerbe despite the absence of a terminal site object.

### 4.9 Isom torsors and their actions

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: An arbitrary specified site `(C,J)`, an actual Cat-valued pseudofunctor F with the existing IsGerbe condition, and a specified AbelianBanding of F by the abelian sheaf A. No bottom-topology, finite, terminal-object or neutralization hypothesis is imposed; The coefficient and fibre-hom types use the same explicit universe `v′` for these sheaves; object and base universes are arbitrary. UniverseNormalizedGerbe supplies the independently sized comparison; All arrows and restriction maps are those of the existing categories. Global nonemptiness is required only by the section-torsor constructor; a chosen anchor is required only by coordinateEquiv.

Its underlying presheaf map is the specified principal map; `BandedIsom.principalSheafIso_hom`: The underlying presheaf morphism of principalSheafIso is heterogeneously equal to the explicit principalPresheafIso morphism, retaining their different definitional carrier presentations.

Prove `BandedIsom.hom_localNonempty`. There is a J-covering sieve R on U such that every arrow `f:V→U` in R has a section of Hom(x restricted to V,y restricted to V). This is obtained from local isomorphism and does not assert a global section.

Here A specified arbitrary site `(C,J)`, Cat-valued pseudofunctors F,G with IsGerbe, one actual abelian sheaf A and actual bandings bF,bG; η is the StrongTrans and preserves the fixed band; Coefficients and fibre Hom types share one universe; arbitrary base/object universes are retained. ### 4.9a Actual Hom products

`BandedIsom.coordinateEquiv` identifies the coefficient group with the actual isomorphism set only after an anchor is specified. `BandedIsom.homEquiv` identifies actual isomorphisms with arrows in the groupoid fibre, and `BandedIsom.homAct` is postcomposition with the target's band automorphism. Their API `coordinate_one`, `coordinate_change`, `homPrincipalEquiv_apply`, `pullHom_act` fixes the anchor, its change, the product formula and restricted action. `BandedIsom.pairPresheaf` is the square of the slice Hom presheaf, while `BandedIsom.actionPresheaf` is its product with the restricted band. Their API `principalPresheafIso`, `pair_isSheaf`, `action_isSheaf`, `principalSheafIso` gives the principal comparison and finite-product sheaf descent. No global arrow is needed for these product comparisons; the `BandedIsom.isomTorsor` additionally requires nonempty actual isomorphisms, as a hypothesis on its global section set. (Groupoid arrows and finite products of Hom sheaves, §4.9.)

**Checks.**

- `BandedIsom.Tests.noPointCreated`: If the actual global isomorphism type is empty, its product with coefficients remains empty.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.homUsesActualArrow`: The `Hom-Isom` equivalence sends p to its actual hom arrow.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.changedAnchor`: The difference from p to q is the coordinate of q in the trivialization based at p.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.pairSheafNative`: The actual Hom-pair presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition on J over U.
- `BandedIsom.Tests.sheafLeft`: The principal sheaf morphism followed by its inverse is the identity on the action sheaf.

Their local existence does not provide a global anchor.; Coefficients and fibre Hom types share one universe; arbitrary base/object universes are retained. No resizing, bottom-topology, finite, terminal-object or neutralization assumption is made..

Prove `BandPreserving.comp`. The vertical composite of two transformations preserving the same fixed band preserves that band; the component automorphism equation is the composite of the two given equations.

Prove `BandedMorphism.map_difference`. differenceG(mapIso(p),mapIso(q))=differenceF(p,q) for actual p,`q:x≅y`. Apply map_act to actF(p,differenceF(p,q))=q and then the target difference cancellation law.

Define `BandedMorphism.preimageIso`. Given an actual `p:x≅y` and target q:ηU(x)≅ηU(y), preimageIso(p,q)=actF(p,differenceG(mapIso(p),q)). The anchor is required data, never inferred from local nonemptiness.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, PDF pp.122–123; authored actual-functor deductions).

The API gives `BandedMorphism.map_preimageIso`: mapIso(preimageIso(p,q))=q, by action compatibility and the target difference-action cancellation. This works for every target isomorphism once the actual source anchor is supplied; `BandedMorphism.preimageIso_map`: preimageIso(p,mapIso(q))=q for actual p,`q:x≅y`, using unchanged difference coefficients and source action cancellation; `BandedMorphism.preimageIso_anchor`: For any actual anchors p,`p′` and target q, preimageIso(p,q)=preimageIso(`p′`,q). Both map to q, and mapIso is injective. No choice of a global anchor is made; `BandedMorphism.preimageIso_act`: preimageIso(p,actG(q,a))=actF(preimageIso(p,q),a), by mapIso injectivity, the inverse law and the forward action equation; `BandedMorphism.preimageIso_id`: For the identity StrongTrans, preimageIso(p,q)=q for every actual source anchor p and actual q, using the identity band-preservation proof and the source inverse law; `BandedMorphism.preimageIso_comp`: For band-preserving `η:F→G` and `θ:G→H`, preimageIso for `θ∘η` at p equals preimageIso for η at p applied to preimageIso for θ at ηU.mapIso(p). Composition uses the actual StrongTrans and functor mapIso, with no surrogate transformation carrier.

- `BandedMorphism.Tests.independentAnchor`: Two actual source anchors give the same preimage of every target isomorphism.
- `BandedMorphism.Tests.emptySourceNotFilled`: An empty global source Isom type supplies no actual anchor for the surjectivity construction.

Prove `BandedMorphism.map_preimageIso`. mapIso(preimageIso(p,q))=q, by action compatibility and the target difference-action cancellation. This works for every target isomorphism once the actual source anchor is supplied.

### 4.11 Strong pullback and Hom sheaves

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: An arbitrary specified site `(C,J)`, Cat-valued pseudofunctors F,G with IsGerbe and one actual abelian sheaf A, with the supplied bandings bF,bG; η is the StrongTrans. The comparison, forward Isom map and forward Hom map are defined without band preservation; the inverse laws, injectivity, equivariance and equivalences assume BandPreserving(bF,bG,η); `f:V→U` and actual x,`y∈F(U)`. Coefficients and fibre Hom types share one universe; base and object universes are arbitrary; An actual source anchor is assumed only where explicitly stated; local nonemptiness is not a global anchor. No finite, neutral, terminal-object, finite-presentation or bottom-topology assumption is imposed.

Define `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`. For `f:V→U` and `x∈F(U)`, `c_f(x)` is the component of Mathlib's strong-naturality isomorphism `η(f):F(f)`⋙ηV≅ηU⋙`G(f)`. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson notes §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, PDF pp.122–123; authored strong-naturality deductions).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison_native`: The component agrees exactly with `Cat.Hom.toNatIso`(η.naturality(f)).app(x); `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison_inv_hom_id`: The inverse comparison followed by its forward comparison is the identity arrow; `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison_band`: Conjugation by `c_f(x)` preserves the specified target-band coefficient.

*Needs:* `BandPreserving`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Cat.Hom.toNatIso`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.nativeComparison`: The component agrees exactly with `Cat.Hom.toNatIso`(η.naturality(f)).app(x).
- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.zeroComparison`: The inverse comparison followed by its forward comparison is the identity arrow.
- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.comparisonBand`: Conjugation by `c_f(x)` preserves the specified target-band coefficient.

Define `GerbeMorphismPullback.mapIso`. For `p:F(f)x≅F(f)y` define `M_f(p)=c_f(y)` ∘ ηV(p) ∘ `c_f(x)`⁻¹, an isomorphism `G(f)`(ηUx)≅`G(f)`(ηUy). Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson notes §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, PDF pp.122–123; authored strong-naturality deductions).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismPullback.mapIso_hom`: For actual local `p:F(f)x≅F(f)y`, the hom arrow of `M_f(p)` is exactly `h_f`(`p.hom`), including both strong-naturality comparison components; `GerbeMorphismPullback.mapIso_restrict`: For every actual global `p:x≅y`, `M_f`(`F(f)`.mapIso(p))=`G(f)`.mapIso(ηU.mapIso(p)). The equality is between actual isomorphisms, not classes; `GerbeMorphismPullback.mapIso_act`: For fixed-band η, actual local `p:F(f)x≅F(f)y` and `a∈A(V)`, `M_f`(actF(p,a))=actG(`M_f(p)`,a). The coefficient is unchanged in `A(V)`, even when `c_f(y)` is not an identity.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.reflexiveImage`: The image of the actual identity isomorphism is the identity at `G(f)`(ηUx).
- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.actualHomImage`: The hom arrow of the transported Isom image equals the transported Hom image.
- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.globalIsoRestriction`: For global actual `p:x≅y`, `M_f(F(f)p)=G(f)(ηU(p))`.

Define `GerbeMorphismPullback.homMap`. For `p:F(f)x→F(f)y`, `h_f(p)=c_f(x)`.inv ≫ ηV.map(p) ≫ `c_f(y)`.hom lands in `G(f)`(ηUx)→`G(f)`(ηUy). Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson notes §31, Definition 31.1 and Lemma 31.3, PDF pp.122–123; authored strong-naturality deductions).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismPullback.homMap_restrict`: For any global actual arrow `p:x→y`, `h_f`(`F(f)`.map(p))=`G(f)`.map(ηU.map(p)). This is naturality of the strong-naturality isomorphism at p; it does not prove compatibility along arbitrary deeper slice arrows; `GerbeMorphismPullback.homMap_injective`: For fixed-band η, `h_f` is injective on the actual Hom carrier for every f,x,y, without an anchor; `GerbeMorphismPullback.homMap_surjective_of_anchor`: For fixed-band η and actual local `p:F(f)x≅F(f)y`, `h_f` is surjective on the actual Hom carrier. The target arrows are invertible by IsGerbe(G,J), so the transported Isom inverse provides their actual preimage hom arrows.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.presheafHom`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.identityHomImage`: The actual identity arrow maps to the actual target identity arrow.
- `GerbeMorphismPullback.Tests.globalHomRestriction`: For a global actual arrow `p:x→y`, `h_f(F(f)p)=G(f)(ηU(p))`.

Base and fibre-object universes are not restricted.

Reuse this theorem; generic sheaf gluing is Mathlib’s sheaf condition; then this step needs the naturality already established for arbitrary slice arrows. Local anchored bijections without that naturality would not supply a sheaf morphism to which the theorem applies.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismPullback.homSheafMap_locallySurjective`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.homSheafMap_locallyInjective`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso`.

### 4.12 Object descent and inverse bandings

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C is an arbitrary category, J its specified Grothendieck topology, and F,G actual Cat-valued pseudofunctors on LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ with strong transformation η. The gerbe hypothesis supplies stack descent, local nonemptiness and local isomorphism, and groupoid fibres; no terminal object, finite site or pullbacks in C are assumed; For component full-faithfulness, lifted overlaps, source descent, and global essential surjectivity, bF and bG are actual bandings by the same sheaf A and η preserves that band. The coefficient sheaf is A : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.`{v′}`. The universeNormalizedGerbe comparison in 4.21 transports this normalized case to independently specified coefficient universes; For overlap and image constructions the family `f_i`, actual local objects `x_i` and image isomorphisms `e_i` are inputs. An actual gluing isomorphism r is input only to the local/global image-of-gluing operations. The generated-sieve covering hypothesis is required for the global image operation. The final global-preimage theorem constructs all these inputs from local gerbe existence and stack effectivity.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful`. For each U construct the FullyFaithful data of the component functor ηU, using the coefficient universe convention. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement componentFullyFaithful).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful_map_preimage`: Mapping `componentFullyFaithful.preimage(p)` by ηU gives p for every arrow between actual image objects; `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful_preimage_map`: The inverse recovers every source arrow from its ηU image; `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful_map_injective`: Equality of images of any two actual source arrows reflects their equality.

*Needs:* `BandedMorphism.full`, `BandedMorphism.faithful`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.ofFullyFaithful`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.arrowRoundTrip`: Every arbitrary arrow between image objects is recovered by mapping the preimage.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.sourceRoundTrip`: For any source arrow p, preimage of ηU.map(p) is p; a constant inverse on Hom types fails this test.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.nonidentityAutomorphism`: A nonidentity source endomorphism remains nonidentity under ηU; forgetting a nontrivial stabilizer fails this test.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve`. For z in `G(U)`, construct the sieve Lz whose arrows `f:V→U` admit an object x in `F(V)` and an isomorphism ηV(x)≅`G(f)(z)`. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement localImageSieve).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_mem`: Membership f∈Lz is equivalent to existence of x in `F(V)` and Nonempty(ηV(x)≅`G(f)z`); `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_covering`: For two gerbes on the specified arbitrary site, Lz belongs to `J(U)`; band preservation is not needed for this local existence step; `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_identity`: The identity of U belongs to Lz exactly when there is y in `F(U)` with an actual isomorphism ηU(y)≅z.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sieve`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.membershipData`: At every base arrow, membership retains both a source object and an actual target isomorphism.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.deeperImage`: A local-image arrow stays in the sieve after every precomposition, including arrows not selected in the initial cover.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.identityImage`: Membership of id U is a global object-and-isomorphism witness through `G.mapId`; being covering alone is not used.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_covering`. For two gerbes on the specified arbitrary site, Lz belongs to `J(U)`; band preservation is not needed for this local existence step.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement localImageSieve_covering).

For the proof, choose a covering sieve R from `F.locallyNonempty`. For each `f:V→U` in R, choose x in `F(V)`; then apply `G.locallyIsomorphic` to ηV(x) and `G(f)z`. Its covering sieve S on V consists of arrows g along which the two target objects become isomorphic; then use `c_g(x)` and the `G.mapComp′` comparison as in downward closure to show `S≤Lz.pullback(f)`. Superset covering makes `Lz.pullback(f)` cover V; then apply `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` to R and Lz. This proves that the local-image sieve is covering. Global lifting in `GerbeMorphismDescent.global_preimage` uses band-preserving full faithfulness to lift the descent arrows and their cocycle before applying stack effectivity.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_mem`, `IsGerbe`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.transitive`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.superset_covering`.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso`. For a family `f_i:X_i→U`, objects `x_i` in `F(X_i)`, and `e_i:η_i(x_i)≅G(f_i)z`, construct an isomorphism ηY(`F(a)x_i`)≅ηY(`F(b)x_j`) on every common test object `q:Y→U` with a≫`f_i=q=b`≫`f_j`. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement targetOverlapIso).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_formula`: The target overlap is `c_a(x_i)`, then `G(a)(e_i)`, then the ofObj(z) overlap, then `G(b)(e_j)` inverse, then `c_b(x_j)` inverse; `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_self`: For `i=j` and `a=b` the targetOverlapIso is the identity isomorphism; `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_comp`: For three local indices i,j,k and maps a,b,c over the same q, the i-to-j overlap followed by the j-to-k overlap equals the i-to-k overlap.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData.ofObj`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData.iso`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescentTests.localNotGlobal`: over ℝ, `B1→B(C₂)` has covering local-image sieve for the torsor `Spec ℂ`, but no global preimage: its only image is the trivial torsor. The morphism does not preserve a common band.

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.selfOverlap`: For the same local index and base arrow, the complete five-factor target comparison cancels to the identity.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.tripleOverlap`: Three distinct local lifts over a common test object satisfy the ordered target cocycle.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.reverseTargetOverlap`: Interchanging the two local lifts reverses the complete target overlap isomorphism.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_self`. For `i=j` and `a=b` the targetOverlapIso is the identity isomorphism.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement targetOverlapIso_self).

For the proof, use the target hom_self law. The outer comparison and image-isomorphism factors cancel with their inverses. Use `Iso.ext` to retain both directions.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_formula`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_comp`. For three local indices i,j,k and maps a,b,c over the same q, the i-to-j overlap followed by the j-to-k overlap equals the i-to-k overlap.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement targetOverlapIso_comp).

For the proof, expand the two five-factor composites. Cancel the intermediate j comparison and image isomorphism; then apply the hom_comp equation of the target ofObj(z) datum; conclude equality of isomorphisms by equality of their forward arrows.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_formula`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso`. Construct the unique isomorphism `F(a)x_i≅F(b)x_j` whose image under ηY is the targetOverlapIso, using the fully faithful component data. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedOverlapIso).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`: ηY.mapIso of the lifted overlap equals the specified target overlap as an actual isomorphism; `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_self`: The lifted overlap from a local object to itself along the same base arrow is the identity isomorphism; `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_comp`: The i-to-j lifted overlap followed by the j-to-k lifted overlap is the i-to-k lifted overlap on every common test object; `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_pullHom`: For `g:Y′→Y`, `q′=g`≫q and specified ga=g≫a, gb=g≫b, `pullHom_F` of the lifted overlap equals the lifted overlap at `q′`,ga,gb, with all base equalities retained.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.preimageIso`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.liftedImage`: Mapping the chosen lifted isomorphism gives the entire target overlap with both comparisons present.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.reflectedCocycle`: The lifted overlap satisfies the actual triple cocycle; lifting arrows independently without faithfulness fails this test.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.reverseLiftedOverlap`: Interchanging source local indices gives the inverse lifted isomorphism, not another arbitrary preimage.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`. ηY.mapIso of the lifted overlap equals the specified target overlap as an actual isomorphism.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedOverlapIso_map).

For the proof, use map_preimage on both forward and inverse components of preimageIso; `Iso.ext` proves the displayed identity.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentFullyFaithful_map_preimage`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_self`. The lifted overlap from a local object to itself along the same base arrow is the identity isomorphism.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedOverlapIso_self).

For the proof, map both forward arrows by ηY and use the target self-overlap equation. Faithfulness reflects their equality, hence equality of isomorphisms.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_self`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.map_injective`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_comp`. The i-to-j lifted overlap followed by the j-to-k lifted overlap is the i-to-k lifted overlap on every common test object.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedOverlapIso_comp).

For the proof, apply ηY.map to the two forward arrows, use `map_comp` and the target cocycle, then reflect equality with the fully faithful component.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_comp`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.map_injective`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_pullHom`. For `g:Y′→Y`, `q′=g`≫q and specified ga=g≫a, gb=g≫b, `pullHom_F` of the lifted overlap equals the lifted overlap at `q′`,ga,gb, with all base equalities retained.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedOverlapIso_pullHom).

For the proof, write `pullHom_F` as source mapComp′ hom, `F(g)` applied to the overlap, then source mapComp′ inv; then map this composite by ηY′. Use naturality of `c_g` on the actual overlap arrow and the incoming `comparison_comp` formula on a,g and b,g. Source mapComp′ terms cancel against the strong-comparison terms; then expand the target five-factor overlap. Naturality of `G.mapComp′` moves `G(g)` applied to `e_i` and `e_j` to G(ga) and G(gb). The target ofObj(z) `pullHom_hom` law replaces the central overlap at q by its overlap at `q′`; then the result is the targetOverlapIso at `q′`,ga,gb. Use `liftedOverlapIso_map` there and reflect equality through ηY′. This varying-base step is required in addition to the triple cocycle.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_formula`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison_comp`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.LocallyDiscreteOpToCat.pullHom`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.map_injective`.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData`. Construct an object of the category `F.DescentData(f)`, with objects `x_i` and overlap morphisms the forward maps of liftedOverlapIso, including all three coherence fields. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement liftedDescentData).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_obj`: The object field of liftedDescentData at i is `x_i`; `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_hom`: For every common test object and pair of indices, the hom field is the forward arrow of the specified liftedOverlapIso; `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_pullHom`: The actual descent-data hom field commutes with every deeper pullHom, with all base equality witnesses retained.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_self`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_comp`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_pullHom`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.retainedLocalObject`: Every object field of the descent datum is the supplied `x_i`, so discarding the local objects fails.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.retainedLocalArrow`: Every overlap morphism is the specified lifted forward arrow, with all base equality witnesses retained.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.varyingBaseDescent`: The lifted datum obeys pullHom under an arbitrary deeper base arrow; a record with only the identity and triple-cocycle laws fails.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso`. Given y in `F(U)` and a descent isomorphism `r:ofObj_F(y)`≅liftedDescentData, construct `G(f_i)(ηU y)≅G(f_i)z` on each chart i. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement imageLocalIso).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_hom`: The forward arrow of imageLocalIso at i is `c_(f_i)(y)` inverse, followed by `η_i`.map(`r.hom.hom(i)`), followed by `e_i.hom`; `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_comm`: The imageLocalIso components satisfy the exact `DescentData.isoMk` comm equation between the target ofObj data of ηU y and z on every common test object; `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_inv`: The inverse arrow is `e_i` inverse, then `η_i` applied to the inverse gluing component, then the forward strong comparison.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_obj`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_hom`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`.

**Checks.**

- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.forwardGluingImage`: The local image starts with the inverse strong comparison, then the image of the forward gluing component, then `e_i`.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.inverseGluingImage`: The inverse local image starts with `e_i` inverse, then `η_i` of the inverse gluing component, then the forward strong comparison.
- `GerbeMorphismDescent.Tests.nativeImageComm`: The chart image isomorphisms obey exactly the target `DescentData.isoMk` comm equation on arbitrary common test objects.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_comm`. The imageLocalIso components satisfy the exact `DescentData.isoMk` comm equation between the target ofObj data of ηU y and z on every common test object.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement imageLocalIso_comm).

For the proof, expand the local forward formula at i and j and the two target ofObj overlap maps; then use the `r.hom.comm` equation in `F(Y)`, then ηY.map and strong naturality for a and b. The composite comparison formulas retain the source and target mapComp′ terms for `f_i`,a and `f_j`,b; then substitute `liftedOverlapIso_map` and the five-factor target formula. The `e_i`,`e_j` and `c_a`,`c_b` factors cancel in the required directions; then what remains is precisely `G(a)(p_i)` followed by the z overlap equals the ηU y overlap followed by `G(b)(p_j)`. This gives an actual target descent isomorphism, not equality of local isomorphism classes.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_hom`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData_hom`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedOverlapIso_map`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.targetOverlapIso_formula`, `GerbeMorphismPullback.comparison_comp`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData.isoMk`.

Define `GerbeMorphismDescent.globalImageIso`. When `Sieve.ofArrows(X,f)` covers U, the given y and Mathlib gluing isomorphism r produce an isomorphism ηU `y≅z`. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), §31 Lemma 31.3, pp. 122–123.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement globalImageIso).

The API gives `GerbeMorphismDescent.globalImageIso_restrict`: Restricting `globalImageIso.hom` by `G(f_i)` gives `imageLocalIso.hom` at every chart i; `GerbeMorphismDescent.globalImageIso_unique`: Any p:ηU `y≅z` whose forward restrictions agree with all the imageLocalIso components equals globalImageIso; `GerbeMorphismDescent.globalImageIso_inv_restrict`: Restricting the inverse global image arrow gives the inverse local image arrow at every chart.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.imageLocalIso_comm`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData.isoMk`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.fullyFaithfulToDescentData`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.preimageIso`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.global_preimage`. For every U and z in `G(U)`, there exists y in `F(U)` together with Nonempty(ηU `y≅z`).

([Martin Olsson (lectures), course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Olsson §31 Lemma 31.3, PDF122–123; authored descent refinement global_preimage).

For the proof, take R=Lz and the actual family of arrows f in `R.arrows.category`. The `ofArrows_category` theorem identifies its generated sieve with R, so it is covering; then for each f in R choose its source object `x_f` and its actual image isomorphism `e_f`, using the membership characterization and classical choice. No global source anchor has been assumed; then build the liftedDescentData. Register F’s `IsStack.essSurj_of_sieve` instance and take objPreimage of this datum; objObjPreimageIso is the actual `r:ofObj_F(y)≅D`; then apply globalImageIso using the covering equality. Return the object y and the actual isomorphism witness; then an empty covering index is legitimate: effectivity still supplies a global source object from the empty descent datum. An empty index without a covering hypothesis gives no conclusion.

*Needs:* `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_covering`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.localImageSieve_mem`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.liftedDescentData`, `GerbeMorphismDescent.globalImageIso`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sieve.ofArrows_category`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.objPreimage`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.objObjPreimageIso`.

Prove `GerbeMorphismDescent.componentIsEquivalence`. The actual ηU is a IsEquivalence functor, using component full faithfulness and the newly specified object descent route.

Prove `GerbeBandEquivalence.fibreNatIso_map_band`. For a fixed test object U, functors P,`Q:F(U)→G(U)`, and a natural isomorphism `e:P≅Q`, suppose `P.mapAut`(bF(U,x)`(a)`)=bG(U,Px)`(a)` for every actual object x and coefficient `a∈A(U)`. Then `Q.mapAut`(bF(U,x)`(a)`)=bG(U,Qx)`(a)`. Conjugation is along the actual component `e_x`, not an equality of objects.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors with groupoid fibres and IsGerbe on J; bF,bG are the specified AbelianBanding data; The coefficient sheaf A lives in an independent universe w; no equation identifying w with the fibre-hom universe is imposed; No global neutralization or terminal object is assumed.

Here A specified site `(C,J)`; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors with groupoid fibres and IsGerbe on J; bF,bG are the specified AbelianBanding data; The coefficient sheaf A lives in an independent universe w; no equation identifying w with the fibre-hom universe is imposed; No global neutralization or terminal object is assumed.

### 4.13 Fixed-band Hom and fibre actions

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C is a fixed small category with topology J; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors with specified object and fibre-morphism universes; F,G have the actual IsGerbe fields, and bF,bG are specified AbelianBanding data for a sheaf A of abelian groups in independent coefficient universe w. The self case uses `F=G` and bF=bG=b; The section Isom carriers need not be nonempty. No terminal object, global neutralization, constant coefficient sheaf, inverse strong transformation or equality `w=v′` is assumed.

Define `BandedMorphism.modificationIso`. For a modification `m:η⇒θ` of strong transformations `F→G` with G a gerbe, construct a modification isomorphism `M(m):η≅θ` whose forward modification is m. Source: Olsson 2007 (Math 274 notes), Definition 31.1, Remarks 31.2/31.5 and Lemma 31.3, p. 122–123; exact Mathlib API specializations..

Here C is a fixed small category with topology J; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors in fixed object and morphism universes; For the modification isomorphism family only G is required to be a gerbe. Fixed-band constructions additionally take IsGerbe `F J`, a specified sheaf A in independent coefficient universe w and actual bandings bF,bG; No terminal object, global neutralization, constant coefficient sheaf, or equality of coefficient and fibre universes is assumed.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), Anton Geraschenko and course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, Remarks 31.2 and 31.5 and Lemma 31.3, printed pp. 122–123; exact API specializations.).

The API gives `BandedMorphism.modificationIso_hom`: For every m, `M(m)`.hom=m as a modification, including every component natural transformation; `BandedMorphism.modificationIso_inv_app`: For every actual test object U and source object x, the `(U,x)` component of `M(m)`.inv equals the inverse of `m(U,x)`; `BandedMorphism.modificationIso_id`: For every η, M(idη) is the identity isomorphism of η; `BandedMorphism.modificationIso_comp`: For composable modifications m and n, `M(m≫n)=M(m)`≪≫`M(n)`. The inverse thus uses reverse composition.

*Needs:* `IsGerbe`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.isoMk`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Cat.Hom.isoMk`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents`.

**Checks.**

- `BandedMorphismTests.modification_forward`: The forward modification of `M(m)` is exactly the supplied m.
- `BandedMorphismTests.modification_inverse_component`: For each U,x the inverse component is the inverse of `m(U,x)`, with both endpoints retained.
- `BandedMorphismTests.modification_composition`: For actual composable m,n the constructed isomorphism of their composite is the composite of their constructed isomorphisms.

Prove `BandedMorphism.modification_iff`. For `m:η⇒θ` between `F→G` and specified bands bF,bG, BandPreserving(bF,bG,η) if and only if BandPreserving(bF,bG,θ). No additional IsIso(m) assumption is required because G is a gerbe.

Here C is a fixed small category with topology J; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors in fixed object and morphism universes; For the modification isomorphism family only G is required to be a gerbe. Fixed-band constructions additionally take IsGerbe `F J`, a specified sheaf A in independent coefficient universe w and actual bandings bF,bG; No terminal object, global neutralization, constant coefficient sheaf, or equality of coefficient and fibre universes is assumed.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), Anton Geraschenko and course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, Remarks 31.2 and 31.5 and Lemma 31.3, printed pp. 122–123; exact API specializations.).

For the proof, apply `GerbeBandEquivalence.modificationIso_iff` to `M(m)`. The reverse implication uses its inverse.

*Needs:* `BandedMorphism.modificationIso`, `GerbeBandEquivalence.modificationIso_iff`.

Define `BandedMorphism.HomCategory`. For A-banded gerbes (F,bF),(G,bG), take the full subcategory of Mathlib StrongTrans(F,G) on the property BandPreserving(bF,bG,η). Its objects are strong transformations with that property; its arrows are all Mathlib modifications between them, with their inherited identity and composition. No quotient of objects or arrows is taken.

Here C is a fixed small category with topology J; F,G are Cat-valued pseudofunctors in fixed object and morphism universes; For the modification isomorphism family only G is required to be a gerbe. Fixed-band constructions additionally take IsGerbe `F J`, a specified sheaf A in independent coefficient universe w and actual bandings bF,bG; No terminal object, global neutralization, constant coefficient sheaf, or equality of coefficient and fibre universes is assumed.

([Martin Olsson (lectures), Anton Geraschenko and course-note contributors](https://stacky.net/files/written/Stacks/Stacks.pdf), Definition 31.1, Remarks 31.2 and 31.5 and Lemma 31.3, printed pp. 122–123; exact API specializations.).

The API gives `BandedMorphism.mk`: An actual band-preserving transformation with its specified band property is an object of the fixed-band full subcategory; `BandedMorphism.homMk`: Every actual underlying modification between fixed-band objects packages as an arrow of the full subcategory; `BandedMorphism.forget`: The inclusion functor forgets only the fixed-band object property and retains every modification; `BandedMorphism.forget_fullyFaithful`: The inclusion of the fixed-band full subcategory has the existing fully faithful data of `ObjectProperty.fullyFaithfulι`; `BandedMorphism.hom_ext`: For m,`n:X⇒Y` in the fixed-band category, equality of their underlying natural transformations at every U implies `m=n`; `BandedMorphism.modification_iff`: For `m:η⇒θ` between `F→G` and specified bands bF,bG, BandPreserving(bF,bG,η) if and only if BandPreserving(bF,bG,θ). No additional IsIso(m) assumption is required because G is a gerbe.
