### 4.18 Global Hom and chart independence

Standing hypotheses for this subsection, unless a target states its own setting: C has object universe u and morphism universe v, J is any Grothendieck topology, and F is an actual Cat-valued pseudofunctor with fibre object universe `u′` and morphism universe `v′`, equipped with IsGerbe `F J`; b is an actual abelian banding by A:Sheaf(J,AddCommGrpCat) in an independent coefficient universe w. X,Y,Z and their modifications belong to the existing HomCategory(b,b). No global object, neutrality, strictification of F, nonempty fibre, or chosen coherent isomorphism system is assumed; Raw presheaves take values in Type(max(`u′`,`v′`)); global sheaves use the explicit ULift to Type(max(u,v,`u′`,`v′`)). The local Hom-sheaf comparison and torsor structures remain requirements, not assumptions hidden in these constructions.

Define `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbitSetoid`. For U in C and X in HomCategory(b,b), put Mathlib's Setoid on pairs `(x,p)`, where x belongs to `F(U)` and `p:x≅X_U(x)`. Source: Stacks, Section 8.11/tag 06NY, Definition 8.11.1 and Lemma 8.11.8; exact.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06NY), Stacks Section 8.11/tag 06NY, Definition 8.11.1 and Lemma 8.11.8; exact fixed-band orbit equations are authored deductions.).

The API gives `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbit_mk_eq`: The classes of arbitrary pairs `(x,p)` and `(y,q)` in the quotient are equal if and only if some `e:x≅y` transports p to q. This is an existence statement and chooses no isomorphism; `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbit_mk_injective`: For each actual x in `F(U)`, the function `p↦[(x,p)]` from isomorphisms `x≅X_U(x)` to chart-pair classes is injective. No global object of the gerbe is required; `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbit_mk_transport`: For every `e:x≅y` in `F(U)`, the class represented by `(x,p)` equals the class represented by (y,`transport_e(p)`). The witness is the supplied e itself.

*Needs:* `BandedMorphism.selfTransportActionIso`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportActionIso_id`, `BandedMorphism.selfTransportActionIso_comp`.

**Checks.**

- `GlobalHomTests.transport_chain`: Two consecutive actual transports give the same quotient class as the initial representative.
- `GlobalHomTests.unequal_arrows`: A supplied pair of distinct isomorphisms at the same chart remains distinct in the raw quotient; existence of such a pair on every gerbe is not asserted.
- `GlobalHomTests.empty_fibre`: An empty fibre forces an empty raw presheaf section carrier. No emptiness of its sheafification is asserted.

### 4.18a Orbit and modification carriers

`BandedMorphism.HomCategory` is the full category of strong transformations preserving the specified common band; its arrows are all modifications. Its API `BandedMorphism.homIso`, `BandedMorphism.hom_isIso`, `BandedMorphism.groupoid` records pointwise inverse modifications. `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbitSetoid` identifies (x,`p:x`≅Xx) with simultaneous transport along a fibre isomorphism; `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbitPresheaf` and `BandedMorphism.selfHomOrbitFunctor` retain base restriction and every modification. Their API `selfHomOrbitRestrict`, `selfHomOrbitMap`, `selfHomGlobalSheafFunctor`, `selfHomChartGlobalIso` is the quotient restriction, the modification action, universe-lifted sheafification and slice chart comparison. The last comparison uses the displayed sheafification/local-bijection assumptions at independent universes; at matched fibre and site universes the instance supplies those assumptions. The intended carriers `GerbeLimitFamily` and `GerbeLimitFamily.Hom` have the componentwise category and evaluation; `GerbeLimitFamily.Hom` stores every stage arrow and its transition square; its API `GerbeLimitFamily.Hom.component`, `GerbeLimitFamily.Hom.naturality`, `GerbeLimitFamily.hom_ext`, `GerbeLimitFamily.evaluation_map` retains the family morphisms. (The transport equations of §§4.15–4.18 and sheafification's universal property.)

**Checks.**

- `GlobalHomTests.unequal_arrows`: A supplied pair of distinct isomorphisms at the same chart remains distinct in the raw quotient; existence of such a pair on every gerbe is not asserted.
- `GlobalHomTests.empty_fibre`: An empty fibre forces an empty raw presheaf section carrier. No emptiness of its sheafification is asserted.
- `GlobalHomTests.inverse_modification`: The actual orbit-presheaf natural transformation for a modification followed by its inverse recovers each section.
- `ChartGlobalTests.matched_universes`: When F has the same fibre object and morphism universes as the base category, the instance proves IsIso for the actual chart map with no WEqualsLocallyBijective hypothesis in the test statement; the coefficient universe stays independent.
- `GerbeLimitChecks.composition`: composition of compatible families is componentwise composition.

### 4.19 Affine stabilizer quotients

Define `affineFactorExistence`. For `f:Γ→Δ` between affine fpqc gerbes over a field, define the canonical factorization `Γ→E→Δ` by dividing each affine Isom torsor by the kernel of its map to Δ. The first arrow is locally full and the second faithful; the factorization and its two-cell comparison are unique up to equivalence. The arbitrary-affine quotient and descent proof is in §4.22.

The API consists of `affineGerbeFactor.locallyFull` identifies the first Isom-map with the quotient epimorphism; `affineGerbeFactor.faithful` identifies the second map with its kernel-free inclusion; `affineGerbeFactor.universal` compares any locally-full/faithful factorization by a unique compatible equivalence; `affineGerbeFactor.baseChange` transports the entire two-arrow factorization and its comparison to every field extension.

**Checks.**

- `AffineFactorChecks.trivial` a map of terminal gerbes has terminal middle gerbe
- `AffineFactorChecks.quotient` BC₄→BC₂ has kernel `C₂` and middle gerbe BC₂
- `AffineFactorChecks.identity` the identity BC₂→BC₂ keeps BC₂ and has trivial kernel.
(Borne–Vistoli, Fundamental gerbes, Proposition 3.9 and proof, pp. 8–9; the arbitrary-affine proofs and tests are in §4.22.)
*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 quotient and stackification, the arbitrary-affine group quotient of §4.22.

### 4.20 Derived classification on arbitrary sites

Work in the sheaf topos of a small site, using its terminal sheaf 1; when the original site has a terminal object this is the usual base. A gerbe on a site without such an object is evaluated on the canonical sheaf-topos site. Define `toposSiteGerbeComparison` as the equivalence induced by this change of presentation, including its equivalences on abelian sheaves, torsors and derived global sections. Effective descent and restriction are transported through this equivalence. Thus no existence of fibre products in the original site is silently required.

The derived input `torsorDerivedH1` is SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3's `NonabelianH1.equivSheafH` for the abelian sheaf A, imported and not rebuilt: it sends the class of an A-torsor P to the class of its associated extension `0→A→E(P)→ℤ→0`, where `E(P)` is the sheaf generated by the points of P modulo the affine A-action relations and the fibre of `E(P)` over 1 is P; it is natural in A and compatible with §2.3's `pullback` and `connecting`. Two extensions are proved here. `torsorDerivedH1.add`: contracted product of torsors corresponds to addition in `H¹(1,A)`, because `E(P×ᴬQ)` is the Baer sum of `E(P)` and `E(Q)`. `torsorDerivedH1.slice`: for an object U the localization `C/U→C` is a morphism of sites, and §2.3's `pullback` compatibility identifies the comparison on `C/U` with the restriction of the comparison on C, compatibly with `torsorDerivedH1.add`. Injective torsor triviality follows: for injective A, Mathlib `Abelian.Ext.eq_zero_of_injective` splits `E(P)`, so P has a global point (§2.3's `mk_eq_one_iff`). The comparison is therefore derived cohomology, not a presumption that a fixed Čech cover computes it. (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3; Stacks, Lemma 21.4.3, tag 03AJ.)

Prove `sliceRestriction_preservesInjective` using the exact extension-by-zero left adjoint on abelian sheaves for the localization to a slice: it takes fibrewise direct sums and is exact, as checked locally on sections. Prove `coverUnit_mono` for an epimorphism `U→1` by the sheaf condition. The direct image J of `I|U` is injective because restriction is exact and direct image is its right adjoint. The injection `I→J` splits by injectivity of I, and `Q=J/I` is injective.

These facts give `injectiveGerbe_neutral` without assuming classification. Choose `x∈G(U)` on a cover `U→1`. The stack of pairs `(y,φ)`, with `y∈G(V)` and `φ:y|(V×U)≅x|(V×U)`, has no nonidentity automorphism: its automorphism kernel is that of `I(V)→I(V×U)`, which is zero. It is therefore a sheaf P. On any slice where y exists, its Isom torsor on `U×V` is trivial since I restricts to an injective there. Consequently P is locally inhabited and is a Q-torsor: changing φ acts by J, and changing y by an I-automorphism identifies exactly I. The preceding injective-torsor argument gives a global section of P, hence a global object of G. This is the split-monomorphism route in Milne, Étale Cohomology, Chapter IV §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, item `(i″)`, p. 9; the quotient-sheaf and slice-exactness steps above are explicit targets needed to complete that sketch.

For `u:A→B` define `changeBand` by replacing every local Isom A-torsor with its contracted B-torsor and stackifying. Composition is induced by addition in B; the old composition compatibility and associativity descend to the contracted products. Its API is `changeBand.unit`, `changeBand.compose`, `changeBand.slice`, `changeBand.map`, `changeBand.mapModification`, `changeBand.band`, `changeBand.isGerbe`. The slice comparison preserves its unit and composition modifications. In particular a map of bands need not be an isomorphism and need not yield a fully faithful map of the old gerbes.

For `0→A→B→D→0` and a left D-torsor P, define `liftingGerbe P` by pairs `(E,α)`, where E is a left B-torsor and `α:E`×ᴮD≅P. Its arrows are actual equivariant B-torsor isomorphisms commuting with α. Its band is the **positive** translation by A. Prove `liftingGerbe.isGerbe`, `liftingGerbe.band`, `liftingGerbe.neutral_iff_lift`, `liftingGerbe.slice`, `liftingGerbe.class_eq_boundary`. Local lifts exist by locally trivializing P; two lifts become isomorphic locally; their automorphism kernel is A. If I is injective, the long exact sequence identifies `δ:H¹(I/A)≅H²(A)`.

To construct `gerbeClass`, extend F along `A↪I` and choose z in the neutralized I-gerbe. Let `P_z` be the sheaf of isomorphism classes of pairs `(x,φ:z|V→j(x))`, with arrows `h:x→y` satisfying `j(h)φ=ψ`. Postcomposition by I induces the simply transitive `D=I/A`-action. Define class(F)=`δ[P_z]`. The orientation `z→j(x)` is material: the torsor `E_x=Isom(z,j(x))` has its positive I-action by postcomposition, an A-automorphism of x acts by positive translation, and `E_x/A≅P_z`. These data define a band-preserving equivalence `gerbeToLifting : F≃liftingGerbe(P_z)`. Local full faithfulness is the Isom-torsor comparison; local essential surjectivity follows by trivializing a lift and taking a local x; stack descent makes the equivalence global. Conversely the quotient torsor of `liftingGerbe P` identifies with P, so `class_liftingGerbe` is exactly `δ[P]`. Prove `liftingGerbe_class` and `class_liftingGerbe`, then independence of z and I by a common injective refinement and the natural connecting-map square. They induce the bijection `gerbeClassification`; class zero is precisely neutrality, contracted sum is addition, and band/site change commutes with class. Sources: Milne IV §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, items (i), (i′) and (i″), pp. 8–9; Breen, (2.13.4) and Proposition 2.14, pp. 55–57, with the hypercover distinction in §2.3, pp. 36–38. Breen's topological presentation alone is not used to assert that one ordinary cover computes arbitrary-site derived `H²`.

**Checks.**

- `ClassificationChecks.zeroBand`: `A=0` gives the terminal gerbe, unique class and unique lift. It rules out retaining a spurious set of neutralization choices.
- `ClassificationChecks.positiveBoundary`: with integer lifts `b₀₁=2`, `b₁₂=3`, `b₀₂=1`, the additive boundary is `b₀₁+b₁₂−b₀₂=4`, and replacing the lifts by `bᵢⱼ+aⱼ−aᵢ` leaves this value unchanged. Using `Isom(j(x),z)` with the same positive band would instead produce the opposite class.
- `ClassificationChecks.rootDegree`: for algebraically closed k, `n>1` invertible in k, the root gerbe of `O(1)` on `P¹` has class 1 modulo n and no global object; `O(n)` has the root `O(1)` and class zero. For `n=1` both are neutral.
- `ClassificationChecks.torsorLift`: on the classifying topos of `C₂`, use constant coefficients `0→ℤ→ℤ→ℤ/2→0`, the first map ×2. The trivial `ℤ/2`-torsor lifts. The regular `C₂`-set is the nontrivial torsor; it cannot lift because every homomorphism `C₂→ℤ` is zero. Its boundary is the nonzero element of `H²(C₂,ℤ)=ℤ/2`. This distinguishes local existence of objects from neutrality.

### 4.21 Intrinsic band on slices

For a gerbe F with abelian automorphism sheaves define `intrinsicBand(U)` as the compatible central natural automorphisms of every fibre `F(V)`, indexed by every `V→U`. Restrictions reindex the arrows. If `x∈F(U)`, evaluation at (`id_U`,x) is an isomorphism of sheaves on `C/U` with `Aut(x)`: every component is obtained by choosing a local isomorphism to `x|V` and conjugating; commutativity makes that conjugation independent of the choice. Prove `intrinsicBand.sliceComparison`, `intrinsicBand.restrictionComparison`, `intrinsicBand.tripleRestriction`, `intrinsicBand.evaluation`, `intrinsicBand.fromBand`, `intrinsicBand.fromBand_inverse` and `intrinsicBand.banding`. Morphism-sheaf descent glues the local evaluations, and two restrictions agree on all further slices; this gives the varying-U conclusion omitted in Stacks Lemma 8.11.8 (0CJY). A preselected A-banding is exactly a compatible isomorphism A≅intrinsicBand, rather than a proposition forgetting that isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- `IntrinsicBandChecks.restrictionChain`: on `U←V←W` take coefficient groups ℤ, ℤ and ℤ with restrictions ×2 and ×3; a coefficient 1 restricts to 6 on W through either path. A constant diagram returns 1 and fails.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.nonconstantSlice`: for the coefficient sheaf `μ₃` on the étale site of ℝ, its ℝ-sections have one element and its ℂ-sections have three. Evaluation recovers these respective automorphism groups of the corresponding neutral torsor objects.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.nonneutral`: the `μ₂`-root gerbe of `O(1)` on `P¹` in characteristic ≠2 has no global object but its intrinsic band is `μ₂`, by evaluation after local trivialization. An intrinsic band construction requiring a global x fails.
- `IntrinsicBandChecks.disconnectedFailure`: on the point site, `B(C₃)`⊔`B(C₃)` has central-section group `C₃×C₃`. Evaluation at the first object is projection and kills the nonzero profile (0,1). This groupoid is not a gerbe.

Define `CoherentInverse.inverse` on a strong transformation `η:F→G` whose every component is an equivalence. Its component `β_U` is the chosen inverse of `η_U`. For a base arrow `f:V→U`, write functor composites in categorical order, first the left factor and then the right. Its naturality is the mate
`G(f) β_V → β_U η_U G(f) β_V → β_U F(f) η_V β_V → β_U F(f)`:
the first arrow inserts the inverse counit at U, the second uses the inverse of `η's` naturality isomorphism, and the third removes the unit at V. Associators are the Cat bicategory associators. The identity and composite-arrow equations follow by cancelling adjacent equivalence units and counits; their triangle equations leave precisely `η's` identity and composite equations. The component units and counits therefore form `CoherentInverse.unitIso` and `CoherentInverse.counitIso`, actual invertible modifications. Their two triangle identities are `CoherentInverse.triangleForward` and `CoherentInverse.triangleInverse`, proved componentwise and then by modification extensionality. Johnson–Yau, 2-Dimensional Categories, Lemma 6.1.13, pp. 180–181, and Proposition 6.2.16, pp. 184–185, gives this mate assembly with both modifications. `CoherentInverse.inverse_app`, `CoherentInverse.unitIso_app` and `CoherentInverse.counitIso_app` identify the components with the selected equivalences through the equality-induced object comparisons, retaining their chosen units and counits. Transporting the band through these modifications gives the inverse band-preserving equivalence. Componentwise equivalence supplied by stackification is thus sufficient only **after this assembly**; no coherent inverse is assumed as a new stackification axiom. (Mathlib, `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans`, its naturality identity/composition equations, `StrongTrans.isoMk`, and `Functor.asEquivalence` with its triangle identities.)

**Checks.**

- `CoherentInverseChecks.identity`: on the identity diagram the unit returns every object up to its chosen equivalence unit, including the empty fibre and the one-object trivial groupoid.
- `CoherentInverseChecks.object`: a nontrivial fibre equivalence followed by β returns each object up to the specified unit; recovery is not limited to a chosen neutral object.
- `CoherentInverseChecks.restriction`: for a nonidentity site arrow, `β's` naturality compares the actual two composites `G(f) β_V` and `β_U F(f)`. The mate construction includes both endpoint equivalences, so replacing the site restriction by identity fails the nonconstant `C₄→C₂` fixture.

Define `universeNormalizedGerbe` for independently specified coefficient and fibre-hom universes. Put w equal to the maximum of the site-object, site-arrow, fibre-object, fibre-arrow and coefficient universes. Replace each fibre category by its `ULiftHom` at w (and, when a common small carrier is needed, `AsSmall`), and each coefficient group by its `ULift` at w. The up/down equivalences transport every restriction functor and its identity/composition isomorphisms; band maps are transported group equivalences, with the same conjugation equations. This gives `universeNormalizedGerbe.up`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.down`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.band`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.restriction`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.unit`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.counit`, `universeNormalizedGerbe.torsorComparison` and `universeNormalizedGerbe.cohomologyComparison`. The sheaf condition is unchanged because the up/down equivalences identify matching families and their unique amalgamations. Groupoid descent is unchanged because they identify objects, arrows and cocycles. The coefficient up/down maps form an additive exact equivalence onto the full subcategory of sheaves whose sections admit the specified smaller size; they are not an equivalence with every sheaf in the larger universe. Define cohomology at w for the independent-universe classification. When both universe models support the original derived cohomology and the free abelian sheaves on sheafified representables, with their subobjects, admit the smaller coefficient size, prove `universeLift_preservesInjective` by the generator criterion: the free abelian sheaves on sheafified representables form a generating family, and every subobject of one such generator is still small by the specified size hypothesis. The extension tests for injectivity are therefore the same before and after lifting. Lift a small injective resolution, identify its section groups degree by degree, and obtain `universeNormalizedGerbe.cohomologyComparison`, compatible with connecting homomorphisms. The generator criterion itself follows by extending a map maximally and using a generating object to contradict any nonzero quotient; it introduces no assumption of enough points. Use explicit `HasSheafify` and enough-injective instances at the enlarged universe where a API asks for them. No automatic universe-resizing instance or equality of universes is assumed. All intrinsic-band identities transport along the up/down equivalences; the derived comparison and classification identities transport back from w under the stated generator-size hypothesis, while the statements here are the normalized ones. (Mathlib, `CategoryTheory.ULiftHom.up`, `CategoryTheory.ULiftHom.down`, `CategoryTheory.ULiftHom.equiv`, `AsSmall.equiv`, and the definitions of `Sheaf` and `Pseudofunctor`.)

**Checks.**

- `UniverseChecks.zero`: lifting the zero coefficient group retains its unique element and has inverse down/up maps.
- `UniverseChecks.coefficient`: lifting the generator 1 of `C₃` and then lowering returns 1, and doubling it returns 2; forgetting the group law fails.
- `UniverseChecks.arrows`: for composable category arrows f and g, the lowered composite of their lifted arrows is f≫g; the comparison retains nonidentity restrictions.

### 4.22 Arbitrary affine kernels and gerbe images

Prove `hopfInclusion_faithfullyFlat`: for a field k and an injective morphism `A→B` of **commutative** Hopf k-algebras, B is faithfully flat as an A-module, without finite-type, reducedness, perfection or characteristic-zero assumptions. `Suggested.lean` states `hopfInclusion_faithfullyFlat`. This target and `affineNormalQuotient` below are owned by this roadmap: no group-scheme roadmap states them for affine groups that are not of finite type, and the pinned Tau Ceti has the finite-type, reduced, algebraically closed case `TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.faithfullyFlat_of_dominant`, which is consumed where it applies. A finite set of elements of a commutative Hopf algebra is contained in a finite-type Hopf subalgebra: take a finite-dimensional subcomodule containing the elements and its coefficient coalgebra, then generate by its coefficients and their antipodes (the antipode squares to the identity in this commutative setting). Choose paired finite-type Hopf subalgebras `Aᵢ⊂Bᵢ` containing each finite set of the map's data. Finite-type faithful flatness gives flatness of the filtered union. If a proper ideal of A generated 1 in B, this finite equation would occur at one `Aᵢ⊂Bᵢ` and contradict its faithful flatness. This is Milne, Algebraic Groups, Lie Groups, and their Arithmetic Subgroups, version 3.00 (2011), Theorem 6.43, pp. 69–72, and Corollary 8.25, pp. 104–105. The commutative condition matters; no assertion is made for arbitrary noncommutative Hopf subalgebras.

For a closed normal subgroup N of an arbitrary affine k-group G, the fpqc sheaf quotient `G/N` is an affine group and `G→G/N` is faithfully flat with kernel N. Define `affineNormalQuotient` together with its quotient map and universal property for homomorphisms killing N; its API is `affineNormalQuotient.kernel`, `affineNormalQuotient.faithfullyFlat`, `affineNormalQuotient.fpqcSheaf`, `affineNormalQuotient.baseChange`, `affineNormalQuotient.homEquiv`, `affineNormalQuotient.doubleQuotient`. On Hopf coordinates write `O(G)` as the union of finite-type Hopf subalgebras `Aᵢ`, and let `Nᵢ` be the scheme-theoretic image of N in `Gᵢ=Spec Aᵢ`. It is normal: lift group elements fpqc locally along `G→Gᵢ` and descend conjugation stability. Its ideal is `Aᵢ∩I(N)`. Finite-type normal quotients `Qᵢ=Gᵢ/Nᵢ` form an inverse system. The union of their coordinate Hopf subalgebras defines Q; arbitrary-affine faithful flatness applies to `O(Q)↪O(G)`. The kernel ideal is the union of the extended ideals `Aᵢ∩I(N)`, hence equals `I(N)`, so the kernel is exactly N. The kernel-pair comparison `G×N≅G`×QG identifies Q with the fpqc quotient. This construction does not require an infinite affine group to admit one faithful finite-dimensional representation. Faithfully flat descent identifies its kernel and sheaf universal property. Source: Milne version 3.00, Theorems 8.70, 8.75 and 8.77, pp. 119–121, with §7k, Proposition 7.73, p. 92. Both theorems are exported from here to any later group-scheme consumer; `affineNormalQuotient` is distinct from an unsupported assertion that every nonnormal homogeneous quotient is affine.

Now `affineGerbeImage` has a geometric proof. For `f:Γ→Δ` over k choose an affine fpqc presentation `U→Γ` and set `R=U`×ΓU. For ξ,η over `U×U`, divide their affine Isom torsor by the normal kernel Kξ of `Aut(ξ)→Aut(fξ)`. After a faithfully flat extension containing a field object ζ of Γ and isomorphisms of ξ,η with ζ, this quotient is the base change of `Aut(ζ)/Kζ`. The exact arbitrary-affine normal quotient theorem makes it affine; effective affine descent makes `R/K` affine over `U×U`. Normality identifies the kernels by conjugation and lets identities, inverse and composition descend to `R/K⇒U`. Its fpqc groupoid quotient E is an affine gerbe, `Γ→E` is locally full, and `E→Δ` is faithful. The quotient Isom sheaf determines E and yields uniqueness with its triangle modification. Source: Borne–Vistoli 2019, Proposition 3.9 and proof, pp. 8–9. Faithfulness alone is equated with geometric representability only in the finite-type case; an arbitrary affine gerbe is not declared algebraic.

**Checks.**

- `AffineKernelChecks.trivial`: `N=1` gives `G/N=G`; `N=G` gives `Spec k` and quotient Hopf algebra k. The normal-subgroup direction is opposite to inclusion of coordinate Hopf subalgebras.
- `AffineKernelChecks.square`: `Gₘ→Gₘ`, `t↦t²`, has kernel `μ₂` and is faithfully flat even in characteristic 2. Over ℝ it misses the negative real points, so pointwise surjectivity cannot define local fullness.
- `AffineKernelChecks.infinite`: for G=∏ᵢ(`C₂`)ₖ, the quotient retaining finitely many coordinates is finite étale, while G itself is not finite type. Arbitrary-affine flatness is needed for its map to the inverse limit.
- `AffineKernelChecks.nonnormal`: `GL₂` modulo its upper triangular subgroup is `P¹` and is not affine. Normality is indispensable.

### 4.23 Cofiltered coherent presentations and finite-stage synchronization

Define `BooleanCofiltered` for a small locally groupoidal 2-category by nonemptiness, a cone under each pair of objects, and a **unique** invertible 2-cell between any parallel 1-arrows. Collapse mutually comparable objects to obtain a cofiltered poset; a choice of representatives gives a biequivalence, and a strict diagram becomes a pseudofunctor on that poset with explicit unit and composition constraints. This is a statement about Boolean cofiltered 2-categories. An ordinary cofiltered category need only admit a cofinal cofiltered-poset replacement and is not in general equivalent to a poset. Define `gerbeLimitFamily` with objects, transition isomorphisms, composition and unit equations, and compatibility with index 2-cells; arrows are compatible component arrows. Prove `booleanCofilteredPresentation.cofinalEquivalence` for a specified cofinal functor with connected refinement categories and transported pseudofunctor constraints. The inverse constructs components using a refinement over each original index; the refinement isomorphisms are independent of choices by further common refinements and unique 2-cells. Sources: Borne–Vistoli 2012, Definitions 3.2–3.5 and Remark 3.4, pp. 4–6.

If Γ=lim `Γᵢ` has an object over a nonempty k-scheme X, its Isom sheaves are lim `Isomᵢ`, represented by the affine limits over `X×T`. A filtered colimit of faithfully flat coordinate algebras over a fixed base is faithfully flat, including when the transition maps are not injective: flatness passes through the colimit, and if a fibre colimit were zero its unit would already be zero at a finite stage. Hence `X→Γ` is an fpqc cover and Γ is an affine fpqc gerbe. The nonemptiness input is retained. Source: Borne–Vistoli, Remark 3.6 and Proposition 3.7, p. 6.

Prove `finiteStageHomEquivalence`: if Δ is an affine fpqc stack with a flat groupoid presentation `RΔ⇒UΔ` in which **both** affine k-schemes are of finite type, then `colimᵢ Hom(Γᵢ,Δ)≃Hom(Γ,Δ)` as groupoids. Choose `X=Spec K→Γ` and write `Rᵢ=X×ΓᵢX` and R=lim `Rᵢ`. Objects in Δ over R, arrows over R and equality of arrows descend to a common finite index because Δ has the specified finite presentation; impose the finite unit and cocycle equations after a further common refinement, using also R×ₓR and the triple product. This simultaneously descends an object, its descent isomorphism, the cocycle, a morphism and equality of modifications. Effective fpqc descent on `Rᵢ⇒X` gives the asserted functor, full faithfulness and essential surjectivity. Source: Borne–Vistoli, Proposition 3.8 and proof, pp. 6–7. A limit of isomorphism classes is insufficient.

For a profinite étale gerbe Γ, let `finiteImageDiagram Γ` have objects locally full maps `Γ→E` to finite étale gerbes, and arrows compatible factorizations with their triangle modifications. The image into a finite product gives a common refinement. Local fullness makes precomposition fully faithful on transformations and modifications: components descend from local objects and their lifted Isom arrows. Thus there is a unique compatible 2-cell between parallel arrows, making the diagram Boolean cofiltered. Any finite-stage map factors through its canonical finite image, so comparison with a chosen presentation is cofinal and retains all limit data. This supplies `locallyFullPresentation`, not merely a list of finite images.

For a locally full map `f:Γ→Δ`, the synchronized index records a locally full finite quotient `Δ→D`, a locally full quotient `Γ→E`, a map `E→D` and an invertible triangle modification. The finite-stage Hom equivalence produces each factorization; taking images and common product refinements synchronizes every finite set of objects, arrows and triangle modifications. The target and source projection functors are cofinal, with the same uniqueness of compatible 2-cells, so `synchronizedPresentation` gives Γ≃lim `Eᵢ` and Δ≃lim `Dᵢ` and f≃lim `fᵢ`. Every `Eᵢ→Dᵢ` is locally full: its coordinate Hopf map is injective because its composite with the faithfully flat `Γ→Eᵢ` is injective; apply arbitrary-affine Hopf faithful flatness. Its finite étale kernel gives a proper étale relative gerbe. For every `C→Δ`, base change and the universal property of coherent limits give Γ×ΔC≃lim(`Eᵢ×DᵢC`), as stacks including arrows. Source: Bresciani, Lemma 2 and proof, p. 135, together with Borne–Vistoli Proposition 3.8, pp. 6–7, and 2019 Proposition 3.9, pp. 8–9; the simultaneous-refinement argument just described is the required additional proof chain.

**Checks.**

- `BooleanChecks.singleton`: the terminal 2-category is Boolean cofiltered; its collapsed poset has one element.
- `BooleanChecks.empty`: the empty 2-category is excluded by nonemptiness, despite satisfying the pair-cone and parallel-arrow conditions vacuously.
- `BooleanChecks.connected`: the codiscrete two-object groupoid, viewed as a locally discrete 2-category, is Boolean cofiltered and its collapsed poset is a singleton.
- `BooleanChecks.parallel`: the one-object category with endomorphism monoid `{1,0}`, where 0 is absorbing, is cofiltered: precomposition with 0 equalizes every parallel pair. It is not equivalent to a poset because it has two endomorphisms. Thus ordinary cofilteredness does not supply the stated biequivalence; the unique-2-cell condition is material.
- `LimitChecks.singleton`: a one-index identity diagram returns the whole fibre groupoid, including all automorphisms; replacing it by its isomorphism classes deletes those automorphisms.
- `LimitChecks.twoCoordinates`: in the tower of products `(C₂)ⁿ`, an object, an arrow and a relation involving coordinates 1 and 2 are all detected at `n=2`. Coordinate 2 is invisible at `n=1`, and checking two relations at separate stages requires passage to their common refinement.
- `SynchronizationChecks.kernel`: the quotient ∏ᵢC₂→`C₂` on coordinate 1 synchronizes at finite products containing that coordinate. Its finite-stage kernel has size `2ⁿ`⁻¹, so each finite relative gerbe is proper étale; the infinite kernel is not of finite type.

### 4.24 Signatures of the Layer 4 carriers

The carriers `IsGerbe`, `AbelianBanding`, `Neutralization`, `IsNeutral`, `BandPreserving`,
`GerbeLimitFamily` with its category, and `intrinsicBandSectionSubgroup` are specified in this layer.
The intrinsic band presheaf and sheaf with its evaluation and banding, the cover comparisons and conjugation transport, the
constant, connected and restriction test diagrams, the Isom torsors and their actions, the pullback,
descent and coherent inverse of banded morphisms, the fibre Hom sheaves with their transport,
base-change and endpoint comparisons, local covers and chart comparisons, and the global orbit
sheaf are targets with the following intended signatures. Throughout, `C` is a category with a
Grothendieck topology `J`, `F` and `G` are `Cat`-valued pseudofunctors on `Cᵒᵖ` and `A` is an abelian
sheaf on `(C, J)`; the variables `variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]` and

```lean
abbrev reduction : Multiplicative (ZMod 4) →* Multiplicative (ZMod 2) :=
  (ZMod.castHom (show 2 ∣ 4 by decide) (ZMod 2)).toAddMonoidHom.toMultiplicative

abbrev chainGroups : Fin 3 ⥤ CommGrpCat :=
  ComposableArrows.mk₂ (CommGrpCat.ofHom reduction)
    (𝟙 (CommGrpCat.of (Multiplicative (ZMod 2))))

abbrev ChainSite := (Fin 3)ᵒᵖ

abbrev chainPresheaf : ChainSiteᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat := unopUnop (Fin 3) ⋙ chainGroups

abbrev chainF := groupDiagram chainPresheaf

abbrev U₀ : ChainSite := op (0 : Fin 3)

abbrev U₁ : ChainSite := op (1 : Fin 3)

abbrev U₂ : ChainSite := op (2 : Fin 3)

abbrev f₀₁ : U₁ ⟶ U₀ := (homOfLE (show (0 : Fin 3) ≤ 1 by decide)).op

abbrev f₁₂ : U₂ ⟶ U₁ := (homOfLE (show (1 : Fin 3) ≤ 2 by decide)).op

abbrev f₀₂ : U₂ ⟶ U₀ := (homOfLE (show (0 : Fin 3) ≤ 2 by decide)).op

abbrev TwoChainSite := (Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 3)ᵒᵖ

abbrev twoChainPresheaf : TwoChainSiteᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat :=
  unopUnop (Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 3) ⋙ chainGroups.sum' chainGroups

abbrev twoChainF := groupDiagram twoChainPresheaf

end RestrictionBandFixtures

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

variable {A : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v'}}

def componentFullyFaithful (bF : AbelianBanding F J A)
    (bG : AbelianBanding G J A) (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    [BandPreserving bF bG η] (U : C) :
    (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.FullyFaithful

def localImageSieve (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G) {U : C}
    (z : G.obj (.mk (op U))) : Sieve U

variable {ι : Type t} {U : C} {X : ι → C}

def targetOverlapIso (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U) (x : ∀ i, F.obj (.mk (op (X i))))
    (z : G.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (e : ∀ i, (η.app (.mk (op (X i)))).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z)
    {Y : C} (q : Y ⟶ U) {i j : ι} (a : Y ⟶ X i) (b : Y ⟶ X j)
    (ha : a ≫ f i = q) (hb : b ≫ f j = q) :
    (η.app (.mk (op Y))).toFunctor.obj ((F.map a.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj (x i)) ≅
      (η.app (.mk (op Y))).toFunctor.obj ((F.map b.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj (x j))

def liftedOverlapIso (bF : AbelianBanding F J A) (bG : AbelianBanding G J A)
    (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G) [BandPreserving bF bG η]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U) (x : ∀ i, F.obj (.mk (op (X i))))
    (z : G.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (e : ∀ i, (η.app (.mk (op (X i)))).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z)
    {Y : C} (q : Y ⟶ U) {i j : ι} (a : Y ⟶ X i) (b : Y ⟶ X j)
    (ha : a ≫ f i = q) (hb : b ≫ f j = q) :
    (F.map a.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (F.map b.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj (x j)

def liftedDescentData (bF : AbelianBanding F J A) (bG : AbelianBanding G J A)
    (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G) [BandPreserving bF bG η]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U) (x : ∀ i, F.obj (.mk (op (X i))))
    (z : G.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (e : ∀ i, (η.app (.mk (op (X i)))).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z) : F.DescentData f

def imageLocalIso (bF : AbelianBanding F J A) (bG : AbelianBanding G J A)
    (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G) [BandPreserving bF bG η]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U) (x : ∀ i, F.obj (.mk (op (X i))))
    (z : G.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (e : ∀ i, (η.app (.mk (op (X i)))).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z)
    (y : F.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (r : Pseudofunctor.DescentData.ofObj (F := F) (f := f) y ≅
      liftedDescentData bF bG η f x z e) (i : ι) :
    (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj ((η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.obj y) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z

def globalImageIso (bF : AbelianBanding F J A) (bG : AbelianBanding G J A)
    (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G) [BandPreserving bF bG η]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U) (hf : Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U)
    (x : ∀ i, F.obj (.mk (op (X i)))) (z : G.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (e : ∀ i, (η.app (.mk (op (X i)))).toFunctor.obj (x i) ≅
      (G.map (f i).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj z)
    (y : F.obj (.mk (op U)))
    (r : Pseudofunctor.DescentData.ofObj (F := F) (f := f) y ≅
      liftedDescentData bF bG η f x z e) :
    (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.obj y ≅ z

end GerbeMorphismDescent

namespace CoherentInverse

open scoped Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

noncomputable def inverse (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (hη : ∀ U : C, (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.IsEquivalence) :
    Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans G F

-- Invertible modifications in the scoped bicategory of pseudofunctors
-- (`Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.homCategory`, Mathlib `FunctorBicategory/Pseudo`).
noncomputable def unitIso (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (hη : ∀ U : C, (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.IsEquivalence) :
    𝟙 F ≅ η ≫ inverse η hη

noncomputable def counitIso (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (hη : ∀ U : C, (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.IsEquivalence) :
    inverse η hη ≫ η ≅ 𝟙 G

theorem triangleForward (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (hη : ∀ U : C, (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.IsEquivalence) :
    (unitIso η hη).hom ▷ η ≫ (α_ η (inverse η hη) η).hom ≫ η ◁ (counitIso η hη).hom =
      (λ_ η).hom ≫ (ρ_ η).inv

theorem triangleInverse (η : Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans F G)
    (hη : ∀ U : C, (η.app (.mk (op U))).toFunctor.IsEquivalence) :
    inverse η hη ◁ (unitIso η hη).hom ≫ (α_ (inverse η hη) η (inverse η hη)).inv ≫
      (counitIso η hη).hom ▷ inverse η hη =
        (ρ_ (inverse η hη)).hom ≫ (λ_ (inverse η hη)).inv

end CoherentInverse

open Pseudofunctor.LocallyDiscreteOpToCat

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

variable {F G : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat.{v', u'}}

variable {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {A : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v'}}

variable [IsGerbe F J] [IsGerbe G J]

variable (b : AbelianBanding F J A)

variable {U V W T S : C}

noncomputable def selfHomChartToOrbit (X : HomCategory b b) (U : C)
    (x : F.obj (.mk (op U))) :
    (fibreHomSheaf b b U x x X).obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{max u v u',v'} ⟶
      (Over.forget U).op ⋙ (selfHomOrbitPresheaf b X ⋙ uliftFunctor.{max u v,max u' v'})

noncomputable def selfHomChartToGlobal (X : HomCategory b b) (U : C)
    (x : F.obj (.mk (op U))) :
    (sheafCompose (J.over U) uliftFunctor.{max u v u',v'}).obj
      (fibreHomSheaf b b U x x X) ⟶ ((selfHomGlobalSheafFunctor b).obj X).over U

noncomputable def selfHomChartGlobalIso [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type (max u v u' v'))]
    (X : HomCategory b b) (U : C)
    (x : F.obj (.mk (op U))) :
    (sheafCompose (J.over U) uliftFunctor.{max u v u',v'}).obj
      (fibreHomSheaf b b U x x X) ≅ ((selfHomGlobalSheafFunctor b).obj X).over U

end BandedMorphism
```

### Examples

The point-site groupoid on two disconnected objects is not a gerbe. For a fixed `C₃` band, inversion differs from the identity at the generator; arbitrary transformations need not preserve the band. A square root of `O(1)` on `P¹` does not exist, whereas `O(2)` has `O(1)` as a root. Arithmetic Frobenius on `μ₅` over `F₂` has exponent 2 and inverse exponent 3. The nonconstant restriction fixtures retain the actual group maps rather than replacing every restriction by identity.

### Dependencies

Mathlib sites, stacks, sheaf-Hom, sheafification, groupoids, enough injectives and derived sheaf cohomology; Layers 1 and 3; SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.15 (torsors), §1.18 (stackification), §1.21 (quotient stacks) and §§2.1–2.4 (site cohomology and torsor classes). The full classification inverse and the affine and profinite constructions are further targets of this layer.

## Layer 5: rigidification and finite correspondences

### 5.1 Inertia subgroups and rigidification

Define `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup`. For an algebraic stack X locally of finite presentation over S, a rigidifiable inertia subgroup is a closed subgroup `G⊂I_X` that is flat and finitely presented over X. For every `T→X` represented by x, it yields `G_x⊂Aut_T(x)`; every base change identifies the pulled-back subgroup, and every isomorphism `x≅y` conjugates `G_x` onto `G_y`. In particular `G_x` is normal; centrality is not required. The site-level carrier records normal subgroups of Aut groups, conjugation, restriction and fppf local membership, with the closed/flat/finitely-presented representability conditions imposed at the algebraic-stack interface.

Here X is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over S; G is a representable closed subgroup of inertia, flat and finitely presented over X.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Appendix A, setup before Theorem A.1, pp.1086–1087; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-groupoids.pdf), Lemma 78.6.1 (06P6), §6, pp.4–5; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06E9), §110.50, Lemma 110.50.1 (06EA)).

The API gives `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.subgroup`: Evaluate G at a test object to obtain the subgroup of its automorphism group; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.conjugation`: For `e:x≅y`, transport by `Aut.autMulEquivOfIso e` maps `G_x` exactly onto `G_y`; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.restrict_mem`: Restriction of an automorphism in `G_x` belongs to the subgroup at the restricted object; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.local_mem`: Membership in `G_x` is equivalent to membership after every arrow of a covering sieve; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.bottom`: The identity subsheaf exists for every stack. It is a rigidifiable geometric subgroup when the unit `X→I_X` is a closed immersion, equivalently when `I_X→X` is separated; this is not imposed by SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.top`: The entire inertia is rigidifiable when the inertia itself is flat and finitely presented; `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.ext`: Two subgroup interfaces are equal when their subgroups agree at every test object; coherence fields are proof-irrelevant.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsGroupoid`.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.test_bottom`: In the bottom subgroup, `a∈G_x` iff `a=1`.
- `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.test_noncentral`: On `B(S_3)` over a field, the full inertia is allowed although a transposition is not central.
- `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.test_not_normal`: The subgroup generated by (0 1) in `S_3` is not normal and cannot define a conjugation-compatible inertia subgroup of `B(S_3)`.
- `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.test_base_change`: For `Bμ_p` in characteristic p, the entire finite flat inertia satisfies arbitrary test-scheme restriction, including nonreduced test schemes.
- `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup.test_not_closed_identity`: For the non-separated group algebraic space `G=A1_k/Z` of Stacks §110.50 over a characteristic-zero field, the identity subsheaf of `I_BG` is not a closed subgroup. It satisfies the site-level bottom interface but not the geometric rigidifiability condition.

Define `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`. Given X and a rigidifiable `G⊂I_X`, construct X▹G by replacing the Isom sheaf between x and y over T by its fppf quotient `Isom_X(x,y)/G_x`, where `G_x` acts by precomposition, and then stackifying the resulting prestack. Normality identifies the right and left actions and makes composition well defined. The map `ρ:X→X`▹G has the same locally presented objects and kills precisely G. X▹G is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over S. The sheaf quotient is essential: its T-sections need not equal the quotient of the T-section sets.

Here the hypotheses of normal-inertia-subgroup; All Hom quotients are taken as fppf sheaves before object descent.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.1 and proof, pp.1087–1089).

The API gives `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`: Construct the groupoid-valued stack X▹G; `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.map`: The restriction-compatible morphism `ρ:X→X`▹G; `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.quotientHom`: The fppf quotient sheaf `Isom_X(x,y)/G_x` on the slice over the test object; `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.homSheaf`: For lifted x,y, `Isom_{X▹G}(ρx,ρy)` is isomorphic to `Rigidification.quotientHom x y`; `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.locallyObjects`: Every object of X▹G lifts to X on a covering sieve; `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.isStack`: The constructed pseudofunctor has effective object descent and Hom sheaves; its fibres are groupoids.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Quotient`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.sheafHom`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsGroupoid`.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.test_trivial`: When the identity inertia subgroup is closed, its geometric rigidification is equivalent to X. The site-level equivalence requires no geometric closedness.
- `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.test_cyclic_four`: For the constant cyclic group C4 and its order-two subgroup, BC4▹C2≃BC2; one residual order-two automorphism remains.
- `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.test_mu_p`: In characteristic p, `Bμ_p`▹`μ_p≃Spec(k)`, although `μ_p` is not smooth.
- `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.test_sheaf_quotient`: For the squaring quotient `G_m`/`μ_2` over R, the fppf quotient is `G_m` and -1 is a quotient section although it has no square root in R. Sectionwise cosets do not give the quotient sheaf.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`. For every stack Y in groupoids over S, precomposition with ρ induces an equivalence of Hom groupoids `Hom_S(X▹G,Y) ≃ Hom_S(X,Y)_{G=1}`, where the right side is the full subgroupoid of morphisms whose induced automorphism maps kill G on every test object. Thus such a morphism has a factorization together with a comparison 2-isomorphism; the groupoid of factorizations with that fixed comparison is contractible. This is a statement about morphisms and compatible 2-morphisms, not equality of chosen factors.

Here X,G,ρ as in rigidification; Y satisfies stack descent; algebraicity of Y is unnecessary.

([Matthieu Romagny](https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/matthieu.romagny/articles/group_actions.pdf), Theorem 5.1(i) and proof, pp.224–225; [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Appendix A quotient-Hom construction and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089).

For the proof, a G-killing functor factors on every quotient Hom sheaf; its restriction coherence descends; then apply stackification universality to extend to objects and morphisms of X▹G; then modifications descend because they satisfy the same Hom-sheaf compatibility. Full faithfulness gives uniqueness relative to the supplied comparison.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.Modification`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stabilizer_kernel`. For `x∈X(T)`, the map `Aut_T(x)→Aut_T(ρx)` is an epimorphism of fppf group sheaves with kernel `G_x`; consequently `Aut_T(ρx)≅Aut_T(x)/G_x` as fppf sheaves. This need not be a surjection on T-valued automorphisms.

Here X,G,ρ as in rigidification.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.1(b), p.1087).

For the proof, specialize the quotient-Hom formula to `x=y`; then identify the identity fibre with `G_x` by the normal congruence; then the quotient-sheaf construction gives local surjectivity; multiplication is specified from composition.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_map_eq_iff`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.geometry`. ρ is an fppf gerbe, smooth and of finite presentation as a morphism of algebraic stacks. It is proper when `G→X` is finite, and étale when `G→X` is étale. If X is Deligne–Mumford, then X▹G is Deligne–Mumford and ρ is étale. Smoothness of ρ does not say that G is smooth or that ρ is representable. When G is nontrivial, ρ is not representable.

Here X,G,ρ as in rigidification; The proper and étale assertions have the extra subgroup hypotheses stated.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.1(a) and final paragraph, pp.1087–1089; [Matthieu Romagny](https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/matthieu.romagny/articles/group_actions.pdf), Theorem 5.1(ii)–(iii), pp.224–225).

For the proof, after an fppf local lift y=ρx, identify `X×_{X▹G}T` with `BG_x`, as in AOV pp.1088–1089; then apply the geometry of classifying stacks as quotient stacks (SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.19–1.21); B of a flat finitely presented group is smooth as a stack even if its torsor atlas is merely flat; then for finite G use finite diagonal and universal closedness of the gerbe to get properness. For étale G use étale stack charts; then for a DM source its flat finitely presented inertia subgroup is unramified and hence étale; the quotient Isom spaces remain unramified.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stabilizer_kernel`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.base_change`. For any morphism `S′→S`, `(X×_S S′)`▹`(G×_S S′)≃(X▹G)×_S S′`, compatibly with ρ and quotient Hom sheaves. More generally, pulling the gerbe ρ back along `T→X`▹G gives the rigidification by the pulled-back subgroup. No flatness or tameness assumption on `S′→S` is needed.

Here X,G,ρ as in rigidification; The subgroup is pulled back with the stack, not held fixed as a group of global sections.

([Matthieu Romagny](https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/matthieu.romagny/articles/group_actions.pdf), Theorem 5.1, last assertion before the proof, p.224; [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Appendix A, pp.1087–1089).

For the proof, flatness and finite presentation of the subgroup survive arbitrary base change; then compare quotient Hom sheaves and use effective stack descent; alternatively use the universal property on the base-changed gerbe; then the comparison respects the map from X and is unique relative to it.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.geometry`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.nested`. Suppose `H⊂G⊂I_X` are compatible closed normal subgroup stacks flat and finitely presented over X, and the descended quotient `G/H` on X▹H is also closed, flat and finitely presented. Then `(X▹H)`▹`(G/H)≃X`▹G, compatibly with the maps from X. On stabilizers the composite removes exactly G; the order of removal is governed by `H⊂G` and cannot be interchanged for arbitrary unrelated subgroups.

Here Both rigidifications are defined with the listed geometric subgroup conditions.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Appendix A construction and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089).

For the proof, use the first quotient-Hom formula to identify the residual subgroup `G/H`; then a stack morphism from X kills G iff it factors through X▹H and kills `G/H`; then apply the universal property twice, including the factor comparison 2-isomorphisms.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stabilizer_kernel`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.coarse`. X admits a coarse moduli space `π:X→M` iff X▹G does; the same M works, and π factors through ρ. The two coarse morphisms have the same universal algebraic-space targets and geometric isomorphism classes. This does not make X▹G fine: it can retain stabilizers and nontrivial forms.

Here X,G,ρ as in rigidification; Coarse moduli space means the definition of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23, universal among all algebraic spaces.

([Matthieu Romagny](https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/matthieu.romagny/articles/group_actions.pdf), Theorem 5.1(iv), pp.224–225; [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.1 and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089).

For the proof, every map to an algebraic space kills all automorphisms, so the universal property identifies the categories of such maps; then over an algebraically closed field, an fppf gerbe with a flat finitely presented band has a local lift and a rational point on a nonempty finite-type local cover; its objects form one isomorphism class over each image; then combine categorical universality and the geometric-point bijection.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.geometry`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.vertical_kernel`. For a morphism `f:X→Y` of algebraic stacks, let `G=I_{X/Y}=ker(I_X→f*I_Y)`. If this kernel is a closed subgroup flat and finitely presented over X, there is a factorization `X→X`▹`G→Y` with a comparison 2-isomorphism, and the final map is representable by algebraic spaces. The rigidification has the universal property of killing the vertical inertia. No such factorization by this construction is asserted when the relative inertia is not flat.

Here X is locally of finite presentation over S; `G=I_{X/Y}` has the stated closedness, flatness and finite-presentation conditions; Y is algebraic.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.1(b), p.1087; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 101.6.2 (04YY), §6).

For the proof, kernel normality and base-change compatibility put G in normal-inertia-subgroup; then f kills G, hence factors by the universal property; then on the quotient stabilizer sheaves the remaining map is injective on every test scheme. Its base change to any scheme over Y is an algebraic stack with trivial inertia, hence an algebraic space by SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20. This proves the representability definition; geometric-point injectivity alone is insufficient.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`, `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stabilizer_kernel`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Define `affineKernelRigidification`. For `f:Γ→Δ` between affine fpqc gerbes, there is a canonical factorization `Γ→E→Δ`. Choose an affine fpqc cover `U→Γ`, put `R=U`×ΓU, and let K be the normal stabilizer-kernel sheaf. The quotient sheaf `R/K` carries an induced groupoid structure over U; its torsor stack E is an affine fpqc gerbe. Affineness of `R/K` follows after a faithfully flat field extension by identifying it with the quotient of an affine group scheme by a normal subgroup and then descending affineness. No general fpqc stackification in unrestricted universes is presumed.

Here Affine fpqc gerbes over a field; The arbitrary-affine normal quotient and affine fpqc descent of 4.22.

([Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.9 and proof, pp.8–9).

The API gives `AffineKernelRigidification.factor`: Produces the displayed canonical factorization of f; `AffineKernelRigidification.homSheaf`: For `f≅h∘g` and source objects x,y, `Isom_E`(gx,gy) is the fpqc quotient `Isom_Γ(x,y)`/Kx, compatibly with composition. It is generally only a subfunctor of `Isom_Δ`(fx,fy), not equal to that final-target sheaf; `AffineKernelRigidification.neutral`: For BG→BH the construction identifies with `B(G/ker f)`→BH.

*Needs:* `canonicalAffineFactorization`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18, 1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `KernelRigidificationTests.zeroKernel`: A faithful f has a trivial kernel and `E≃Γ`.
- `KernelRigidificationTests.allKernel`: For BG→`Spec k`, the quotient gerbe is `Spec k`.
- `KernelRigidificationTests.notOrbitSet`: The quotient `B(Z/4Z)→B(Z/2Z)` retains `Z/2Z` as inertia; its middle gerbe is not an orbit-set sheaf.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.affine_gerbe`. Let `f:Γ→Δ` be a morphism of affine fpqc gerbes over a field k such that Γ is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over k and the stabilizer kernel `G=I_{Γ/Δ}` is a closed subgroup of `I_Γ`, flat and finitely presented over Γ. Then the intermediate affine gerbe E of `affineKernelRigidification` is equivalent to Γ▹G, compatibly with the maps from Γ, the factorizations through Δ and the quotient Isom sheaves. The comparison imports the affine construction and its field-extension descent. Conditions on the kernel alone do not make Γ algebraic, so the algebraicity of Γ is a separate hypothesis; without it only the site-level quotient of `affineKernelRigidification` is defined. The theorem does not assert that every representable final gerbe morphism is full on Isom sheaves.

Here the hypotheses of the affine-kernel rigidification; Γ algebraic and locally of finite presentation over k, as required by `ArithmeticModuli.NormalInertiaSubgroup` and `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stack`; the kernel closed, flat and finitely presented over Γ.

([Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Appendix A, setup before Theorem A.1 and Theorem A.1, pp.1086–1089; [Niels Borne and Angelo Vistoli](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.07341v3), Proposition 3.9, pp.8–9).

For the proof, on a common fpqc neutralizing field extension both constructions quotient the same normal stabilizer subgroup; then compare their quotient Isom sheaves and factor comparisons; then descend the equivalence by descent of affine gerbes (§4.22) and the universal property of `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.universal`, which is available because Γ is algebraic and locally of finite presentation.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.vertical_kernel`, `affineKernelRigidification`, `zHatNotAlgebraicFp`.

**Checks.**

- `AffineGerbeComparisonChecks.zHatIdentity`: the identity of `B(Ẑ)_k` has trivial, closed, flat and finitely presented stabilizer kernel, and `affineKernelRigidification` returns `B(Ẑ)_k` itself. `B(Ẑ)_k` is not algebraic (`zHatNotAlgebraicFp`), so the geometric comparison is not asserted; a hypothesis only on the kernel would wrongly include it.
- `AffineGerbeComparisonChecks.cyclic`: for the constant groups, `B(ℤ/4)→B(ℤ/2)` has kernel the order-two subgroup; both constructions give `B(ℤ/2)→B(ℤ/2)`, the identity.
- `AffineGerbeComparisonChecks.muP`: in characteristic p, `Bμ_p→Spec k` has kernel `μ_p`, flat and finitely presented but not smooth; both constructions give `Spec k`.

### 5.2 Levels and quotient recovery

Throughout this topic, To infer an algebraic space, trivial inertia is proved on all test schemes.; p is representable; all automorphism assertions are about sheaves..

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.auxiliary_level_comparison`. A representable auxiliary-level morphism `p:L→X` identifies `Aut(ℓ)` with the stabilizer subgroup of `Aut(pℓ)` preserving the chosen level. It removes automorphisms by taking a subgroup and changes the objects; rigidification `X→X`▹G keeps locally lifted objects and takes the quotient `Aut(x)/G_x`. These operations coincide only after an additional comparison is proved. A rigidifier with trivial level-preserving automorphisms gives an algebraic-space moduli object if its full sheaf-valued inertia is trivial, but a coarse space merely records geometric isomorphism classes. Concrete elliptic rigidifiers are those of ModularCurves §4C; abelian and PEL levels belong to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli and PELModuli.

(ModularCurves §4C, rigidifiers and Katz–Mazur 4.7.0; §9D, Galois rigidifiers; [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Theorem A.`1(b)`, p.1087).

For the proof, apply representability to inject `Aut(ℓ)` into `Aut(pℓ)` and identify the preserving subgroup using the moduli definition; then compare with the epimorphism and kernel for rigidification; then use SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 only after the full inertia vanishes; import the concrete representability and Galois-rigidifier hypotheses from ModularCurves §4C.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.Rigidification.stabilizer_kernel`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, ModularCurves §4C.

Define `rigidLevelStructure`. A level functor on a moduli problem `P`: a representable finite étale surjective `P_N → P` equipped with an action of a fixed finite étale S-group G, making `P_N → P` a G-torsor over the stack P; pullbacks, the torsor action and their cocycles are part of the datum. Each fibre over `x/T` is consequently a `G_T`-torsor with the induced `Aut(x)`-action. The level is *rigid* if an automorphism of `x` fixing a point of `P_N(x)` is the identity.

Assume `G → S` finite étale; `P` a stack in groupoids on `(Sch/S)_fppf`.

The API consists of `LevelStructure.torsor` gives the G-action and the isomorphism `P_N×G≅P_N×_P P_N`; `LevelStructure.IsRigid` means every stabilizer of an actual level point is trivial as a sheaf; `LevelStructure.autAction` is functorial in objects, base changes and arrows, and commutes with the G-action.

**Checks.**

- `LevelTests.ellipticThree` full level `N ≥ 3` with N invertible on the base on elliptic curves is rigid
- `LevelTests.ellipticTwo` over a base where 2 is invertible, level `2` is not, `[-1]` fixes `E[2]`
- `LevelTests.characteristicDividesLevel` has `μ_p ⊂ E[p]` for an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic p, so full p-torsion level does not furnish the finite étale torsor required by this definition. Fibrewise torsor structures without a compatible global G-action do not supply the quotient of the next theorem.
(ModularCurves §4C supplies the elliptic level rigidifier and the elliptic examples.)
*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.15), ModularCurves §4C, 0E.
The definition is generic in `P`. Its abelian instance (rigidity of full level `N ≥ 3` on polarized abelian schemes, which needs the abelian-scheme carrier, finiteness of polarized automorphism groups and the rigidity lemma for families) is a target of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, which applies `rigidLevelStructure`; it is not an input here, and the elliptic checks do not supply it. `LevelTests.unpolarizedProduct` uses only elliptic curves: on A = E × E in characteristic zero the automorphism `(P,Q)` ↦ (P+NQ,Q), with matrix `(1,N;0,1)`, is nonidentity but fixes `A[N]`, so the level functor on products of elliptic curves with all automorphisms is not rigid; a polarization is needed in the abelian instance.

Prove `levelRemovalQuotient`. If the level of §5.2 is rigid and `P` is algebraic with finite inertia, then `P_N` is an algebraic space with a finite étale `G`-action, `[P_N/G] ≃ P` ("removal of level"), `P_N → P` is the finite étale cover by the fine space ("addition of level"), and the coarse space of `P` is the quotient space `P_N/G`, a scheme when `P_N` is quasi-projective over `S`.
(SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.17, 1.21 and 1.23; ModularCurves §0C and §4C. The quotient-stack equivalence is descent of the specified G-torsor, not a consequence of a mere fibrewise free action.)
*Needs:* §5.1, §5.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21), ModularCurves §0C.

### 5.3 Finite correspondences

Define `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence`. For separated Deligne–Mumford stacks X,Y of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and with finite inertia, a finite correspondence is a span `X←p Z→q Y` over S, with both p and q representable by algebraic spaces and finite. Morphisms are equivalences of the middle stacks with compatible 2-isomorphisms on both legs. The correspondence is not defined as its image in `X×_S Y`: the middle stack and its multiplicities are retained. Since Y is separated over S, the joint map `Z→X×_S Y` is finite: factor through the graph over X and use the proper quasi-finite diagonal of Y. This supplies a finite-algebra presentation for descent.

Here X,Y are separated finite-type DM stacks over locally Noetherian S, with finite inertia; Both legs, not just one, are representable and finite.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Definition 101.37.1, pp.80–81, and representable morphisms in §6; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), Lemmas 74.11.23 and 74.11.29).

The API gives `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.apex`: The middle stack, with both legs and their common S-map; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.identity`: The identity span `X←X→X`; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.transpose`: Exchange the two legs, retaining the same middle stack; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.compose`: Compose `X←Z→Y` and `Y←W→V` using `Z×_Y W`; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.baseChange`: Pull back the whole span along `S′→S`, including both legs; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.jointFinite`: Under the separated DM endpoint hypotheses the map to `X×_S Y` is finite; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.Iso`: An isomorphism of spans is an equivalence of their middle stacks with compatible 2-isomorphisms on both legs. For schemes it is an apex isomorphism commuting with both legs; `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.groupoid`: Finite correspondences with these span isomorphisms form a groupoid; identities, composition and inverses preserve both leg comparisons.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.9, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.test_identity`: The identity span has middle X and both legs equal to the identity.
- `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.test_double_point`: Over `Spec(k)`, the span with middle `Spec(k×k)` and both structure maps has degree two on each leg although its image is the single point.
- `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.test_two_legs`: The span `A1_k`←id `A1_k→Spec(k)` is not a finite correspondence: the right leg is not finite.
- `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.test_empty`: The empty middle scheme defines a finite correspondence between any two endpoint schemes; its composition is empty.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.composition`. Composition of finite correspondences by the two-fibre product has representable finite legs. It is associative up to the canonical associator equivalence, has identity spans as units, and commutes with arbitrary change of base. If all legs are finite locally free, the composite legs are finite locally free as well. These are stack-level statements; a coarse-space operation is not asserted to preserve the middle fibre product.

Here Correspondences have the endpoint and leg hypotheses of finite-correspondence.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), §11, Lemmas 74.11.23 and 74.11.29; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), §6 and §37, pp.80–81).

For the proof, each projection of `Z×_Y W` is a base change of one of the finite legs; then compose with the remaining finite leg; use stability under base change and composition; then use the universal properties of two-fibre products for associators, units and base-change comparisons.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.fpqc_descent`. For an fpqc cover `S′→S`, finite correspondences between the fixed endpoints X,Y over S form a groupoid equivalent to finite correspondences between `X_{S′}`,`Y_{S′}` supplied with an isomorphism over `S′×_S S′` satisfying the identity and triple-overlap cocycle, including the 2-isomorphisms on both legs. A descended span is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the specified descent identification. Finite locally free legs descend too.

Here the endpoint hypotheses of finite-correspondence; An actual fpqc descent datum is supplied on the middle stack and both legs, not merely matching geometric isomorphism classes.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-descent.pdf), Proposition 74.4.1 and Lemmas 74.11.23 (0426), 74.11.29 (042C); AlgebraicVectorBundles L1A–L1B; Suggested.lean, relativeSpecUniversalProperty, relativeSpecPushforwardIso, relativeSpecBaseChangeIso and relativeSpecEquiv).

For the proof, regard the joint finite map as a commutative quasi-coherent finite algebra on `X×_S Y`; then descend this algebra, its multiplication and unit using SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1 and the stack chart version of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22; then recover the middle as the relative Spec of the descended algebra: on each scheme chart it is AlgebraicVectorBundles L1A's relative Spec, which commutes with base change (L1B), so the chart spectra descend along the presentation (affine morphisms satisfy fpqc descent, ModularCurves §0E); descend each leg and the leg compatibility 2-isomorphisms; then finiteness and finite local freeness are fpqc local on the target. Descend morphisms by full faithfulness of algebra descent.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.coarse_finite`. A finite correspondence `X←Z→Y` as above induces `M_X←M_Z→M_Y` between the Keel–Mori coarse spaces, and both induced maps are finite. Formation of these maps commutes with flat change of the common base. Arbitrary base change is valid when each of X,Y,Z is tame. Neither preservation of degree nor preservation of middle fibre products follows in general.

Here X,Y are separated finite-type DM stacks over locally Noetherian S, with finite inertia; The middle Z and both legs satisfy finite-correspondence; Z is then separated, finite type and has finite inertia; The arbitrary-base assertion requires tameness of all three stacks.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 101.37.6, p.81; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A4X), Lemma 30.21.1 (02OG) and algebraic-space Lemma 76.35.1 (0A4X); [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Corollary 3.3(a), p.1078).

For the proof, use SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23 for the three coarse spaces and categorical universality for the induced maps; then for the left induced map, `π_X∘p`=ar `p∘π_Z` is proper. After any base change, surjectivity of `π_Z` descends universal closedness to ar p; separatedness and finite type come from the endpoint/coarse separation and local finite-type results; then after passage to an algebraically closed field, the classes in a coarse fibre are images of the finite fibre of p after choosing an isomorphism in X; this yields finitely many geometric points, hence quasi-finiteness for the finite-type coarse map; then apply the algebraic-space theorem proper plus quasi-finite implies finite. Repeat for q; use coarse uniqueness for flat or tame base-change compatibility.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.9, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.tame_finite_flat_descent`. Let `π:X→M` be the coarse space of a locally Noetherian tame algebraic stack with finite inertia. For a representable finite locally free `p:Z→X`, let `A=p_*O_Z`. If every stabilizer at a closed geometric point of X acts trivially on the fibre of A, then `B=π_*A` is a finite locally free commutative `O_M`-algebra, the adjunction `π*B→A` is an isomorphism of algebras, and `Z≃X×_M Spec_M(B)`. The descended finite locally free morphism has the same rank. The condition is on the entire finite algebra, including its stabilizer action; a coarse geometric point bijection is insufficient.

Here X is locally Noetherian, tame, and has finite inertia; p is representable finite locally free; All closed geometric stabilizers act trivially on A fibres.

([Jarod Alper](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2833.pdf), Theorem 10.3 and Remark 10.4, pp.2386–2387; [Dan Abramovich, Martin Olsson, Angelo Vistoli](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2378.pdf), Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp.1077–1078; AlgebraicVectorBundles L1A–L1B; Suggested.lean, relativeSpecUniversalProperty, relativeSpecPushforwardIso, relativeSpecBaseChangeIso and relativeSpecEquiv).

For the proof, exact coarse QCoh pushforward and `O_M≅π_*O_X` make this tame coarse morphism a good moduli space in Alper’s sense; then apply Alper Theorem 10.3 to the vector bundle A; then full faithfulness of pullback on vector bundles descends multiplication and unit; faithfulness verifies associativity, commutativity and the unit identities; then form the relative Spec of the descended algebra chartwise (AlgebraicVectorBundles L1A) and use its compatibility with arbitrary base change (L1B) to obtain the cartesian square and rank preservation.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.11, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

### 5.4 Closures and normalization

Define `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.stack`. Let X be a locally Noetherian DM stack. Choose an étale scheme atlas `U→X`, set `R=U×_X U`, and normalize U and R in the total rings of fractions of their reductions. Smooth normalization compatibility gives `R^ν≅R×_U U^ν≅U^ν×_U R` and the normalized étale groupoid. Its quotient `X^ν` has a representable integral map `ν_X:X^ν→X`, and for every smooth scheme chart `V→X` its pullback is the ordinary normalization `V^ν`. This characterizes the construction up to unique comparison isomorphism. On scheme charts use Mathlib’s relative normalization `Scheme.Hom.normalization` of the disjoint union of the generic points; normalizing the identity map would be incorrect.

Here X is locally Noetherian and DM; more generally require the locally finite-component condition of Stacks Lemma 101.46.1; Ordinary normalization removes nilpotents before integral closure.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Lemmas 101.46.1–101.46.2 and Definition 101.46.3 (0GMI–0GMK), pp.96–97; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 67.49.5 (07U4), pp.106–108).

The API gives `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.stack`: The normal DM stack `X^ν` with its map `ν_X` to X; `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.map`: The representable integral normalization morphism `ν_X`; `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.smoothChart`: For a smooth `V→X`, the pullback of `ν_X` is ordinary `V^ν→V`; `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.mapOfGeneric`: Maps preserving generic points of components lift uniquely to normalizations; `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.normalIso`: If X is normal, `ν_X` is an isomorphism; `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.schemeComparison`: For a scheme X, the construction agrees with Mathlib’s `Scheme.Hom.normalization` of the inclusion of the generic points.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.14, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationPullback`.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.test_node`: For Spec(`k[x,y]`/(xy)), the normalization is `Spec(k[x])` ⨿ `Spec(k[y])`; the node has two points above it.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.test_normal_stack`: For a finite constant group H over a field, BH is normal and its normalization morphism is an equivalence; inertia is retained.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.test_nilpotents`: The normalization of `Spec(k[ε]/ε²)` is `Spec(k)`, unlike relative normalization of its identity map.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.test_scheme_comparison`: For an integral affine scheme `Spec(A)`, the atlas construction agrees with Spec of the integral closure of A in `Frac(A)`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.finite`. If X is a finite-type DM stack over a locally Noetherian Nagata scheme S, then `ν_X` is finite. In particular this holds over a locally Noetherian excellent base. The statement includes purely inseparable finite generic field extensions; separability is not needed for finiteness. A generic finite field extension requires its own integral-closure normalization rather than ordinary normalization of X.

Here X is finite type and DM over locally Noetherian Nagata S.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 67.49.9 (0BB5), p.109; scheme input Morphisms Lemma 29.55.11).

For the proof, étale finite-type scheme charts over S are Nagata; then apply SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20 to their ordinary normalizations; then use the chart characterization and target-local descent of finite morphisms to prove `ν_X` finite.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.stack`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

Define `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.stack`. For a quasi-compact morphism `f:Z→X` of locally Noetherian DM stacks, define its schematic image `C⊂X` to be the smallest closed substack through which f factors. For a smooth chart `U→X` the corresponding closed subscheme is cut out by `ker(O_U→(f_U)_*O_{Z_U})`; these ideal sheaves descend to X. For a quasi-compact immersion of an object over a dense open base this is its schematic closure. The construction retains scheme structure and commutes with flat base change. No nonflat comparison is asserted.

Here f is quasi-compact; X,Z are locally Noetherian DM stacks; The closure use requires a specified immersion into the ambient stack.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Definition 101.38.1 (0CMI), Lemmas 101.38.3 (0CPU) and 101.38.5 (0CMK), pp.81–83).
