The API gives `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.stack`: The schematic image C with its closed immersion into X; `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.factor`: The canonical factor `Z→C` and its composite equality with f; `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.minimal`: Every closed substack `D⊂X` containing f also contains C; `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.flatBaseChange`: The image of f after flat base change is the pullback of C; `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.schemeComparison`: For a scheme morphism the construction is exactly `Scheme.Hom.image`.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage`, Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.imageι` (whose composite is the original morphism).

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.test_nilpotents`: The schematic image of id on `Spec(k[ε]/ε²)` is the entire nonreduced scheme.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.test_closed_point`: The image of `Spec(k)→Spec(k[ε]/ε²)` given by `ε↦0` is the reduced closed point, with ideal `(ε)`.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.test_nonflat`: `Spec(Z[1/p])→Spec(Z)` has schematic image `Spec(Z)`; after reduction mod p the source is empty and its image is empty.
- `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.test_scheme_comparison`: For a scheme morphism f, the defining immersion and factor agree with `f.imageι` and `f.toImage`.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.finite_schematic_closure`. Let S be integral locally Noetherian excellent, let `U⊂S` be dense open, and let X,Y be separated finite-type DM stacks over S with finite inertia. Suppose a finite correspondence `C_U` between `X_U` and `Y_U` has a quasi-compact joint immersion `C_U→X_U×_U Y_U`. Let C be its schematic closure in `X×_S Y`. If both projections `C→X` and `C→Y` are representable, proper and quasi-finite, then they are finite, so C is a finite correspondence extending `C_U`. Properness follows, for example, if both endpoint stacks are proper over S; quasi-finiteness is an additional condition. This procedure is for immersed spans and cannot replace finite-algebra extension for a general multiple-cover span.

Here All conditions in the statement, including the joint immersion and quasi-finiteness of both projections; U is used rather than an unqualified generic fibre so that `C_U` embeds as the open-base restriction of C.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), §38, pp.81–83; §37, pp.80–81; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A4X), Lemma 30.21.1 (02OG) and algebraic-space Lemma 76.35.1 (0A4X)).

For the proof, construct the closure and restrict to U; an immersion already closed over U has its original schematic image there. The joint map of a finite span is finite, so the given immersion is closed over U; then if X,Y are proper over S, the product projections and closed-substack inclusions give properness of both legs; then a proper locally quasi-finite morphism of algebraic spaces is finite (Stacks, Lemma 76.35.1, tag 0A4X); apply this on each target chart; descend finiteness.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.DMSchematicClosure.stack`, `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `ArithmeticModuli.normalized_finite_correspondence`. Under finite-closure, the middle C has finite normalization `C^ν` because it is finite type over excellent S. Composing `C^ν→C` with the two finite legs gives a normal finite correspondence. If `C_U` is normal, its restriction to U is the original `C_U`; otherwise the restriction is its normalization. No preservation of rank on special fibres or commutation with arbitrary base change is asserted.

Here the finite-closure hypotheses, including proper quasi-finite representable projections; `C_U` normal is required to retain the original open-base middle.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/stacks-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 101.46.2 and Definition 101.46.3, pp.96–97; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-morphisms.pdf), Lemma 67.49.9 (0BB5), p.109).

For the proof, use dm-normalization-finite and composition of representable finite morphisms; then use the smooth/open chart comparison to commute normalization with restriction to U; then for normal `C_U` the normalized restriction is isomorphic to `C_U`.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticModuli.finite_schematic_closure`, `ArithmeticModuli.DMNormalization.finite`, `ArithmeticModuli.FiniteCorrespondence.composition`.

### Examples

Rigidifying BC₄ by its order-two subgroup gives BC₂, retaining order-two target inertia. Level two does not kill −1. On an unpolarized product of elliptic curves the matrix `[[1,N],[0,1]]` fixes N-torsion and is nonidentity. Normalization requires the source generic points to map to target generic points; a map into the node does not choose a branch.

### Dependencies

Layer 4; SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 (inertia), §1.23 (coarse spaces and tame stacks) and §0.20 (Nagata normalization); ModularCurves §0E (finite descent and polarized level structures).

## Layer 6: G-rings and algebraic approximation

### 6.0 The approximation predicate

Define `Approximation.HasArtinApproximation A` for a commutative local ring A: for each finitely presented A-algebra B, each A-algebra map B→Â to the maximal-ideal completion, and each `n≥0`, there is an A-algebra map `B→A` agreeing modulo the extended maximal ideal to power n on every element of B. Finite presentation translates this to finitely many polynomial equations and variables. Its basic theory gives this translation, transport by local ring isomorphism and the congruence of every polynomial in the chosen generators. This definition does not require A to be complete or henselian. The G-ring approximation theorem below gives the predicate for henselian Noetherian local G-rings. (Stacks, Smoothing Ring Maps, Theorems 16.13.1–16.13.2, tags 07QY–07QZ, pp. 32–33.)

**Checks.**

- `ApproximationTests.complete`: a complete Noetherian local A has the predicate by identifying A≅Â; every formal solution is matched exactly, at every n.
- `ApproximationTests.field`: a field has zero maximal ideal and completion itself; the solution at `n=1` is already the original solution. This distinguishes exact equations from merely solving their reductions.
- `ApproximationTests.nonhenselian`: for `A=ℚ[t]_(t)`, the formal branch of `z²=1+t` with z≡1 modulo t exists in `ℚ[[t]]`, but no rational function squares to `1+t`, since its valuation at `t+1` is odd. Thus A lacks the predicate even though it is a local G-ring. A pointed étale extension, rather than A itself, is necessary in the nonhenselian approximation theorem.

### 6.1 Approximation and common étale neighborhoods

Prove `gRing_essentiallyFiniteType`. If R is a Noetherian G-ring and `R→B` is essentially of finite type, B is a G-ring. In particular the local rings of a finite-type scheme over a G-ring have geometrically regular formal fibres.

Here R is Noetherian; G-ring means regularity of each local completion map.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/more-algebra.pdf), Proposition 15.51.10, tag 07PV, pp. 129–130).

This is a convenience corollary of SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21, which owns the substantive permanence theorems. For the proof, write B as a localization of a finite-type R-algebra C; C is a G-ring by *IsGRing.of_finiteType*, and B is a G-ring by *IsGRing.localization*.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21 (*IsGRing.of_finiteType*, *IsGRing.localization*).

Prove `polynomial_approximation`. Let `(R,m)` be Noetherian local and a G-ring. Every solution in R̂ of a finite polynomial system over R can, for each `N≥1`, be approximated modulo `m^N` by a solution in a pointed étale R-algebra `R′` with the same residue field. If R is henselian the solution can be chosen in R itself.

Here Finitely many equations and variables; `N≥1`; the completion of `R′` at its specified point is identified with R̂.

`Suggested.lean` states the pointed étale form as `Approximation.polynomial_approximation` and the
henselian form as `Approximation.artinApproximation`, with conclusion
`Approximation.HasArtinApproximation`. The definition
`Approximation.HasGeometricallyRegularFormalFibres` expresses the formal-fibre hypothesis using
`Ideal.ResidueField`, finite residue-field extensions, tensor products and `IsRegularRing`: for
Noetherian local R this says the completion map is regular. In the pointed étale statement an
R-algebra map `ι:R′→R̂` specifies the point; its composite with `R̂→R/𝔪` is surjective and has
residue field `R/𝔪`. The solution is compared with the given formal solution through ι.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/smoothing.pdf), Theorems 16.13.1–16.13.2, tags 07QY–07QZ, pp. 32–33).

For the proof, encode congruence by auxiliary variables and chosen generators of `m^N`; then factor the resulting finitely presented solution algebra through a smooth R-algebra using Néron–Popescu desingularization (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.15); then lift its residue-field point after an étale base change; henselian lifting gives an R-point in the henselian case.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.15, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21, `gRing_essentiallyFiniteType`.

Prove `henselizationAlgebraicElements`. For a Noetherian local G-ring domain `A` with fraction field `K`, `A^h ⊂ A^∧` is the set of elements algebraic over `K`. Consequently `x² = 2` has a root in `ℤ_7` (`3² ≡ 2 mod 7`) and in `ℤ_(7)^h` but none in `ℤ_(7)`, and has no root in `ℤ_2` at all.
(Stacks, Example 16.13.3 (tag 0A1W) (the henselisation as the algebraic elements); the `x² = 2` instance is a computation made here, not in the source.)
*Needs:* `polynomial_approximation`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.14, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21, Mathlib `AdicCompletion`.

Prove `artinApproximationClassical`. For `R` a field or an excellent discrete valuation ring, `A` the henselisation of a finite-type `R`-algebra at a prime ideal and `𝔪` a proper ideal of `A`, a solution in the `𝔪`-adic completion `A^∧` of a polynomial system over `A` is approximated to any order (modulo `𝔪^c`) by a solution in `A`. For `A` the henselisation of `k[x_1, …, x_n]` at the origin, `A` is the ring of algebraic power series and `A^∧ = k[[x_1, …, x_n]]`: formal solutions of polynomial systems are approximated by algebraic ones.
(Artin 1969 (Publ. IHÉS 36), Theorems (1.10) and (1.12), p. 26; (1.12) is the functorial form. The algebraic-power-series statement is the case `A = k[x]^h` of (1.10) and carries no separate number.)
*Needs:* `polynomial_approximation`, `gRing_essentiallyFiniteType`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.14, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21.

Prove `common_etale_neighbourhood`. For schemes `X₁`,`X₂` locally of finite type over a field or an excellent discrete valuation ring S, pointed at finite-type points with a specified S-isomorphism of completed local rings, there is a common pointed S-scheme U with étale maps to `X₁` and `X₂` inducing residue-field isomorphisms. Any fixed finite jet of the specified formal isomorphism can be matched; equality of the entire formal map is not promised.

Here the points have identified residue fields and lie over the same point of S; the given isomorphism respects S.

([Michael Artin](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1969__36__23_0.pdf), Corollaries 2.5–2.6, pp. 28–29; Theorem 1.10, p. 26).

For the proof, approximate the finitely presented equations defining the formal graph and its inverse; then invert the Jacobian conditions to obtain étale projections and preserve the prescribed finite jet; then compare completions at the common point; no assertion that every chosen formal automorphism is algebraic is needed.

*Needs:* `polynomial_approximation`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

### Examples

A complete Noetherian local ring approximates its own solutions exactly. A prescribed formal isomorphism can be matched to every fixed finite order on a common étale neighborhood; this does not make that entire formal map convergent or algebraic. The G-ring condition is needed at the source point.

### Dependencies

SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21 (G-rings), §0.15 (Néron–Popescu) and §0.14 (henselian lifting); Mathlib adic completion and finite polynomial systems.

## Layer 7: space Picard, Artin representability and arithmetic coefficients

### 7.1 Formal points, gluing and module obstructions

Define `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`. For a covariant affine functor F from commutative rings to sets, RS* means that `F(A×_C B)→F(A)×_{F(C)}F(B)` is bijective for every cospan `A→C←B` with `B→C` surjective and square-zero kernel. For a category fibred in groupoids use equivalence with the 2-fibre product, retaining the gluing isomorphism.

Here Use a fixed universe; the relative version uses rings over the affine base.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), 98.18, pp. 28–29; 98.5–98.6, pp. 5–8).

The API gives `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing.of_preservesLimits`: A functor preserving finite limits satisfies RS*; `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing.comparison_bijective`: Each permitted ring pullback has a bijective canonical comparison; `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing.transport`: A natural isomorphism of functors transports RS*.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackComparison`, Mathlib `CommRingCat.pullbackConeIsLimit`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4.

**Checks.**

- `StrongGluingTests.forget`: The commutative-ring forgetful functor satisfies RS*.
- `StrongGluingTests.terminal`: The terminal constant functor satisfies RS*.
- `StrongGluingTests.zeroKernel`: For `A→C←C` with the second map the identity, the comparison is bijective.
- `ArtinCriteria.StrongGluingTests.subsetFailure`: The functor R↦Set(R), with direct-image maps, fails RS*. For both maps `Q[ε]/ε²→Q`, the diagonal subset and the whole pullback have the same two projections but are distinct: `(ε,0)` is in the latter only. Thus the comparison is not injective even for a square-zero surjection.

Define `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint`. For an affine set-valued functor F, a ring R and ideal I, FormalPoint(F,R,I) consists of `ξ_n∈F(R/I^(n+1))` for every `n≥0`, compatible with every quotient transition. Restriction sends `x∈F(R)` to its family. In the geometric criterion take `I=m_R`, R complete Noetherian local over S, and residue field finite type over S.

Here the affine prototype has no completeness restriction; the criterion adds it explicitly. For stacks replace equality compatibility by coherent pullback isomorphisms in the formal-object groupoid.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definition 98.9.1, pp. 11–12; Section 98.15, pp. 25–26).

The API gives `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.ofPoint`: Restrict an actual point to every positive quotient power; `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.ext`: Equality of every component implies equality of formal points; `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.ofPoint_value`: The n-th component is restriction along `R→R/I^(n+1)`; `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.transition`: Restriction from the m-th component to the n-th agrees for `n≤m`; `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.map`: A natural transformation `F→G` sends a compatible family to the family of its component images; `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint.map_value`: The n-th component of the image family is η at `R/I^(n+1)` applied to the original component.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Ideal.Quotient.factorPow`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.8.

**Checks.**

- `FormalPointTests.affineLine`: For the ring forgetful functor the components are x modulo `I^(n+1)`.
- `FormalPointTests.terminal`: The terminal functor has only one formal point.
- `FormalPointTests.allOrders`: Agreement at every order forces equality of compatible families.
- `FormalPointTests.specialFibreInsufficient`: For `R=Q[ε]/ε²` and `I=(ε)`, the points 0 and ε have the same reduction modulo I but different reductions modulo `I²=0`. Their formal points have equal value 0 and unequal value 1; the special fibre alone cannot define FormalPoint.
- `ArtinCriteria.FormalPointTests.firstOrderInsufficient`: For `R=Q[t]/t³` and `I=(t)`, the points 0 and `t²` agree modulo I and modulo `I²`, but differ modulo `I³=0`. Their formal points have equal values 0 and 1 and unequal value 2, so the residue together with the first-order jet does not determine a formal point.

Define `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective`. Affine set-valued effectivity at `(R,I)` is surjectivity of `F(R)`→FormalPoint(F,R,I). The Artin space criterion quantifies this over all complete Noetherian local S-algebras with finite-type residue field. For a stack, effectivity means essential surjectivity of restriction to its formal-object groupoid. The stronger equivalence interface also retains unique compatible lifting of morphisms; with represented diagonal this is the standard supplied effectivity interface.

Here Use the restriction map of formal-point, not a separately postulated algebraization predicate.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definition 98.9.4 and Lemma 98.9.5, pp. 12–14; 98.14 and 98.17.1, pp. 24–27).

The API gives `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective.iff_lift`: Every formal point is the restriction of an actual point; `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective.lift`: Choose a realizing point from an effectivity proof; `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective.lift_spec`: The chosen lift restricts to the specified whole formal family; `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective.transport`: A natural isomorphism of functors transports effectivity at the same `(R,I)`.

*Needs:* `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10.

**Checks.**

- `EffectivityTests.terminal`: The terminal functor is effective for any ideal.
- `EffectivityTests.zeroIdeal`: For `I=0`, quotient powers are R and any functor is effective.
- `EffectivityTests.topIdeal`: The affine-line functor is effective at `I=R` because every quotient is the zero ring.
- `ArtinCriteria.EffectivityTests.emptyScheme`: For `F=Hom_CommRing`(ZMod 1,−), `R=Q` and I=top, every quotient has its unique zero-ring point, giving a formal point, but `F(Q)` is empty. Thus IsEffective is false. A constant-true predicate would fail this test.

Define `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber`. For `x∈F(k)`, define the tangent fibre as the fibre over x of `F(k[ε]/ε²)→F(k)`, with zero tangent given by the split inclusion `k→k[ε]/ε²`. For a stack take isomorphism classes of lifts with a specified identification with x; infinitesimal automorphisms are the kernel of the automorphism restriction of the split lift. RS supplies their natural k-vector-space structures.

Here k is a field; relative functors and dual numbers are taken over the base.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), 98.8, pp. 9–11).

The API gives `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber.zero`: The split lift is a tangent element over x; `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber.ext`: Two tangent elements with equal underlying lift are equal; `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber.map`: A natural transformation induces a map between the corresponding tangent fibres.

*Needs:* `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`, Mathlib `TrivSqZeroExt`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4.

**Checks.**

- `TangentTests.affineLine`: The affine-line tangent fibre at x is equivalent to k via the ε coefficient.
- `TangentTests.terminal`: The terminal functor has a one-element tangent fibre.
- `TangentTests.zeroRestriction`: The split tangent element restricts to the specified residue point.
- `TangentTests.twoElements`: For the affine-line functor over `F₂` at 0, the tangent fibre has exactly two elements. Unframed dual-number points have four; an empty or trivial tangent has zero or one.

Define `ModuleObstructionTheory`. For locally Noetherian S and `x∈X(Spec A)`, with Spec `A→S` factoring through an affine open, an obstruction theory assigns an A-linear functor `O_x` on A-modules, natural in module maps, and to each square-zero extension `A′→A` of kernel M a class `ob_x(A′)∈O_x(M)`, compatible with morphisms of deformation situations. For every ring map `A→B`, `y=x|_B` and A-linear map `M→N` to a B-module, it includes a natural A-linear map `O_x(M)→O_y(N)`. Its class vanishes exactly when the groupoid of lifts of x with specified identification is nonempty. `T_x(M)` and `Inf_x(M)` respectively describe differences between liftings and their infinitesimal automorphisms.

Here For the openness theorem use the full module-functor axioms of 98.22.1, including naturality in extensions and in the object; the finite-dimensional obstruction space of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.5 alone is insufficient; A, its square-zero extensions and the modules are not required to be Noetherian or finite. Only S is locally Noetherian; the source obstruction theory ranges over all these deformation situations.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definition 98.22.1, pp. 39–40).

The API gives `ModuleObstructionTheory.pushout`: A map `M→N` sends the obstruction to that of the pushed-out extension; `ModuleObstructionTheory.zero_iff_lift`: The obstruction vanishes exactly when a framed lift exists; `ModuleObstructionTheory.lifting_torsor`: If lifts exist their framed isomorphism classes form a torsor under `T_x(M)`, with `Inf_x(M)` their infinitesimal automorphisms; `ModuleObstructionTheory.mk`: Bundle the actual module functor, the extension-indexed classes, their naturality equations and the zero-iff-framed-lift proof; `ModuleObstructionTheory.obstruction`: Evaluate the obstruction class of a specified object and specified square-zero extension, in the module assigned to its actual kernel; `ModuleObstructionTheory.split`: The class for a split square-zero extension is zero because the split framed lift exists; `ModuleObstructionTheory.baseChange`: For `A→B`, `y=x|_B` and an A-linear map `M→N` to a B-module, expose the natural map `O_x(M)→O_y(N)`, with identity and composition laws.

*Needs:* `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`, `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.5.

**Checks.**

- `ObstructionTests.split`: A split extension has zero obstruction and its split lift exists.
- `ObstructionTests.zeroKernel`: A zero-kernel extension has the original object as lift.
- `ObstructionTests.curveLineBundle`: For a line bundle on a proper smooth curve over k, `O_x(M)=H²(X,O_X)⊗M=0`, though `H¹` may parametrize different lifts.
- `ObstructionTests.doublePoint`: For `Spec Q[t]/(t²)`, the point `t↦ε` over `Q[ε]/ε²` does not lift to `Q[ε]/ε³`. The equation obstruction is the nonzero `ε²` in the square-zero kernel `(ε²)`: every prospective `ε+cε²` has square `ε²`. This rules out a constant-zero obstruction theory.

Prove `formal_object_approximation`. Let S be locally Noetherian, X a category fibred in groupoids limit preserving on objects, R a complete Noetherian local S-algebra with finite-type residue field, and `x∈X(R)`. If `O_{S,s}` is a G-ring at the image s, then for every `N≥1` there are a finite-type S-algebra A, a maximal ideal `m_A`, an object `x_A`, and an S-isomorphism `R/m_R^N≅A/m_A^N` identifying the restrictions of x and `x_A`. One can also identify the associated graded rings at the specified points.

Here the algebra A is over an affine neighbourhood of s; residue fields are identified. This is finite-order approximation, not an isomorphism `R≅A` or full algebraization of x.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.10.1, tag 07XB, pp. 14–16).

For the proof, descend x to a finitely presented algebra by limit preservation on objects; then present R as a quotient of a completed polynomial local algebra; encode kernel generators and syzygies; then use Artin–Rees and sufficiently accurate polynomial approximation to preserve the prescribed jet and the associated graded ring.

*Needs:* `gRing_essentiallyFiniteType`, `polynomial_approximation`.

Prove `openness_of_versality`. Let X be a category fibred in groupoids over locally Noetherian S with representable diagonal, RS*, limit preservation and a module-valued obstruction theory. Suppose for every S-algebra A mapping into an affine open, every x and every countable family `(M_i)` of A-modules the map `T_x(∏M_i)→∏T_x(M_i)` is an isomorphism and `O_x(∏M_i)→∏O_x(M_i)` is injective. For an object over a finite-type S-scheme U, its formal versality at a finite-type point implies versality at all finite-type points in some open neighbourhood.

Here Formal versality is the smooth lifting property of its complete-local deformation functor, as for the hulls of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4; retain both product conditions and the representable diagonal; The algebra A and modules in the product condition need not be Noetherian or finite; both maps must be available on the product modules themselves.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.22.2, tag 0CYF, p. 40, using the openness bridge of §98.20).

For the proof, use the tangent comparison to identify simultaneous lift differences; then use injectivity of the obstruction comparison to detect simultaneous vanishing; then apply the finite-presentation algebra and openness argument of 0CYF; do not infer openness merely from finite-dimensional tangent spaces.

*Needs:* `ModuleObstructionTheory`, `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `openness_of_versality_strongEffective`. Let S be locally Noetherian and X a category fibred in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf` with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces, RS* and limit preservation. Suppose X is strongly effective: for every affine open `Spec Λ⊂S`, every inverse system `(R_n)` of Λ-algebras with surjective transition maps such that `Ker(R_m→R_n)` has square zero for all `m≥n`, and every compatible system of objects `ξ_n` over `Spec R_n`, there is an object over Spec(lim `R_n`) restricting to the system. Then X satisfies openness of versality. No obstruction theory and no perfectness of a deformation complex is used.

Here S locally Noetherian; effectivity is required only for systems in which every kernel `Ker(R_m→R_n)`, `m≥n`, has square zero; the rings `R_n` need not be Noetherian and lim `R_n` need not be complete local.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CXU), Lemma 98.20.3, with Remark 98.20.2 (tag 0CXT) and Lemma 98.20.1, Section 98.20, tag 0CXR).

For the proof, argue by contradiction. If versality fails at finite-type points `u_n` accumulating at a versal point, with no specializations among them, the construction of Lemma 98.20.1 produces first-order thickenings `U→U_1→U_2`→… and objects `x→x_1→x_2`→… such that no neighbourhood of `u_n` in `U_n` carries a lift of `x_n` compatible with the original object; RS* glues the successive square-zero extensions. Strong effectiveness realizes the system over the limit ring, limit preservation descends that object to a finite-type stage, and versality at the accumulation point then yields the excluded local lifts.

*Needs:* `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`, `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `StrongEffectiveChecks.affine`: an affine S-scheme `Spec B` is strongly effective, since compatible ring maps `B→R_n` are one ring map B→lim `R_n`.
- `StrongEffectiveChecks.trivialExtensions`: for a finite-type k-algebra A and distinct closed points `u_1`,`u_2`,…, the trivial square-zero extensions `R_n=A⊕(κ(u_1)⊕…⊕κ(u_n))` have kernels `Ker(R_m→R_n)=κ(u_(n+1))`⊕…⊕`κ(u_m)` of square zero and limit `A⊕∏κ(u_i)`, which is neither local nor Noetherian. These are the systems of the proof; effectiveness over complete Noetherian local rings does not cover them.
- `StrongEffectiveChecks.emptyLocus`: for `X=A¹_S` and the object over `U=S` given by the zero section, versality fails at every point; the lemma asserts openness of the versal locus, which here is empty, not its nonemptiness.

Prove `artin_space_criterion`. An étale sheaf `F:(Sch/S)^op→Sets` satisfying the listed hypotheses is an algebraic space locally of finite presentation over S. Limit preservation means `colim F(Spec A_i)→F(Spec colim A_i)` is bijective for every filtered system of affine S-algebras.

Here F is an étale sheaf; S is locally Noetherian; `O_{S,s}` is a G-ring for every finite-type point s. A fixed universe bounds the cardinalities of finite-type field fibres. The diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. The functor preserves filtered affine limits, satisfies local RS, and all finite-type field tangent spaces are finite dimensional. Every complete-Noetherian-local formal object with finite-type residue field is effective, and versality for finite-type families is open.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Proposition 98.16.1, tag 07Y1, p. 26; Sections 98.13 and 98.15, pp. 20–26).

For the proof, construct formal versal hulls from RS and finite tangent spaces by Schlessinger's theorem (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4); then use effectivity to realize the compatible formal point and approximation to obtain a finite-type family with the prescribed tangent jet; then use the openness hypothesis and representable diagonal to obtain smooth charts. The sufficient obstruction criterion is openness-versality; then take the bounded coproduct of charts at finite-type field points, prove surjectivity by openness, and apply Artin's bootstrap (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17); limit preservation supplies local finite presentation.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFilteredColimits`, `formal_object_approximation`, `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective`, `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `artin_stack_criterion`. An étale stack in groupoids X over S satisfying the listed hypotheses admits a smooth surjective atlas by schemes and is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over S. Limit preservation is equivalence of the 2-colimit of affine fibre groupoids with the fibre over the filtered colimit.

Here X is a stack for the étale topology; S is locally Noetherian; `O_{S,s}` is a G-ring for every finite-type point s. A fixed universe bounds the cardinalities of both isomorphism classes and arrows over finite-type fields. The diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. The functor preserves filtered affine limits, satisfies local RS, and all finite-type field tangent and infinitesimal automorphism spaces are finite dimensional. Every complete-Noetherian-local formal object with finite-type residue field is in the essential image of restriction, and versality for finite-type families is open.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.17.1, tag 07Y4, p. 27; Section 98.14, pp. 24–25).

For the proof, construct versal deformation hulls, retaining infinitesimal automorphisms; then use essential effectivity, approximation and open versality to obtain smooth charts. Represented diagonal identifies Isom sheaves with spaces and supplies fully faithful compatible restriction of morphisms; then take the bounded coproduct, test surjectivity at finite-type points after base change, and conclude algebraicity.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, `formal_object_approximation`, `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective`, `ArtinCriteria.TangentFiber`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4.

### 7.1a A concrete gluing failure

`ArtinCriteria.StrongGluingTests.subsetImage` sends a commutative ring to its set of subsets and a ring map to direct image. Direct image sends the empty set to the empty set and `{1}` to `{1}`, and it is functorial. It is a covariant functor, but it does not satisfy strong infinitesimal gluing: distinct subsets of a ring pullback can have identical images under both projections. (Direct-image functoriality and the explicit dual-number pullback.)

**Checks.**

- `SubsetImageChecks.empty`: the image of the empty set is empty.
- `SubsetImageChecks.unit`: the image of `{1}` is `{1}`, including a map between different rings.
- `ArtinCriteria.StrongGluingTests.subsetFailure`: The functor R↦Set(R), with direct-image maps, fails RS*. For both maps `Q[ε]/ε²→Q`, the diagonal subset and the whole pullback have the same two projections but are distinct: `(ε,0)` is in the latter only. Thus the comparison is not injective even for a square-zero surjection.

### 7.2 Perfect-complex rank loci

Prove `fibre_betti_semicontinuity`. For a perfect complex K on an algebraic space Y, `β_i(y)=dim_{κ(y)}Hⁱ(K⊗^Lκ(y))` is upper semicontinuous, étale locally constructible, and invariant under arbitrary residue-field extension. The finite alternating sum `χ(K_y)=Σ_i(−1)ⁱβ_i(y)` is locally constant. Apply this to the perfect pushforwards of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.9 (`perfect_proper_pushforward`).

Here Finite Tor amplitude is imposed locally, so the Euler sum is finite; the fibre is derived.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-perfect.pdf), Lemmas 75.26.1–75.26.3, p. 64).

For the proof, represent K locally by a bounded finite locally free complex; then compute differential ranks by determinantal ideals and their changes under field extension; then subtract successive ranks for `β_i` and cancel them in the alternating sum.

*Needs:* EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.9 (`perfect_proper_pushforward`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18.

Prove `single_degree_free_locus`. For a perfect complex K on Y, a fixed integer i and rank `r≥0`, the condition that `K_y` has cohomology only in degree i and `β_i(y)=r` is represented by an open subspace `U⊂Y`. Universally for `T→Y` it means `K_T≅V[−i]` for a locally free rank-r module V on T. This equivalence is local on T and commutes with arbitrary base change.

Here Use a perfect K; the condition covers all degrees, not merely `β_i=r`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-perfect.pdf), Lemma 75.26.4, pp. 64–65).

For the proof, split invertible blocks in a finite free complex near the specified fibre; then discard its contractible summands to isolate the single free module; then prove the resulting locus represents the condition after all base changes.

*Needs:* `fibre_betti_semicontinuity`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18.

Prove `lowest_degree_rank_stratum`. Let K be perfect of Tor amplitude `[a,b]`. The locus `β_a=r` has a finitely presented locally closed structure representing, for every `T→Y`, the condition that `H^a(K_T)` is locally free of rank r and its formation commutes with every further base change. On the open `β_a≤r` locus this stratum is closed.

Here `a≤b` and `r≥0`; use cohomological degree a, even when `a≠0`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-perfect.pdf), Lemma 75.26.6, tag 0D21, pp. 65–66, corrected in its final clause).

For the proof, use a finite free complex in degrees a,…,b and the determinantal locus of its first differential; then the rank condition yields a free kernel with arbitrary-base-change compatibility; then construct its universal locally closed scheme structure and descend étale locally.

*Needs:* `fibre_betti_semicontinuity`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18.

Prove `universal_functions`. If `f:X→Y` is proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically reduced, geometrically connected fibres, then `O_T→(f_T)_*O_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every `T→Y`. More generally the same conclusion holds when `H⁰(X_k,O)=k` for every field-valued point `Spec k→Y`. Étale locally `Rf_*O_X` splits as `O_Y⊕P` with P perfect of Tor amplitude at least 1.

Here the field-valued test is quantified over every point; geometric connectedness alone without geometric reducedness does not suffice.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/spaces-perfect.pdf), Lemmas 75.26.7–75.26.8, pp. 65–66).

For the proof, apply the perfect complex theorem to `O_X`; then split its unit summand after detecting a one-dimensional `H⁰` and a unit nonzero in every field fibre; then the complementary positive-amplitude complex has no `H⁰` after any base change.

*Needs:* EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.9 (`perfect_proper_pushforward`), `single_degree_free_locus`.

### 7.3 Picard stack carriers and algebraic representability inputs

Define `PicardStackSpaces`. For `f:X→B` define the stack whose fibre over `T→B` is the groupoid of invertible `O_{X_T}`-modules with all isomorphisms, and whose pullback functors are pullback of invertible modules. Tensor product, the structure sheaf and duals make this a commutative group stack. It is not the discrete groupoid on the relative Picard sheaf.

Here X and B are algebraic spaces; invertible modules are taken on their small étale ringed sites; morphisms include line-bundle automorphisms.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/quot.pdf), Section 99.10, tag 0D02, p. 26).

The API gives `PicardStackSpaces.ofLineBundle`: An invertible module on `X_T` defines an object in the fibre over T; `PicardStackSpaces.pullback`: Pullback respects tensor, unit and composition up to the canonical coherent isomorphisms; `PicardStackSpaces.automorphism`: Automorphisms of a line bundle are `Γ(X_T,O_X_T×)`; under universal functions this is `Γ(T,O_T×)`; `PicardStackSpaces.unit`: The structure sheaf on `X_T` is the tensor unit in the fibre groupoid; `PicardStackSpaces.tensor`: Tensor product of invertible modules induces the fibrewise Picard groupoid operation, with associativity, symmetry and unit constraints; `PicardStackSpaces.dual`: Dualizing an invertible module gives its tensor inverse with the evaluation isomorphism to the unit; `PicardStackSpaces.hom_equiv`: Arrows over `id_T` are precisely the isomorphisms of invertible `O_X_T`-modules, not equality of their Picard classes; `PicardStackSpaces.descent`: For each fppf cover of T the comparison to descent data is an equivalence of groupoids, retaining morphisms and cocycle isomorphisms.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.7, `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

**Checks.**

- `PicardStackTests.point`: For `X=B=Spec k` the fibre stack is B `G_m`, although the relative Picard sheaf is zero.
- `PicardStackTests.disjointPoints`: For two points over k the trivial line bundle has automorphism group `k××k`×.
- `PicardStackTests.baseChange`: Restricting the stack to Sch/T agrees with the Picard stack of `X_T/T`.

Prove `cohStackFiniteTypeModel`. Let `f : X → B` be a separated morphism of finite presentation between algebraic spaces, and write `Coh_{X/B}` for the stack whose fibre over `T→B` is the groupoid of finitely presented T-flat quasi-coherent modules on `X_T` with support proper over T. (i) For every morphism `B′ → B`, with `X′ = X ×_B B′`, `Coh_{X′/B′}` is the 2-fibre product of `Coh_{X/B}` with `B′` over B; in particular an étale surjection `B′ → B` from a scheme gives an étale surjection `Coh_{X′/B′} → Coh_{X/B}`. (ii) If `B = Spec Λ` is affine and `Λ = colim Λ_i` is a filtered colimit of finite-type ℤ-algebras, there are an index i and a separated finitely presented `X_i → Spec Λ_i` with `X ≅ X_i ×_{Spec Λ_i} Spec Λ`. Hence algebraicity of Coh over every finite-type affine ℤ-scheme implies algebraicity of `Coh_{X/B}`.

Here f separated and of finite presentation; B an arbitrary algebraic space; the models are over finite-type ℤ-algebras.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09DS), proof of Theorem 99.6.1, reduction steps; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08LP), Remark 99.5.5; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07SK), Lemma 70.7.1; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0851), Lemma 70.6.9).

For the proof, (i) holds because an object over `T → B′` is a module on `X_T = X′ ×_{B′} T`, which depends only on the composite `T → B`; algebraicity is stable under base change and étale local on the base (SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18–1.20). For (ii), `Spec Λ` = lim `Spec Λ_i` with affine transition maps; choose an affine étale presentation `U → X` with relation `R = U ×_X U`, descend U, R and the groupoid maps to some stage by `finite_presentation_limits` of SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9, enlarge the index until the source and target maps are étale and `R → U × U` is a monomorphism, and descend separatedness of f to a finite stage as in Lemma 70.6.9. Then (i) applies to `Spec Λ → Spec Λ_i`.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 (`noetherian_approximation`, `finite_presentation_limits`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.2–1.6, 1.18–1.20, `spaceQuasicoherentModules`.

**Checks.**

- `CohModelChecks.finiteType`: when Λ is already of finite type over ℤ, the index with `Λ_i = Λ` and the model X itself are allowed.
- `CohModelChecks.field`: for a field k, `P¹_k` is the base change of `P¹_{Λ_i}` for every finite-type ℤ-subalgebra `Λ_i ⊂ k`, and `Coh_{P¹_k/k}` is the base change of `Coh_{P¹_{Λ_i}/Λ_i}`.
- `CohModelChecks.etaleCover`: for B an algebraic space and an étale scheme cover `B′ → B`, an object of `Coh_{X/B}` over T lifts to `Coh_{X′/B′}` only after the étale cover `T ×_B B′ → T`; T-points need not lift globally.

Prove `universalFlatteningProperSupport`. Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces and F a finitely presented `O_X`-module whose support is proper over Y. Then F is universally pure relative to Y, and the functor sending `T → Y` to a point when `F_T` is flat over T, and to the empty set otherwise, is represented by a monomorphism of finite presentation `Y′ → Y`, the universal flattening of F. Its formation commutes with base change in Y.

Here f of finite presentation; F finitely presented with support proper over Y; no Noetherian hypothesis. Generic flatness of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12 gives only a dense open of flatness and does not replace this theorem.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CVI), Lemma 77.3.6; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CX1), Theorem 77.11.7; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CX2), Lemma 77.11.8; scheme case [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05UF), Lemma 38.27.4).

For the proof, proper support makes F universally pure: an associated point of a fibre specializes inside the proper support to a point over the closed point of any henselian test trait. The flattening functor is an fppf sheaf and a subfunctor of Y, so its diagonal is that of Y, and representability is étale local on Y because a monomorphism of finite presentation is separated and quasi-finite and such morphisms descend. On an affine scheme Y, use descending induction on n for the subfunctors of flatness in fibre dimensions at least n, applying the scheme theorem for pure modules at each step and re-establishing purity after each quasi-finite base change.

*Needs:* `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `FlatteningChecks.flat`: for F flat over Y the universal flattening is Y itself.
- `FlatteningChecks.point`: for `Y = Spec k[t]`, `X = Y` and `F = k[t]/(t)`, `F_T = O_T/tO_T` is flat exactly when `V(t)` is open and closed in T, so the universal flattening is `Spec k` ⊔ `(Y ∖ {0}) → Y`. It is a bijective monomorphism of finite presentation but not an immersion; neither the closed point nor the open complement alone represents the functor.
- `FlatteningChecks.baseChange`: in the same example, base change to the closed point `Spec k → Y` gives the identity of `Spec k`, as F becomes free of rank one there; formation commutes with base change.

Compatible perfect ring-complex systems use DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.E.1
(`perfectInverseSystemEffectivity`).

Prove `coherentModuleHom`. Let `f:X→B` be a morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces, F a finitely presented quasi-coherent `O_X`-module, and G a finitely presented quasi-coherent `O_X`-module, flat over B with support proper over B. The functor on schemes over B sending T to `Hom_(O_(X_T))`(`F_T`,`G_T`) is represented by an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over B. Its API `coherentModuleHom.evaluation` gives the universal module homomorphism on `X×_B Hom(F,G)`; `coherentModuleHom.composition` represents composition whenever the three Hom functors satisfy these hypotheses; `coherentModuleHom.baseChange` identifies `Hom(F,G)×_B B′` with `Hom(F_(B′),G_(B′))` for every algebraic-space base change `B′→B`, respecting evaluation and composition. F need not be B-flat or have proper support. The representing space is not asserted flat over B.

Here modules use `spaceQuasicoherentModules` on the ringed small étale site, with pullback defining `F_T` and `G_T`. This Hom functor concerns module maps, distinct from Layer 2's Hom schemes of schemes.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08K6), Proposition 99.3.10; Situation 99.3.1, tag 08JT, and Remark 99.3.4 for the base-change functor.)

*Needs:* `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 (Noetherian approximation and finite-presentation limits), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (affine morphisms, étale descent of algebraic spaces). The affine representability construction for module Hom is a target here.

**Checks.**

- `CoherentModuleChecks.movingSectionsHom`: for `B=Spec k[t]`, `X=Spec k[t,x]`, `F=O_X/(x)` and `G=O_X/(x−t)`, both supports are sections and both modules are B-flat. On a k[t]-algebra R, every map is multiplication by `b∈R` with tb=0, so `Hom(F,G)=Spec k[t,z]`/(tz).
- `CoherentModuleChecks.specialFibre`: in that example `f_*Hom_X(F,G)=0` on B, while at `t=0` the representing Hom fibre is `A¹_k`. Its coordinate ring has t-torsion, so it is not B-flat; pulling back the single module `f_*Hom_X(F,G)` would give the wrong functor.
- `CoherentModuleChecks.nonflatSource`: for `X=B=Spec k[t]`, `F=O_B/(t)` and `G=O_B`, the same space `Spec k[t,z]`/(tz) represents Hom. The source F is not B-flat and imposes no proper-support condition in the Hom theorem.

Prove `coherentModuleIsom`. Under the hypotheses of `coherentModuleHom`, suppose also that F is B-flat with support proper over B. Represent `Isom_(O_(X_T))`(`F_T`,`G_T`) by the fibre over (`id_F`,`id_G`) of
`Hom(F,G)×_B Hom(G,F)→Hom(F,F)×_B Hom(G,G)`, sending `(u,v)` to `(v∘u,u∘v)`.
The identity section is a closed immersion of finite presentation, because both endomorphism spaces are affine and of finite presentation. Thus `Isom(F,G)` is affine of finite presentation over B. Evaluation, composition, identities and inversion represent the corresponding module operations, and arbitrary base change preserves the construction. The base change of the relative diagonal of `Coh_{X/B}` by the pair of families `(F,G)` on T is exactly this Isom space over T.

Here f is of finite presentation, and both F and G are finitely presented, B-flat and have proper support; no algebraicity of Coh is an input to this construction.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08K9), Proposition 99.4.3; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08W6), Lemma 99.5.3; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DLY), Lemma 108.4.1.)

*Needs:* `coherentModuleHom` with evaluation, composition and base change; SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (finite-presentation closed sections and fibre products).

**Checks.**

- `CoherentModuleChecks.movingSectionsIsom`: for the two section modules above, a map is invertible exactly when its multiplier b is a unit and tb=0. Thus `Isom(F,G)=Spec k[t,z,z⁻¹]/(t)`, empty away from `t=0` and `G_m` over `t=0`.
- `CoherentModuleChecks.line`: for `X=B` and `F=G=O_B`, `Hom(F,G)=A¹_B` and the two-composite identity fibre is `G_m`,B, the diagonal fibre of the rank-one component of `Coh_{B/B}`.
- `CoherentModuleChecks.zero`: `Isom(0,0)=B` with its unique identity; `Isom(0,O_B)` is empty over a nonempty base. The rank-zero component of Coh retains this identity arrow.

Prove `rigidification_gm_torsor`. For proper flat finitely presented `X→B` with a section σ, the map from the stack of σ-rigidified line bundles to the Picard stack is representable, smooth and surjective: over L on `X_T` its fibre is the `G_m`-torsor of trivializations of `σ_T*L`. This conclusion does not require universal functions.

Here Rigidification is an isomorphism `O_T≅σ_T*L`; a global trivialization need not exist on T.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/quot.pdf), Lemma 99.11.6, pp. 28–29).

For the proof, pull back along an arbitrary object L; then identify the fibre with the sheaf of trivializations of its invertible module on T; then this is a `G_m`-torsor, hence represented smoothly and surjectively.

*Needs:* `sectionRigidifiedPicard`, `PicardStackSpaces`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.9.

Prove `picard_infinitesimal_lifting`. Let `X₀` be proper over k and `X_A⊂X_A′` a flat small Artinian thickening of kernel I annihilated by the maximal ideal. For a line bundle `L_A` the obstruction to a lift with specified reduction lies in `H²(X₀,O_X₀)⊗_k I`. When it vanishes, framed lift classes form a torsor under `H¹(X₀,O_X₀)⊗I` and infinitesimal automorphisms are `H⁰(X₀,O_X₀)⊗I`. Extend the existing scheme statement to algebraic spaces by étale descent.

Here Use framed lifts. Unframed fibres of `Pic(X_A′)→Pic(X_A)` can be quotients by unit boundary maps. `H²=0` is sufficient for smoothness, not a necessary condition.

([Steven L. Kleiman](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504020), Proposition 5.19 and proof, p. 47; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/moduli.pdf), Lemma 108.8.5 and proof, pp. 13–14).

For the proof, on the ringed étale site use the square-zero unit sequence `1→1+I O_X₀→O_X_A′×→O_X_A×→1`; then identify `1+I O_X₀` with the additive quasi-coherent module and read the connecting classes; then import the scheme calculation and descend it on space charts, retaining the framing and automorphisms.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6, `PicardStackSpaces`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.10, `ModuleObstructionTheory`.

ComplexComparisonPartII §§C3.2f.1–C3.2f.2 defines the identity-component subfunctor `picardZeroSheaf` and proves `picardZeroCriterion`. These use the general algebraic-space component construction of §7.9 and retain the full nonreduced structure.

Define `RaynaudNStar`. For a proper flat finitely presented scheme X over a discrete valuation trait S, condition N means the special fibre has no embedded associated points and X is normal at the generic points of that fibre. Condition N* adds `f_*O_X=O_S`. The last equality is over S itself; universal cohomological flatness is a conclusion of the degree-one criterion, not part of the definition.

Here S is a discrete valuation trait; this definition is not a condition on an arbitrary base.

([Michel Raynaud](https://www.numdam.org/article/PMIHES_1970__38__27_0.pdf), Definition 6.1.4, pp. 48–49; Example 9.1.2, p. 67).

The API gives `RaynaudNStar.noEmbedded`: The special fibre has no embedded associated points; `RaynaudNStar.genericNormal`: The total space is normal at every generic point of the special fibre; `RaynaudNStar.functions`: The structure-sheaf direct image over the trait is `O_S`; `RaynaudNStar.mk`: Bundle the absence of embedded special-fibre associated points, normality at its generic points and the specified canonical `O_S≅f_*O_X` comparison; `RaynaudNStar.ofIso`: An isomorphism of proper flat models over the same trait transports N*.

*Needs:* StableReduction Layer 2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20.

**Checks.**

- `RaynaudTests.regularPoint`: For `X=S` with the identity morphism, N* holds.
- `RaynaudTests.embeddedPoint`: In Raynaud 9.1.2 (p. 67), pinch two distinct rational points in the special fibre of `P¹` over a trait. The resulting reduced proper flat model has generic fibre `P¹`, but its special fibre has an embedded point at the node, so it fails N. Generic normality alone is insufficient.
- `RaynaudTests.nontrivialConstants`: For a nontrivial finite unramified trait extension `X→S`, N holds but N* fails because `f_*O_X` is the extension ring.

Prove `raynaud_degree_one_cohomologicallyFlat`. Let `f:X→S` be a proper flat finitely presented relative curve over a discrete valuation trait satisfying N*. If the generic fibre after strict henselization of S has a divisor of degree one, f is cohomologically flat in degree zero: formation of `f_*O_X` commutes with every base change. A section also implies cohomological flatness in degree zero. When the section meets the smooth locus of the generic fibre, it supplies a degree-one Cartier divisor there.

Here the divisor is on the generic fibre after strict henselization. A generic degree-one divisor without N* does not meet the theorem; The section conclusion uses the curve Picard formal-smoothness route; an arbitrary section is not asserted to be a Cartier divisor at a singular point.

([Michel Raynaud](https://www.numdam.org/article/PMIHES_1970__38__27_0.pdf), Theorem 8.2.1, pp. 66–67; Theorem 7.2.1, p. 60; Corollary 2.3.2, p. 37; [Stefan Schröer](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.07025), Proposition 8.1, p. 22).

For the proof, apply Raynaud 8.2.1(ii)⇒(iii)⇒(iv) to the strict-henselian generic degree-one divisor; retain N* throughout; then for the section case use the étale quasi-section in Raynaud 7.2.1 and formal smoothness of the curve Picard functor (2.3.2, or the `H²`-vanishing lifting argument). A section need not meet the regular generic locus; then if the section does meet the smooth generic locus, its generic point is a degree-one effective Cartier divisor, giving the first route as well.

*Needs:* `RaynaudNStar`, StableReduction Layer 2, `picard_infinitesimal_lifting`.

### 7.4 Nonarchimedean analytic space comparisons

Define `SpaceAnalytification`. For an algebraic space X locally of finite type over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, take an étale scheme presentation `R⇉U` and use an existing analytic quotient of the analytified relation `R^an⇉U^an`; separated X has such a quotient by the next theorem. Its quotient sheaf is represented, and `U^an→X^an` is an étale cover with `R^an≅U^an×_{X^an}U^an`.

Here AdicSpacesPartII R1.3 supplies rigid scheme analytification. Existence is not assumed for every locally separated X.

([Brian Conrad and Michael Temkin](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/analgpaper.pdf), Introduction, p. 1; Lemma 2.2.1, Definition 2.2.2, Theorem 2.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.4, pp. 7–9).

The API gives `SpaceAnalytification.chart`: The analytic chart is étale and surjective, with relation equal to its fibre product; `SpaceAnalytification.quotient`: Maps out are exactly maps out of `U^an` equalizing the two relation arrows; `SpaceAnalytification.scheme`: For a scheme, this agrees with the existing scheme analytification, including the structure sheaf; `SpaceAnalytification.map`: A morphism of analytifiable algebraic spaces induces the canonical analytic morphism independent of chart refinements; `SpaceAnalytification.map_id`: Analytifying an identity gives the identity after the canonical quotient comparison; `SpaceAnalytification.map_comp`: Analytification respects composition with the canonical presentation-independent identifications.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.14, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.5, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.4, AdicSpacesPartII R1.3.

**Checks.**

- `AnalytificationTests.dualNumbers`: For `Spec K[ε]/ε²` the analytic local ring contains the nonzero class ε with `ε²=0`.
- `AnalytificationTests.point`: A single field point analytifies to the existing analytic field point.
- `AnalytificationTests.presentation`: A disjoint union presentation of the same scheme gives the same analytification and its actual overlap relation.

Prove `separated_nonarch_analytification`. Every separated algebraic space locally of finite type over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field admits rigid analytification, compatible with the scheme construction. On the Berkovich side an étale equivalence relation `R⇉U` with closed-immersion diagonal has a separated analytic quotient; good and strictly analytic properties descend.

Here Separatedness, not merely local separatedness, guarantees existence. AdicSpacesPartII supplies the rigid scheme substrate; §7.10.2 builds the additional Berkovich/graded-germ quotient substrate; this target is their separated finite-type space extension by the same étale-relation quotient construction.

([Brian Conrad and Michael Temkin](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/analgpaper.pdf), Theorems 4.2.1–4.2.2, p. 20 and proofs §§4.3–5; Example 3.1.1, pp. 14–15).

For the proof, choose separated étale scheme charts; the analytified relation has closed diagonal; then apply the analytic quotient theorem, reducing étale-locally to free finite-group actions and gluing their quotients; then use the good strictly analytic/rigid comparison to return to rigid spaces; the named nonarchEtaleQuotient construction below supplies the Berkovich quotient theorem, including its finite-group and graded-valuation steps.

*Needs:* `SpaceAnalytification`, AdicSpacesPartII R1.3, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `analytification_descent`. For analytifiable algebraic spaces over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field, the quotient analytification is independent up to unique canonical isomorphism of the chosen étale presentation. It is functorial in morphisms and compatible with fibre products whenever the terms are analytifiable. The scheme comparison respects these identifications.

Here étale morphisms stay étale and need not be local isomorphisms for the rigid topology.

([Brian Conrad and Michael Temkin](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/analgpaper.pdf), Theorem 2.2.3, pp. 7–8; §2.3, pp. 11–13 (Theorem 2.3.1 and Example 2.3.2)).

For the proof, use the common refinement of two étale presentations and the quotient universal property; then lift morphisms on refinements and descend them; uniqueness gives identity and composition; then apply the scheme fibre-product theorem to charts and descend the resulting comparison.

*Needs:* `SpaceAnalytification`, AdicSpacesPartII R1.3.

Prove `proper_space_gaga`. For a proper morphism `h:X→Y` of analytifiable finite-type algebraic spaces over K and coherent F, `(R^j h_*F)^an→R^j h^an_*F^an` is an isomorphism for every `j≥0`. For X proper over K, analytification induces an exact tensor equivalence of coherent-module categories.

Here K is complete and nontrivially valued; the source is the étale ringed site of an algebraic space. This is the space extension of the existing proper scheme theorem. The proper scheme GAGA input is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.7.

([Brian Conrad and Michael Temkin](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/analgpaper.pdf), §3.3, Example 3.3.1, pp. 16–17).

For the proof, construct the morphism of étale ringed topoi using analytic charts and flat local stalk comparisons; then use coherent-module equivalence between rigid Tate and étale sites; then apply Chow modifications and coherent dévissage for algebraic spaces to reduce to proper scheme GAGA; use cohomological descent rather than claiming proper spaces are projective schemes.

*Needs:* `analytification_descent`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.10, AdicSpacesPartIII R3.7 (*proper-gaga*), AdicSpacesPartIII R3.7 (*proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence*), Layer 3.

### 7.5 Valuations, boundary duality and K/O

Prove `arithmetic_normalization_genericallyEtale`. For a field k, a reduced finite-type k-algebra A and a finite extension E of its total fraction ring, its relative normalization is finite by `nagata_normalization_finite` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20). For `A=k[t₁,…,t_d]` and a finite separable extension `E/k(t₁,…,t_d)`, the finite normalization is generically étale. Finite normalization also holds for reduced finite-type schemes over an excellent base without a separability assumption.

Here Finite many generic field extensions; separability is used only for the generic-étale conclusion, not for finite normalization.

([Philip Dittmann and Florian Pop](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.01307), Proposition 3.8 and proof, pp. 10–11; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20).

For the proof, use `nagata_normalization_finite` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20); then for a separable function-field extension, invert the nonzero discriminant of a primitive element and compare the normalization on this open; then apply the same theorem to excellent bases, which are Nagata (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21); retain inseparable finite extensions for the finiteness assertion.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `ArithmeticCoefficients.valuation_prolongation_integrality`. Let F be a field, `E/F` a finite extension, (`V_i`) any family of valuation subrings of F and B=`∩_i` `V_i` inside F. The integral closure of B in E is the intersection of all valuation subrings W of E whose intersection with F is one of the specified `V_i`, taking every prolongation of each `V_i`. No equality `Frac(B)=F` is required.

Here Empty families are interpreted as `B=F` and the intersection in E as E; all prolongations, not one chosen prolongation per `V_i`, are used.

([Philip Dittmann and Florian Pop](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.01307), Lemma 5.3 and proof, p. 17; the statement for a specified family generalizes the arithmetic statement of the source).

For the proof, to extend a `V_i` to the finite normal splitting extension `N/F`, regard its image as a local subring of N and apply `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`. Contract the dominating valuation ring to F; `ValuationSubring.isMax_toLocalSubring` identifies this contraction with `V_i`. This works without `Frac(B)=F`; then if x belongs to every specified prolongation in E, every F-conjugate of x lies in the chosen prolongation to N: contract the valuation subring along each embedding `F(x)→N` and extend to E by the same domination argument. Apply `ArithmeticCoefficients.root_coefficient_descent`, retaining inseparable root multiplicities, to place all minimal-polynomial coefficients in each `V_i`, hence in B; then conversely an integral equation over B also holds over each `V_i`, and every prolongation is integrally closed. The existing `iInf_valuationSubring_superset` is the general integral-closure comparison; the specified-family arithmetic form is proved here.

*Needs:* Mathlib `integralClosure`, `ArithmeticCoefficients.root_coefficient_descent`, Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`, Mathlib `ValuationSubring.isMax_toLocalSubring`, Mathlib `iInf_valuationSubring_superset`, Mathlib `ValuationSubring.comap`.

Prove `ArithmeticCoefficients.root_coefficient_descent`. Let V be a valuation subring of F, W a valuation subring of an extension field N with `W∩F=V`, and `p∈F[T]` monic. If p splits in N and every root, including its multiplicity, belongs to W, then every coefficient of p lies in V. In particular, let `E/F` be finite, `x∈E` and `N/F` a finite normal extension containing every conjugate of x. Let V be a valuation subring of F and W a prolongation to N. If every F-embedding of `F(x)` into N sends x into W, every coefficient of the monic minimal polynomial of x lies in V. Therefore the coefficients lie in ∩`V_i` when the condition holds for each specified `V_i` and prolongation.

Here For inseparable extensions retain multiplicities of roots in the minimal polynomial; separability is not required for this coefficient conclusion.

([Philip Dittmann and Florian Pop](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.01307), Lemma 5.3 and proof, p. 17; the statement for a specified family generalizes the arithmetic statement of the source).

For the proof, write the minimal polynomial as the product of all conjugate roots with their inseparable multiplicities in N; then each elementary symmetric polynomial belongs to W because every root does; then coefficients already lie in F, so `W∩F=V` places them in V.

*Needs:* Mathlib `integralClosure`, Mathlib `ValuationSubring.comap`, Mathlib `Polynomial.Splits.eq_prod_roots_of_monic`, Mathlib `minpoly`.

Prove `cartier_duality_restriction`. Let S be Noetherian and `f:X→Y` an embeddable morphism between embeddable S-schemes X,Y, both local complete intersections of the same pure relative dimension n over S. Let F be locally free of finite rank r on Y and h a section of a line bundle L with h regular on Y and `f*h` regular on X. Write `D=V(h)`, `D′=V(f*h)` and `f_D:D′→D`. Then the canonical comparison `(f^!F)|_{D′}≅f_D^!(F|_D)` is an isomorphism of locally free sheaves of rank r. Here `f^!O_Y≅ω_{X/S}⊗f*ω_{Y/S}^{−1}` lies in degree zero; f itself is not assumed lci. For finite flat f the comparison on affine charts is `Hom_A(B,F)⊗_B(B/hB)≅Hom_{A/h}(B/hB,F/hF)`, and commutes with evaluation at one.

Here S is Noetherian; embeddability has the finite-type separated convention of the upper-shriek pseudofunctor of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19. Regularity of both Cartier equations and equal relative dimensions are retained. F need not be invertible; r is arbitrary.

([George Boxer, Frank Calegari, Toby Gee and Vincent Pilloni](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.09269v3), Lemmas 3.8.9–3.8.10, p. 59, arXiv v3, where the statement is read for locally free F of arbitrary rank; duality with perfect coefficients is SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.18–2.19).

For the proof, use the composition law of `f^!` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19) and the lci formulas for `X/S` and `Y/S` to identify f!`O_Y` with the indicated line bundle in degree zero, then tensor with `f*F`. Do not infer that f is lci from the two lci structure maps; then represent `O_D` by the perfect two-term complex L⁻¹→`O_Y`. Apply the base-change comparison for perfect complexes (SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.18–2.19); regularity on both sides and local freeness eliminate higher Tor. This identifies the restriction with the duality expression for `D′/D`; then glue the canonical comparisons and check composition coherence. In the finite-flat specialization use the formula `pushforwardRightAdjoint_affine_finite` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19) and its evaluation-at-one trace.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.19–2.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19 (`pushforwardRightAdjoint_affine_finite`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2.

Prove `ArithmeticCoefficients.boundaryDual_mulInput`. For an A-algebra B and ideals `I ⊆ A`, `J ⊆ B`, the
A-linear maps `ℓ : B → A` with `ℓ(J) ⊆ I` are Mathlib's `Submodule.compatibleMaps (J.restrictScalars A) I`,
and `Submodule.mapQLinear` sends such ℓ to the induced A-linear map `B/J → A/I`, whose value at the
class of `1` is `ℓ(1)` modulo I. If `n ≥ 1`, `Jⁿ` ⊆ IB and `c ∈ J^(n−1)`, then for every A-linear
`ℓ : B → A` the functional `b ↦ ℓ`(cb) is compatible in this sense: for `b ∈ J` we have cb ∈ `Jⁿ` ⊆ IB,
and A-linearity sends IB into I.

Here no division by n and no separability hypothesis; `n ≥ 1`.

([George Boxer, Frank Calegari, Toby Gee and Vincent Pilloni](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.09269v3), Proposition 3.8.17 proof, pp. 61–62).

The construction of the induced map, its value on classes and its uniqueness are Mathlib's
(`Submodule.mapQLinear`, `Submodule.mapQ_apply`); no separate carrier of boundary functionals is
introduced.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Submodule.compatibleMaps`, Mathlib `Submodule.mapQLinear`, Mathlib `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ`.

**Checks.**

- `BoundaryTests.zeroFunctional`: the zero functional is compatible with every pair of ideals.
- `BoundaryTests.identity`: for `B = A` and `J = I`, the identity is compatible and induces the identity of `A/I`.
- `BoundaryTests.dualNumbers`: for `B = ℚ[ε]/ε²`, `I = 0` and `J = (ε)`, the ε-coefficient functional is not
  compatible because it sends ε to 1; multiplying its input by ε gives the compatible
  constant-coefficient functional.

Prove `fundamental_class_boundary`. Let `f:X→Y` be an embeddable morphism between S-schemes of the same pure relative dimension. Let `Θ : O_X → f^!O_Y` be its fundamental class, constructed here in two cases: from the trace of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.21 (`trace_finite`) when f is finite flat, and from the determinant of the differential under the hypotheses of Pilloni 4.2.4.1(1); the two agree where both are defined. Let `D_X`,`D_Y` be reduced relative effective Cartier divisors with `f⁻¹(|D_Y|)=|D_X|`. For the determinant construction assume the normal/smooth dense open and relative normal-crossings conditions of Pilloni 4.2.4.1(1); for the trace construction assume f finite flat as in (2). Then Θ sends `O_X(−D_X)` into `f^!O_Y(−D_Y)`. Under an open base change or, in the finite-flat case, any base change for which the Cartier divisors remain Cartier, this boundary map agrees with the base-changed map.

Here A determinant fundamental class over a nonflat general morphism is not declared compatible with arbitrary base change. The two construction hypotheses are kept separate; After arbitrary finite-flat base change the retained Cartier divisors can be nonreduced. Compatibility compares the base-changed boundary morphism, without reasserting the reduced-divisor construction hypotheses on the new base.

([Vincent Pilloni](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~pilloni/complexhidatheorygsp4.pdf), Lemmas 4.2.3.1–4.2.4.1 and Proposition 4.2.5.1, pp. 17–19; Fakhruddin–Pilloni, *Hecke operators and the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties*, Propositions 2.6–2.7, pp. 8–9).

For the proof, construct the two fundamental classes and prove that they agree on their common domain, using the upper-shriek functor and traces of SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.19–2.21; then on the smooth boundary chart take the determinant of the logarithmic differential; its twist maps the source boundary ideal into the target twisted dualizing module; then in the finite-flat case use the trace and boundary quotient calculation; compare the two constructions only under their common hypotheses; then for an open base change use restriction; for finite-flat base change use finite-projective Hom base change.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.19–2.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2, Mathlib `Submodule.compatibleMaps`, `cartier_duality_restriction`.

Prove `ramified_divisor_trace`. Let `f:X→Y` be finite flat between smooth varieties over a field, `D⊂Y` and `D′⊂X` smooth effective Cartier divisors with `f^*D=nD′`, `n≥1`. The canonical-bundle trace restricts to `f_*ω_X(−(n−1)D′)→ω_Y`. Restriction and adjunction give a compatible divisor map `f_{D′*}(ω_{D′}⊗O_X(−nD′)|_{D′})→ω_D⊗O_Y(−D)|_D`. These maps commute with ambient trace and quotient restriction.

Here the pullback is the scheme-theoretic equality nD′, not equality of supports. Characteristic may divide n; the statement does not divide by n.

([George Boxer, Frank Calegari, Toby Gee and Vincent Pilloni](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.09269v3), Proposition 3.8.17 and proof, pp. 61–62).

For the proof, write `I=I′ⁿ` on finite-flat affine charts. A multiplier in `I′^(n−1)` makes the dual functional kill `I′` modulo I; then use `ArithmeticCoefficients.boundaryDual_mulInput` to obtain the quotient trace, then evaluate at one; then identify the dualizing modules by adjunction to the two smooth Cartier divisors and retain their normal-line twists; then the arithmetic quotient-power trace is a separate multiplicity check; it does not supply geometric dualizing-module adjunction.

*Needs:* `cartier_duality_restriction`, Mathlib `Submodule.compatibleMaps`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.19 (`pushforwardRightAdjoint_affine_finite`), SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.19–2.21, Tau Ceti `Algebra.trace_quotient_pow_mk`.

Define `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients`. For a commutative ring O, an O-algebra K and O-module M, define KOCoefficients(M)=`(K⊗_O M)/im(m↦1⊗m)`. For a discrete valuation ring O, fraction field K, uniformizer π and flat M this identifies with `M⊗_O(K/O)`, and `0→M`/πM→KOCoefficients(M)→KOCoefficients(M)→0 is exact with first map `m↦π⁻¹⊗m` and second map multiplication by π. Apply the same construction to a locally free coherent sheaf.

Here Flatness is required for the exact identification and injection; the raw quotient construction exists for every M.

([Frank Calegari and David Geraghty](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.4224), Section 3.2, proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 19; the relative-curve and cofinite conclusions use SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.6, 2.19–2.21 and JacobianChallenge Layer C).

The API gives `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.mk`: A fractional tensor determines a class modulo integral tensors; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.integral_zero`: The class of `1⊗m` is zero; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.mk_add`: The quotient class map is additive; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.mk_surjective`: Every quotient class has a fractional-tensor representative; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.lift`: An R-linear map `K⊗_R M→N` killing every integral tensor `1⊗m` factors uniquely through the quotient; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.lift_mk`: Evaluating the induced map on mk(z) gives the original linear map evaluated at z; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.hom_ext`: R-linear maps out of KOCoefficients agreeing on every mk(z) are equal; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.map`: An R-linear map `M→N` induces a map of quotients by tensoring with `id_K`; integral tensors map to integral tensors; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.map_mk`: map(f)(mk(z))=mk((`id_K⊗f`)`(z)`); `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.map_id`: The induced quotient map of the identity is the identity; `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients.map_comp`: The induced quotient map of `g∘f` is map(g)∘map(f).

*Needs:* Mathlib `TensorProduct.mk`, Mathlib `Submodule.mkQ`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18, Mathlib `Submodule.liftQ`.

**Checks.**

- `KOTests.baseField`: For `K=O` every quotient coefficient is zero.
- `KOTests.zeroModule`: For `M=0` the coefficient module is zero.
- `KOTests.integralClass`: An integral tensor `1⊗m` is zero in the quotient, although it need not be zero in `K⊗M`.
- `KOTests.halfIntegralNonzero`: For `O=Z`, `K=Q` and `M=Z`, the class of `(1/2)⊗1` is nonzero in KOCoefficients. This tests the general raw quotient construction; it makes no DVR claim about Z and rules out defining the quotient as zero.

Prove `ArithmeticCoefficients.dvrTorsionCofiniteCriterion`. Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring, K its fraction field, π a uniformizer and k its residue field, without any finiteness assumption on k. For a π-power-torsion O-module M with `r=dim_k M[π]<∞`, construct an O-linear embedding `M↪(K/O)^r` and prove that its Matlis dual `D(M)=Hom_O(M,K/O)` is a quotient of `O^r`, hence finitely generated. Cofinite means finite generation of this algebraic Matlis dual.

Identify `K/O` with the injective hull of k: divisibility gives injectivity over the DVR, and every nonzero submodule meets its π-torsion. Embed the socle `M[π]` in the socle of `(K/O)^r`, extend by injectivity, and use essentiality of the socle in a power-torsion module to prove the extension injective. Exact Matlis duality and `D(K/O)=O` for complete O give the asserted finite quotient. (Stacks, Lemma 47.7.2, [tag 08Z3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08Z3), and §47.7, [tag 08Z1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08Z1), especially Remark 47.7.9.)

*Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.M.2 (*Matlis duality and completion inputs*, arbitrary residue field).

**Checks.**

- `DvrCofiniteChecks.zero`: `M=0` has `r=0`, the zero embedding and zero dual.
- `DvrCofiniteChecks.divisible`: for `O=ℚ[[π]]` and `M=(K/O)²`, `r=2` and `D(M)=O²`, although M is an infinite set and the residue field is infinite.
- `DvrCofiniteChecks.infiniteSocle`: `M=⊕_{n∈ℕ}k` has infinite-dimensional π-torsion and dual `∏_{n∈ℕ}k`, which is not finitely generated over O; it lies outside the criterion.

Prove `ko_cohomology_cofinite`. Let X be a proper flat finitely presented relative curve over a complete discrete valuation ring O with fraction field K, uniformizer π and residue field k, and let L be locally free coherent. Cohomology with `L_{K/O}` is zero above degree one; `H¹(X,L_{K/O})` is π-divisible, and `H⁰` and `H¹` are cofinite O-modules. Here cofinite means that the algebraic Matlis dual `Hom_O(M,K/O)` is finitely generated, for either cohomology module M; the residue field need not be finite. `H⁰(X,L_{K/O})[π]≅H⁰(X_k,L_k)`, and `H¹(X,L_{K/O})[π]` is a quotient of `H¹(X_k,L_k)`.

Here Use proper finiteness, curve cohomological dimension, filtered-colimit compatibility and the exact coefficient sequence. Do not identify cofinite with finite cardinality.

([Frank Calegari and David Geraghty](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.4224), Section 3.2, proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 19; the relative-curve and cofinite conclusions use SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.6, 2.19–2.21 and JacobianChallenge Layer C).

For the proof, apply cohomology to `0→L_k→L_{K/O}→π L_{K/O}→0`; then the curve vanishing `H²(X_k,L_k)=0` gives surjectivity of multiplication by π on `H¹`; then proper finite-dimensional special-fibre cohomology bounds the π-torsion. Filtered-colimit compatibility applied to `L_{K/O}=colim_n L/π^nL` makes both cohomology groups π-power torsion; apply `ArithmeticCoefficients.dvrTorsionCofiniteCriterion` to each. Coherent duality supplies the geometric pairings, separately from this module-duality criterion.

*Needs:* `ArithmeticCoefficients.KOCoefficients`, JacobianChallenge Layer C, StableReduction Layer 2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2, `ArithmeticCoefficients.dvrTorsionCofiniteCriterion`, DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.M.2 (*Matlis duality and completion inputs*).

Prove `rigidifiedPicardSetoid`. Under universal OT≅fT*OXT, an automorphism of `(L,α)` is identity. Any two choices of α for the same L give isomorphic rigidified objects, because their ratio is a base unit.

Here A scheme S, algebraic spaces X and B over S, and a specified S-morphism `f:X→B`; Test objects are schemes `T→B` in a fixed-universe model of Sch/B with the fppf topology; `X_T=X×_B T` and `f_T:X_T→T`. Pic uses invertible modules on the small étale ringed sites; For every scheme `T→B`, the canonical map of sheaves of rings `O_T→(f_T)_*O_(X_T)` is an isomorphism; the compatible comparison on global units is supplied; A specified S-morphism `σ:B→X` with `f∘σ=id_B` and its induced sections `σ_T:T→X_T`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Lemma 99.11.7 and proof).

For the proof, an invertible-sheaf automorphism is multiplication by a unique global unit on XT; then the rigidification makes its restriction along σ equal1; the global-functions comparison therefore makes the unit1; then for two trivializations, multiply by their ratio pulled back from T to obtain a rigidified isomorphism.

*Needs:* `sectionRigidifiedPicard`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

### 7.6 Picard sheafification and section splitting

### 7.6.1 Relative classes and section rigidifications

Throughout this topic, A scheme S, algebraic spaces X and B over S, and a specified S-morphism `f:X→B`.; Test objects are schemes `T→B` in a fixed-universe model of Sch/B with the fppf topology; `X_T=X×_B T` and `f_T:X_T→T`. Pic uses invertible modules on the small étale ringed sites..

Define `relativePicardSheaf`. For `f:X→B`, define PicX/B as the fppf sheafification on Sch/B of `T↦Pic`(XT), where Pic denotes invertible modules up to isomorphism. Equivalently sheafify the quotient presheaf Pic(XT)/fT*`Pic(T)`, since every line bundle on T is locally trivial. Tensor product supplies the abelian group law.
