([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Situation99.11.1).

The API gives `RelativePicard.ofLineBundle`: An invertible sheaf on XT gives a point of PicX/`B(T)`; `RelativePicard.pullback`: Base morphisms pull classes back, respecting identity and composition; `RelativePicard.baseLineBundle`: A line bundle pulled back from T maps to zero; `RelativePicard.quotientSheaf`: Sheafifying `T↦Pic(X_T)/im(f_T*:Pic(T)→Pic(X_T))` gives the same fppf sheaf as sheafifying `T↦Pic(X_T)`; injectivity of `f_T*` is not presumed.

*Needs:* `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.LineBundleClass`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, JacobianChallenge Layer A, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.HasSheafify`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.sheafifyLift`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.sheafifyLift_unique`.

**Checks.**

- `PicardSheafTests.identity`: For `X=B` and f=id, the relative Picard sheaf is zero, even when `Pic(B)` is nonzero.
- `PicardSheafTests.baseChange`: Restricting to Sch/T gives PicXT/T.
- `PicardSheafTests.needSheafification`: Without a section or a separate obstruction-vanishing hypothesis, a point of the sheaf need not have a representative invertible sheaf on XT.

Prove `relativePicardBaseChange`. For a scheme `T→B`, the restriction of PicX/B to Sch/T is naturally PicXT/T. Equivalently it is the fibre product of the relative Picard sheaf over B with T.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Paragraph after Situation99.11.1).

For the proof, the two presheaves agree under the canonical fibre-product identifications; then fppf covering families in Sch/T agree with their restrictions from Sch/B, so the sheafification comparisons are inverse; then tensor and morphism pullback laws agree.

*Needs:* `relativePicardSheaf`.

Prove `relativePicardKernel`. If OT→fT*OXT is an isomorphism for every scheme `T→B`, then `0→Pic(T)→Pic`(XT)→PicX/`B(T)` is exact. No surjectivity at the last arrow is asserted.

Here For every scheme `T→B`, the canonical map of sheaves of rings `O_T→(f_T)_*O_(X_T)` is an isomorphism; the compatible comparison on global units is supplied.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Lemma 99.11.3 and proof).

For the proof, a base line bundle with trivial pullback is trivial by local trivialization and the universal global-functions isomorphism; then a line bundle mapping to zero is fppf-locally trivial after base cover; then its overlap trivializations differ by units on XTij; the global-functions hypothesis identifies these with units on Tij; then their cocycle descends a base line bundle whose pullback is the original line bundle.

*Needs:* `relativePicardSheaf`, `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`, `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `sectionRigidifiedPicard`. For a section `σ:B→X` of algebraic spaces, extend the scheme rigidifications already supplied by Tau Ceti to invertible modules on the small étale ringed site. A rigidified Picard object over T is an invertible sheaf L on XT and an isomorphism α:OT≅σT*L. An arrow is an isomorphism of line bundles preserving α. Under universal OT≅fT*OXT every such object has only the identity automorphism, and its isomorphism class lies in ker(σT*:Pic(XT)→`Pic(T)`).

Here A specified S-morphism `σ:B→X` with `f∘σ=id_B` and its induced sections `σ_T:T→X_T`; The universal structure-sheaf isomorphism is required only for the asserted trivial-automorphism conclusion, not for defining the rigidified groupoid.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Definition before Lemma 99.11.5, Lemma 99.11.7).

The API gives `RigidifiedPicard.lineBundle`: The underlying invertible sheaf on XT; `RigidifiedPicard.trivialization`: The specified isomorphism OT≅σT*L; `RigidifiedPicard.pullback`: For `q:T′→T` over B, pull back L and α along `X_(T′)→X_T` and q, using the structure-sheaf unit and σ-square comparison. Identity and composite pullbacks satisfy the specified module-pseudofunctor constraints; `RigidifiedPicard.mk`: An invertible sheaf L on `X_T` and an isomorphism `α:O_T≅σ_T*L` construct a rigidified object, without a universal global-functions hypothesis; `RigidifiedPicard.hom`: In the fixed T-fibre an arrow `(L,α)→(M,β)` is a sheaf isomorphism `φ:L≅M` satisfying `σ_T*(φ)∘α=β`. Identity and composition are those of the underlying sheaf isomorphisms; `RigidifiedPicard.hom_ext`: Two rigidified arrows are equal exactly when their underlying sheaf isomorphisms agree; `RigidifiedPicard.trivial`: The structure sheaf `O_(X_T)`, with the canonical pullback unit isomorphism `O_T≅σ_T*O_(X_T)`, is the trivial rigidified object.

*Needs:* `spaceQuasicoherentModules`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

**Checks.**

- `RigidifiedPicardTests.identity`: For `X=B` the unique class is the trivial line bundle with its rigidification.
- `RigidifiedPicardTests.automorphisms`: An arbitrary scalar automorphism of L is not a rigidified arrow unless it restricts to 1 along σ.
- `RigidifiedPicardTests.P1`: For P1 with its section, the classes of `O(d)` retain all integer degrees; rigidification does not force `d=0` on X.

### 7.6.1a Rigidified representatives

Throughout this topic, A scheme S, algebraic spaces X and B over S, and a specified S-morphism `f:X→B`.; A specified S-morphism `σ:B→X` with `f∘σ=id_B` and its induced sections `σ_T:T→X_T`.; For every scheme `T→B`, the canonical map of sheaves of rings `O_T→(f_T)_*O_(X_T)` is an isomorphism; the compatible comparison on global units is supplied.; Test objects are schemes `T→B` in a fixed-universe model of Sch/B with the fppf topology; `X_T=X×_B T` and `f_T:X_T→T`. Pic uses invertible modules on the small étale ringed sites..

Prove `sectionPicardSplit`. If `σ:B→X` is a section and OT→fT*OXT is an isomorphism for all `T→B`, then `0→Pic(T)→Pic`(XT)→PicX/`B(T)→0` is split exact, with retraction σT*. Equivalently PicX/`B(T)≅ker` σT*, naturally in T.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24), Lemma 99.11.4 and proof).

For the proof, the section gives σT*fT*=id, splitting Pic(XT) into base classes and the kernel; then for locally matching kernel classes choose trivializations along σ and overlap isomorphisms; then on `T_ij` normalize the overlap map `φ_ij` by the base unit measured by `α_j`⁻¹∘`σ*φ_ij∘α_i`. Pull back the inverse of that unit to scale `φ_ij`. The inverse on `α_j` is necessary for this composite to be well typed; then the triple cocycle discrepancy restricts to 1; the universal global-functions condition makes it 1, so actual invertible-sheaf descent applies; then descend the trivializations as compatible maps and verify their inverses; this supplies a detail the source omits; then the kernel presheaf is thus an fppf sheaf and equals the relative Picard sheaf.

*Needs:* `relativePicardKernel`, `sectionRigidifiedPicard`, `rigidifiedPicardSetoid`, `spaceFpqcQuasicoherentDescent`, `finiteLocallyFreeDescent`.

### 7.6.2 Normalization over excellent bases

Prove `properSpaceNormalizationExcellent`. An algebraic space of finite type over an excellent (more generally Nagata) base is Nagata, so its normalisation (§5.4) is finite, and proper over the base when `X` is.
(Stacks, Lemma 67.26.1 (tag 0BAU), Lemma 67.26.2 (tag 0BAV), Lemma 67.49.9 (tag 0BB5).)
*Needs:* §5.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.20).

### 7.6.3 Polarized Isom comparison

Prove `polarisedIsomScheme`. Let S be locally Noetherian, X, `Y → S` projective flat, L on X and M on Y invertible, and assume the fppf relative Picard functor `Pic_{Y/S}` is represented by a separated S-scheme (for instance by ComplexComparisonPartII §C3.2d.2 `relative_picard_algebraicSpace` when that space is a scheme, or by Kleiman for projective flat families with geometrically integral fibres). Then the subfunctor of `Isom_S(X,Y)` of φ for which the relative Picard classes of `φ^*M` and L agree is represented by a closed subscheme `Isom_S((X,L),(Y,M))`, the pullback of the diagonal of `Pic_{Y/S}` along `φ ↦ [(φ^{-1})^*L]` and `φ ↦ [M]`; `Aut_S((X,L))` is a closed subgroup scheme of `Aut_S(X)`. No statement is made without separatedness of `Pic_{Y/S}`. Checks: `Isom_k((P¹,O(1)),(P¹,O(1))) = PGL_2`; `Isom((E,O(p)),(E,O(p)))` is the finite group `Aut(E,p)`.
(Kleiman, The Picard scheme, arXiv:math/0504020, Theorem 4.8, pp. 27–28 (published numbering 9.4.8); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`.)
*Needs:* §2.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.4, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.rigidifiedPicardFunctor`.
Equality of classes means equality after fppf sheafification. A global formula `φ^*M ≅ L ⊗ f_T^*N` follows when `O_T ≅ f_{T*}O_{X_T}` universally (the kernel theorem below); it is not part of the assertion for arbitrary projective flat families. `PolarisedIsomTests.sheafEquality` distinguishes this local condition from a chosen global line-bundle isomorphism.

### 7.6a Scheme Picard presheaf

`RelativePicard.relativePicardPresheaf f` sends `T→B` to line-bundle classes on `T×_B X`, using the existing `LineBundleClass` carrier. This is the raw scheme version. Its API `RelativePicard.relativePicardPresheaf_id_obj`, `RelativePicard.relativePicardPresheaf.map`, `RelativePicard.relativePicardPresheaf.map_id`, `RelativePicard.relativePicardPresheaf.map_comp` gives the identity-family comparison and contravariant pullback of classes. Its fppf sheafification gives the relative Picard sheaf, including quotienting base classes locally. The algebraic-space construction of §7.7 uses the ringed small étale site. (Stacks, §99.11, Situation 99.11.1 and the pullback discussion preceding it, tag 0D24.)

**Checks.**

- `PicardPresheafChecks.identity`: the identity family's raw value is `Pic(T)`, before sheafification kills base classes.
- `PicardPresheafChecks.field`: every line bundle on `Spec k` is trivial for a field k.
- `PicardPresheafChecks.empty`: the empty scheme has one line-bundle class.

### 7.7 Ringed étale sites, invertible modules and derived objects

For an algebraic space X, use the small étale site of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.10: objects are schemes étale over X, coverings are jointly surjective étale families, and the ring sheaf sends U to `Γ(U,O_U)`. The comparison for an étale chart `U→X` includes its map of ringed topoi and the identification of the restricted structure sheaf with `O_U`. Define `SpaceInvertibleModule X` as a sheaf of modules on this ringed site which is étale locally free of rank one. Its isomorphism groupoid, tensor product, unit, inverse dual and pullback use the sheaf-of-modules operations. The API `SpaceInvertibleModule.pullbackId`, `SpaceInvertibleModule.pullbackComp`, `SpaceInvertibleModule.tensorPullback`, `SpaceInvertibleModule.dualEvaluation`, `SpaceInvertibleModule.chartDescent` supplies actual natural isomorphisms and their coherence. Chart descent is an equivalence of groupoids of modules with descent isomorphisms on `U×_X U` and the cocycle on the triple product. Descent of invertibility is tested after the cover, rather than encoded by a field asserting the conclusion. This is the algebraic-space extension of the scheme line-bundle carrier; the scheme tensor and pullback operations remain imports. (Stacks, Cohomology of Algebraic Spaces, §3, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, pp. 2–3; Descent and Algebraic Spaces, §4 and §8, sheaf and quasi-coherent descent.)

**Checks.**

- `SpaceLineChecks.point`: over `Spec k`, an invertible module has rank one and automorphism group k×; its isomorphism classes form the trivial Picard group.
- `SpaceLineChecks.twoPoints`: over two disjoint k-points, automorphisms of the unit are `(k×)²`; replacing all automorphisms by scalar k× fails.
- `SpaceLineChecks.nilpotents`: over `k[ε]/(ε²)`, multiplication by `1+ε` is a nonidentity automorphism of the unit with inverse `1−ε`, including in characteristic two. Reduction loses this automorphism.
- `SpaceLineChecks.cocycle`: for a split cover, transitions `u_01=2` and `u_12=3` over Q force `u_02=6`. The reversed transition is `1/6`, so the overlap direction and triple equation are material.

Define `spaceDQCoh X` as the full subcategory of the derived category of `O_X`-modules whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. It is the one quasi-coherent derived category of an algebraic space: for a scheme, `spaceDQCoh.schemeEtaleEquivalence` identifies it with SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.18's `DQCoh`. Define `spacePerfect X` by étale-local quasi-isomorphism to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. Its API is `spaceDQCoh.chartRestriction`, `spaceDQCoh.schemeEtaleEquivalence`, `spaceDQCoh.derivedPullback`, `spaceDQCoh.derivedPushforward`, `spaceDQCoh.tensor`, `spaceDQCoh.cohomologyComparison`; `spacePerfect.isLocal`, `spacePerfect.pullback`, `spacePerfect.tensor`, `spacePerfect.dual`, `spacePerfect.torAmplitude`, `spacePerfect.chartCharacterisation`. The category and localization use Mathlib's derived category; X and its ringed site come from SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1. These are predicates on actual complexes and sheaves, not new unspecified carriers. For qcqs `f:X→Y`, derived pushforward preserves quasi-coherent cohomology, as checked after every affine étale chart of Y. Derived pullback uses the ringed-site map and its left-derived tensor; its composition isomorphism and the derived base-change map retain the canonical natural transformation, rather than selecting an arbitrary isomorphism. Perfectness descends through faithfully flat étale charts because a finite complex and its quasi-isomorphism can be descended after a common finite cover. (Stacks, Derived Categories of Spaces, §§5, 13 and 21; Cohomology of Algebraic Spaces, Lemma 3.3, p. 3.)

**Checks.**

- `SpaceDerivedChecks.zero`: the zero complex is perfect of every finite Tor-amplitude and its derived pushforward is zero.
- `SpaceDerivedChecks.dualNumberResidue`: k over `k[ε]/(ε²)` is coherent but is not perfect; its unbounded Tor groups forbid identifying coherence with perfectness.
- `SpaceDerivedChecks.nonflatPullback`: for `A=k[ε]/(ε²)→k`, derived tensor of the two-term complex A --ε→ A has zero differential after pullback. Ordinary tensor of its cohomology alone misses the extra Tor contribution.
- `SpaceDerivedChecks.degree`: `O_X` placed in cohomological degree a restricts to a locally free module in degree a; the lowest-degree base-change export is `H^a`, including `a≠0`.

### 7.8 Proper-space formal existence and Artin charts

Prove `properSpaceCompletionEquivalence`: for a complete Noetherian ring A with ideal of definition I and a separated finite-type algebraic space `X/A`, completion gives an equivalence between coherent sheaves with proper support and compatible coherent sheaves on `X_n=X×Spec(A/I^(n+1))` with proper support. For proper X this includes every coherent sheaf. Morphisms are recovered by the complete inverse limit of Hom, not by choosing unrelated objects at each level. The algebraic-space proof uses Chow's lemma and Noetherian dévissage: a projective modification `Y→X` is an isomorphism over a dense open; pull the formal sheaf to a projective closure of Y and use scheme formal existence. Its support stays in Y because I is in the Jacobson radical and the formal support is proper. Push the algebraized sheaf to X. The kernel and cokernel of the comparison are supported on a smaller closed subspace, killed by a fixed coherent ideal, and the dévissage induction algebraizes them. Full faithfulness identifies the descended maps and extensions. The induction starts with the zero support. This proves effectivity for spaces from the scheme theorem without assuming the desired space theorem as an input. (Stacks, More on Morphisms of Spaces, Theorem 42.11, tag 08BE, pp. 103–104; Lemmas 42.6 and 42.9, pp. 100–103.)

For an algebraic stack over a locally Noetherian base, with a complete local test ring whose residue field is of finite type over that base, `stackFormalPointEquivalence` is the equivalence between objects over a complete Noetherian local A and compatible objects over all `A/m^(n+1)`. Choose a smooth scheme presentation after a finite étale residue-field extension `A→A′`, lift a point successively through smoothness, effect its compatible scheme-valued points using completeness, and effect its Isom arrows on `A′⊗_A A′` using the represented diagonal. Full faithfulness forces the triple cocycle; fppf descent returns the object over A. This retains arrows and the specific restriction functor. (Stacks, Artin's Axioms, Lemma 9.5, pp. 12–14.)

**Checks.**

- `SpaceExistenceChecks.identity`: for `X=Spec` A, finite A-modules are recovered from their entire compatible adic towers; completion of A is A.
- `SpaceExistenceChecks.arrows`: a compatible multiplication map on the tower of the unit effects to that multiplication map over A. Effectivity only on isomorphism classes would not recover it.
- `SpaceExistenceChecks.support`: the zero sheaf effects to zero; proper support permits a nonproper ambient X, whereas an arbitrary nonproper support is outside the theorem.
- `SpaceExistenceChecks.allLevels`: an object specified only modulo `m²` is a jet and not a formal object; compatibility over every n is required.

The Artin interfaces use the full module-valued obstruction theory: for every affine base A and every A-module M, tangent and infinitesimal automorphism modules `T_x(M)`, `Inf_x(M)`, and an A-linear obstruction `O_x(M)` commute with the prescribed object and module base changes. A vanishing obstruction is equivalent to existence of the specified framed lift, and compatible extensions induce compatible obstruction maps. Openness of versality uses the product condition on T for countable module products and injectivity of O(product `M_i`)→product `O(M_i)`, as well as RS*, limit preservation and a represented diagonal. Finite-dimensional tangent data alone is insufficient. (Stacks, Artin's Axioms, Definition 22.1 and Lemma 22.2, pp. 39–40.)

Prove `effectiveHull_smoothChart` with a hull retaining its tangent isomorphism, full formal effectivity, limit preservation, the G-ring approximation hypothesis and openness of versality. Approximate the effective universal object with agreement modulo `m²` and equal associated-graded lengths; formal versality gives a map to its completed local chart. Complete-local Nakayama makes this map surjective, and equality of the lengths of every quotient makes each quotient map an isomorphism. Taking the complete inverse limit identifies the completed chart with the hull. Openness makes the induced finite-type map a smooth presentation near the chosen point. For a space criterion use a sheaf and a represented diagonal; for a stack use groupoid fibres and either a represented diagonal or the weak-diagonal criterion with its full arrow-effectivity and diagonal-versality assumptions. Do not infer a hull from an arbitrary padded smooth presentation. (Stacks, Artin's Axioms, Lemma 12.7, pp. 20–21, Lemmas 13.3–13.8, pp. 22–24, Propositions 16.1 and 17.1–17.2, pp. 26–28.)

**Checks.**

- `ArtinChartChecks.pointHull`: the point functor has hull k and a zero-dimensional minimal chart.
- `ArtinChartChecks.paddedChart`: `A¹_k→Spec k` is smooth and versal; its completed ring `k[[t]]` and tangent kernel k show that it is not the hull of the point functor.
- `ArtinChartChecks.nodePoint`: the point at the fixed node xy=0 has hull `k[[x,y]]`/(xy) and tangent dimension two. The curve-deformation smoothing parameter in xy=t belongs to a different functor.
- `ArtinChartChecks.framing`: at BG, framed automorphisms over A are `ker(G(A)→G(k))`; at `A=k` they are trivial. Unframed `G(A)` does not describe this fibre.

### 7.9 Components through the identity section

Prove `spaceSectionComponentCriterion`. Let B be locally Noetherian and P a quasi-separated group algebraic space locally of finite presentation over B. If its geometric identity components are smooth of locally constant dimension, the fibrewise identity-component subfunctor is an open group subspace `P⁰` of finite type over B. It is smooth over reduced B; over nonreduced B, formal smoothness along `P⁰` is an additional sufficient hypothesis. If those components are proper and P is separated over B, `P⁰` is proper over B and closed in P. Formation of the component subfunctor commutes with arbitrary base change and retains its full induced structure.

First construct the neutral component of a quasi-separated group algebraic space locally of finite type over a field, with its full induced structure: quasi-separatedness makes the space decent and hence separated; the group space is then a scheme. Its neutral component is an open and closed quasi-compact geometrically irreducible subgroup, compatible with field extension. (Stacks, Lemmas 79.9.4 and 79.10.2, tags 08BH and 0B8F; Proposition 39.7.11, tag 0B7R.) Translation by geometric group points carries the identity component to every component, so the smoothness assumption implies that every geometric fibre of P is smooth and geometrically reduced, and that its identity component is geometrically irreducible. The relative unicomponent locus of a finite-presentation algebraic space with geometrically reduced fibres is open; the irreducible component through a section in that locus is also open and commutes with every base change. This is an algebraic-space statement, not just a scheme assertion: Romagny proves it for algebraic stacks by smooth presentations, common refinements and descent of the resulting open subspaces. Apply this on finite-presentation neighbourhoods of the identity section and then translate them; their compatible unions give the open `P⁰` even when P is only locally finitely presented. Thus openness uses the actual space component construction and does not assume flatness prematurely. (Romagny, Proposition 2.2.4 and proof in §2.4.2, pp. 7 and 10–12.)

For smoothness over reduced B, use the dimension hypothesis separately. Pull the section to an étale scheme chart after an étale base neighbourhood. The dimension of its geometrically irreducible section component is constant. EGA IV₃, Proposition 15.6.3, p. 237, proves universal openness along that component by reduction to a DVR and closure of its generic component. Corollary 15.2.3, p. 227, and Proposition 15.6.6(ii), pp. 239–240, then give flatness over the reduced base at its geometrically reduced points. Flatness is local on source and target in the étale topology, so it descends to `P⁰`; finite presentation and smooth geometric fibres give smoothness. Over a nonreduced B, explicitly impose formal smoothness along `P⁰` instead: a locally finitely presented formally smooth morphism is smooth, and the argument never deduces flatness from fibre smoothness alone. The component subfunctor commutes with base change because geometric identity components do; the extra hypotheses needed to prove its smoothness are not silently transported to an arbitrary nonreduced new base.

For finite type, work over a Noetherian affine base and choose a quasi-compact open `U⊂P⁰` containing the image of its identity section. Such a U exists because that image is quasi-compact. Every `U_s` is a nonempty open in the geometrically irreducible smooth group `P⁰_s`. For any geometric g, the nonempty opens `U_s` and `gU_s` intersect, so g belongs to `U_s U_s^(−1)`. Consequently `U×_B U→P⁰`, `(u,v)↦uv⁻¹`, is surjective. Its source is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness, hence `P⁰` is quasi-compact and therefore of finite type. Multiplication and inverse preserve the component on geometric fibres and factor through its open subspace.

For properness, apply the separated finite-presentation, geometrically connected-fibre criterion to `P⁰→B`. The identity section makes the structural map universally submersive; properness of each fibre and the section-component valuative argument give properness near each base point. The proof passes to spaces by étale presentations, the space valuative criterion and effective descent of properness, with the same prescribed section. Since P is separated, the map from proper `P⁰` to P is proper; an open immersion which is proper is also closed. (EGA IV₃, Proposition 15.6.8, pp. 241–242, and Corollaries 15.7.10–15.7.11, p. 247; Kleiman, Proposition 5.20 and proof, pp. 47–48.)

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.13 (group algebraic spaces), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (étale presentations and descent).

**Checks.**

- `SectionComponentChecks.zero`: the zero group has a smooth proper component of dimension zero over reduced and nonreduced bases.
- `SectionComponentChecks.fullStructure`: in characteristic two, the identity component of `μ₂` is `μ₂` with its nilpotent structure.
- `SectionComponentChecks.baseChange`: the fibrewise component subfunctor commutes with base change to `Spec(k[ε]/(ε²))`.
- `SectionComponentChecks.nonreducedBase`: `Spec(B_red)→Spec B` for `B=k[ε]/(ε²)` has smooth point fibres but is not flat; fibre smoothness alone does not give smoothness over B.

### 7.10.2 Nonarchimedean local models and étale quotients

AdicSpacesPartII R0–R1 supplies complete rank-one nonarchimedean fields, affinoid algebras, their finite and étale maps, affinoid domains, rational/Laurent refinements, Tate acyclicity, rigid spaces and scheme rigid analytification. It does not supply a Berkovich carrier or germ reductions. Define the required extension `BerkovichAnalyticSpace`: a locally Hausdorff space with a net of compact affinoid domains, coordinate algebras and compatible domain restriction maps, with morphisms obtained by refining these nets. An affinoid domain has carrier the bounded multiplicative seminorm spectrum `M(A)`, with its evaluation topology and completed residue field `H(x)`. The API `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.affinoid`, `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.refineAtlas`, `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.domain`, `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.glueDomains`, `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.fibreProduct`, `BerkovichAnalyticSpace.rigidModel` comprises affinoid models, refinement equivalences, domain inclusion, compatible domain gluing and fibre products, and the rigid model for Hausdorff strictly analytic spaces. The G-topology uses finite affinoid covers on every compact domain. For nontrivially valued k, the last functor is fully faithful; its equivalence assertion is restricted to paracompact strictly analytic spaces and quasi-separated rigid spaces admitting an affinoid cover of finite type (each member meets finitely many others). On quasi-compact separated algebraic spaces the quotient constructed below is paracompact: the affine atlas has an exhaustion by compact balls, and their images under the open quotient exhaust the Hausdorff quotient. General locally finite-type separated spaces are obtained by gluing quasi-compact opens. (Berkovich, *Étale cohomology*, Definition 1.2.3 and Remarks 1.2.4, pp. 16–17; construction of morphisms following Proposition 1.2.10, pp. 20–21; Theorem 1.6.1 and Lemma 1.6.2, pp. 35–37; Conrad–Temkin, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, pp. 25–26.)

**Checks.**

- `BerkovichChecks.point`: `M(k)` has its single bounded seminorm; its rigid model is Sp k.
- `BerkovichChecks.gauss`: `M(k⟨T⟩)` includes the Gauss norm and is not just the set of k-rational points.
- `BerkovichChecks.dual`: the spectrum of `k[ε]/(ε²)` has the same points as k but retains its nilpotent coordinate algebra.
- `BerkovichChecks.refinement`: a rational cover and its Laurent refinement give the same morphisms and ringed G-space.

Define `GradedValuationSpace K k` for an extension of multiplicatively `R_{>0}`-graded fields. Its points are graded valuation subrings of K containing k, with basic opens specifying membership of finitely many nonzero homogeneous elements. A graded field requires inverses only for nonzero homogeneous elements. Its API `GradedValuationSpace.basicOpen`, `GradedValuationSpace.patchTopology`, `GradedValuationSpace.finiteExtensionMap`, `GradedValuationSpace.orbitFibre`, `GradedValuationSpace.generalizationLift` gives the basis, the compact Hausdorff constructible topology, restriction of valuations and the orbit and generalization formulas for finite automorphism groups. Define `analyticGermReduction` at x by the graded spectral-norm filtration `A_{≤r}/A_{<r}` and the image of the affinoid coordinate reduction in the graded residue field of `H(x)`, then glue reductions of a finite affinoid-domain cover of the germ. Its API `analyticGermReduction.domainEquiv`, `analyticGermReduction.inter`, `analyticGermReduction.union`, `analyticGermReduction.pullback`, `analyticGermReduction.separated`, `analyticGermReduction.goodIffAffine` identifies analytic subdomain germs with quasi-compact open subobjects of this birational space, respects intersections/unions and inverse images, detects separatedness, and identifies good germs with affine reductions. These are new prerequisites, not imports from a broad analytic roadmap title. The graded ring and valuation constructions reuse graded rings, localization and valuation-ring operations. (Temkin II §§1–2, pp. 3–10; Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.5 and Proposition 4.8, pp. 15–19; Theorem 5.1, pp. 20–21.)

Prove `gradedOrbitAffineNeighborhood`: a finite group orbit in a separated graded birational space has a group-stable affine open neighbourhood. For `L=K^G`, the graded Artin degree formula is `[K:L]=|G`| for faithful G; reduce to the degree-one field and the support-group inertia pairing. For the finite extension `K/K^G`, an extension of a fixed graded valuation ring is determined by its degree-one extension: split the field extension into the support-index and residue-field parts, and use homogeneous powers in the first and the factorial power/value argument in the second. Thus restriction `P_K→P_L` is surjective, its fibres are exactly G-orbits and it lifts generalizations. Patch compactness follows by embedding valuation membership sets in `{0,1}^{K_homˣ}`; each failure of closure, base-field containment or the valuation alternative is witnessed by finitely many coordinates. In the separated birational open containing the orbit, the intersection of inverse images of all affine neighbourhoods of the corresponding point of `P_L` is the set of generalizations of that orbit. It lies in that open. Patch compactness gives a finite intersection already inside the open; it is group-stable and affine. This argument applies to an orbit, not to an arbitrary finite set. (Conrad–Temkin Theorem 5.2.3, p. 30, Lemmas 5.3.1–5.3.3 and Corollaries 5.3.4–5.3.5, pp. 31–33; Lemma 5.3.6 and the final proof, pp. 33–34.)

For `analyticGermReduction.goodIffAffine`, lift a finite Laurent covering of an affine reduction to rational domains in the analytic germ. For a two-member Laurent cover, the two coordinate algebras agree on their overlap up to a strictly smaller spectral error. Shrink around x to obtain compatible affinoid presentations with that error smaller than the defining radii. Split Laurent series into positive and nonpositive powers and iteratively correct the overlap error; its strict norm bound makes the correction converge. Corrected generators agree on both sides and give a surjection from a weighted annulus Tate algebra to the kernel of the difference map. For quotient presentations first carry out this construction in the free algebras and then descend their compatible closed ideals. The kernel is therefore affinoid, and its rational domains recover both pieces. Induction on the Laurent covering glues an affinoid neighbourhood. This proves the implication from affine reduction to a good germ rather than assuming it. It uses the affinoid and acyclicity statements just specified. (Temkin II Theorem 5.1, pp. 20–21; Temkin I, Theorem 3.1 and proof, pp. 11–15 in the author version, published pp. 595–599.)

**Checks.**

- `GradedValuationChecks.trivial`: trivially graded fields recover ordinary valuation subrings and the usual patch topology.
- `GradedValuationChecks.support`: in a quadratic support extension with `t²=a∈k_homˣ` and degree(t)≠1, both t and `t⁻¹` belong to every graded valuation ring containing k. This follows by squaring their values; discarding non-degree-one elements would lose these units.
- `GradedValuationChecks.orbit`: `G=1` gives a singleton orbit and an affine neighbourhood at the corresponding birational point; an arbitrary finite set is not substituted for an orbit.
- `GermReductionChecks.affinoid`: an affinoid neighbourhood gives an affine reduction and a good germ.
- `GermReductionChecks.laurent`: the domains |`f|≤r` and |`f|≥r` lift their respective graded basic opens; union and intersection are respected.
- `GermReductionChecks.refine`: changing the affinoid-domain cover gives the same reduction under their common refinement.

Prove `finiteAffinoidInvariants`: for a finite group acting continuously on a k-affinoid algebra A, `A^G` is affinoid and A is finite over it. Choose finitely many topological algebra generators, enlarge their family by G-translates and use coefficients of their orbit polynomials to make a topologically finite-type subalgebra B of `A^G` over which A is finite. The finite Banach-module topology and the affinoid Artin–Tate argument give affinoidness of `A^G` and the quotient topology. No averaging by |G| is used, so residue characteristic dividing |G| is allowed. A free action on the analytic space means freeness on geometric points; it then makes `M(A)→M(A^G)` finite étale with the action relation equal to its fibre product. (Conrad–Temkin, proof of Lemma 5.2.2, pp. 29–30, the affinoid invariant step; the finite-generator argument here supplies that step from the affinoid finiteness statement.)

Define `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient U G` for a free right action of a finite group whose action map `U×G→U×U` is a closed immersion. Its API `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.projection`, `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.relationIso`, `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.finiteEtale`, `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.domain`, `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.strict`, `finiteFreeAnalyticQuotient.good` gives the projection and its full relation, finite étaleness, compatibility with invariant domains and preservation of strictness and goodness. At x, use the isotropy group of the topological point (which can be nontrivial even for a geometrically free action). The graded orbit theorem and germ reduction provide finitely many invariant affinoid-domain germs covering a neighbourhood. Shrink their representatives and intersect all translates to make them actually invariant, form their affinoid quotients by `finiteAffinoidInvariants`, and glue the quotients on their invariant overlaps. Shrink to avoid translates by elements outside the isotropy group and then saturate under G. These quotient neighbourhoods cover `U/G`; overlap and triple identities follow from the quotient universal properties. Separatedness follows from the closed action relation. (Conrad–Temkin Theorem 5.1.1, p. 26, Lemmas 5.2.1–5.2.2 and proof, pp. 28–30.)

**Checks.**

- `FiniteAnalyticQuotientChecks.identity`: `G=1` returns U with its ring sheaf.
- `FiniteAnalyticQuotientChecks.permutedCopies`: a group acting freely by permutation on its indexed disjoint copies of an affinoid has quotient that affinoid, including nilpotents.
- `FiniteAnalyticQuotientChecks.residueTwo`: an unramified quadratic extension in residue characteristic two gives a geometrically free order-two action and its original base as quotient; no inverse of two is required.
- `FiniteAnalyticQuotientChecks.notFree`: `z↦−z` at zero has a fixed geometric point; the quotient algebra can exist, but its projection is not an étale torsor there.

Define `nonarchEtaleQuotient R U` for an étale equivalence relation in this analytic category with `R→U×U` a closed immersion. Its API `nonarchEtaleQuotient.projection`, `nonarchEtaleQuotient.relationIso`, `nonarchEtaleQuotient.descent`, `nonarchEtaleQuotient.separated`, `nonarchEtaleQuotient.strict`, `nonarchEtaleQuotient.good` gives the étale cover, fibre-product identification and invariant-map universal property, and preserves the stated properties. Étale-local descent of quotient existence is obtained by forming pulled-back relations and gluing the representing quotients by unique isomorphisms. Near a point, extend its completed residue field by a finite Galois extension splitting the finitely many relation points; their étale maps then have residual isomorphisms and are local analytic isomorphisms. On a compact domain around the point, shrink away the compact image of every unwanted relation branch. The remaining branches form a finite group of germ automorphisms; shrink to a common invariant open, where the relation is its free finite-group action. The previous quotient supplies local existence. Descend and glue. Analytification of a separated algebraic-space relation satisfies the closed-immersion condition. Returning to the rigid model uses the paracompactness and local finite étale quasi-sections above, not an assertion that all nonarchimedean étale maps are local isomorphisms. (Conrad–Temkin Theorems 4.2.1–4.2.2, p. 20; Lemmas 4.3.1–4.3.3 and proofs, pp. 23–25.)

**Checks.**

- `NonarchRelationChecks.identity`: the diagonal relation returns the existing affinoid or scheme analytification.
- `NonarchRelationChecks.twoCopies`: the full relation on two equal chart copies returns one copy with its nilpotent structure.
- `NonarchRelationChecks.closed`: separated finite-type spaces satisfy the closed diagonal hypothesis; the smooth locally separated nonanalytifiable surface of Conrad–Temkin Example 3.1.1, pp. 14–15, does not justify dropping it.

### Examples

For the identity family the Picard stack is B`G_m` while its relative Picard sheaf is zero. For two points its trivial line has automorphism group `(k×)²`, so scalar automorphisms require universal functions. The dual numbers distinguish full `μ₂` in characteristic two from its reduction. In `K/O` a class of π⁻¹ is nonzero and killed by π; no division by a ramification index is used in boundary trace.

### Dependencies

Layers 3–6; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 (limits and Noetherian approximation), §0.21 (excellence), §1.10 (ringed small étale sites), §2.2 (Leray), §2.11 (Hilbert 90), §2.18 (derived categories) and §4.10 (formal existence); StableReduction Layer 2 (coherent cohomology and base change); JacobianChallenge Layers A and D (Picard theory of curves); EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.9 (`perfect_proper_pushforward`); AdicSpacesPartII R0–R1 and AdicSpacesPartIII F0.5–F0.`7/R3`.7 (affinoid algebras, formal existence, rigid spaces and proper GAGA).

## Layer 8: framed deformation and completed local comparisons

### 8.1 Framing, tangent spaces and stabilizers

Define `deformationGroupoid`. For `𝒳` fibred in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`, `k` a field of finite type over `S`, `x₀ ∈ 𝒳(Spec k)`: the category `𝒟ef_{𝒳,x₀}` cofibred in groupoids over Artinian local `S`-algebras with residue field `k`, objects over `A` being pairs `(x ∈ 𝒳(Spec A), x|_k ≅ x₀)`; a predeformation category, and a deformation category when `𝒳` satisfies (RS). The converse concerns (RS) restricted to this framed point and coefficient category, rather than global (RS) for every object of `𝒳`.

Assume `S` locally Noetherian; `k` of finite type over `S`.

The API consists of `DefGroupoid.fibre` gives framed objects and arrows inducing identity on the residue framing; `DefGroupoid.isDeformation_of_RS` gives the groupoid equivalence for an Artinian fibre-product square; `DefGroupoid.changeOfField` pulls back the object and framing with its cocycle.

**Checks.**

- `DefGroupoidTests.scheme` for a scheme the groupoid is discrete
- `DefGroupoidTests.bg` for BG, deformations are G-torsors over Spec A with a chosen trivialization over k; the automorphisms of the trivial framed torsor are `ker(G(A) → G(k))`, so over A = k this group is trivial. `G(k)` acts by changing the framing
- `DefGroupoidTests.noRS` the covariant ideal functor does not satisfy RS: on `k[ε₁,ε₂]/(ε₁²,ε₁ε₂,ε₂²)=k[ε]×_k k[ε]`, the distinct ideals `(ε₁+ε₂)` and `(ε₁,ε₂)` have the same two projected ideals `(ε)`, so the fibre-product comparison is not injective on the set of ideals. As a functor of discrete groupoids it is faithful but not full, hence not fully faithful or an equivalence.
(Stacks, Section 98.3 (tag 07T2), Section 98.6 (tag 07WT).)
*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18).

Prove `deformationFunctorOfPoint`. `Def_{𝒳,x₀}(A) = π₀ 𝒟ef_{𝒳,x₀}(A)` is a predeformation functor; under (RS) its tangent space `T𝒟ef` and the infinitesimal automorphisms `Inf(𝒟ef)` are `k`-vector spaces, finite-dimensional under axiom `[3]`, and `Inf = 0` when `𝒳` is a functor.
(Stacks, Section 98.8 (tag 07WY).)
*Needs:* §8.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4).

Prove `stabiliserActionOnDeformations`. `Aut(x₀)` acts on `𝒟ef_{𝒳,x₀}` by changing the chosen identification `x|_k ≅ x₀`. `Inf(𝒟ef_{𝒳,x₀})` is the tangent space of the stabilizer at the identity. No identification of a coarse-space deformation functor with pointwise orbits is asserted. Finite inertia alone also does not make the full inertia flat, as required for full-inertia rigidification.
(Stacks, Section 98.8 (tag 07WY), Section 98.21 (tag 07Y6).)
*Needs:* §5.1, §8.1.
`StabiliserTests.signQuotient` in characteristic different from 2 uses `[A¹/(ℤ/2)]` with coarse coordinate `t = x²`. At `x = 0` and A = k[ε]/(ε²), every framed source point `x ∈ (ε)` has `x² = 0`, whereas the coarse deformation `t = ε` exists. Thus even a tame finite quotient does not identify coarse deformations with orbits of source deformations.

### 8.2 Formal effectivity, versality and algebraization

Define `formalObject`. A formal object of `𝒳`: a Noetherian complete local `S`-algebra `R` with residue field of finite type over `S`, objects `ξ_n` over `Spec(R/𝔪ⁿ)` for `n≥1` with compatible cartesian transition morphisms `ξ_n → ξ_{n+1}`; the restriction functor from objects over `Spec R`, *effective* meaning in its essential image, *versal* meaning versal in the predeformation category of §8.1.

Assume `S` locally Noetherian.

The API consists of `FormalObject.restrict` retains the object and all compatible transition morphisms on every R/𝔪ⁿ; `FormalObject.IsEffective` is essential-image membership for that exact restriction functor, with a chosen comparison when used; `FormalObject.IsVersal` is lifting for the framed Artinian deformation category, and does not assert tangent bijectivity.

**Checks.**

- `FormalObjectTests.scheme` for a scheme, a compatible system of `R/𝔪ⁿ`-points
- `FormalObjectTests.powerSeries` the universal deformation of a smooth point lives over `k[[t_1, …, t_d]]`
- `FormalObjectTests.nonEffective` for the functor Nil(A) of nilpotent elements, the compatible points t mod `tⁿ` over `R=k[[t]]` are nilpotent at every finite level, but their unique limit t is not nilpotent in R; hence this tower is not effective.
(Stacks, Definition 98.9.1 (tag 07X4), Definition 98.9.4 (tag 07X7), Definition 98.12.1 (tag 0CXJ).)
*Needs:* §8.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.8, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, AdicSpacesPartIII F0.5.

Prove `formalObjectsEffectiveAlgebraic`. For an algebraic stack the restriction functor of §8.2 is an equivalence: every formal object is effective, and every compatible formal isomorphism lifts uniquely. Automorphism groups are preserved, not made trivial; uniqueness refers to a lift of a specified formal comparison.
(Stacks, Lemma 98.9.5 (tag 07X8).)
*Needs:* §8.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20).
`EffectivityTests.scalarAutomorphisms` for `B𝔾_m` over a complete R has automorphism group `Rˣ`; these persist in the compatible formal system. This rules out unframed uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.

Prove `completedLocalRingProRepresents`. For an algebraic space X locally of finite type over a field k and a k-rational point `x₀`, suppose an étale scheme chart `U → X` with a specified k-rational lift u of `x₀` is given. Then `Def_{X,x₀}` on local Artinian k-algebras with fixed residue k is pro-represented by the completion of `O_{U,u}`; its identification is independent of such a chart. For a stack and a smooth scheme presentation `U → 𝒳` with a lift u and matching residue field, the completion gives a versal formal object. It is a hull if, in addition, its map on tangent spaces is bijective. Neither vanishing infinitesimal automorphisms nor smoothness of the presentation supplies that tangent condition.
(Stacks, Section 98.9 (tag 07X3) (the bijection for representable `X`), Lemma 98.12.3 (tag 0CXK).)
*Needs:* §8.1, §8.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.6).
`CompletionTests.smoothPadding` takes `A¹_k → Spec k` at 0: the versal ring `k[[t]]` has a one-dimensional tangent space while `Def_{Spec k}` has tangent zero, so it is not a hull even though `Inf = 0`. `CompletionTests.etaleResidueField` records that an étale chart whose residue field extends k belongs to a different coefficient category until the residue-field identification is specified.

Prove `presentationCompletionVersal`. For `U → 𝒳` smooth and `u` a finite-type point, the object `U → 𝒳` is versal at `u`, and for `R = O^∧_{U,u}` its formal restriction is versal; in general an object `x/U` is versal at `u` iff its formal restriction is.
(Stacks, Definition 98.12.2 (tag 07XF), Lemma 98.12.3 (tag 0CXK).)
*Needs:* §8.2.

Prove `versalApproximation`. If `ξ` is a versal effective formal object over `R` with residue field `k`, `O_{S,s}` is a G-ring at the image point, and `𝒳` is limit preserving on objects, then there are a finite-type `S`-scheme `U`, a point `u₀` with `κ(u₀) = k`, and `x/U` versal at `u₀` restricting to `ξ_n` over `Spec(O_{U,u₀}/𝔪ⁿ)` for all `n`.
(Stacks, Lemma 98.10.1 (tag 07XB), Lemma 98.12.7 (tag 07XH).)
*Needs:* §6.1, §8.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21).

Prove `algebraisationVersalFormal`. If `𝒳` satisfies axioms `[1]`–`[4]` (§7.1) over an excellent base and `ξ` is a versal formal object over `R` with finite-type residue field, then `ξ` is effective and algebraises: an algebraic space `U` of finite type over `S` and `x/U` versal at `u` with `O^∧_{U,u} ≅ R` inducing `ξ`.
(Stacks, Lemma 98.12.7 (tag 07XH), including its proof of the complete-local-ring isomorphism; effectiveness is axiom `[4]`, limit preservation is axiom `[1]`, and excellence supplies the G-ring condition. )
*Needs:* §7.1, §8.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.21), SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10).

Prove `deformationExamples`. For a k-rational point of a smooth k-scheme of dimension d, Def of the point is pro-represented by `k[[t_1,…,t_d]]`. For the origin of the fixed node `Spec k[x,y]`/(xy), Def of the point is represented by `k[[x,y]]`/(xy), with tangent dimension 2. Separately, the deformation functor of the nodal singularity has the smoothing family xy = t over `k[[t]]` (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6). For BG with G smooth affine and the trivial framed torsor, every Artinian local k-algebra with residue k has one isomorphism class of framed deformation, infinitesimal automorphisms Lie(G), and automorphism group `ker(G(A) → G(k))`.
(Stacks, Section 98.8 (tag 07WY); SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6.)
*Needs:* §8.1, §8.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10).
`DefExamples.nonsmoothGroup` uses `μ_p` in characteristic p over `k[ε]/(ε²)`: the torsor `z^p = 1+ε` reduces to the trivial torsor and is nontrivial, since a p-th power has no ε term. `DefExamples.nodePoint` contrasts the two-dimensional tangent of a moving point on a fixed node with the one-parameter smoothing of the singularity.

### 8.3 Exact completion and tangent interfaces

Define `FramedDeformation`. For a category fibred in groupoids X over S, an object `x₀` over k, and a local Artinian S-algebra A with specified residue identification `A/m_A≅k`, `Def_X`,`x₀(A)` has objects `(y,α)`, `y∈X(A)`, `α:x₀≅y|k`. An arrow `f:(y,α)→(z,β)` is an isomorphism over A with `(f|k)∘α=β`. Base change uses the chosen pullback coherence. The set-valued deformation functor is the set of isomorphism classes of this framed groupoid, not the raw set of objects and not the unframed fibre `X(A)`.

Here Fix universes and an affine open `Spec Λ⊂S` containing the image of the point. Use a Noetherian Λ and finite `Λ→k` with the Artinian coefficient category of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.2 and its completion. The classical hull case additionally requires Λ complete local and `Λ→k` its residue quotient; For Stacks 98 use k of finite type over S. For a geometric point with a larger residue field use a specified base change to a k-rational point; do not identify its functor with the completion of the original stalk.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), 98.3, equation (98.3.1.1) and Lemmas 98.3.1–3, pp. 4–5).

The API gives `FramedDeformation.reframe_object`: Reframing by g∈`Aut(x₀)` leaves the A-object y fixed; `FramedDeformation.reframe_frame`: The new frame is `α∘g`; composition is `g.hom` followed by α; `FramedDeformation.arrow_criterion`: An underlying arrow f lifts to a framed arrow exactly when its reduction carries α to β; this lift is unique.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.toSkeleton_eq_toSkeleton_iff`.

**Checks.**

- `FramedTests.residueIdentity`: For reduction=id on `X(k)`, between any two framed objects there is exactly one arrow.
- `FramedTests.discrete`: For a discrete fibre and identity reduction, its framed object is the specified point, agreeing with the structured-arrow fibre.
- `FramedTests.nontrivialFrame`: A nonidentity automorphism g changes the identity frame to g. Collapsing the frame to a Boolean condition fails this test.

Prove `framedDeformation_twoFibre`. A morphism `X→Y` and a chosen identification of its special-fibre object induce `Def_X`,`x₀→Def_Y`,`y₀`. These assignments preserve 2-fibre products: for `W=X×_Y Z` and `w₀=(x₀,z₀,γ₀)`, `Def_W`,`w₀≃Def_X`,`x₀×_(Def_Y,y₀)Def_Z`,`z₀`. A representable formally smooth morphism induces a smooth morphism of predeformation categories.

Here S locally Noetherian; residue k finite type over S; all products are 2-products with their specified gluing isomorphism; Smoothness means essential surjectivity of the lifting comparison for Artinian surjections; its groupoid definition is `deformationGroupoid` (§8.1).

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemmas 98.3.2–3, p. 5).

For the proof, transport the frame through the morphism using the pullback comparison; then an object of a 2-product consists of two deformations and an isomorphism whose residue is `γ₀`; the framed constructions match on arrows; then use representable infinitesimal lifting after forming the fibre product over an Artinian test scheme.

*Needs:* `FramedDeformation`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4.

Define `InfinitesimalStabilizer`. For a deformation y over `A′` and its restriction z over A, `Inf(y/z)` is the kernel of `Aut_A′(y)→Aut_A(z)`. The infinitesimal stabilizer at `x₀` is this kernel for the trivial dual-number deformation over `k[ε]→k`. Its group law is specified from automorphisms. It is distinct from the entire residual stabilizer `Aut_k(x₀)`.

Here Pullback supplies the reduction functor and a specified comparison to z; The dual-number definition uses the split extension `k→k[ε]→k` and the trivial pullback of `x₀`.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Definitions 90.19.1–2 and Remark 90.19.3, pp. 55–56).

The API gives `InfinitesimalStabilizer.mem_iff`: Membership means the induced automorphism after reduction is the identity; `InfinitesimalStabilizer.framedAut`: The automorphism group of a framed object is multiplicatively equivalent to its reduction kernel; `InfinitesimalStabilizer.faithful`: For a faithful reduction functor the kernel is trivial.

*Needs:* `FramedDeformation`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 (`inertia`).

**Checks.**

- `StabilizerTests.identity`: Identity reduction has bottom kernel.
- `StabilizerTests.allKilled`: On the one-object category of a group G, the functor induced by the trivial homomorphism `G→G` has top kernel.
- `StabilizerTests.frameKernel`: For a frame α, g belongs to the reduction kernel iff reduction(g)∘`α=α`.

Prove `infinitesimalStabilizer_linearization`. If X satisfies the Rim–Schlessinger condition, `Inf_x₀(X)` has a natural k-vector-space structure and its addition agrees with composition. For a surjection `A′→A` of kernel I killed by `m_A′` (in particular a small extension), `Inf(y/z)` is canonically the corresponding additive group `Inf_x₀(X)⊗_k I`, with identity as its origin. If `Inf_x₀(X)=0`, every framed Artinian fibre is a setoid and `Def_X`,`x₀` is equivalent to its isomorphism-class functor.

Here k and the coefficient category follow the framed conventions; RS is an equivalence of groupoids for the prescribed Artinian ring pullbacks, not merely a surjection on classes.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Lemmas 90.19.6–13, pp. 56–58).

For the proof, apply RS to the automorphism functor at the identity. The two split dual-number directions define addition and scalar multiplication; then functoriality of composition and its shared identity force vector addition to agree with composition; then identify the kernel for a surjection annihilated by the maximal ideal with lifts of the identity. Factor arbitrary Artinian surjections into small extensions to propagate vanishing.

*Needs:* `InfinitesimalStabilizer`, `ArtinCriteria.StrongInfinitesimalGluing`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Prove `framedTangent_exactSequence`. For `X→Y←Z` satisfying RS and a point `w₀` of `W=X×_Y Z`, there is a natural exact sequence of k-vector spaces `0→Inf_W→Inf_X⊕Inf_Z→Inf_Y→T_W→T_X⊕T_Z→T_Y`. Here T means isomorphism classes of framed dual-number deformations; the map `Inf_Y→T_W` changes the gluing isomorphism by an infinitesimal automorphism.

Here S locally Noetherian; `w₀` over a field k finite type over S; Use the chosen gluing identification at `w₀` to compare the Y-valued objects. The two difference maps use compatible opposite signs.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.8.2, p. 11; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Lemma 90.26.2, p. 66).

For the proof, use framed 2-fibre compatibility; then construct the boundary by changing the gluing arrow of the trivial dual-number pair. RS makes this construction linear; then an arrow lifts precisely when the corresponding change of gluing can be absorbed into the two source autos; this gives exactness at `Inf_Y` and `T_W`. Check the remaining kernels directly.

*Needs:* `framedDeformation_twoFibre`, `infinitesimalStabilizer_linearization`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3.

Define `CompletedLocalRing`. For a scheme X and point x, CompletedLocalRing(X,x) is the maximal-ideal adic completion of the actual stalk `O_X`,x. Its structural map is the algebra map from the stalk; its n-th jet, indexed from zero, is the projection to `O_X`,`x/m_x^(n+1)`. Under Noetherianity it is a complete Noetherian local ring with the same residue field. This construction alone says nothing about a stack having a canonical completed local ring.

Here Noetherianity is required for the stated complete-local properties and for the prorepresentability comparison; A geometric point with residue extension requires a specified coefficient-compatible model; the original stalk is not relabelled as a k-algebra.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.12.3 and its proof, pp. 18–19; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/algebra.pdf), Lemmas 10.97.4–6, pp. 227–228).

The API gives `CompletedLocalRing.ofStalk`: The canonical local ring map `O_X`,x→CompletedLocalRing(X,x); localness uses Noetherianity; `CompletedLocalRing.jet`: Projection to `O_X`,`x/m_x^(n+1)`; `CompletedLocalRing.jet_ofStalk`: Projection of a stalk element equals its quotient class; `CompletedLocalRing.ext`: Equality of every positive-order jet implies equality in the completion; `CompletedLocalRing.isAdicComplete`: For a Noetherian stalk, its completion is complete for its own maximal ideal, using the maximal-ideal-completeness theorem; `CompletedLocalRing.isNoetherianRing`: For a Noetherian stalk, its completed ring is Noetherian (Stacks, Lemma 10.97.5, tag 05GH).

*Needs:* Mathlib `AdicCompletion`, Mathlib `AdicCompletion.evalₐ`, Mathlib `AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ`, Mathlib `AdicCompletion.isLocalRing_of_fg`, Mathlib `AdicCompletion.residueField_map_bijective`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.7, Mathlib `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete_of_fg`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4.

**Checks.**

- `CompletionTests.field`: at the point of `Spec k`, the completion is k and every jet projection is the identity.
- `CompletionTests.line`: at the origin of `A¹_k` the completion is `k[[x]]`, with jets given by truncation modulo `x^(n+1)`. Every compatible tower of these quotient classes is induced by a unique completed element. Over ℚ the tower of truncations of `Σ_{j≥1}x^(j!)` is effective here and has no antecedent in `ℚ[x]_(x)`: rational power-series coefficients satisfy an eventual finite linear recurrence, which these increasingly separated nonzero coefficients cannot satisfy.
- `CompletionTests.node`: at the origin of `Spec k[x,y]`/(xy), the completion is `k[[x,y]]`/(xy), with xy=0 and x,y both nonzero; its residue field is k. The jet maps preserve these products and the structural map induces the identity on k.

Prove `schemeFramedCompletionEquiv`. Let X be locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and x a finite-type point with `k=κ(x)`. On `C_Λ`, the framed deformation functor of X at x is naturally isomorphic to `h_R`, where `R=Ô_X,x` and `h_R(A)` consists of continuous local Λ-algebra maps `R→A` inducing the specified identity on k. Thus the identity formal family prorepresents this scheme-point deformation functor.

Here Choose `Spec Λ⊂S` containing the image of x and the associated residue structure; For an algebraically closed geometric residue k work with the appropriate k-rational base-changed model. This is a deformation of a point into X, not a deformation of X as a scheme.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.12.3, proof identification of predeformation categories, pp. 18–19).

For the proof, a map Spec `A→X` restricting to x factors through any chosen affine neighbourhood of x and induces a local map `O_X`,`x→A`; then its maximal ideal maps to the nilpotent maximal ideal of A, hence the map factors through some finite jet and extends uniquely to the completion; then the two operations are inverse and compatible with maps in `C_Λ`. Scheme fibres have no nontrivial arrows, so the groupoid reduces to the represented set-valued functor.

*Needs:* `FramedDeformation`, `CompletedLocalRing`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.7.

Prove `spaceFramedEtaleCompletionEquiv`. For an algebraic space X locally of finite type over S, a pointed étale chart `(U,u)→(X,x)` with `κ(u)=κ(x)=k` induces an equivalence of framed Artinian deformation functors. Consequently `Ô_U,u` prorepresents the point-deformation functor, and another such chart gives a unique compatible isomorphism of prorepresenting pairs. Do not use an arbitrary smooth chart for this conclusion.

Here S locally Noetherian and x finite type; Specify the residue comparison and the chart lift of the point. For a geometric point first pass to the specified residue-field base change.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.3.2, p. 5 and Lemma 98.12.3, pp. 18–19; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-spaces.pdf), Lemma 87.33.3, pp. 74–75).

For the proof, étale formal lifting uniquely lifts the nilpotent Artinian test morphism through the chosen residue point; then compare any two charts through their pointed fibre product, using unique étale lifting; then apply the scheme completion comparison and uniqueness of the representing natural isomorphism.

*Needs:* `schemeFramedCompletionEquiv`, `framedDeformation_twoFibre`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `schemeRelativeTangentEquiv`. For `X/S` as in the scheme comparison, the tangent space of its framed point functor is `Der_Λ(O_X,x,k)` at the specified residue point. For a k-rational point of a k-scheme this is naturally `Hom_k(m_x/m_x²,k)`, hence the existing ZariskiTangentSpace(X,x). For a general relative base retain relative differentials or derivations; the absolute stalk cotangent dual is not asserted to equal the relative tangent.

Here the k-rational special case fixes base `S=Spec k` and its structural k-algebra map; For an arbitrary point map use the algebra structure it induces on k in a fresh local scope, as required by the dual-number equivalence.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.8.1, proof pp. 10–11; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Example 90.11.11, p. 34; equation 90.15.0.1, p. 44).

For the proof, restrict the natural comparison to `k[ε]`; then apply the dual-number lift–derivation equivalence with the correct algebra tower; then the affine rational-point cotangent localization equivalence is already Tau Ceti. Dualize that equivalence and use the derivation–cotangent universal property (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.derivationToDualNumberEquivLift`); reduce a non-affine point to its affine neighbourhood. Only the geometric functor transport is new.

*Needs:* `schemeFramedCompletionEquiv`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.derivationToDualNumberEquivLift`, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskiTangentSpace`, Tau Ceti `AlgHom.kernelCotangentLinearEquivZariski`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Define `FormalObject`. For a fixed complete Noetherian local S-algebra R with residue k, a formal object of X is a tower `ξ_n∈X(R/m_R^(n+1))`, `n≥0`, with restriction isomorphisms `ξ_(n+1)|_(R/m^(n+1))≅ξ_n`. Morphisms are levelwise arrows commuting with these comparisons. Composites of adjacent comparisons define all longer transitions. The category is a groupoid at fixed R, and changes of complete local base use coherent pullback.

Here Use positive quotient powers indexed from zero and the actual restriction functors; In the Stacks convention k is finite type over S. The general statement takes a specified tower of groupoids; assembling the tower `X(R/m^(n+1))` from a stack uses the restriction functors of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definition 98.9.1, pp. 11–12; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Definitions 90.7.1 and 90.7.3, pp. 15–16).

The API gives `FormalObject.evaluation`: The n-th object/arrow evaluation is a functor to `X(R/m^(n+1))`; `FormalObject.hom_ext`: Two formal arrows are equal if all their levelwise arrows agree; `FormalObject.isomorphism_iff`: An isomorphism of formal objects is equivalent to a family of levelwise isomorphisms commuting with gluing.

*Needs:* `FramedDeformation`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.7, `ArtinCriteria.FormalPoint`.

**Checks.**

- `FormalTests.point`: The constant discrete point tower has one object up to isomorphism.
- `FormalTests.compatibleArrows`: Every formal arrow must commute with each gluing square; an incompatible component sequence is excluded.
- `FormalTests.automorphisms`: For a constant one-object groupoid tower with identity reduction, evaluation at level zero identifies formal automorphisms with the group at that level, even when gluing is nontrivial.

Define `IsEffective`. Let `res_R:X(R)→FormalObject_X(R)` be the coherent restriction functor. A formal object ξ is effective if there is `y∈X(R)` with a specified isomorphism `res_R(y)≅ξ`. Effectivity of all objects is essential surjectivity. Full faithfulness of `res_R` is a separate property required to compare arrows and descend algebraizations; equivalence combines both properties.

Here R complete Noetherian local over S with the fixed residue convention; The affine set-valued effectivity predicate `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective` (§7.1) applies only after passing to sets of isomorphism classes; it does not imply groupoid equivalence.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definition 98.9.4 and equation 98.9.3.1, p. 12).

The API gives `IsEffective.ofRestriction`: Every object actually restricted from `X(R)` is effective; `IsEffective.iso_iff`: An isomorphism of formal objects transports effectivity; `IsEffective.all_iff`: All formal objects are effective iff `res_R` is essentially surjective.

*Needs:* `FormalObject`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.EssSurj`, `ArtinCriteria.IsEffective`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

**Checks.**

- `EffectiveTests.identity`: Identity restriction makes every object effective.
- `EffectiveTests.empty`: A functor from the empty groupoid cannot effect any object of a nonempty formal target.
- `EffectiveTests.notFullyFaithful`: The constant functor from the one-object groupoid of `(ℤ,+)` to the formal point tower is essentially surjective and is not faithful. Object effectivity must not imply equivalence.

Prove `completeLocalSpaceRestriction_bijective`. For any algebraic space X over S and a complete Noetherian local S-algebra R, restriction gives a bijection `Mor_S(Spec R,X)→lim_(n≥0) Mor_S(Spec(R/m^(n+1)),X)`. No properness, separatedness or finite-presentation condition on X is required for this statement.

Here R is complete, separated, local and Noetherian; This theorem concerns maps from the fixed complete local base, not existence of a finite-type algebraization of an arbitrary formal scheme.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-spaces.pdf), Lemmas 87.33.2–3, tags 0AQG/0AQH, pp. 74–75).

For the proof, for schemes every map from the local test rings lies in a single affine neighbourhood; compatible ring maps have a unique complete limit; then for space injectivity, the equalizer is a locally quasi-finite separated scheme; all-order agreement forces equality at its local ring; then for surjectivity choose a pointed étale cover after a finite separable residue extension, lift to its finite étale complete-local extension, effect the scheme maps, then descend using injectivity on the finite product of complete local overlap rings.

*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.7, `FormalObject`.

Prove `algebraicStackRestriction_equivalence`. Let S be locally Noetherian and X an algebraic stack over S. Restriction from objects over complete Noetherian local S-algebras with residue field finite type over S to formal objects is an equivalence, compatible with change of such bases. In particular each `res_R` is fully faithful and essentially surjective.

Here Algebraicity of X is already established; this result cannot supply the effectivity hypothesis while algebraicity is still being proved; The diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and an actual smooth surjective atlas exists.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.9.5, tag 07X8, pp. 12–14).

For the proof, for full faithfulness represent `Isom(y,z)` by an algebraic space and apply complete-local space restriction; then for objects choose a smooth atlas, pass to a finite separable residue extension and its finite étale complete local ring, and recursively lift a compatible atlas point across successive square-zero quotients; then effect the scheme map; full faithfulness identifies descent arrows over the overlap and proves their cocycle. Effective fppf descent gives the object over R and its specified all-order comparison.

*Needs:* `completeLocalSpaceRestriction_bijective`, `IsEffective`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.20–1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Prove `restriction_twoFibre_equivalence`. If complete-local restriction is an equivalence for X, Y and Z, it is an equivalence for `X×_Y Z`. Compatible objects and the comparison isomorphism are all algebraized; uniqueness of the isomorphism follows from full faithfulness for Y.

Here the three categories are fibred in groupoids over S; equivalences are compatible with base change; All three equivalences are hypotheses; mere object effectivity in Y is insufficient.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.9.6, p. 14).

For the proof, identify restriction for the product as the 2-product of the three restriction functors; then effect the two objects, lift the gluing isomorphism through the Y equivalence, and transport the coherence; then use equivalence invariance of 2-products for arrows and base maps.

*Needs:* `IsEffective`, `FormalObject`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

Define `FamilyVersalAt`. Let U be locally of finite type over S, `y∈X(U)`, u a finite-type point and `x₀=y|κ(u)`. The family is versal at u if the induced map `Def_U`,`u→Def_X`,`x₀` is smooth: for each Artinian surjection `B→A` the comparison `Def_U`,`u(B)→Def_U`,`u(A)×_(Def_X,x₀(A))Def_X`,`x₀(B)` is essentially surjective. The 2-product retains its comparison arrow. A formal object ξ over R is versal if `h_R→Def_X`,`x₀` has the same lifting property.

Here S locally Noetherian, X fibred in groupoids, `k=κ(u)` finite type over S; Use the groupoid version of the smoothness of deformation functors of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, not an unframed surjectivity statement on objects.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Definitions 98.12.1–2, p. 18; Lemmas 98.12.3–5, pp. 18–19; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Definition 90.8.1, Lemma 90.8.2 and Remark 90.8.3, pp. 20–21; Situation 90.29.1 and Lemma 90.29.5, pp. 71–73).

The API gives `FamilyVersalAt.smallExtension_iff`: It suffices to test small extensions: surjections with nonzero principal kernel killed by the source maximal ideal. Equivalently one may test all surjections with kernel killed by that ideal; `FamilyVersalAt.completion_iff`: The family is versal at u iff its completed-local formal object is versal; `FamilyVersalAt.finiteResidueExtension`: Under RS, finite residue extensions preserve the smooth pointed deformation morphism.

*Needs:* `FramedDeformation`, `FormalObject`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18.

**Checks.**

- `VersalTests.identity`: The identity family of a locally finite-type scheme is versal at every finite-type point.
- `VersalTests.excessParameter`: `A¹_k→Spec k` is smooth and versal at zero; its tangent map `k→0` is not bijective, so it is not a hull.
- `VersalTests.closedPoint`: `Spec k→A¹_k` at zero is not versal: the dual-number point `t↦ε` cannot lift through the closed point.

Prove `familyVersalAt_completion_iff`. For y over U locally of finite type over locally Noetherian S and a finite-type u, let ξ be its formal restriction over `R=Ô_U,u`. Then y is versal at u iff ξ is versal. For a morphism `U→V` of schemes locally of finite type over S, this is also equivalent to the morphism being smooth at u.

Here Use the same coefficient and residue maps for `h_R` and `Def_U`,u; The scheme smoothness conclusion applies to a genuine locally finite-type scheme morphism; no arbitrary CFG is declared smooth from a predicate alone.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemmas 98.12.3–4, pp. 18–19).

For the proof, identify `Def_U`,u with `h_R` by the completed-local universal property; then the morphism induced by y under this identification is exactly the morphism of its formal object; then for schemes apply the local infinitesimal criterion of smoothness with the stated finiteness assumptions.

*Needs:* `FamilyVersalAt`, `schemeFramedCompletionEquiv`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `smoothChart_versalHullComparison`. A smooth representable chart `U→X` at a specified lift u of `x₀` induces a smooth `h_(Ô_U,u)→Def_X`,`x₀`, hence a versal formal family. In the classical equal-residue coefficient setting, its isomorphism-class transformation is a hull exactly when its tangent map is bijective. Under RS and `Inf_X`,`x₀=0` the framed category is setoid-valued; if the chart map is also tangent-bijective, Schlessinger's prorepresentability criterion (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4) makes this pair prorepresent the framed functor. `Inf=0` alone does not make an arbitrary smooth-chart ring prorepresent it.

Here S locally Noetherian; U locally finite type over S; u finite type with the fixed residue field; For the hull/prorepresentability clause use coefficient residue k and the conditions H1–H4 of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3. Exclude the inseparable-residue orbit notion of minimality from the tangent-bijective clause.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.3.2, p. 5; Lemma 98.12.3, pp. 18–19; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Lemma 90.18.1, p. 54; Lemmas 90.19.12–13, p. 58).

For the proof, representable smooth lifting makes the pointed chart morphism smooth; use the completion identification; then the definition of hull adds tangent bijectivity to this smooth transformation; then when `Inf=0`, RS passes through the setoid equivalence to give the required set-valued gluing. Apply Schlessinger's prorepresentability criterion and the hull comparison of SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4.

*Needs:* `familyVersalAt_completion_iff`, `framedDeformation_twoFibre`, `infinitesimalStabilizer_linearization`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.3.

Prove `completedAtlasPresentation_equivalence`. For a smooth pointed atlas `U→X` of an algebraic stack, the framed deformation category at `x₀` is equivalent to the groupoid quotient of `Def_U`,u by `Def_(U×_X U)`,r, where r is the identity relation point (u,u,id). The object functor is represented by `Ô_U,u`; the relation functor is represented through a pointed étale chart of the algebraic space `U×_X U` at r. Source, target, identity, inverse and composition are the induced formal maps, and their coherence is retained. This is a presentation, not a choice-independent ring attached to X.

Here Residue points u,r have the fixed k; use the geometric base change when needed; U is locally finite type over S locally Noetherian. X satisfies RS, as algebraic stacks do; The relation chart is étale with the prescribed residue field; its completion represents the identity-framed relation functor. The unframed stabilizer has other residual arrows that are not included in this single formal neighbourhood.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.3.3, p. 5; [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/formal-defos.pdf), Lemma 90.26.1, pp. 65–66 and Lemma 90.26.2, p. 66).

For the proof, apply framed 2-fibre compatibility to `U×_X U` at the identity arrow; then smooth lifting of the atlas makes `Def_U`,u essentially surjective onto the framed category on Artinian tests; then the relation arrows and composition recover that category by the presentation of SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 (`stack_presentation`); replace the scheme/space point functors by their completion representatives.

*Needs:* `spaceFramedEtaleCompletionEquiv`, `smoothChart_versalHullComparison`, `framedDeformation_twoFibre`, `framedTangent_exactSequence`, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.20–1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.18, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1.

Prove `effectiveVersal_algebraization`. Let S be locally Noetherian, X fibred in groupoids and limit preserving on objects, and ξ a formal object over a complete Noetherian local S-algebra R with residue k finite type over S, image `s∈S`. If ξ is effective and versal and `O_S`,s is a G-ring, there are `U→S` of finite type, a finite-type `u∈U` with `κ(u)=k`, and `y∈X(U)`, versal at u, with an isomorphism `R≅Ô_U,u` and a compatible identification of all the `ξ_n` with the formal restrictions of y. The isomorphism and family need not be unique.

Here All four inputs—effectivity, versality, local G-ring and limit preservation on objects—are supplied before applying the theorem; No representable-diagonal or Artin-algebraicity conclusion is used in this theorem; The completion isomorphism is existential. It is not a promise to algebraize a prescribed arbitrary formal coordinate change exactly.

([Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/download/artin.pdf), Lemma 98.12.7, tag 07XH, pp. 20–21; Example 98.12.8, p. 21).

For the proof, effect ξ by an object over `Spec R`. Apply the approximation theorem `formal_object_approximation` (§7.1) at `N=2`, preserving the second jet and associated graded dimensions; then versality recursively lifts the approximation to all orders and gives a compatible local map `R→Ô_U,u`. The second-jet agreement makes this map surjective by the complete form of Nakayama's lemma (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 8.4); then associated graded dimension equality gives equal finite lengths at every quotient, making the surjections isomorphisms. Pass to the complete limit and transfer versality back to the algebraic family.

*Needs:* `IsEffective`, `FamilyVersalAt`, `familyVersalAt_completion_iff`, `formal_object_approximation`, `gRing_essentiallyFiniteType`, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4.

Define `ParameterFormalExports`. Over a locally Noetherian S, given a locally finite-type parameter scheme `P→S` and a parameter functor F on S-schemes with a supplied natural representation `θ:Hom_S(-,P)≅F` and a finite-type `p∈P`, let `ξ₀=θ(p)`. Transport schemeFramedCompletionEquiv through θ to obtain `h_(Ô_P,p)≅Def_F`,`ξ₀`. Export the representation, universal object, pullback naturality and this formal comparison under named projective-bundle, Grassmannian, flag, Hilbert, Quot, Hom and Isom interfaces. Space-valued parameters use the pointed étale chart comparison instead. Their original representability and geometric hypotheses are those of Layers 1 and 2 and SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 1; this target proves only the uniform point/completion transport.

Here For the scheme completion use P locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and p a finite-type point. For the space version use such a pointed étale chart with the same residue field; a chart with a residue extension is a different coefficient problem; For projective bundles, Grassmannians and flags use the quotient convention of §1.1: locally free quotients, flags of quotients with compatible kernels; For Hilbert/Quot use the exact base, projectivity, finite-presentation, sheaf and polynomial conditions from the representing theorem. `Hom/Isom` require their own representability hypotheses; they are not asserted representable for arbitrary schemes; Fix the functor’s base-change and isomorphism-class conventions.
